543223|2026-06.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
543223|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.</overview>

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 5,343 mn, down from INR 6,112 mn; EBITDA margin 6.3% vs 17.9%, hit by deferred order and FX loss.

segments.name: Marketable Molecules (cholesterol, Vitamin D and analogues)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided to single digits; France and Swiss CDMO growth slower than planned.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected similar to FY26, possibly slightly higher.
Indian entity revenue guided to grow 25-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10% (analyst's characterisation, not explicitly confirmed by management).
FY28-29: at least double-digit growth in France and India; group revenue growth above 10% YoY; EBITDA margin closer to 25-26% seen before EDQM issues.
No quarterly guidance; management said Q2 is difficult to guide. Net debt expected CHF 140-150 mn (excluding promoter infusion), reducing by about CHF 8-9 mn.
Interest expense guided at about INR 130-140 crores for the full year (about INR 35-40 crores per quarter).
Promoter ECB up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive, 10-year tenor, to prepay high-cost India debt; expected in 60-90 days. RBI approval reportedly received.
capex_capacity: Two tech transfers from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to India: one commercial contract signed with a US company (Switzerland to Bavla, to complete within FY27); a second legacy project approved by a Swiss MNC and already initiated; three more in advanced discussion.
Second co-investment with the Japanese ADC customer is in progress, with operations expected in calendar 2027.
Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.
Restarting some API production at the Netherlands entity.
Inspections scheduled for later in 2026 at Carbogen Amcis sites (no details given).
demand_pricing: New commercial leadership: Angela Ameriks joined as Global CCO; new India sales leadership; hiring in UK, Central Europe and US West Coast (start 1 Sept).
SPRINT early-phase acquisition initiative reported as successful; over 13 late-phase projects in drug substance portfolio, including PPQ campaigns.
Drug product (Saint-Beauzire, France): RFP volumes up and quotation rates raised, though market is challenging; big pharma audits had positive outcomes.
Naroda: CDMO RFPs rising steeply, several in final negotiation; semiconductor and fine-chemical projects in progress.
Biotech funding slowdown is weighing on development revenue; destocking by customers after pandemic stockpiling noted.
ADC-related revenue in the quarter was about INR 150 crores, including linker, payload and hyper molecule.
Specialty business: new wool grease sources at better prices; new markets in Vietnam, Africa and South America.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue and EBITDA margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit revenue growth for FY27; EBITDA margin similar to last year, maybe slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will the high-cost debt be refinanced?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter entity to raise up to CHF 200 mn in foreign currency and infuse it as ECB into the Indian entity, at 4% all-inclusive for 10 years; expected in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 net debt and interest expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about CHF 140-150 mn, falling CHF 8-9 mn; interest expense about INR 130-140 crores for the full year, excluding promoter infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 550 crore EBITDA for the remaining three quarters achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not be INR 200 mn each quarter, but expects EBITDA similar to last year, with focus on the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company swung between profit and loss quarter to quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lumpy B2B shipments tied to new chemical entities, a largely fixed cost base (employee cost about 50% of P&L), and Q4 typically the strongest quarter; each INR 10 mn revenue could add about 70% to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much goodwill remains and is it amortised?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated goodwill is above INR 4,000 crores, restated at closing rates and not amortised; standalone goodwill is about INR 550 crores and is amortised; original INR 1,350 crores.

544477|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 170.6% YoY to INR 304.3 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR 4.8 crore and PAT was INR 1.1 crore on toll traffic hit.
544477|2026-06.overview: Management attributed weak Q1 profitability to temporary factors: lower traffic at the Moti Naroli toll project from geopolitical and trade disruption, an NHAI temporary bidding restriction, and voluntary surrender of an unfavourable toll project. Consolidated order book stood at about INR 778 crore at June 30, 2026, with new toll wins in Tamil Nadu (INR 28.7 crore Kozhinjipatti; INR 80 crore Krishnagiri-Thumbipadi NH-44 LoA; INR 120 crore total mentioned in Q&A). Management said traffic has largely normalised outside Western-front regions and expects Q1/Q2 near break-even with recovery in H2. Guidance: FY27 turnover target of INR 850 crore (INR 700 crore toll, rest EPC) and FY28 INR 1,200 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Margin dropped per management; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.metric: EPC order book (as cited in Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: approx. INR 507 crore across 24 executable projects

segments.name: Tollway collection
segments.commentary: Asset-light model; Moti Naroli toll hit by lower traffic from geopolitical and trade disruption. New wins: INR 28.7 crore Kozhinjipatti (Tamil Nadu, NH-44) and LoA for INR 80 crore Krishnagiri-Thumbipadi toll; management cited INR 120 crore new Tamil Nadu toll projects in Q&A. Kaza described as outperforming expectations.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Focus on profitable, timely-executable projects in roads, bridges, urban, industrial and commercial. Beverly Hills private project started in Q1: about INR 70 crore, 15-16 months, expected to add at least INR 150 crore EPC revenue (about 40-45% of revenue over 15-16 months per management). Executable EPC orders: about INR 150 crore in FY27 and INR 200 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Named as a vertical in the opening remarks and closing comments; no figures disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover target about INR 850 crore, of which INR 700 crore from toll and rest from EPC.
FY28 turnover target INR 1,200 crore.
Management expects Q1 and Q2 to hover around break-even, with rapid recovery in Q3 and Q4 (past pattern); full-year results not expected to be significantly impacted.
Q2 EPC seasonally slow due to monsoon; focus on bidding quality tenders with shorter execution periods.
Management says traffic has largely normalised outside Western-front regions; Western-front recovery will take longer.
capex_capacity: Prequalification (PQ) expected to rise as current EPC projects complete, enabling sole bids for larger tenders.
Geographic expansion: Tamil Nadu entered for the first time; Andhra Pradesh and Telangana priority; West Bengal and Assam under research.
New EPC departments being targeted include MES and CPWD (central), per management.
Renewable energy/EV EPC is a new segment under preparation; no bids or pipeline size disclosed.
demand_pricing: Traffic in regions away from Western-front ports has resumed to normal per management; Western-front recovery slower as factories and trade were hit.
Bid success ratio 25-30% for both toll and EPC.
Management prefers larger toll contracts due to less competition; cited Moti Naroli as roughly 70% larger than Kaza.
Q1 EPC pipeline described as an early accumulation, not the final pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How has traffic recovered, and will it lift EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traffic in non-Western-front regions is normal; Western front will take time. Margin drop was from the geopolitical situation, expected to recover if no new shocks.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 weakness affect full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Saurabh Mittal said no significant full-year impact: Q1 and Q2 typically near break-even, with stronger Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnover target INR 850 crore for FY27 and INR 1,200 crore for FY28; FY27 split INR 700 crore toll and rest EPC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPC order book and execution timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 507 crore EPC order book across 24 executable projects: about INR 150 crore to convert in FY27 and INR 200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bid success ratio for toll and EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Both about 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Beverly Hills project's value and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 70 crore, execution of 15-16 months, expected to contribute about 40-45% of revenue over that period per management.

risks_watch: Western-front traffic and trade recovery pace, and any renewed geopolitical disruption.
Q1 and Q2 near break-even: whether Q2 EBITDA and PAT actually recover as indicated.
FY27 INR 850 crore turnover target requires a steep H2 ramp; INR 700 crore toll target is large relative to current order book.
Concentration in a few states and NHAI bidding restriction status.
Renewable/EV EPC entry and technology initiatives lack quantified targets; management declined to give numbers.
544477|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and growth, but cautious and often non-specific on numbers. Management repeatedly deferred details on renewables, technology initiatives and new states ("unless we have something concrete"), and some answers were vague or repetitive.
key_quotes: Importantly, we have already started witnessing signs of improvement in the traffic trends.

544491|2026-06.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.
544491|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 9% YoY to INR83 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR99 crore versus INR88 crore, helped by a seasonally soft Q1. Margins compressed on product mix, clove raw-material costs after Madagascar floods, and a higher fixed cost base at the new Dahej plant. Consolidated PAT was a loss of INR7.9 crore, pressured by INR9.1 crore of higher depreciation after capitalisation of most of the INR270 crore Dahej capex. Management says the new verticals (cooling agents, Safranal/Citral, phenol derivatives) start contributing from Q2 to Q4 FY27, with FY27 framed as a ramp-up year and no guidance given.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR76 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +9% YoY)
vs INR88 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +12% YoY)
Higher depreciation of INR9.1 crore after Dahej capitalisation

segments.name: Gem (core: clove and mint)
segments.commentary: Clove volumes and sales were hit by Madagascar cyclone/floods, with Toamasina port shut for close to 30 days; incoming raw material resumed from May. Mint harvest runs May to July, with export orders now flowing, though some May-June shipments were not yet recognised as they had not reached destinations.

segments.name: Krystal Ingredients (Dahej, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Safranal commercial production has started, with revenue expected by end-Q2 FY27 and meaningful from Q3. Cooling agents Gemcool 3, 5 and 23 are in production with initial orders; meaningful contribution expected from Q3 FY27. Phenol derivatives: trial production by end-Q2, commercial production targeted Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management will give guidance toward calendar year-end for the next year.
Krystal products expected to exceed 50% of overall revenue in FY28.
Management expects Eugenol and derivatives to be fairly close to planned numbers by year-end FY27, per Yash Parekh.
Cooling agents: management expects a large part of the targeted volumes (on 500-ton capacity, about 25% utilisation with two customers) to show up in Q3 and Q4.
Operating leverage expected to support margins and profitability over the medium term as utilisation rises.
capex_capacity: Total Dahej plant capex about INR270 crore; nearly INR265 crore incurred and substantially capitalised.
Standby capacity at Dahej is already absorbing depreciation, interest and manpower costs ahead of revenue.
Cooling agents: 500-ton capacity referenced by analyst; management said utilisation would be close to the analyst's 25% figure.
Phenol derivatives: commercial production targeted Q3 FY27, subject to approvals and quality processes.
Brazil subsidiary approved to expand Latin America distribution for essential oils, aroma chemicals and specialty chemicals.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is back to normal levels, with Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) demand ramping up.
Cooling agents are used in oral care, confectionery and specialty flavours; cooling agent approvals from two of the world's largest consumers, per management.
Clove raw-material pricing rose after Madagascar supply disruption, weighing on margins.
Shipping challenges out of India and to the Western Hemisphere are a key concern for timing.
Currency: management said the rupee depreciation is neither a tactical advantage nor disadvantage, since imports are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Where is demand coming from in the core business, and which geographies are growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is back to normal; Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) is ramping, with export deal flow and new product seasonality expected to show in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol derivatives ramp delayed, and what is the timeline to commercial production?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end-Q2 FY27, commercial production in Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; pilot batches are approved and customers want plant-level trials. Traders and distributors are being targeted for faster approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Madagascar disruption materially delay the Eugenol ramp, and is clove tree supply structurally at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Port reopened and material is flowing; management expects Eugenol numbers close to plan by year-end. Trees are still productive and sourcing is diversified across Madagascar and East Africa, so no major structural issue foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business reach sustainable consolidated profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a timing mismatch: depreciation, interest and manpower costs are already in the P&L while higher-margin Krystal revenue has not yet arrived. Profitability should improve as the new products ramp.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital evolve for Krystal?
qa_highlights.answer: Krystal is synthetic and needs less inventory, so its working cycle should be lower than Gem's; factoring is also being used to reduce debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the Gemcool orders, and are new products higher margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Order values and customer names are not being disclosed. Management said each new product is intended to be more margin-accretive than existing products; several are in approval stages with revenue expected from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Did the tariff-relief restocking show up in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mint harvest timing, clove delays and shipping issues pushed revenue into later periods; May-June exports were made but not yet recognised as they had not reached final destinations, with roll-over expected in July-August.

risks_watch: Consolidated loss and 3.3% EBITDA margin until Krystal revenue ramps; depreciation of INR9.1 crore per quarter will persist.
Qualification timelines for cooling agents, Safranal and phenol derivatives; any slippage from Q2/Q3/Q4 FY27 targets.
Clove supply from Madagascar and shipping disruptions to the Western Hemisphere.
Clove and raw-material cost pass-through, given higher clove costs in Q1.
Working capital and cash generation at the consolidated level; standalone cash PAT (INR8.9 crore) compares with consolidated cash PAT of INR1.3 crore.
Customer and order disclosure is limited; no order values or customer names given.
544491|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term commercialisation and the Krystal pipeline, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: no FY27 guidance, no order values, and no margin ballpark. Near-term weakness is attributed to Madagascar, shipping, mix and the timing of new-plant costs.

505726|2026-06.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crore, with PAT up to INR 38.06 crore, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on.
505726|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crore and PBDIT rose 26.46% to INR 88.46 crore, with margin at 5.79% of revenue versus 5.34%. PAT was INR 38.06 crore (2.5% of revenue) against INR 25.36 crore a year earlier. Management said commodity and forex headwinds are not behind the company and that it has not been able to pass them on in price, relying instead on cost initiatives (INR 42-43 crore in Q1). Home Appliances (HAD) revenue grew about 18%, with July described as good, while gross margin fell about 160 bps.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 vs Q1 FY26; FY26 HAD growth was about 9.8-10%
FY26 full year: about INR 67 crore
Attributed to raw material price increase of about INR 4,125 per tonne in the quarter

segments.name: Home Appliances (HAD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 18% in Q1; front-load volume up 9-10%, top-load volume up over 20%, AC volume up 6-8%, and IFB-branch refrigerator volume up 14% per management. Gross margin down about 160 bps on material costs.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales up 17% YoY and above budget; EBITDA in line with budget. Management expects similar growth going forward, with festive season supportive. Stated FY ambition of about INR 2,000 crore revenue; current base about INR 1,000-1,100 crore.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Loss-making in Q1 due to steel price increases, which management expects to recover from customers in coming quarters. Management cited ROCE of about 20%.

segments.name: Services (HAD)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 17% in the quarter per management. Profitability described as double-digit at PBT level; management did not give a figure.

segments.name: IFB Refrigeration (associate, 41.40% stake)
segments.commentary: Company PBT INR 80 lakh; IFB share INR 0.33 crore (INR 33 lakh) in Q1 versus a loss last year. Company revenue growth stated at 2%. Management declined to discuss it in detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects about 20% growth, with Q1 at 18% and July described as good; it said it is 'working towards' 20%.
Cost initiatives target of INR 120-150 crore for FY27, with INR 42-43 crore already in Q1; the company said it is not cutting counters or in-store promoters.
Management has no near-term view that commodity and forex pressure is over and did not expect to pass it fully through.
PBDIT should be early double digit in the long term, per the CEO (in response to an analyst question on margin aspiration).
Engineering expects growth similar to Q1. The INR 2,000 crore target depends partly on a battery project (LOI about INR 150 crore from Tata) that is now under review after Tata Sons' decision.
Full-year capex is about INR 110 crore; the Engineering stamping capex plan is about INR 400 crore.
AC aspiration: 7-10% market share, with no timeline given.
capex_capacity: AC capacity about 75,000 units per month; peak month utilisation about 85%. Debottlenecking and automation planned to reach 75,000-80,000 per month without adding shifts.
Management said there is no current capacity constraint in HAD and that new products for unserved capacities are expected within 3-6 months.

Engineering acquired land in Gujarat for EV and stamping. Stamping capacity expansion planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore, with a business target of about INR 1,000 crore against about INR 400 crore stamping capex.
Tata LOI (about INR 150 crore) for battery project under review; land already acquired, and machinery not yet ordered.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken across all HAD categories in the last quarter, but not enough to cover commodity and forex; management said it had led some price increases where the market had not.
Management said it has not been able to pass commodity and forex cost increases to customers in full; pricing is constrained by competitiveness.
Front-load washer share estimated to be top-2 by management, but no published market-share data is available. Top-load may be lower.
Trade schemes and discounts of about INR 1,800 crore were questioned by an analyst; management said it is an industry practice and under review for leakages.
RAC transition: old-rating AC stock was run down by about January, and the company did not build older-rated stock. Management said the new-rated models are 10-15% more expensive than the market.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commodity and forex headwind (about INR 170 crore across Q4 and Q1) been passed on, and is it behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Not behind us. Management said it has not passed commodity or forex costs to customers; savings came from efficiency initiatives instead.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RAC growth (about 10%) lag the industry (20%+)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company chose not to carry older-rated AC stock through the BEE rating change, so it lost the price advantage. It is focusing on higher-capacity models.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company sustaining 20% growth and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 HAD revenue grew 18%, and management said distribution fixes (counters, displays, promoters) drove growth; it says the trend should continue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 2,000 crore Engineering target still achievable given the battery project uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 250 crore of business is near closing, and that the existing business grows about 20%. The battery project is under review, and other projects are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Was the company's cost-savings guidance lowered from INR 150-200 crore to INR 120-150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR 120-150 crore for FY27, after INR 67 crore in FY26; SKU rationalisation is expected to add benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IFB refrigeration company growth (2%) differ from IFB-branch refrigerator sales growth (14%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 14% is IFB Industries branch volume and that the company's own figure could differ because of branch structure; it declined to discuss the associate.

risks_watch: Commodity (steel, copper and others) and forex pressure with no pass-through; gross margin down about 160 bps.
Steel division loss in Q1 with recovery depending on customer price pass-through in coming quarters.
Engineering growth target depends on OEM business wins and the Tata battery project, which is under review.
Trade-scheme spend of about INR 1,800 crore (per an analyst) and its scrutiny by management.
Motor division loss; management deferred the question to an offline discussion, so the cause is unclear.
Inconsistent Fine Blanking Q1 FY26 revenue figure (INR 185-186 crore vs INR 176 crore) in the presentation; management said it would revert.

500249|2026-06.headline: KSB H1 FY27 revenue INR 12,920 mn with weak Q1 sales (2–3% growth); management targets double-digit FY growth on H2 export recovery.
500249|2026-06.overview: Management presented at an institutional investor meet (held 19 Aug 2026) covering H1 FY27 (April–June 2026 quarter as described in the call). H1 revenue from sales was INR 12,920 mn, EBITDA INR 1,465 mn and PBT INR 1,279 mn. Management attributed the subdued quarter to Middle East export shipments held up by the geopolitical situation, supply-chain constraints on castings after gas availability issues, a delayed KUSUM 2.0 solar scheme, and slow project-pump order inflow. Management expects a much better H2 and aims for double-digit growth, though it flagged NPCIL test-bed delays on nuclear and continued fixed-price margin pressure.

financial_highlights.change: Management said Q1 sales grew only 2–3% over the prior period
Well below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay
Down from mid-teens levels the analyst cited; management called it temporary

segments.name: Order intake mix
segments.commentary: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves about 19% of order intake, per management.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order on hand INR 1,235 crore covering GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5 and 6 and the Kudankulam safety package; Shirwal nuclear capacity at 80–90% utilisation with a new shed adding about 7,000 sq m (about 20% plant capacity).

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Margin fell to single digits in H1 on commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales; management expects a return to double-digit margins.

segments.name: SupremeServ
segments.commentary: Management targets 25–30% aftermarket share in India (group target 35%); business growing about 15% per annum.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar pumps are 5–7% of current order book versus a 10–12% target; Maharashtra tender orders expected to help in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Goal is double-digit growth for the full year; management said 15–17% average growth over time is achievable (10–15% volume, about 15% value).
H2 expected to be much better, with export shipments recovering from Middle East disruption and supply chain now around 85–90% stable.
Nuclear GHAVP testing expected to start in September 2026 once NPCIL resolves test-bed issues; first pump needs about 500 hours of testing (2–3 months), with up to six pumps a year possible.
EBITDA target of 13–14% reiterated; gross margin under pressure on fixed-price project business, partly offset by internal cost reduction.
Export order book about 15% of sales, with a target of 20%.
S/4HANA implementation in H1 of next year, with group cost allocation expected in FY28 OpEx; amount not yet decided.
Capex of about INR 80–120 crore per year (sustenance plus growth).
capex_capacity: Shirwal plant is about 115,000 sq m (15,000 sq m added with recently bought land); a new shed of about 7,000 sq m adds about 20% capacity.
Shirwal capacity about 1,200–1,300 pumps across energy, oil and gas and nuclear combined.
Nuclear: first indigenous pump made in 2025, under testing at NPCIL test bed in 2026; ISO-19443 certified.
Reciprocating pumps being developed under BP&CL technology; EIL approval in process, requiring a running pump supplied within 12 months.
Split-case pump of 10,000 cubic metres per hour under development for export and river-linking projects.
demand_pricing: Management sees energy (thermal, nuclear, renewable) and water/wastewater infrastructure as main growth drivers; supercritical thermal boiler circulation pump win broke an import jinx.
Project market (oil and gas, petrochemical) slowed; Dangote refinery expected to contribute later.
Price increases: foundry costs up 12–15%; KSB standard market price hikes so far single-digit, being phased in.
Export demand hit by Middle East war and earlier US tariffs cancelling some orders; US boiler feed pump orders for gas plants noted.
Data centre: orders from KSB Germany's OEM customers and an international OEM in India for liquid cooling; no size quantified.
Pump content of projects estimated at 3–5% of total project value.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 performance subdued, and how much export was to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the war affecting exports (pumps ready but undelivered) and supply-chain constraints; sales grew only 2–3%, and H2 is expected to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is double-digit growth; nuclear test-bed delay is the main risk, which management sees as low risk. 20% top-line is possible but with peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution and competition for the next primary coolant pump tender?
qa_highlights.answer: GHAVP testing delayed by NPCIL test-bed issues, with testing expected from September; a new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) expected in a few months, and KSB is the approved supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
500249|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.

532768|2026-06.headline: Fiem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.6% to INR769.9 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 13.5%; FY27 4-wheeler ramp pushed out to FY28.
532768|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales grew 18.62% YoY to INR769.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR104.06 crore at a 13.5% margin, versus 13.46% a year ago. PAT increased 16.31% to INR65.19 crore. Management said raw material and employee cost increases will be passed on with a lag over the next few quarters, and reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and about 14% EBITDA margin. The main negative was the 4-wheeler lighting ramp, which management now expects to slip into FY28 from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 13.46% YoY; about 130 bps QoQ compression as stated by an analyst

financial_highlights.metric: LED share of automotive lighting revenue

financial_highlights.change: Analyst figure; company has no debt per analyst

segments.name: 2-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: Core growth engine. Management says volumes are in line with TVS, Honda and Suzuki; Yamaha lagged, with exports up only 2-3% against domestic up 40-50% per an analyst. Industry production reached 7.25 million units in Q1, about 22.8% growth per management.

segments.name: EV lighting
segments.commentary: EV share of 2-wheeler volume is above 9%, up from about 6% a year ago. Supplies commenced for Ather Konarc (sole supplier on the new model), River RX02 and Royal Enfield EV Flying Flea. Hero Vida lamps for its Andhra Pradesh plant will ship from Hosur from next quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of revenue. Management now expects FY27 to stay at a similar level, with meaningful scale-up pushed to FY28 because customer conversion is taking longer. Mahindra supplies are scaling as planned; Force Motors and other OEM development is ongoing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 15-20%, unchanged; management said this holds for the years to come until a significant move into another business.
EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for the full year; Q1 carried cost increases in employee cost and raw materials.
Raw material cost increase (about 80 bps of the margin impact per management) expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters.
Employee cost run-rate expected to stay at the Q1 level for the next three quarters after the minimum wage revision (Haryana first, about 35% increase there, other states following).
FY27 capex target about INR100 crore, versus about INR110 crore in FY26; most of it for Hosur (EV capacity for TVS and others), some at Tapukara.
4-wheeler lighting revenue for FY27 now expected at about 2.5% of revenue, versus the earlier INR100-150 crore indication; the ramp shifts to FY28.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR41.15 crore; FY27 target about INR100 crore, largely Hosur (Kelamangalam and Thally Road) for EV capacity.
Customers expanding: TVS 2-wheeler capacity 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by year-end; Hero Vida capacity 15,000 to 45,000 units per month.
Hands-off detection POC built and shown to almost all customers; light control module (LCM) expected to launch with 2-3 customers soon.
In-house EMI/EMC lab supports faster validation and shorter development time.
demand_pricing: Industry: record Q1 2-wheeler volume of 7.25 million units, supported by GST rationalisation, retail financing and rural demand; exports and EVs grew faster.
Management says wallet share with top customers is same or better; more than 100 models are with Fiem across customers.
Mercedes: samples submitted, with 1.5-2 years of vehicle-level testing before an RFQ/RFI for mass production.
Ambient lighting using optical fibre: technology not yet uniform; business expected to be cracked in about a year with customers.
LED share of automotive lighting at 63%; management expects new models to move to LED and targets about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY27 4-wheeler lighting guidance (INR100-150 crore in the prior quarter) cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is pushed out by about two quarters, with FY27 slightly lower and 4-wheeler at about 2.5% of revenue. Orders are lumpy and conversion cycles with customers are longer.

qa_highlights.question: How will LED penetration move in 2-wheeler lighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new models are coming with LEDs only and it expects about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months. It does not expect 100% because older models and aftermarket demand will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Yamaha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Yamaha to be flat to growing for the year. Exports were weak on the cycle of European and US demand; domestic models such as R15, Aerox and XSR were slower in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and cost pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 14% EBITDA margin for FY27. Raw material cost increases are expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters; the employee cost run-rate should hold for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is capital allocation given about INR280 crore cash and no debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited organic and inorganic opportunities, plus possible future 4-wheeler and electronics capex. It will fund capex from internal accruals and would raise debt if needed for a larger opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company disclose wallet share by customer and segment?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst asked for annual wallet share disclosure by segment. Management declined to share it in advance, citing customer confidentiality, and said it will announce models after customer launches.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler ramp has slipped again; FY28 is now the earliest meaningful scale-up, and analysts questioned competitive share gains.
Yamaha exports and domestic models slowed in Q1; management expects recovery but gave no quarterly targets.
Input cost and rupee pressure: pass-through has a lag, so margin in the next 1-2 quarters depends on recovery.
Employee cost step-up from minimum wage revisions across states, which management expects to persist for the next three quarters.
Hands-off detection and LCM remain at POC or pre-launch stage with no order value disclosed; ambient lighting timing is about a year away.
Analysts asked about share loss at top customers; management did not give a quantified wallet share figure.
532768|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on 2-wheeler and EV demand and the festive outlook, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the 4-wheeler timeline and on customer-level market share. Management repeatedly declined to give specifics on new products and wallet share.
key_quotes: So the margin guidance for the year is around 14%.
We look at overall revenue guidance of around 15% to 20%.
But next year onwards, we should see some significant increase.
There are no procedural delays.

540704|2026-06.headline: Matrimony.com Q1 FY27 PAT rose 127.5% YoY to Rs 19.1 crore on consolidated revenue of Rs 130.5 crore (+13.2% YoY).
540704|2026-06.overview: Consolidated billing was Rs 136.0 crore (+7.8% QoQ and +7.8% YoY) and revenue Rs 130.5 crore (+11.7% QoQ, +13.2% YoY), with consolidated EBITDA margin of 20.1% versus 12.4% in Q4 and 11% a year ago. Matchmaking EBITDA margin rose to 26.9%, helped by deferred revenue from last year's introduction of a one-year package. Management guided Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to double-digit YoY growth and PAT to triple-digit YoY growth, with profit similar to or slightly above Q1. The non-matchmaking wedding services business remained loss-making (EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore) and is being shifted from subscription to a commission model.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.4% in Q4, 11% a year ago
vs 22% in Q4, 17.6% a year ago
vs Rs 43.5 crore in Q4, Rs 46.7 crore a year ago
vs loss of Rs 5.7 crore in Q4

segments.name: Matchmaking
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 135.3 crore (+8.0% YoY) and revenue Rs 109.5 crore (+13.6% YoY); EBITDA Rs 34.9 crore at 26.9% margin. Management said EBITDA would have been about Rs 40 crore had billing equalled revenue.

segments.name: Marriage services and other businesses
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 74 lakh (-13.8% YoY, +0.5% QoQ) and revenue Rs 96 lakh (-24.3% YoY, +13.1% QoQ); EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore. Q4 included an impairment, which management said drove the higher loss.

guidance_outlook: Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to grow double digits YoY.
Q2 PAT to grow triple digits YoY; profit expected at a similar level to Q1 or slightly better.
Marriage services billing expected to be higher in Q1 than in the current quarter (management said Q2 billing would exceed Q1).
Revenue-to-billing conversion expected at roughly 96-99% in a given quarter, depending on billing mix.
Wedding services targeted at a Rs 100 crore run rate before it contributes to profit; management said clarity likely in about a year.
capex_capacity: Marketing spend to be held and slightly stepped up to support growth and new initiatives such as love.com and Malayalee Love.
Manyjobs remains focused on Tamil Nadu; national expansion not planned until next year or later, and it needs a run rate before breakeven.
Goodwill impairment was taken in Q4; further impairment depends on the performance of the newer businesses.
Rs 4 crore invested in an AI astrology startup (Bharat Ek Khoj) as a long-term investment.
demand_pricing: Paid subscriptions added: 2.72 lakh in the quarter (+15.9% QoQ, +3.7% YoY).
Matchmaking ATV fell 6.7% QoQ but rose 4.2% YoY; management said ATV should not be read too much into, citing package mix, discounts and the Jodi and love.com low-price products.
No ASP or ticket price increase planned; pricing handled through segmentation and analytics.
One-year package is a small share of users; management said it is individual choice and not an incentive lever.
Over 25,500 success stories in the quarter.
Management said it is not seeing a reduction in competitive ad intensity but is not fully slowing down; plans to slightly step up marketing.

qa_highlights.question: How is revenue recognised and how big is the billing-revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised over the membership period (3 months to 1 year). The gap was about Rs 5 crore in Q1 and is expected to be Rs 3-5 crore on an ongoing basis, mainly due to the one-year package introduced last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the triple-digit profit growth sustainable, given flat revenue in recent quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to continued growth plus deferred revenue from the one-year package introduced last year, and guided Q2 PAT to a similar or slightly higher level than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for AI, growth and investor presentation data?
qa_highlights.answer: AI is used for profile and photo validation, chatbots and product work. Growth comes from profile acquisition, conversion and launches such as love.com and regional versions. Management agreed to update the investor presentation data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ATV falling and will ASPs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ATV is not in a steady state, citing segment, package and discount mix plus low-priced Jodi and love.com products. There are no plans for a ticket price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Wedding services: break-even timeline and ad spend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on reaching a Rs 100 crore run rate rather than breakeven, with a commission model being piloted. It expects marketing to be held or stepped up slightly rather than cut.

qa_highlights.question: Legal fees increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sushanta Swain said the rise is from registering a large number of trademarks to prevent misuse.

risks_watch: Revenue quality: Q2 profit guidance depends on deferred revenue from the one-year package, and ATV fell 6.7% QoQ.
Marriage services: still loss-making, with the commission model unproven and a Rs 100 crore run rate target about a year away.
Marketing intensity: matchmaking marketing spend rose to Rs 46.5 crore and management plans a slight step-up.
Impairment risk on the newer businesses after the Q4 goodwill impairment.
Management declined to disclose business split, geography mix and whether there will be any cash deployment (acquisition or shareholder reward).
540704|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on matchmaking profitability and Q2 guidance, but evasive on pricing, geography, segment split and capital deployment, citing competitive reasons. Cautious on wedding services, described as still in piloting with no firm breakeven timeline.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have delivered on that guidance with the PAT increasing by 127% year-on-year.
So, I think Matchmaking has reached a certain level of threshold in terms of EBITDA margins.
We changed the model which we communicated some time back. We moved from the subscription business model to a commission-led model.

530813|2026-06.headline: KRBL Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR261 crores (16.7% margin) on price hikes and investment gains, while exports fell about 50% on Middle East disruption.
530813|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue for operations was INR1,496 crores, down about 6% YoY, as Middle East exports collapsed to INR244 crores (from INR485 crores) after the Strait of Hormuz disruption. Exports to all other regions grew 37%. Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores, driven by about 9-11% higher realisations, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined. Gross margin (including other income) jumped to 36.3% from 25.7%, and EBITDA margin to 23.8% from 13.9%, helped by INR64 crores of other income including MTM and forex gains. Management called the margins unsustainable and guided FY27 to about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin.</overview>

segments.name: Export - Middle East
segments.commentary: Exports to the Middle East fell sharply, driving total export revenue down about 50% to INR244 crores; management attributes the decline entirely to route closure and freight costs.

segments.name: Export - other regions
segments.commentary: Exports to all other regions grew 37% in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Domestic (India business)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores; consumer pack and regional rice performed well, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined on timing of purchases. Modern trade rice volume grew 6.5% and value 13%; e-commerce primary sales grew about 50%.

segments.name: Masala and regional rice
segments.commentary: Masala portfolio grew 74% in value YoY with an annualised run rate of about INR9 crores, targeting INR25 crores by FY27-end. Branded regional rice grew 25%, against a base of about INR270 crores in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic volume growth guided at about 10%, maintained for the next 2-3 years; bulk-pack volumes expected to resume in Q2 and Q3.
Export shortfall described as timing; export volumes expected to recover progressively from Q2 and meaningful full-year export growth maintained.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 30% and EBITDA margin at 17-18%; management says Q1 margins are not sustainable.
No further branded price hikes planned in Q2; pricing for Q3 to be decided after the paddy crop season unfolds.
Gangavathi facility for regional products expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY27.
Plans to buy more paddy and rice inventory this season, citing a comfortable 389,000 tons of rice and 71,000 tons of paddy.
capex_capacity: Inventory at 30 June 2026: 389,000 tons of rice (vs 392,000 tons a year earlier) and 71,000 tons of paddy (vs 91,000 tons).
New Gangavathi facility for regional products expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY27.
Management said it will buy more paddy this season; no capex amount was disclosed.
Distributor management system rolled out across top 190 distributors, covering about 65% of general-trade consumer pack business.
demand_pricing: Basmati realisations up about 20% YoY and 13% QoQ in Q1; branded realisations about 9% higher vs Q4 and rice realisation up 11% YoY.
Basmati export volume about 1.5 million tons vs 1.7 million tons in Q1 FY26; Middle East volumes down about 11% YoY.
Container freight from west coast India to Middle East rose from about US$500 to as much as US$5,000 per container at peak.
Pakistani basmati priced about USD100 per ton above comparable Indian material; Pakistan rice exports for year to June 2026 fell about 26% in volume.
Market share in traditional trade down about 2 percentage points YoY, per management; India Gate e-commerce share about 41%.
Global rice production expected at about 537 million tons in MY26/27 vs 546 million tons, with consumption rising to about 543 million tons (USDA).

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi Arabia entity, and are direct bookings continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is searching for a distributor after past problems with a wrong partner; 3-4 candidates identified, with finalisation awaiting peace in the region. The direct entity programme is deferred, while wholesaler shipments continue.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 exports be higher, and can restocking absorb high freight costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gulf benchmark prices have risen, letting it pass on freight costs; Q2 export numbers expected to be much better, though container space and equipment shortages are slowing movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins are not sustainable; FY27 guidance is about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin, versus about 15% last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will domestic volume grow, and what is the regional/quick commerce plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the next 2-3 years; Q1 volume dip was due to deferred bulk-pack orders. More regional rice varieties will be listed on quick commerce platforms later this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why not buy more inventory given available cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will buy more paddy this season, but purchases depend on market conditions; current stock of 389,000 tons of rice is considered comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the regional rice and overall revenue targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Regional rice is targeted to grow 25% on about INR270 crores; overall guidance is about 10% volume growth, with price guidance withheld because of West Asia uncertainty and the upcoming paddy season.

qa_highlights.question: Will basmati prices rise if the Gulf supply gap reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices would rise if peace returns, but the size of the new crop is uncertain after late rains; crop size clarity expected around 25 August.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross margin structurally sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gross margin is not sustainable, driven by price increases and MTM gains; FY27 gross margin guided at about 30%.

543969|2026-06.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 10% and capacity utilisation only 62%.
543969|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, driven mainly by price pass-through of raw material increases, while volumes were 1,292 MT against 20,936 MT per quarter installed capacity (about 62% utilisation). Gross margin compressed to 23% and EBITDA grew 50% YoY at about 10% margin; PAT rose 32% YoY to ₹10.5 crore at about 5% margin. Management said EBITDA per ton was ₹16,380 versus ₹11,252 a year earlier and ₹15,053 in Q4 FY26, but also said the figure reflects a temporary price spike that is expected to normalise. Management announced a ₹20-25 crore Kutch (IBC) plant due by March 2027 and government subsidy approvals of about ₹24.9 crore (WADA) and ₹10.5 crore (Bharuch unit 7) over 10 years.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state utilisation and the path from 62%?

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per ton of ₹16,380 persist?

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA reach ₹85-86 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q1 margin below expectations and why no inventory gain?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kutch subsidy cash or GST-linked, and when is it received?

544578|2026-06.headline: Rubicon Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR5,343 million and operating EBITDA margin hit 24.2%; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to 23%.

Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR5,343 million, up 52% YoY, with operating EBITDA of INR1,291 million (24.2% margin) and PAT of INR848 million including a one-off insurance claim in other income. Gross margin rose about 140 bps QoQ to 67.7% as management gave up lower-margin US business and reduced reliance on contract manufacturing. USD revenue was USD55 million, up 32% YoY but slightly down QoQ. Operating cash flow was weak at INR285 million due to delayed GST refunds, which management expects to normalise in Q2. Arinna Lifesciences (acquired April 2026) contributed about INR12 crore of revenue and immaterial EBITDA. Management also announced a CFO transition and the acquisition of a New Jersey manufacturing site.</overview>

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.</overview>

segments.name: Africa (geography)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 32% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus about 4.47% in Q1 FY26, offsetting lost Middle East revenue. Management said it sees the shipping and business cycle as established.

segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

Inventory expected to stay at similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in lower double digits, with conversion over about 2 quarters.
Expects to see results from strategic investments in 3 to 6 quarters.
Expects operational manpower costs to keep rising over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Consolidated inventory of about INR96.8 crores at June 30, 2026, of which about INR84.4 crores sits at overseas subsidiaries.

Management says the investments are transient (inventory, working capital, manpower) rather than fixed capex or plant machinery.
Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.
demand_pricing: Africa is now a major market; management said the Middle East revenue gap was partly filled by Africa.
Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?

Africa accounts for about 32% of revenue; management said it is not viewing any single geography in isolation.
Freight costs depend on oil prices, which management said it cannot forecast; geopolitical route closures are extending shipping times.

We would not like to provide an absolute revenue number at this stage.
At present, we are focusing on strengthening our operations and expanding our manufacturing capabilities.

524816|2026-06.headline: Natco Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR794.4 crores (from INR1,390.6 crores) on lower Lenalidomide, while Adcock associate profit share jumped to INR84.3 crores.
524816|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue declined sharply year-on-year to INR794.4 crores, mainly due to lower Lenalidomide sales, partly offset by double-digit growth in the base business. EBITDA including other income was INR245.7 crores (30.9% margin), improving quarter-on-quarter on international and domestic performance and lower operating costs. Consolidated PAT was INR206.5 crores versus INR269 crores in Q4 FY26, which included a one-time INR115 crore deferred tax benefit; management said normalised PAT grew 34% QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores and cautioned against annualising the flu-season-boosted Adcock contribution.</overview>

segments.commentary: INR477 crores in the quarter, down QoQ; Brazil grew 180% to INR178 crores on oncology portfolio, Canada about INR56 crores. Management did not split rest-of-world.

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: INR136 crores; base business about INR130 crores vs about INR107 crores normal, helped by semaglutide and third-party orders. Management expects domestic volumes to grow about 25% this year.

segments.name: Associate: Adcock Ingram (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Associate revenue INR1,582.8 crores and PAT INR242.2 crores; NATCO share INR84.3 crores on 35.75% holding, boosted by strong flu season. Stake raised by 13.25% in July 2026 to 49%.

segments.name: Crop Health Sciences
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR40 crores with an EBITDA loss; FY26 revenue about INR138 crores. Management targets EBITDA breakeven for FY27 and a stronger Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores retained; management said it is not changing guidance and advised against annualising Q1 Adcock profit.
FY27 gross sales guided at INR3,300-3,400 crores (unchanged), with Crop Health revenue of about INR750 crores for the year as previously stated.
Crop Health Sciences expected to break even for FY27; Q2 expected to be significantly better than Q1.
Domestic formulation volumes expected to rise about 25% this year.
Two US launches expected in the next financial year, to be launched with exclusivity; carfilzomib launch on track, timing to be confirmed closer to launch date.
Organic capex about INR250-300 crores per year.
Crop Health demerger now likely around March (about 2-3 months later than December) because of the proposed fundraise.
NATCO product registrations in South Africa via Adcock filed (three dossiers); launch expected around 2028.
Semaglutide filing not made in Canada or Brazil; South Africa dossier still some way off.
capex_capacity: Carfilzomib plant under upgrade; completion expected by end of calendar 2026, and launch to follow once US launch date is set.
Organic capex run-rate about INR250-300 crores per year.
Management plans ANDA filings of 8-10 per year and 2-3 FTF filings per year; expects at least one or two FTF filings this year.
Crop Health portfolio of about 35 products, 8 CTPR-related; CTPR contributes an estimated 30-35% of Crop Health revenue; CTPR technical exports have started but are not significant.
demand_pricing: Semaglutide market in India described as cutthroat and pricing still settling; the brand earns about INR2 crores per month, with some third-party volumes not expected to repeat. It does not lose money but makes little profit.
Adcock profit spike driven by a strong South African flu season, which management called cyclical.
Lenalidomide revenue was negligible in Q1 FY27.
Crop Health sales hit by El Nino concerns and delayed rains, which pushed back the cropping season.
Brazil growth driven by the oncology portfolio; management expects further launches in FY27 subject to patent litigation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR2,000 crore fundraise planned, given the existing cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash is around INR1,400 crores after about INR3,000 crores of investments over the last year, mainly Adcock. Funds are needed for short-term loans, capex and two acquisition opportunities (one in India, one outside). QIP, rights issue or other options are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT guidance of about INR750 crores still valid, given Adcock contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept guidance at around INR750 crores. It said the Q1 Adcock bump was seasonal, normal profit is around INR100 crores per quarter at the 100% level, and asked analysts not to annualise the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall sharply QoQ and YoY, and is this the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's Q1 had high R&D and legal costs. R&D spend is lumpy and tied to batches and trials, so this quarter is not the run-rate. Spend will be higher in future quarters, and management suggested an annual view.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India effective rate is about 25.16% under the new regime, about 27% after disallowances such as CSR. Q1 was higher because Brazil contributed more profit at above 35% tax rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Health reach breakeven and what is its revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven for the year and a much stronger Q2. Q1 revenue was about INR40 crores against INR138 crores in FY26; guidance was not updated beyond the existing FY27 targets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for South Africa, and can NATCO increase its stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites synergies: NATCO pipeline distribution through Adcock and Indian partner alliances, with value expected in 2-3 years. Bidvest holds 51% and is not selling; NATCO has a first right of refusal but no near-term opportunity.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
544239|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR219.18 mn in Q1 FY26 (flat); vs INR241.53 mn in Q4 FY26
vs 12.0% in Q1 FY26; vs 11.7% in Q4 FY26

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 59% of revenue (up from 40% share implied by mix of prior year's 60:40 comparison noted on call; management said mix moved slightly toward CCR YoY). Pricing pressure is most intense here; management said margin erosion is more evident in ETS. 15 new ETS clients added in the quarter, described as one of the highest ever for ETS.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rentals)
segments.commentary: 41% of revenue. Management cited healthy recovery in corporate and travel mobility demand, though inbound international travel remains subdued. 46 new clients added, the majority by number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin now expected around 10%, versus the earlier 11-13% range; management hopes to maintain margins at this level through the year.
Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 18% for FY27 was reiterated.
Employee cost expected to grow around 20% in FY27.
Operating leverage expected to kick in at a scale of over INR 1,000 crore of revenue; no timeline given.
B2C app launch expected this quarter; management set no high target for FY27 and promised guidance from next year.
Management is evaluating acquisitions after hiring a senior strategic finance professional last month; no buyback or shareholder return decision announced.
capex_capacity: Domestic footprint expanded to 151 cities, adding 20 in the quarter, from 130+ at end FY26.
Owned and vendor-operated fleet of about 19,500 vehicles as of June 30, 2026; the vast majority is vendor-supplied, keeping the model asset-light.
Management said 10,000-11,000 vehicles are used daily, with the rest held for demand spikes.
EV fleet increased to 460 vehicles from 390 at end Q4 FY26; EV adoption remains measured.
New CCR technology rolled out this quarter to automate contact centre, dispatch and billing; transition expected to settle within the quarter, with productivity gains to follow.
Upgraded proprietary technology platform completed this quarter; direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Trips of about 1.48 million in the quarter, up 27% YoY and ~7% QoQ; revenue grew slower than trips because of price reductions.
Active enterprise client base of about 1,400, up ~18% YoY; 61 new clients added vs 53 in Q1 FY26.
About 51% of revenue comes from customers with more than five years' relationship with ECOS.
Pricing pressure more intense than anticipated, particularly in ETS; management has set internal thresholds below which it will not bid, but did not disclose the level.
Gross margins declined as lower client rates were absorbed partly from vendor margins; management said it would negotiate harder with vendors.
Online/app bookings were about 14% of bookings in Q1, similar to 15-16% in Q4 FY26.
Management said few clients were lost to competition this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What changed since the 11-13% margin guidance, what is driving pricing pressure, and at what margin will the company walk away from business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and pricing pressure were higher than anticipated, especially in ETS. It has set internal client-level thresholds below which it will not bid, and did not disclose a level; company-wide margin is expected to be held at around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost savings and productivity be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Automation of CCR contact centre, dispatch, billing and booking, expected mainly to reduce employee expense and improve vehicle utilisation; management said it would also negotiate harder with vendors. Savings were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge given low entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three elements: long-standing enterprise relationships, a large reliable vendor supply base built over decades, and processes and people. It said the market is only 15-20% organised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins decline and how low can they go?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rates given to win business are absorbed partly from vendor margins, most evident in ETS. Management declined to specify a floor but said it has internal thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: When and by how much will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given; management said it is guiding to maintain margins because competition duration is uncertain, with operating leverage expected at a much larger scale (over INR 1,000 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Will ETS and CCR EBITDA margins be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said costs are shared across the organisation, so a segment EBITDA split is not practical to provide.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: FY27 guided to ~10% after Q1 at 10.3%; 11-13% range has been withdrawn, and further cuts are possible if pricing pressure persists.
Employee cost growth of ~21.9% YoY vs revenue growth of 16.7% is compressing operating leverage; watch whether productivity from automation offsets it.
Gross margin erosion in ETS from new competitors entering the market.
Credit risk and client quality: management stresses high-quality enterprise wins, but pricing reductions may affect contract economics.
Capital allocation: INR1,558 mn cash with no clear acquisition or shareholder return plan; watch for M&A announcements.
Guidance credibility: an investor criticised the sudden guidance change within one quarter, and management said competitive behaviour is hard to predict.
Other expenses fell only because a prior-year one-time provision did not recur, so the base is not a structural saving.

544202|2026-06.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 9,935 lakhs (from 10,861 lakhs) and PAT was just INR 65 lakhs, on delayed handovers and B2B shipment disruption.
544202|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs in Q1 FY27, driven by slower retail conversions as residential handovers slipped 12 to 18 months and by B2B billing that stalled due to West Asia freight disruption. Management said gross margin was maintained and EBITDA was INR 1,722 lakhs (17.3% margin), with PAT of INR 65 lakhs. The company opened 3 Bangalore stores and closed 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai), entered Sri Lanka via a JV, opened a Jaipur store, and announced a store-format overhaul (Stanley Superlative Living) plus a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries. An internal audit flagged a fraud by the company secretary, under investigation.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 10,861 lakhs in Q1 FY26 (about -8.5% YoY)

financial_highlights.value: Maintained (no figure given on Ind AS basis)

financial_highlights.metric: Pre-Ind AS gross margin (average, all formats)
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin (average, all formats)

financial_highlights.value: About INR 90 lakhs per month (about 2.25% of annual revenue)
