segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise)
segments.commentary: Customer inquiries and footfall are encouraging but conversions are slower as buyers (80-85% new premium/luxury home buyers) await possession. Network: 47 COCO stores, of which 35 are store-level EBITDA positive per management. FOFO franchisees are on a cash-and-carry model with no credit given.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: Products are produced and held, but invoicing did not happen in Q1 due to freight and logistics disruption from the Middle East conflict; management called the B2B visibility the highest ever. US tariffs have stalled export talks, and the company is pinning hopes on BIS certification enforcement for imports from 14 August 2026.

segments.name: Sofas & More / Stanley Boutique / Stanley Level Next
segments.commentary: Average annual revenue per store: Sofas & More INR 4.5 to 6 crores; Stanley Boutique INR 4 to 6 crores; Stanley Level Next INR 10 to 14 crores (some stores up to INR 20 crores). Boutiques to be converted into Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years in the six metros.

guidance_outlook: Brand architecture change (3 brands into one Stanley and one Sofas & More) expected to complete in about 3 to 4 quarters; conversion of Boutiques to Sofas & More is gradual, taking 2 to 3 years.
Target of 15% to 20% YoY same-store growth for mature stores; Q1 SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes.
Store-level EBITDA break-even expected 6 to 12 months after opening; ROI (capital with interest) expected in 24 to 36 months.
Management says manufacturing can scale to about 2x current revenue by recalibrating the factory with a few added machines.
No explicit margin guidance given; corporate costs expected to stay roughly flat as the company adds people for the new formats.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity utilisation about 68% to 70%; over 1,000 skilled artisans said to be fully utilised.
Sofas & More capex about INR 2 crores per store (5,000 to 6,000 sq ft). Large single-city flagship stores (Stanley Superlative Living) capex up to INR 20 crores.
Hyderabad Jubilee Hills (Road No. 45) Superlative store said to be 2 to 3 weeks from opening; large-format plans for Mumbai, Bangalore and Delhi, with one city one mega store in four cities.
Q1 openings: 3 Bangalore stores (2 Varthur, 1 Mysore Road). Closures: 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai); management said 2 of the Bangalore closures had already been relocated.
New stores: Stanley Boutique Colombo, Sri Lanka (July 2026, JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC) and Sofas & More Jaipur (first Rajasthan store).
demand_pricing: Demand demand: customer inquiries and footfall encouraging, but conversions slowed as residential handovers were delayed 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain issues constrained construction material availability.
Stanley Superlative Living targets buyers with budgets of INR 3 to 5 crores and above, aiming for average ticket size up to about 10x current levels with full home design, build and install.
Management said 6 COCO cities (Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai and one other) account for about 80% of India's luxury housing, per company claim.
Sofas & More: about 95% of customers are direct buyers without designers or specifiers; Stanley relies more on specifiers and design-led purchases.
Export exposure is small; management said the business is mainly domestic and US tariffs have stalled talks with large US buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation about INR 15 crores per quarter (above INR 50 crores a year)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sudhir Iyer attributed it to Ind AS accounting; IGAAP depreciation would be lower, and the charge is front-loaded in the earlier years of asset lives. He did not give asset-class detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report pre-Ind AS margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said only Ind AS numbers will be published, but pre-Ind AS figures are available offline. Management then gave pre-Ind AS averages: gross margin 56% to 60%, EBITDA margin 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the order book and B2B billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book stood at INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026, up from INR 62 crores at March 2026. Products are produced but cannot be invoiced until logistics clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stanley Superlative Living format?
qa_highlights.answer: A large-format store in mature markets, replacing smaller Stanley stores. Management said Hyderabad is the proof of concept; the format consolidates Boutique and Level Next. Sofas & More becomes the value-premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores are store-level EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: 35 of 42 mature COCO stores are EBITDA positive, after cash rent (the answer refers to 42 stores out of 47 total). Break-even takes 6 to 12 months and ROI 24 to 36 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are same-store sales growth and mature store revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 mature-store SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes; target is 15% to 20% YoY. Average annual revenue: Sofas & More about INR 5 crores, Boutique INR 4 to 5 crores, Level Next about INR 10 crores plus.

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.</overview>

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)

segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

540762|2026-06.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
540762|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

544028|2026-06.headline: Tata Technologies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% QoQ in constant currency to $175.4M (25.2% YoY), with management reiterating double-digit FY27 organic growth.
544028|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue was $175.4M, up 4.3% QoQ and 25.2% YoY in constant currency, with Services at $136.6M (approximately 78% of revenue). Operating EBITDA was about $28M, a 16.1% margin, up 10 bps QoQ, while PBT fell to INR 252 crores from INR 283 crores because Q4 included a one-time Labour Code provision reversal. Management highlighted the $100M Tenneco engagement and a Japanese OEM full-vehicle program, and reiterated double-digit FY27 organic growth with growth expected to be much greater in H2 than H1. Near-term margin expansion may moderate due to upfront ramp-up investments and a Germany wage increase in Q2.</overview>

Further tariff refund of about Rs7.5 crore pending, expected to be filed and resolved in FY27 after legal vetting.
Saudi Arabia plant: land expected by end of CY2026, plant ready by December 2027, operations by March 2028. US (Houston/Orange) plant: land already acquired, contractor being finalised.
capex_capacity: Foundry expansion and gate and valve manufacturing expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27; management says capacity is up about 30%.

Capex estimates of about $12 million for the US plant and $4 million for Saudi Arabia; about $3 million already held as deposits in the US; the rest from internal accruals and debt (management expects debt of about $3-4 million); US banks reportedly willing to fund.
Data-centre pressure vessels: capacity of about 75-80 vessels a year in the existing Indore setup; management says a new plant may be needed if order flow is sustained.
Chennai plant ramp-up is still in progress; new production head moved there two weeks before the call.
demand_pricing: Pipeline: orders worth Rs72 crore already negotiated; a further Rs60 crore under negotiation; management expects about Rs72 crore more to be added in the current month.

Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 units; a 32-unit order under negotiation; more than 600 vessels quoted. Management says per-vessel value is Rs30-60 lakh and margins will be similar to other business.
US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.
About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.
Mahr Maschinenbau (Austria): taking orders now, with manufacturing in UK and India; first jobs are 16 screens (2 for UK, 14 for Iraq); expected revenue about Rs15 crore per the presentation.
Competition in domestic water control gates and industrial process equipment: Tega, Delkor, Metso Minerals named as main competitors.

Singapore: a Rs6,000 crore figure discussed earlier was for project reports, not a bid; management says the overall Singapore investment is around Rs50,000-60,000 crore, spread over 15-20 years, and Jash's equipment is about 10% of project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book of Rs932 crore is not all executable this year because some orders are deferred to FY28; there is scope to exceed Rs875 crore but it is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.
527001|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose about 19% YoY to INR1,616 crore, while reported EBITDA was broadly flat at INR188.9 crore as higher fuel, marine freight and input costs absorbed the gain. PBT declined about 1.4% YoY to INR130.03 crore and EPS rose to INR12.07 from INR11.5. Guinea bauxite volumes fell to 2.34 million tons from 3.16 million tons in Q4, with bauxite EBITDA per ton rising to USD6.3 from USD5.9. India businesses were hit by fuel, freight and sulphuric acid costs, with the bleaching clay JV under the most pressure.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.16 mt in Q4 and 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Guinea bauxite and iron ore
segments.commentary: Turnover about INR1,360 crore (84% of group) and EBITDA INR163 crore; volumes 2.34 mt, EBITDA USD6.3/t. Iron ore is in trial production with revenue not disclosed and EBITDA reported is bauxite-only.

segments.name: India bentonite and allied minerals / white performance minerals
segments.commentary: Wholly owned; bentonite broadly stable with domestic growth offsetting weaker exports, while white performance minerals profitability was hit by higher sales and distribution costs. No segment figures given.

segments.name: Bleaching clay (Ashapura Perfoclay, 50% JV)
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid, a key raw material, rose about five-fold over the past year to above INR30/kg, adversely affecting the business. No figures given.

segments.name: Advanced ceramics (Orient Ceratech, 32%)
segments.commentary: Management said segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium product mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume target of 10-12 million tons retained with a potential variance of ±10% (about 9-11 mt); Q2 is seasonally weakest, with most sales in late Q3 and Q4.
Bauxite EBITDA per ton expected near USD6 (USD5.5-6 range) for the next one or two quarters; return toward ~USD10 is a medium to long-term expectation, timing not predicted.
Iron ore: 15 million ton target by FY28 reaffirmed ("achieve or even cross"), but long-term iron ore guidance needs a couple more quarters.
Guinea export quota system expected before end of CY2026, seen as supportive of realisations and freight.
Management expects bauxite revenue near USD1 billion (about INR10,000 crore) at 15 mt once conditions normalise.
India capex of close to INR200 crore planned across projects and verticals.
capex_capacity: Boffa port fully operational with capacity raised from 5 mtpa to 8 mtpa; no further expansion to 10-12 mt planned near-term, to be decided as volumes ramp.
GSM second port new jetty under construction, expected operational by Q4 FY27, raising capacity from 6 mtpa to 10 mtpa; combined port capacity about 23 mt.
Total bauxite export capacity stated at 18 million tons.
Bauxite washing plant set up with ~20,000 tons/day capacity, on an operate-and-transfer model; a comparable plant would cost about USD15 million and take about one year to build if expanded.
Ashapura has over 1 million tons of bentonite grinding capacity, which management described as the world's largest.
demand_pricing: Freight remains highly volatile and elevated; management expects volatility through 2027 and freight is the main margin overhang.
Chinese index bauxite price around USD72/t, up from ~USD61, mostly due to ocean freight rather than FOB Guinea price.
Alumina prices under pressure; management is positive on medium-term demand, citing four new Chinese refineries adding 20-30 mt of bauxite demand.
Middle East and Europe customer demand impacted by geopolitics and freight; company focusing on India, Asia and Africa.
Customer demand volatile; customers may take time to absorb market and cost changes.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of Guinea bauxite export quota system and expected realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the quota system before end of 2026 and sees realisations flat until then; margins also flat with freight overhang. FY28 15 mt target described as on track.

qa_highlights.question: Response to new entrants such as Nimba selling bauxite via monthly tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a new development with slow materialisation and will not significantly disrupt the market, with volumes likely going to other traders; Ashapura may participate in tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and expansion of the washing plant on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is roughly EBITDA neutral and mainly a sustainability and throughput tool; no EBITDA quantification given; expansion would take about one year.

qa_highlights.question: Boffa port expansion beyond 8 mt to 10 mt by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No near-term plan; 8 mt is seen as reasonable for now, with expansion to 10-12 mt to follow volume ramp-up without a fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Fako deposit and China Railway arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an MOU; details under study and little progress to report, with possible update next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why no iron ore revenue disclosure, and is the 10 mt guidance achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore is in trial production with low revenue, so it is not split out; EBITDA disclosed is bauxite only. Guidance is 10-12 mt with ±10% variance, and management said it is broadly on track.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per ton outlook for Q2, FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term USD5.5-6/t; a return toward USD10/t is expected over the medium to longer term, timing uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of Orient Ceratech's EBITDA doubling and India growth levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are oil and gas product demand with debottlenecking and steel-industry materials replacing imports; India growth from cat litter, foundry, oil and gas, and kaolin for paper and paint.

541302|2026-06.headline: Dhruv Consultancy Q1 FY27 net sales fell to INR15.55 crore with an operating loss of about INR3 crore, while Q1 order inflow reached about INR90-100 crore.
541302|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales were INR15.55 crore and total income INR15.95 crore, with management attributing the operating loss to estimate corrections, tax reversals and a fixed-cost base ahead of revenue conversion. Management said Q1 order inflow was about INR90-100 crore, including a INR40.92 crore OBCC order, the largest ticket the company has booked. Unexecuted order book is stated at INR300 crore, with the company also citing a total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer. Management guided that billing on new orders starts around Q3 and that the company is entering wayside amenities through a 55% SPV. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, citing SEBI LODR constraints.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 stated as about INR8 crore (sequential increase)

financial_highlights.value: About INR3 crore (analyst cited operating margin of minus 23%)
financial_highlights.change: Management said operating loss reduced more than 50% vs Q4

financial_highlights.metric: Total expenditure (Q1 FY27, as reported by management)

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer

financial_highlights.value: 60-90 days typical; up to 120 days in Northeast/difficult-access states

segments.name: Infrastructure consultancy (PMC, authority engineer, independent engineering, DPR/lender engineering)
segments.commentary: Q1 orders of about INR90 crore included INR19.34 crore Rowghat-Jagdalpur railway authority engineer and PMC work (140 km), INR8.34 crore MPRDC Ujjain-Jaora IE, and INR40.92 crore from OBCC. Company is executing 65-70 assignments.

segments.name: Wayside Amenities (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Formed SPV Verul Drivehub Private Limited with 55% stake; first 15-year lease-based development and O&M agreement signed 4 August 2026, with revenue expected from around February 2027. Three further LOAs expected in September 2026.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 revenue or profit guidance given; management cited SEBI LODR restrictions.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger than Q1 and Q2 as billing on new orders starts, with billing expected around Q3.
Management said bids are being submitted at better margins; the company has no specific margin target.
Management targets 10-15% of order book from international markets (Ghana preferred bidder, Mozambique empanelment, Saudi Arabia bids).
Wayside Amenities: first site revenue expected around February 2027, 7-8 months after possession for subsequent projects.
capex_capacity: Railway project (Rowghat-Jagdalpur) requires 108 manpower; management said about 60-70% already deployed and project commencement expected in about a month.
Company is building AI dashboards to track 65-70 assignments and aims to handle around 120 assignments a year.
Head office staff of about 80-85 are receiving monthly project-management training; BIM training underway (currently 3D, aiming for 6D).
Wayside Amenities site: fuel pump installation (4-5 months) is the critical path; sites are 50-60% constructed by NHAI and concessionaires.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow of about INR90-100 crore, compared with about INR90-100 crore for full FY26 per management.
Q2 to date additional orders of about INR60-65 crore cited.
Average ticket size has risen from INR5 crore to INR10 crore to INR20-40 crore; minimum ticket of recent LOAs cited as about INR8 crore.
Assam Brahmaputra 6 km bridge: company is H1 with bid of INR33 crore against competitor bids of INR12, INR13 and INR20 crore (LOA pending).
Company rated 9th among about 100 consultants by NHAI; management said the new rating framework gives technical scores more weight.
Lender's engineer fees cited at about INR2 lakh per month in India vs INR4-5 lakh per month internationally.

qa_highlights.question: What FY27 revenue guidance can the company achieve given Q1 income of about INR16 crore and new mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined numeric guidance citing SEBI LODR; said Q1 and Q2 typically make up 30-40% of annual revenue and Q3-Q4 are higher due to monsoon and award timing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q1 orders will convert to FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 15-20% of the order book converts to revenue annually; based on INR250-300 crore unexecuted book, around INR200 crore is expected over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q1 operating margin negative and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the loss largely a paper loss from estimate corrections after NHAI removed network survey vehicle scope; said the correction was about INR30-35 crore (under 5% of order book), and margins should improve as billing starts in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Wayside Amenities contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: First site possession given 4 August 2026; fuel pump installation takes 4-5 months and revenue is expected from around February 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 60-90 days; up to 120 days in Northeast or difficult-access states.

qa_highlights.question: Will new orders be billed in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said billing on new assignments starts after two quarters, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be better on margins.

risks_watch: Operating loss of about INR3 crore and negative operating margin in Q1; watch whether Q2 and Q3 billing turns margins positive as management expects.
High fixed employee cost (about INR15 crore in Q1) relative to revenue; new railway hiring of about 100 staff adds to costs.
Management's inconsistent order-book figures (INR250 crore, INR300 crore, INR360 crore, INR600 crore) need reconciliation.
International conversion is slow (Ghana contract conversion takes 4-6 months); Middle East war has caused some bids to be missed.
Client policy changes (NHAI removing network survey vehicle scope) led to a scope reduction and estimate correction.
Q2 FY27 order inflow of about INR60-65 crore to be confirmed; Wayside LOAs expected in September 2026.
541302|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on order wins and long-term positioning, but evasive on quantitative guidance (citing SEBI LODR) and on the cause and timing of the Q1 loss. Management attributed the loss to estimate correction and cost absorption, and said Q3 should improve.
key_quotes: So this is a paper loss, what is the INR3 crores or INR4 crores what is there in Q1.
So the principal issue in Q1 is if you can see the operating leverage, our technical and project delivery it is a combination of fixed cost and variable cost.
So these billing is expected to start somewhere in Q3.
So it's difficult for me to give any numbers as the SEBI LODR doesn't allow us to do that.

530365|2026-06.headline: Orient Bell Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores, with EBITDA margin at 8.7% and a record 39.7% gross margin.
530365|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores on 22.9% volume growth and about 15.9% higher ASP, with EBITDA up to INR17.6 crores from INR5.6 crores. Management attributed the quarter to Morbi shutdowns (late March to mid-May) that opened a supply gap, plus its own demand-generation push and dealer sell-out support. The company remains debt-free, reports a working capital cycle of 18 days, and is weighing deployment of its cash. Management declined to give any revenue or margin guidance.</overview>

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: South volume grew about 37% and West about 60% in Q1; retail has grown faster than enterprise in recent quarters.

segments.name: Projects
segments.commentary: Project revenue was 18% of Q1 sales, including retail-sourced projects above 3,000 meters and key account projects.

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT was about 47% of Q1 sales by value; about 15-20% of GVT came from Dora plant, bulk from SKD, and a low single-digit share from Morbi.

segments.name: Tile adhesives (Masterbond)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, cash-and-carry business with INR2.5 crores of sales in Q1, currently scaling in North and part of East India.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give revenue or margin guidance; it cited volatile Middle East and gas-price conditions.
Current gas prices are broadly stable, with July close to Q1 levels; no price cuts taken yet, with management monitoring the market.
Management said it is watching the market and will be competitive if selling prices soften.
Company is holding INR75 crores-plus in cash and plans to announce deployment of the larger part over the next three to four months.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation rose to 73% in Q1 from 64% in Q4 and about 60% blended in FY26.
Plan to invest around INR10 crores to convert 1 million meters of existing ceramic capacity to GVT.
Small capex of about INR15 crores over the next four to five months, internally financed, covering line conversion, digital printing machine replacement and polishing machines.
Next phase of manufacturing expansion under evaluation; decision expected in two to three months.
No plans to enter bathware; focus on tiles plus adhesives.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 18-19% taken versus pre-war levels, with almost all of it realised.
Sell-out was about 40% of primary sales in Q1 versus 26% last year; DSO improved by 5 days.
Morbi-Organised gap narrowed to INR50-55 from about INR100 on comparable products, which benefits organised players.
Dealers are adding suppliers in other geographies to reduce dependence on Morbi.

Gas: Q1 average about INR60 per unit; Sikandrabad (North) moved from INR44-45 pre-war to INR60-62. Morbi exports fell to about INR800 crores a month average in April-May versus INR1,500-1,600 crores earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q1 and are prices sustainable as gas prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increase of about 18-19% versus pre-war, almost fully realised; no cuts yet, with management watching gas and Morbi pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% volume growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi supply gap during the shutdown plus OBL's demand generation, with about 40% sell-out support to dealers and 24/7 TV advertising; management pointed to input KPIs rather than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Dora plant utilisation, and share of GVT and EBITDA from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-level utilisation is misleading due to inter-plant transfers; South and West growth was used as proxy. About 15-20% of GVT comes from Dora.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Company policy is no guidance on revenue or margins; management cited positive quarter-on-quarter KPIs only.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR75 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15 crores of internally financed capex over four to five months; the larger part is to be invested in the business, with a decision in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Tile adhesives progress and bathware plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives generated INR2.5 crores in Q1 on a cash-and-carry basis, expanding from North to East; no bathware plans.

risks_watch: Gas and propane prices remain volatile; any fall could force price cuts, and management has not yet committed to holding prices.
Morbi capacity is back at full run-rate since mid-May, so the supply-gap tailwind may fade.
Exports from Morbi remain depressed by higher freight costs (5-6x to Gulf).
Deployment of about INR75 crores of cash and the next manufacturing expansion are undecided.
530365|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on results and market share, but cautious and non-committal on outlook, repeatedly declining guidance and calling pricing and gas costs too volatile to forecast.
key_quotes: Our demand generation initiatives have ensured a sellout of approximately 40% of the primary sales volume in Q1 versus 26% sellout last year.
As a result, we achieved our highest ever gross margin of 39.7% during this quarter.
As a policy, we do not give any guidance for future.

533941|2026-06.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
533941|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.</overview>

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue close to INR 25 crore, up 34% YoY, driven by online-first approach, rapid launches and data-led merchandising. About 40% of brand revenue came via aggregator bulk orders booked at wholesale prices under marketplace channel.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.
Insurance claim (fire incident, about INR 21 crore of stock insured) expected to settle soon; debt and interest cost expected to normalise after realisation.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is fully utilised for the last few quarters; the company uses job work and rented capacity to meet demand.

Target manufacturing mix: about 50% in-house, 35-40% outsourced (per-piece labour charges, with in-house quality control), and about 5% bought-out goods.
Capex is consistent each quarter but described as modest; the main effort is workforce hiring, training and line efficiency.
Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.
Customer acquisition cost is about 4-6% of GMV, with the quarter at the higher end; no precise CAC or payback figure was given.
Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.
Women's wear is still in a test-and-scale phase; scaling could strain returns and inventory.
Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.

532699|2026-06.headline: Royal Orchid Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, but PAT fell to INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore.
532699|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, with EBITDA up 39% to about INR 33 crore and margin at roughly 30.7% versus 30%. Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR 12 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about INR 2.5 crore in the quarter
financial_highlights.change: company-wide, due to 5% output GST regime

segments.commentary: Occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 vs INR 5,488 a year earlier. These hotels account for the bulk of revenue; ICONIQA is the newest asset, opened November 2025.

segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

segments.name: ICONIQA (single hotel)
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 occupancy was hit by April-June travel disruption (April about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%) versus about 80% in Feb-March. Breakeven estimated at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; target INR 100 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting ROCE of 20%+ within about a year, once ICONIQA stabilises.
Target of INR 100 crore annualised ICONIQA revenue, dependent on Q3 and Q4 performance.

Management declined to give a revenue growth rate for the next 2-3 years and said it is not assuring any date for INR 150 crore management fees; Vision 2030 target not specified as revenue or fees.
Keshav Baljee expects employee cost to stabilise within range over about another year as new properties open.
capex_capacity: Added five hotels with 237 keys in Q1 FY27, all managed or franchised, with no capex by the company.

Lakshminarayan Palace in Vadodara opened, branded under an ICONIQA collection brand, positioned upper upscale.
demand_pricing: April-June demand hit by flight cancellations linked to the war; management said about 50% of India inbound travel runs through three Middle Eastern carriers, which went to zero.
Business hotels seasonally weakest in Q1 (April-June); management said Q3-Q4 are the strongest quarters.
Leisure destinations performed well while business and airport hotels were hit.
Rain in Mumbai in July and August has weighed on ICONIQA occupancy.
Nearby supply: Fairmont (50 keys), Hilton Garden Inn (170 keys) and Roswin (110 keys) opened around the same time as ICONIQA, adding about 1,000 keys within walking distance.
ICONIQA missed the corporate RFP season, so management is relying on online travel portals and repeat guests.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said April was about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%; Q4 about 80%. Q1 is seasonally weak and the war hit inbound travel. August occupancy was hit by heavy Mumbai rains.

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said no date is committed for INR 150 crore; fees grew about 14% last year, and the company aims to double fees as quickly as possible.

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
524342|2026-06.overview:
Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.</overview>

segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.

Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.

Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.

513023|2026-06.headline: Nava Q1 FY27 consolidated total income hit an all-time quarterly high of INR1,269 crore; Phase 2 thermal (MEL) slips to Q2 FY28-29 commissioning.
513023|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record consolidated total income of INR1,269 crore for Q1 FY27, with standalone total income at a record INR689 crore, helped by lower coal and manufacturing costs and dividend income from Nava Global. The 300 MW MEL plant ran at an 89.3% PLF. Phase 2 thermal commissioning has been pushed by a couple of months to around July 2027 (Q2 FY28, per management wording) due to logistics delays on critical equipment linked to the geopolitical conflict. A 100 MW solar project is slated for commissioning by end-September 2026. Management did not disclose consolidated profit or margin figures in the call.</overview>

543482|2026-06.headline: Eureka Forbes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.3% YoY to INR701 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell 46 bps to 10.5% on a 131 bps gross margin drop.
543482|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 15.3% YoY to INR701 crore, led by water purifiers (high-teens growth on double-digit volume growth) with broad-based strength across retail, direct and e-commerce. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10.5% to INR74 crore, but margin slipped 46 bps to 10.5% as gross margin fell 131 bps to 58.4% and A&SP spend was front-loaded. Service revenue growth was similar to Q4 FY26, while AMC bookings softened after price increases of roughly 3% to 12%. Management guided to a clear step-up in full-year growth and to FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26.

segments.name: Water purifiers
segments.commentary: Grew high-teens on double-digit volume growth, with market share gains driven by economy range, stainless steel range, and premium Hot/UTC/IoT models. Management says growth was ahead of the category.

segments.commentary: Grew late teens, broad-based across retail, direct and e-commerce, each with strong double-digit growth.

segments.name: Emerging categories (robotics, softeners, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: Strong growth across all emerging categories; robotics driven by premium mix (fully automatic cleaning station), softeners by volume. Robotics campaign launched with Shraddha Kapoor.

segments.commentary: Revenue growth similar to Q4 FY26 levels, but AMC bookings growth moderated after price increases; filter portfolio grew well. Filter gross margin is slightly below AMC but still high.

Management says no supply-side help from competitors' disruptions; market share gains attributed to own initiatives and point-of-sale investment.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said service revenue grew in line with Q4 FY26 levels; AMC bookings were deferred by customers after the 3-12% price hike, with an 18-month AMC tenure creating a lag into revenue. Filters are being used to offset.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly volume-led for water and softeners, while robotics growth came from premium mix. Pricing had some impact in water; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the service liability (deferred revenue) help FY27 service growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it helps FY27 revenue. However, in-year bookings must sustain growth, and the softness in AMC bookings is expected to show more in the later part of the year. Q2 service growth is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins be maintained in FY27 with A&SP rising faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin decline reflects upfronted growth investment. Management cited COGS and opex efficiency workstreams and operating leverage, with the aim to hold FY26 margins; it noted FY26 ended with ~55 bps expansion after a similar Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Could the company reverse price hikes if commodity costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if costs correct, it would pass benefits to consumers to stay competitive and grow share, rather than retain them.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2x revenue ambition by FY30 hold for products vs services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects products and emerging categories to grow faster than services, with filters growing ahead of AMC. It reaffirmed 2x revenue vs FY25 (about 17-18% CAGR) and 3x EBITDA by FY30.

532482|2026-09.headline: Granules pivots to four growth engines; plans ~2,000 crore organic capex over 3-4 years after warrant-funded move to net cash.

535789|2026-06.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.

Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.name: Indian Chaska (brand)
segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to move back toward 8% to 9% over coming quarters, with margin in Q1 not treated as steady state.
Positive operating cash flow expected by H1 FY27; conversion of current assets built up in FY26 into cash targeted.
8 to 10 new stores targeted by FY27, each expected to generate about INR1 crore per month in revenue.
Capacity utilisation targeted at around 80% to 82% by end-FY27 to FY28.
Expansion into Western suburbs and Pune/PCMC over the next five years, cluster-based; more gaps still being identified.
capex_capacity: Current processing utilisation 50% to 55%; medium-term target 80% to 82%.
New store payback about 24 months to recover capex and inventory rotation; store size and investment about 5,000 to 6,000 per sq ft as stated.
Automation being introduced at processing facilities, aimed at labour cost reduction and unified quality.
Store additions in Q1 at Rasayani and Babgaon; Uran (53rd store) opened after quarter-end.

Online remains touch-and-feel in Tier-2/3/4 locations; society-focused activation and 30-60 minute delivery trials underway.
Private label planned as combo packs (e.g., rice, dal, salt) to make per-SKU listing and ad costs sustainable on quick commerce.
Plans to launch 2 to 3 more Indian Chaska categories (e.g., protein-related) from next quarter, targeting categories with INR2,000 to 3,000 crore market size.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 8% to 9% depends on raw material cost stability; Q1 EBITDA margin about 6.3%.
Operating cash flow guidance for H1 FY27 unverified; balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; inventory and receivables elevated after FY26 build.
Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.
Internal inconsistencies in disclosed figures (133 bps vs 233 bps margin decline; export share 40% vs 35% to 40% export contribution to bottom line) need clarification.
Store maturity: some stores still not up to mark per management; 8 to 10 new stores in FY27 execution.
544487|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and store ramp-up but cautious and somewhat non-specific on margin and cash flow timing; several answers deferred figures (e.g., online targets, five-year scale) and the call had audio breaks during key answers.

544865|2026-06.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.
544865|2026-06.overview: LEAP India, India's largest on-demand pallet pooling company, reported its maiden post-listing quarter with total income up 19% YoY to INR2,134 million and EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million. PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

financial_highlights.change: up 1.26 million vs Q1 FY26 (13.65 million)
vs INR1.45 in same quarter last year

segments.name: Pallets (pooling)
segments.commentary: Pooled pallet count at around 9.2 million; management targets about 850,000 net additions in FY27 and says pooling growth of 17-18% YoY is achievable. Price increases of 5-6% were taken, linked to the German wood price index.

segments.name: Containers / crates
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of about 13% with asset additions of only 3-4%; management is deliberately slowing crate purchases because crate cost rose from about INR650 to INR1,000-1,200.

segments.name: MHE (TARON)
segments.commentary: 174 new machines added in Q1 and INR35.3 crores revenue (+33%); average monthly MHE pooling turnover rose from INR9.6 crores to INR11.6 crores. Management expects TARON to stay in a 14-17% growth bracket long-term.

segments.name: Middle East (GCC)
segments.commentary: Entities set up in Saudi Arabia (MISA licence), ADGM and Dubai; about five staff and about 20 customer discussions; Q1 capex in the region was held back due to the conflict. Management sees INR150-200 crores revenue in three years.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to about 20% YoY revenue growth (confirmed on the call as YoY, not QoQ), with GCC treated as additive to India growth.
EBITDA margin expected to stay within 47-56% for the next couple of quarters; management sees 100-200 bps potential margin expansion over time, but not a steady quarterly rise.
EBITDA growth expected to exceed revenue growth on a full-year basis, per management's answer to an analyst.
Target of about 3.7 million Movement Hire pallet moves in FY27, with 800,000-900,000 pallets added to the pooling model.
DSO expected to fall 10-15 days per quarter, with working capital normalising within two to three quarters.
Two more warehouses (about 250,000-300,000 sq ft) to be closed in Q2-Q3; a small 40,000-pallet pool may open in Silvassa.
Acquisition opportunities in India and abroad are at an early stage; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 asset spend about INR76 crores vs INR110 crores in Q1 FY26; management is slowing purchases given input cost inflation and is repairing more (1.4 million pallets repaired in Q1 vs 1.2 million a year earlier).
Utilisation target: above 90-91% in the next quarter and 92%+ over the next couple of years; a buffer of about 900,000 pallets is available.
Movement Hire fleet of 400-plus lithium-ion battery forklifts and 140 machines ready for delivery; 1,440 forklifts in total.
Planned 3D printing for inserts and automated crate cleaning by next quarter.
Warehouse network reduced to 28 fulfilment centres after the CHEP integration; 10,500 touchpoints.
demand_pricing: 48 new customers in Q1 (normal run-rate 15-20), including Lear Automotive, Minda Instruments, Havells Logistics, Woodpecker, Green Agri and Sriram Foods; expected to add about 120,000 static-hire pallets.
Beverage and cola demand was extended by a late rainy season (Adhik Maas), shifting demand from March into April-May; this drove positive net pallet additions in Q1.
E-commerce and quick-commerce added about 25,000 pallets (Zomato, Blinkit) and 3PLs added about 30,000 (DP World, DHL, Yusen).
Textile was subdued due to raw-material shortages and cost increases; this reduced Movement Hire volumes.
Pricing: 5-6% annual price increases, linked to the German wood price index, are embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 contracts were renewed in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from churn; FY26 moved about 2.8 million pallets and FY27 is targeted at about 3.7 million. Movement Hire rose 8% and textile/other sectors contributed the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have ranged 47-56% over six to seven years; FY26 was 50.7% and Q1 was 53.5%. Management expects 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and does not expect steady quarterly expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed YoY. Middle East is additive. Management expects INR150-200 crores of GCC revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is container revenue growth modest at 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in demand; management is limiting purchases because crate costs rose sharply, and is retrieving existing assets faster.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pallet 'sales' revenue look up about 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sells pallets only selectively, to customers who will eventually return to pooling; it says this is not a core focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue uplift from static to Movement Hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-pallet yield is INR1.54 (about INR562 a year). Management says it could rise to INR600-712 as Movement Hire share increases from about 0.3x toward 0.5-0.6x, with no new assets needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Movement Hire only 0.3x in India and what would lift it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a fragmented truck market (about 1,000 body sizes) and recommended standardising to about 10. It said that when one large player adopts pooling, peers follow.

544181|2026-06.headline: Awfis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR425 crores and cash EBITDA reached INR44 crores, while blended occupancy held flat at 76%.
544181|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR425 crores and reported EBITDA rose 28% to INR162 crores (38.2% margin), with PBT of INR24 crores. Management introduced cash EBITDA as a new metric: INR44 crores (10.1% margin), up about 34% YoY. Occupancy was flat at 76% QoQ, though the mature cohort dipped to 83% from 84% after one enterprise client with about 3,000 seats across five centres exited. Management guided to FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 expected to outperform H1.

segments.name: Co-working and allied services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR352 crores, up 27% YoY. GCCs contribute 24% of rental revenue from 100+ unique GCC clients across nine cities.

segments.name: Transform (construction and fit-out)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR73 crores, up 25% YoY. Third-party share about 92% this quarter; management says blended margin is around 17-18% (15% on landlord-partner work, 18-20% on third-party). Over 200 crores of mandates won for FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross seat additions of 22,000-25,000.
Co-working revenue growth of 23-25% YoY for FY27.
Transform growth of about 20%; total FY27 revenue to exceed INR1,800 crores.
FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 better than H1 and Q4 expected to show a meaningful improvement in occupancy and margins.
FY27 capex of roughly INR200-210 crores.
Premium mix expected to move from about 85:15 to about 80:20 by end FY27, as about 10 of 13 pipeline properties are premium (Gold/Elite).
capex_capacity: Operational seats about 159,000 across 242 centres in 18 cities; 9 centres under fit-out (total 251); pipeline of 267 centres including LOIs.
Total capacity including fit-out about 170,000 seats; including signed LOIs over 185,000 seats.
Q1 gross seat additions about 4,600 against about 1,800 seats exited in portfolio consolidation.

Malpani Estates developer partnership (Pune, two Grade A+ assets, 1.4 lakh sq ft). Developer partnership centres expected to go live in 9-15 months; company contributes about 50% of fit-out value upfront as a security deposit; 9-year agreements.
Seven premium properties in the portfolio (two live, five under construction), priced 30-50% above the existing portfolio. Elite centres rose from 8 to 10; Gold held at 27.
Management expects over 12,000 seats on track in H1 FY27 across the three multiformat pillars.
demand_pricing: Active clients over 3,600; corporates and MNCs about 64% of base. Weighted average client tenure 38 months; average lock-in 26 months.
Mix by sector: technology 39%, professional services 21%, BFSI 13%, manufacturing 12%, healthcare and life sciences 5%. Domicile: 52% India-headquartered, 43% North American or European.
Clients with 500+ seats make up 37% of portfolio. Q1 sold 13,000 seats.
Blended occupancy 76% (flat QoQ); mature cohort (over 12 months old) 83%, down from 84%.
Pricing: 4-7% contractual escalation within same client; management says price per seat has risen every quarter over eight quarters. No exact figure given.
Replacement of vacated capacity: significant part pre-committed, some at higher pricing than the exited client paid.
Industry: H1 2026 flex leasing 8.4 million sq ft (+55%); GCC leasing 16.5 million sq ft (+38%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did rental payments jump from about INR85 crores in Q4 to about INR130 crores in Q1, and is the company shifting toward straight lease?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the cash-flow rent figure excludes rent booked in other expenses (MA profit shares and out-of-lock-in leases not under Ind AS 116); that line was flat, so combined growth is in line with indices. Management said MA is 57% of current supply (down from 62%), and the mix is opportunistic, not a shift away from MA.

qa_highlights.question: How do developer partnerships work: construction stage at signing, delivery timing, capital contribution and access period?
qa_highlights.answer: Centres could go live 9-15 months after signing. Company contributes about 50% of fit-out value on day one as a security deposit until go-live. Nine-year agreements start at signing, with the nine years counted from OC and possession.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-seat revenue trend given chargeable area growth versus revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 68% vs 65% comparison, because chargeable area includes unlive fit-out seats. Net operational seats rose 59% from about 100,000 to 159,000 against 65% revenue growth. Price per seat rises through 4-7% escalations and premium mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Transform's third-party share about 92%, and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Transform has shifted to third-party work; the 92% reflects this quarter's delivery mix and is expected to stay structurally high. Margins: about 15% on landlord-partner work and 18-20% on third-party, blending to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the implied FY27 cash EBITDA margin only about 10% when occupancy is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the exit of one large client, where the company kept fixed costs on five centres to refill them, and a timing gap of 3-4 quarters between landlord rent resets (many 2021 leases) and customer repricing. H2 is expected to be better, with Q4 showing a meaningful improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio is premium, and is the new supply institutional?
qa_highlights.answer: About 37 of 242 live centres (about 15%) are Gold/premium. Of the 13 properties in LOI or fit-out, about 10 are premium. The premium mix is expected to reach about 80:20 by end FY27. All pipeline assets are institutional.

500201|2026-06.headline: India Glycols Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR1,130 crore and record EBITDA of INR170 crore (+13%), with PAT up 32%.
500201|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue reached INR1,130 crore (+9% YoY) and EBITDA INR170 crore (+13%), with EBITDA margin at 15.0% versus 14.3%. Management said PAT rose 32% and finance costs fell to INR25 crore from INR45 crore on debt reduction. The NCLT sanctioned the demerger scheme on 17 July 2026 and the company is now reporting under three entities. Management attributed part of the quarter's gains to the war-driven crude spike, which made bio-based EO competitive with Reliance's product again. Sequential EBITDA comparison is distorted by Q4 FY26 including about INR39 crore of Clariant dividend income.
