segments.name: IGL Spirits (potable spirits)
segments.commentary: Spirits net revenue INR371 crore with EBITDA margin 22.9% (+207 bps). IMFL revenue grew 26% to 1.4 million cases (+55% volume); non-IMFL revenue was flat at INR279 crore with volume of 7.5 million cases (+6%).

segments.name: Bio-Fuel (ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR323 crore (+7%), EBIT INR27 crore (+19%), EBIT margin 8.4%; management also cited EBITDA margin of 10.8% (+250 bps).

segments.name: Chemicals (India Glycols)
segments.commentary: Chemicals revenue INR332 crore (+25%) at 11.4% EBITDA margin; small gases INR13 crore at 23.1% margin. Glycols value up 83%; green solvents and glycol ethers volume +6%, value +13%, gross margin close to 50%. Performance chemicals grew 40%, below target.

segments.name: Ennature Bio Pharma
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarter at INR83 crore revenue (per call) / INR90 crore net revenue under new structure, up 53-65%; EBITDA up ~188% per the prepared remarks. Nicotine sales doubled QoQ on European customer conversions; thiocolchicoside up 26% QoQ.

segments.name: Clariant JV (Kashipur)
segments.commentary: JV net revenue up 21% QoQ with EBITDA up in high double digits QoQ; JV profit cited at about INR21 crore versus about INR19 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: IGL Spirits: EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 (INR120 crore already delivered in Q1); IMFL volume to roughly double versus FY26 (FY26 IMFL volume 3.4 million cases).
Spirits: management expects healthy double-digit growth in FY28 and aims to be debt-free from FY28; target EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in four to five years.

Chemicals aspiration (explicitly not a projection): EBITDA about INR400 crore and revenue about INR2,500 crore in four to five years; FY27 revenue aspiration INR150 crore-plus for the new performance chemicals business; margin targeted to rise toward 30% gross margin.
Ennature aspiration: EBITDA INR130-150 crore over the next four to five years.
Capex in chemicals expected to be small: INR5-20 crore incremental in the current year; no INR400-500 crore plant expected for at least two years.
capex_capacity: Chemicals capex plans: incremental INR5-10 crore, possibly up to INR15-20 crore this year, via modular expansion; new plant additions to date about INR50-60 crore.
Ennature started nicotine crude processing at its Kashipur plant, adding capacity.
Spirits: captive ENA capacity described as sufficient, supporting cost advantage in UP, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

Demerger: after effectiveness, Spirits, Bio-Fuel and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies; IGL Spirits will hold potable spirits, Bio-Fuel and biopolymers; Ennature retains nutraceuticals and APIs. Effective date not yet communicated.
demand_pricing: Spirits: management says the industry grew at a 4-5% CAGR over the last one to two years; IMFL growth attributed to launches in deluxe whisky, semi-premium vodka and white spirits. Prestige & Above volume ~0.5 million cases, roughly double last year.
Mix: revenue lagged volume in Spirits because of state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium grew faster).

Chemicals: ethylene oxide became similar to or slightly cheaper than Reliance's EO for a few months, increasing specialty chemicals off-take. Oil and gas and Middle East exports were hit by propylene oxide shortages and freight volatility (westbound freight up 5-20x).
Ennature: raw material availability and pricing volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for potable spirits for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA above INR500 crore, with INR120 crore delivered in Q1; volume to double versus last year, with healthy double-digit growth expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the NSU (chemicals) business and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex limited to about INR5-20 crore this year; cumulative new plant investment about INR50-60 crore. Aspiration of INR150 crore-plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years, with margins improving over time.

qa_highlights.question: Are JV profits sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a fair assumption; JV PAT about INR19 crore a year ago versus INR21 crore now, with the improvement linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: Prestige & Above volumes and IMFL revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A about 0.5 million cases, roughly double last year. FY26 IMFL volume was 3.4 million cases; FY26 IMFL revenue was not disclosed and will be sent later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes grow faster than revenue in Spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium growing faster); revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth as premium mix rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IMFL margin versus country liquor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins in deluxe and semi-premium whisky are almost the same as in P&A and did not give separate EBITDA margins.

544526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
544526|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational module capacity is 4.8 GW. Q1 sales were 334 MW against production of 408 MW. Management said the module market has become crowded.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (Odisha Phase 1)
segments.commentary: 2.4 GW cell capacity is under installation, with tool move-in done and a ramp of about 200 MW per month planned. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27 and says DCR cell orders have started for own cells.

segments.name: Non-module business (EPC, IPP, storage, B2C, transformers)
segments.commentary: Non-module revenue was 4-5% of total, with a target of 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1 and the transformer market is about INR 30,000 crore, targeted at INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 3.5-4 GW sales, revenue of about INR 6,000 crore, EBITDA margin of about 12%, PAT margin of 6-7%.
Management expects cell-led margin expansion in H2 FY27 and said cell EBITDA impact would be in the 'high double digits' (number not quantified).
ALMM-2 implementation was postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027 because of domestic cell shortages.
FY28 guidance to be discussed in Q3 FY27. Management called FY28 a 'milestone year' as utility DCR demand starts from April 2027.
Encapsulant capacity to rise from 2 GW to 5 GW; the announcement on equipment is expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha Phase 1 (57 acres): 2.4 GW cell and 4 GW module. About INR 1,000 crore of capex incurred so far; Phase 1 total is about INR 1,850 crore.
Phase 2 (27 acres): 3.6 GW cell, taking total cell capacity to 6 GW. Site work to start by end-Q2 FY27, completion by end-FY28, capex about INR 1,600-1,700 crore.
Phase 3: 6 GW ingot and wafer, targeted for FY29 and aligned with ALMM-3. Planning has started.
Total capex across the programme is roughly INR 3,500 crore. Peak net debt is expected at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.
Cell line ramp-up expected by end-August or early September 2026, with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026.
demand_pricing: Confirmed order book of about 6.35 GW (about 132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore per management, with execution over 12-18 months.
Mix: about 70% utility and 30% C&I/open access. About 30% of orders are DCR. Retail is excluded from the book and runs at about 20% of monthly sales.
Pricing: about 30% of C&I orders are fixed-price. In utility, about 30-40% are variable-price (cost pass-through) and the rest fixed-price.
New orders: INR 138 crore module order in July 2026 (execution by December 2026) and about INR 400 crore accepted by a subsidiary on 11 August 2026 (execution by March 2027).
DCR cell margins are quoted at 18-20%. Management said spot cell-purchase orders are not in the order book.
Customers deferred purchases amid the Iran war, cost volatility and ALMM-1 vs ALMM-2 uncertainty. Management said demand was weak in May-June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. It also said it declined to execute orders where input costs could not be passed on. Q1 margin of 8.33% was better than Q4 FY26's 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected by end-August or early September 2026, with 200 MW per month from the 2.4 GW line. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27. Full ramp-up is expected in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR 1,250 crore. Capex incurred is about INR 1,000 crore out of a roughly INR 3,500 crore programme. Net debt is expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers until Q3 FY27. It said large utility projects tendered from December 2025 (18-24 month cycles) will drive DCR demand from April 2027, making FY28 a milestone year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-module business is 4-5% of revenue, targeted at 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1. Management targets 8-10% of a transformer market of about INR 30,000 crore (INR 55,000 crore by 2031) and INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

544124|2026-06.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
544124|2026-06.overview:
Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.</overview>

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.

About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.

Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.
544911|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and qualifications, with a clear long-term structural narrative. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to confirm order book targets, FY28 growth, bid pipeline, and solar savings, and deferred several answers to later follow-up.

504380|2026-06.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
504380|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: How does management view FY27 revenue growth for Flomic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue to be better on higher freight rates, with momentum for three to four quarters, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and margin profile of the project logistics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described oversized, dimensional project cargo needing special equipment and permits, with higher margins than routine freight forwarding and higher execution risk; no revenue scale was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipment growth was about 6-7% YoY; the remainder came from freight rate increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin after excluding the one-time INR28 lakh benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT margin was still significantly higher YoY even after excluding the INR28 lakh, and that manpower cost has already been reduced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehousing margin and growth potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said warehousing gross margin is 15-16% (15-20% range), with Ind AS 116 inflating reported segment margin because rent on leased assets is excluded; share of revenue is to rise to about 20%.

qa_highlights.answer: No savings figure was given; management said closed branches were non-performing and located where the company lacked customers.

543389|2026-06.headline: Sigachi Q1 FY27 revenue INR121.27 cr with EBITDA margin 13.6%; management reiterates FY27 guidance of INR650-675 cr revenue and ~18% EBITDA despite run-rate gap.
543389|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 total operating income was INR121.27 crore, with EBITDA of INR16.5 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR8.14 crore (6.76% margin). MCC contributed INR82.74 crore, API INR21.68 crore and O&M INR13.06 crore. Average MCC realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, while capacity utilisation was 76.8% across plants. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR650-675 crore revenue and ~18% full-year EBITDA margin, but the Q1 run-rate of ~INR121 crore implies a steep H2 ramp that the call did not fully reconcile.</overview>

capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

500271|2026-06.headline: Axis Max Life VNB rose 33% in Q1 FY27 with VNB margin up to 23.2% from 20.3%, while APE grew 15%.
500271|2026-06.overview: Axis Max Life posted 15% APE growth and 19% GWP growth to INR10,610 crore in Q1 FY27, with individual adjusted first-year premium up 17%. VNB margin expanded about 3 points year on year to 23.2%, driving 33% VNB growth despite the residual GST impact, which management says is now behind them. Solvency was 198% after Axis Bank's INR381 crore equity infusion, which took Axis to 19.99%. Management reiterated plans for structure simplification (merger of MFSL into AMLI, subject to NCLT timelines of 6–12 months) and kept the INR1,600 crore QIP enabling approval open, with a sub-debt raise planned to replace the redeemed sub-debt.

capex_capacity: Solvency ratio 198% at end-June 2026 after Axis Bank's INR381 crore infusion (Axis stake now 19.99%); Axis has signalled interest in going up to 30%, subject to its internal evaluation.
INR1,600 crore QIP enabling approval taken at MFSL, valid until May 2027; management said there is no immediate need, and it would be used if RBC framework is delayed.
Sub-debt of roughly INR480–490 crore was called on 31 July 2026; a fresh sub-debt raise is planned to replace it.
Individual new business sum assured up 32% YoY to about INR1,17,000 crore; rank 3 in private sector on this metric.

demand_pricing: Participating products strongest growth; non-par declined on high base, with management expecting the non-par trend to move toward flat or positive as quarters progress.

Persistency: 13th-month persistency at 83%; decline attributed to discontinuation of a product variant decided in March 2026; 37th, 49th and 61st month persistency improving.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin increase, residual GST effect, and why did solvency stay flat despite protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the ~3-point margin gain as ~30% protection mix and operating leverage, ~70% yield curve. About 80% of the GST effect was taken in Q4 and no further GST impact is expected. Solvency rose to 198% on the Axis infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the structure simplification timeline intact, and how does Axis's potential stake increase affect plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filing followed by NCLT approval takes 6–12 months and those timelines hold. Management is still doing internal and shareholder consultation; Axis is evaluating going to 30% and both sides will disclose in due course.

qa_highlights.question: Opex-to-GWP improvement despite GST input tax credit loss, and the offline proprietary slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was held down by productivity gains and cost cuts (travel, advertising, negotiations). Management said some of this will normalise. Offline prop growth was affected by deliberate cancellation of certain sourced policies that did not meet quality standards.

qa_highlights.question: How long can solvency be run before a capital raise is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can stay above its internal threshold for at least two to three quarters comfortably, helped by debt capacity from the Axis equity infusion; RBC and Ind AS 117 clarity expected in the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the annuity push raise any product margin concerns; what is the variable annuity risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity and non-par margins are broadly similar in aggregate. The variable annuity has a fixed return component hedged in line with other products; the equity-linked component is borne by the annuitant, so no additional company risk is claimed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the protection-led margin expansion sustainable given the June yield curve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that the June curve moved lower and may unwind some Q1 yield benefit, but said repricing is normal and maintained the aspiration of VNB growth outpacing APE growth; it did not accept the 70% yield benefit would fully reverse.

543386|2026-06.headline: Fino Payments Bank Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 43.1 crore from INR 56 crore in Q4 FY26, while net revenue margin hit a record 42.8% after the UPI P2M B2B pause.
543386|2026-06.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as one of the toughest quarters in the bank's history, with the UPI P2M B2B business paused for recalibration and relaunch tentatively in Q4 FY27. Fee income was INR 234 crore and made up over 75% of revenue, while CASA's share of revenue rose from 45% to 54% QoQ. Referral loan disbursals rose to INR 628 crore (up 214% YoY). The bank reiterated its small finance bank (SFB) transition timeline, with the readiness submission to RBI targeted for end-Q4 FY27 and the RBI deadline of 5 June 2027. Throughput fell 10% YoY but rose 3% QoQ.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: Does the bank benefit from the proposed MDR changes?

segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 30% in Q1; plant utilisation about 60%. Sunny Beaches reported as performing well here.

segments.name: Odisha
segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 40% in Q1; plant utilisation about 70%.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh brewery
segments.commentary: Commercial production started around June 9, 2026; about 10 million cases annual beer capacity; about INR300 crore spent on Phase 1 with no pending capex per management. Utilisation not yet meaningful given lean season. Management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.

segments.name: IMFL (Mahavat)
segments.commentary: Realisation up about 3% YoY to INR1,047 per case. Mahavat launched in Bhopal, Delhi and UP; supply resumption from Bhopal is a stated focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore from earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore; margin guidance deferred to next call.
Management says the MP licence issue should be resolved in the current month, but it is not in management's control and is sub judice.
Andhra Pradesh direct sales expected to start by first week of September 2026, pending export permissions from Karnataka.
Plan to step into the Indian single malt category before end of FY27 (in-house developed).
Phase 2 (distillery) at UP: permissions applied; firmer execution view in three to four months.
capex_capacity: UP brewery Phase 1: about INR300 crore spent, no pending capex; commercial production from around June 9, 2026.
UP brewery capacity about 10 million cases per year; management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.
Hassan utilisation about 60%; Odisha about 70%; Bhopal (MP) suspended.
Company has four beer capacities; MP is one of them and is currently suspended.
Management did not give a firm Phase 2 capex figure; said more clarity in three to four months.
demand_pricing: Karnataka and Odisha recovery offsets MP loss; management says market share retained or growing where brands were available, except MP and partly Delhi.
Raw material and packaging costs up about 7.5-8% YoY; cans rely on a single supplier (Ball Corporation) for the industry.
Excise duty paid rose because more volume was sold in Karnataka and Odisha, where excise is paid before dispatch unlike MP.

Beer portfolio: Hunter, Black Fort, Power Cool, Sunny Beaches, Legend (management listed five; analyst cited Woodpecker as well). Management says the multi-brand approach targets different price segments.
Receivables: most sales are to government wholesalers in the states where the company operates, and management sees no material receivable risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the MP closure in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR250-260 crore of revenue was lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhopal (MP) be restored, and what was the FY27 outlook if it is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is in courts and with authorities and is sub judice; it is hopeful of resolution this month. It declined to discuss a plan B or give numbers for a no-approval scenario, and reiterated FY27 revenue of INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Could Karnataka or other plants supply Bhopal to lift utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said importing from Odisha or UP to MP would be uneconomic because of MP's very high import fees, potentially leading to a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Andhra Pradesh entry go live?
qa_highlights.answer: Excise and corporation permissions were delayed until end-July; export permissions from Karnataka are pending, and brands are expected in AP by first week of September.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company use contract manufacturing in states with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it compares local contract brewing against importing and chooses whichever is better on margin and quality, and that capacity is planned over five to 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Hassan plant not converted into a 100% subsidiary like UP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate and revert soon, with no commitment.

risks_watch: MP licence restoration timing: court and authority dependent; management has already missed its earlier 15-day restart timeline.
Consumer share loss in MP after a prolonged stock-out; management says recovery will be slow in long-closed markets.
FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore; margins not guided.
Cost pressure: packaging and raw material inflation of about 7.5-8%; single-supplier dependency for cans.
UP brewery utilisation in off-season and competition from new entrants such as UBL in UP.
Related-party/structure questions (SOM Distilleries Private Limited, Hassan 78% holding) were not answered on the call.
507514|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Karnataka, Odisha and UP, but defensive and evasive on MP, deferring to courts and declining to discuss a no-approval scenario or plan B. Management also declined to discuss the private group entity and gave limited detail on margins.
key_quotes: Let me begin by acknowledging that Q1 was an extremely difficult quarter for the company.
The facility adds approximately 10 million cases of annual beer capacity, giving us a significant new manufacturing and marketing -- market access platform.
We generated close to INR28 crores of cash from operations during the quarter.
I think I will stay with my guidance of INR1,000 crores of revenue.

524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.
524164|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR756 crore against INR551 crore a year earlier, up 37%. EBITDA rose 60.7% to INR111 crore, lifting margin to 14.6% from 12.4%, and PAT grew 89.9% to INR64.5 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher capacity utilisation, product mix, export realisations and operational efficiencies, and said there was no material inventory gain in the quarter. FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 36% in Q1 FY26; non-ibu revenue up 67% YoY
Management did not split volume vs price

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (API)
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen products were 43% of pharma revenue, up 67% YoY; growth described as broad-based across the portfolio. Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, with paracetamol lower at about 55% of enhanced 10,800 MTPA capacity.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said the chemical segment margin trended up in the quarter, helped by higher ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride capacity, better realisations and higher exports. Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production only in May 2026, with steady-state revenue potential of about INR120 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth of 15-20% (management said around 20% in Q&A), EBITDA margin 14-15%, exports about 25-30% of revenue.
Management said the INR2,600-2,700 crore full-year revenue guidance remains unchanged, may be crossed in the current scenario, but will not be upgraded.
FY28 (indicative, conditional on current scenario): revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 15-17%.
Near term: non-ibuprofen to reach about 50% of pharma revenue, with roughly 50% ibuprofen; by FY29, non-ibu expected at 50-55% of API segment with margins similar to ibuprofen.
Capex of about INR200 crore a year; about 60% expansion and new products, 40% infrastructure and efficiency. Next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27.
Regulatory: two to three more quarters expected for Triacetin approvals.
capex_capacity: Paracetamol capacity tripled from 3,600 MTPA to 10,800 MTPA; operating at about 55%, targeted near 70% by end FY27.
Triacetin plant of 6,000 MTPA commenced production in May 2026; capacity to ramp as market penetration grows. Inputs are acetic acid and glycerol.
Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.
Capex of around INR200 crore per year, with INR100-200 crore spent annually over the last four to five years.
R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.
524164|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the diversification story, but guarded on forward numbers: management held guidance, declined to upgrade it, and said FY28 targets depend on current conditions. It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.</overview>

segments.name: Revenue mix by business
segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake
segments.commentary: Q1 order intake over INR 3,400 crore: EPC ~INR 2,960 crore, O&M ~INR 470 crore. International 77%, India 23%.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Record INR 19,400 crore: 66% EPC, 34% O&M; roughly balanced India vs international. Management put Middle East at about 35-40% of backlog. Two framework orders (~INR 600 crore) were removed as not yet effective.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for the year; management said it expects to meet it and to deliver above guidance.
EBITDA margin: medium-term blended band 13-15%; FY27 expected at 13-14%, with a stated aspiration of 15% by year end.
Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.
Backlog expected to execute over about 36 months; international EPC cycles 24-30 months, India about 36 months.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: management said no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints.
Perur desal project (Chennai, JICA-funded): about 75% complete, 1 lakh cubic metres of concreting done, marine works finished; commissioning over the next few quarters.
Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Forex gains formed a significant part of Q1 profit; management says they are operational, but the standalone operating margin excluding forex fell from 15.8% to 8.9% (as cited by an analyst).
Middle East geopolitical exposure: 35-40% of backlog is in the Middle East; execution risk around logistics, imports and prices, with force majeure notices issued.
Rising provisions for delays or defaults in other expenses under the new, more stringent policy.
O&M growth slowed to about 7% YoY; recurring revenue growth depends on project completions moving into O&M.
TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.
533269|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and defensive. Management pushed back repeatedly on margin, forex and geopolitical questions, calling forex operational and the Middle East impact minimal. It was evasive on the Perur revenue recognised and on the EPC/EP split for the quarter.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remained net cash positive for the 14 th consecutive quarter, reinforcing the strength of our balance sheet and our disciplined approach to the growth.
Our order book position reached a historic high of INR 194 billion, that is INR 19,400 crores, almost $1.8 billion, which is over four times of our revenue base
So we have a natural hedge when it comes to it. Whatever is the small component of difference between the revenues and the cost, that is anyway covered through a PCFC.

PAT rose about 14% to INR 29.28 crore and EBITDA was INR 559 million at a stated 42% margin. Management said the step-up depends on the Sharon AI GPU deal (8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney), now expected to bill from Q3 FY27 after a delay from the earlier mid-September target. Management declined to give any forward revenue or profit guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue or profit figures.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview:
Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.</overview>

Purestudy stake diluted from 59% to 39.33%, making it an associate rather than a subsidiary.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 5 km of projects in June 2026 versus 102 km in May; construction in June fell 32% YoY to about 274 km; April-May construction about 638 km, down 34% YoY.
Bid pipeline: NHAI/MoRTH about INR1 lakh crore, states about INR25,000 crore, railways about INR50,000 crore; bids submitted but not yet opened about INR8,000 crore.
Order book INR15,251 crores as of 30 June (excluding about INR450 crores won after quarter-end). Road and railway about 63.3% (INR9,648 crores), Power T&D about 33.2%, building EPC about 3.5%.
International presence in 7 countries, with a plan to reach about 10. Margins and competition vary by country.
Management expects good road awarding in Q3-Q4 FY27 and says NHAI is moving to larger packages, which should rationalise competition.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Arclin/DuPont renewal (talks expected Q4 CY26 to Q1 CY27); the contract is a large share of volume and margins.
Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.
506687|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the balance sheet, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on Silox monetisation, contract volumes and product-level margin disclosure, and gave specific but unverified timelines for new products and Odisha.
key_quotes: Transpek has been a consistent 9-year supplier now. Without not a single kilo even rejected by the customer in terms of quality.
Margins, of course, we have to target, and we are targeting 15% to 20% overall margins.
We are looking at almost INR 250 Crores over 5-6 years.
Payback would be 4 to 5 years.

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
544111|2026-06.overview:
Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.</overview>

segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Management said All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter, versus about 2% for the company as stated in analyst question; domestic passenger traffic flat and international inbound air traffic down about 10%.
City-level domestic passenger declines cited: Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%.
Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Pricing on EM Bypass service apartments: average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Juhu acquisition at about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels cited near Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.

543434|2026-06.headline: Supriya Lifescience Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to Rs 190 crore, but EBITDA fell 8.1% to Rs 47 crore (25% margin) on water and power disruptions.
543434|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 31% YoY to Rs 190 crore against Rs 145 crore in Q1 FY26, with management citing about Rs 35 crore of sales deferred by a water shortage at the Lote MIDC site. EBITDA fell 8.1% YoY to Rs 47 crore and margin was 25%, which management attributed to roughly Rs 10.5 crore of extra solvent and power costs, including about Rs 8 crore from a Maharashtra solar tariff change. PAT was Rs 24 crore (12.7% margin) versus Rs 35 crore a year earlier. Management reiterated the Rs 1,000 crore FY27 revenue goal and a 33-35% EBITDA margin guidance, while deferring the Q2 maintenance shutdown and flagging a customs/export documentation matter on one small consignment.

financial_highlights.change: +31% YoY (vs Rs 145 crore in Q1 FY26)
Below 33-35% guided range; management says ex one-offs it would have been within range
vs Rs 35 crore in Q1 FY26
Solar policy impact about Rs 8 crore at EBITDA
Maintenance, smaller projects, formulation plan, Isambe project
Described as high; to be liquidated over next 3-4 quarters

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 81% of Q1 FY27 revenue, split Asia 39%, Europe 35%, LATAM 20%. Management said over 80% of revenue comes from exports, with a large part from regulated markets.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Management cited a sequential improvement from four to five US DMFs filed, with customers starting validation volumes. North America is a small share, roughly 3% by an analyst's estimate.

segments.name: Backward integration
segments.commentary: 72% of total revenue is fully backward integrated, per management.

segments.name: Products launched in FY26
segments.commentary: Cardiovascular advanced intermediate (launched Q3 FY26) is commercialised; ADHD product scaling on LATAM and Europe demand; liquid anesthetic on steady monthly supplies.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue trajectory towards about Rs 1,000 crore is reiterated as on track, though growth is expected to be non-linear across quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% is maintained; management said margins should stay at 33-35% for at least the next three to four years.
Management expects to recover about Rs 25-30 crore of sales lost to the water disruption over coming quarters, and says the Q1 one-off cost will not recur in Q2.
Q2 FY27 planned annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D is cancelled; replaced by smaller debottlenecking work, so Q2 production is not expected to be majorly affected.
Management said it expects about 20% CAGR, with potential to grow beyond 20% in coming years.
Ambernath depreciation is about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year overall depreciation is seen at Rs 35-40 crore.
capex_capacity: Patalganga land: all clearances received; Phase-1 capex about Rs 200 crore for API and utility blocks, with formulation blocks later in Phase-2; boundary wall construction has started.
Management expects about 40% completion around 2.5 years from acquisition, per MIDC requirements.
Block F at Lote: construction not yet started, expected to start in the next couple of quarters.
Ambernath: two anesthetic liquid inhalation products launched; EU GMP audit scheduled for second half of November 2026; CEP expected October-November 2026.
Contrast media (Iohexol) launch delayed about two quarters; now expected in H2 FY27 as R&D fine-tunes the technology.
Two ADHD product launches in the pipeline; SAP go-live expected in four to five months.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong in Q1, but water shortage at Lote MIDC (Koyna river supply) cut production for about 15-20 days, deferring about Rs 35 crore of sales.
Company works on purchase-order basis and says it can pass on solvent, power and raw-material price increases to customers.
Solar tariff: Rs 4.5-5 crore retrospective charge, sub judice; management says the ToD-related and other increases will be passed through to customers.
Cardiovascular product: commercial-level volumes reached, but management said a larger contribution would take 9-12 months as customers complete qualification.
ATS-8 product: management reiterated 250 metric tonnes target over two years, not in the current year.

CMO/CDMO: term sheet close on a large anesthetic CDMO contract, expected to be announced next quarter; quality already approved; DSM vitamin ramp at near-peak volumes with a dedicated facility running.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Patalganga construction delayed, given Lote is full and greenfield pharma takes three to four years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said boundary-wall work has started and ground is broken. API blocks and utilities come first, as Lote is nearly capacity-exhausted; formulation blocks come in Phase-2. Ambernath is the formulation scale-up site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customs/export issue and is there a provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a two-day lapse let an export authorisation expire before the shipping bill was raised. A new CBN export authorisation has been received, the matter is sub judice, and no provision has been made. Management said the consignment is small and limited to one shipment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 water and power, and is guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the water issue is resolved, the solar charge is largely retrospective, and price increases will be passed on. It reiterated FY27 guidance of close to Rs 1,000 crore revenue and 32-35% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath alone adds about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year depreciation is expected at about Rs 35-40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How big is inventory and how will it unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory is about Rs 230-240 crore, built up for the planned shutdown. It will be liquidated over the next three to four quarters now that the shutdown is cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Is there potential for growth above 20%, and what is the H2 ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 FY27 ramp-up will be much stronger than the current run rate, and growth beyond 20% is possible given CMO/CDMO, new products and capacity additions, subject to regulatory approvals.

535602|2026-06.headline: Sharda Motor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% to INR1,011.1 crores, but gross profit grew only 8% to INR203.9 crores and EBITDA 5% to INR103.2 crores.
535602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY to INR1,011.1 crores, driven by pass-through catalyst sales and product mix, while gross profit grew 8% to INR203.9 crores. Management attributed the weak gross profit growth to a supplier fire at a key customer and one-time premium raw material and freight costs linked to the geopolitical situation in April and May, which it said stabilised in July. EBITDA was INR103.2 crores (10.2% margin, up 5%), and PAT was INR86.5 crores. Management said the lightweighting, export and emission order book is moving into SOPs, but gave no numerical guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items (after JV and associate share)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR107.7 crores last year, which excluded INR22.4 crores exceptional gains

segments.name: Lightweighting (control arms, links, subframes, torsion beams)
segments.commentary: Previously announced control arm and link programmes continue to ramp up. Donghee licence extends the portfolio into subframes and torsion beams, with RFQs generated for multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, with a target share of mid-teen to high-teen percentage.

segments.name: Emissions and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Multiple WLTP replacement orders secured from leading passenger vehicle OEMs in Q1. The temperature-controlled tube order for an off-highway equipment maker has begun SOP and is ramping up as planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Three North American engine and genset orders with combined annual value of about US$10.7 million and lifetime value of about US$58.5 million; SOPs expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 revenue from these orders.

segments.name: Purem JV (CV above 4 litres)
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable. A new programme started in Q4 FY26 and will ramp up through FY27. Sharda receives 50% of PAT and is not in management control.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. Management said the exact quarterly trajectory depends on customer production schedules, SOPs and programme ramp-ups.

FY27 growth drivers cited: full-year benefit of lightweighting orders, ramp-up of additional lightweighting programmes, temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, North American export SOPs, and supportive domestic OEM volumes.

Management said it is now ready to be more assertive on acquisitions, subject to filters for strategic fit, valuation, integration and ROCE. Capital will be split between organic growth, technology partnerships, acquisitions and shareholder returns.
Management said it expects the lightweighting market share, last measured at 14% at FY26 end, to rise. The number will be calculated only at FY27 year-end.
capex_capacity: Chakan 3 lightweighting facility has started SOP and is ramping up in line with customer schedules; capacity is modular and tied to confirmed programmes.
New Uttarakhand facility, about INR20 crores investment, is progressing per the customer plan. It will co-locate relocated business first and later serve other North India customers.
Utilisation is expected to rise progressively as the announced control arm and link orders ramp up.
demand_pricing: Management cited industry domestic production up over 22% YoY to 93.6 lakh units. Passenger vehicle production rose 16.8% to 14.53 lakh units and utility vehicles rose 21.2%. LCV production rose 20.8% to 1.91 lakh units.
Management said the addressable market grew 8-10%, and Sharda's gross profit growth of 8% was broadly in line. The company is not present with Japanese OEMs, which it adjusts for.

Substrate (catalyst) prices are customer-directed and passed through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Steel and aluminium impact was said to be immaterial to gross profit.

CAFE III draft (16 July 2026, proposed from 1 April 2027) and BS6.3/WLTP from 1 April 2027 expected to lift emission content. BS7 is not yet notified; Euro-7-aligned content would rise in hot-end aftertreatment, catalyst loading and GPF.
Premium two-wheeler emission opportunity under evaluation for domestic supply (above a particular cc). TREM3 integrated muffler market estimated at INR60-100 crores, which management called small.

qa_highlights.question: Can export orders be converted into FY27 and FY28 top-line, for example about INR100 crores in FY27 and INR200 crores in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying revenue depends on customer schedules. It said SOP dates are unchanged and a new platform usually takes one to two years to reach peak volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Gross profit growth of 8% versus steel and aluminium price increases: is there a one-quarter lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said catalyst and substrate are fully pass-through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed on a one-to-two-quarter lag, and one-time premium freight and RM costs were absorbed in Q1. It said the impact was built into the 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth lagging the industry, and when will it converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the serviceable market grew 8-10% after adjusting for the Japanese OEM exposure and a supplier fire at a key customer, and Sharda grew 8%. Growth drivers are existing orders, RFQ conversion and industry growth. No guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Donghee TLA opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint showcasing to OEMs has generated RFQs across multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, and targets a mid-teen to high-teen percentage share.

qa_highlights.question: What content uplift comes from BS6.3, CAFE III and BS7?
qa_highlights.answer: WLTP content uplift may be limited because catalyst efficiency and calibration change rather than a full redesign. BS7 content would rise through hot-end aftertreatment, high catalyst loading and GPF, but depends on Euro-7 adoption. CAFE III supports lightweighting and multi-powertrain engineered emission systems.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emission export pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export focus is CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components and small agri genset exhaust systems. It pointed to announced orders across emissions, agri and tubes, and said no pipeline figures would be given.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% against 34% revenue growth shows pass-through dilution; the Q2 gross margin trend needs watching as one-time costs normalise.
The supplier fire at a key customer affected Q1 production; recovery timing was not disclosed.
Management said the one-to-two-quarter raw material indexing lag can shift timing, though it claimed no net vacuum.
Export SOPs for the North American orders are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and the timing of revenue ramp was not quantified.
The lightweighting market share gain (from 14%) will only be disclosed at FY27 year-end.
Geopolitical risk and premium raw material procurement costs are flagged as ongoing risks.
Management said it is ready for larger acquisitions, but no target or timeline was given.

541974|2026-06.headline: Manorama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore, with PAT margin at 19.5%.
541974|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore, crossing INR 400 crore for the first time, with management attributing growth mainly to volume (about 85% YoY per management). EBITDA rose 42.2% to INR 106 crore at a 26.3% margin, and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore. Management said the QIP of about INR 500 crore has closed and it has lined up a ~INR 460 crore capex plan spanning India and Burkina Faso, with commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on guidance, Brazil revenue, and subsidiary losses.</overview>

segments.name: Value-added specialty fats (CBE and stearin)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE is about 30% and stearin about 70% of the contribution from these products; per-ton realisations were not shared, but pricing was described as largely stable.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (consolidated vs standalone)
segments.commentary: Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to about INR 3 crore from about INR 8 crore in Q4 FY26, with negligible subsidiary revenue; West African entities are sourcing vehicles and Brazil is in build-out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation guidance is about 80% (management internal target 80-85%) on expanded capacity of about 52,000 tonnes per annum after 4,500 t debottlenecking; the company declined to restate the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance from November, pointing to utilisation metrics instead.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR 225-250 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date and about INR 220 crore more planned in FY27.

Gross margin expected in a 45-50% range, with EBITDA margin the preferred tracking metric; management said margins should hold broadly stable at current range, with quarter-to-quarter movement possible.

Burkina Faso facility (about INR 120-130 crore) has an estimated payback of about 3 years once operational; the remainder of the ~INR 460 crore plan is for India (solvent fractionation 3 and refinery).
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact expected in FY29 as plants ramp up.
Balance sheet: no further equity dilution planned; working capital to be funded via existing banker lines led by SBI, plus ~INR 150 crore FDR outside the QIP proceeds.
capex_capacity: Current fractionation capacity 47,500 t per annum; additional 7,500 t already operational, with a further 4,500 t debottlenecking targeted around Q3 FY27, taking capacity to about 52,000 t.
Debottlenecking cost estimated at INR 5-6 crore.

Burkina Faso: about 10 hectares (24 acres) land acquired for shea nut and mango nut processing with regulatory approvals pending; facility covers extraction and expelling, solvent fractionation and related capacity, about INR 120-130 crore.
Overall proposed capex plan about INR 460 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date; Q1 spend about INR 20 crore across Manorama and subsidiaries.
Brazil (LatAm) partner: trial production started in the last quarter; ramp-up expected gradually over the next 2-4 quarters, with production sourced from the Indian plant.

544602|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% YoY to INR3,522 crores; EBITDA turned positive at INR33 crores versus a INR31 crore loss a year ago.
544602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR3,522 crores, up 5.8% YoY and 20.8% QoQ, with gross profit of INR733 crores (up 2.5% YoY, 6.5% QoQ). EBITDA was INR33 crores against a loss of INR31 crores in Q1 FY26 and INR17 crores in Q4 FY26. Losses narrowed at EBIT (loss of INR18 crores) and PAT (loss of INR28 crores), and standalone borrowings fell to INR272 crores from INR314 crores at March 31, 2026. Management attributed the volume recovery to sequential trade-lane improvement after inventory corrections, while the Middle East conflict continued to weigh on FCL volumes.

segments.commentary: Mainstay and highest-margin business; about 14.5% global market share. Volumes up about 5% QoQ, but down about 4% YoY and about 10% below levels of two years ago.

segments.name: FCL (full container load)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 1% QoQ and down double digits YoY, weighed by Middle East exposure. FCL market share is under 1%.

segments.name: Air freight
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 5% QoQ; double-digit YoY decline per management. Smaller part of the business.

Intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms over the coming couple of years, including employee and admin expenses.

Ballpark of 12% to 15% volume growth from current levels needed to reach desired profitability trajectory; part from market share, part from trade rebound.
