No guidance on return on capital employed, though management said it should return to the historical 'north of 20%' zone broadly.
capex_capacity: Business described as asset-light with minimal owned capital assets; capex a tiny fraction of P&L.
Non-core divestments: warehousing and office assets, combined about USD10 million to USD15 million.
Network optimisation: loss-making trade lanes reduced; focus on container utilisation.
Cost initiatives: AI/agentic automation, offshoring to lower-cost geographies, single global system for finance, HR and operations.
Management said no further acquisitions needed near term; growth to come organically by hiring teams for new products and markets.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q1 was about half market growth and half market outperformance, per management.
Middle East conflict has depressed volumes for about 5 to 6 months; inventory corrections drove momentum on transatlantic, transpacific and intra-Asia lanes.
Carrier capacity constrained by disruptions, keeping freight rates elevated; management said freight rates rose about 20% to 30% (per analyst question) and is passed through in revenue and costs.
Gross profit growth of about 6.6% QoQ versus about 4.1% implied by volume mix; management attributed the extra 2 to 2.5% to freight environment and efficiencies.
Industry volumes down about 13% to 14% over last two years; Allcargo outperforming by about 3% to 4%. Growth in Latin America, Southeast Asia and India offset declines in Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry cyclical and why have yields fallen since FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the post-COVID 21 to 24 month period was exceptional for FCL margins, and excluding it yield has improved continuously; volumes, not yields, have been the drag. It described the business as shadowing trade conditions rather than cycling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are volumes declining when global trade is broadly flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCL has declined more than the industry on a YoY basis, while FCL decline is higher for Allcargo due to Middle East exposure. No alternative to LCL exists except air for small shipments averaging 3 to 4 cubic metres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost base and is it flat in USD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms; about 80 to 85% of business sits outside India and ocean freight is the largest cost in USD. Rupee translation affects both revenue and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt composition and net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is mainly working capital plus acquisition funding. Consolidated gross debt about INR942 crores and net debt about INR570 crores at June quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and ROCE normalisation path is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA margin guidance, since margins are not a relevant metric in this business. Management said ROCE was historically above 20% and should return there broadly; a 12% to 15% volume increase from current levels is the ballpark needed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, no; management said the strategy is to grow by investing in people rather than buying businesses, as all key markets and products are already covered.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing to depress FCL volumes, particularly in and out of the region, with knock-on impact on North Asia.
LCL volumes still about 4% below last year and about 10% below two years ago; no guidance for substantial growth.
Rupee translation and USD cost base: management intends flat USD cost, but reported INR figures will move with exchange rate.
Net debt reduction targeted over two to three quarters depends on working capital release and divestments; still to be evidenced.
Company does not provide gross or EBITDA margin guidance; a monthly yield trend update (indexed, not absolute) is promised from this month.
PAT still negative (loss of INR28 crores); profitability relies on volume recovery and cost discipline.

the business has actually, you know, generated cash in the recent times.

Management guided FY27 top-line to lower single-digit growth, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be better.</overview>

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.
544709|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore against ₹17.8 crore in Q1 FY26, with management attributing the slow growth to seasonality and pre-launch work. Reported EBITDA fell 52.96% to ₹2.4 crore and PAT from continuing operations fell 42.27% to ₹1.8 crore, which management tied to front-loaded expansion costs and a one-time pan-India marketing push for the SiD and ERICA AI embryology tools. EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

Disruption from the Middle East war cited as a headwind; no quantification given.
Possible acquisitions in India, with no details on size or timing.
539636|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Indian standalone business and its program pipeline; cautious and somewhat non-committal on EMOSS, where management repeatedly said it is too early to predict the outcome. Management gave few specifics on order-book timing, capex amounts or EMOSS losses.

522205|2026-06.headline: Praj Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 116.1 mn (vs INR 53.4 mn) on INR 7.16 bn revenue, with order intake of INR 10 bn and backlog of INR 45.9 bn.
522205|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated income from operations rose to INR 7.16 bn from INR 6.4 bn a year earlier, and PBT before exceptional items more than doubled to INR 210.5 mn. Order intake was INR 10 bn, with 57% domestic, and backlog stood at INR 45.9 bn at June 30, 2026. Management said execution remains slowed by first-generation ethanol funding issues and supply-demand imbalance, while new verticals (Praj GenX data-center work, Bio-IBA demo plant, Brazil corn-to-ethanol plant, ZLD/HiPurity for semiconductors) are starting to show orders. Margins were described as subdued on volume and mix, and management declined to give margin guidance.</overview>
<parameter name="financial_highlights">[{"metric":"Consolidated income from operations","value":"INR 7.16 bn","change":"vs INR 6.4 bn in Q1 FY26 (up c.12%)"},{"metric":"PBT before exceptional items","value":"INR 210.5 mn","change":"vs INR 96.09 mn in Q1 FY26"},{"metric":"Profit after tax","value":"INR 116.1 mn","change":"vs INR 53.4 mn in Q1 FY26"},{"metric":"Order intake","value":"INR 10 bn","change":"57% domestic; 62% bioenergy, 28% engineering, 10% HiPurity"},{"metric":"Order backlog (June 30, 2026)","value":"INR 45.9 bn","change":"63% domestic"},{"metric":"Cash in hand (June 30, 2026)","value":"INR 6.16 bn","change":""},{"metric":"Revenue mix","value":"Bioenergy 66%, Engineering 22%, HiPurity 12%","change":""},{"metric":"Export share of revenue","value":"25%","change":""}]

segments.name: Bioenergy
segments.commentary: 66% of revenue and 62% of order intake; bioenergy revenue cited at INR 474 crore in the quarter. Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield slowed; brownfield, DCO and ENA demand holding up.

segments.name: Engineering (incl. Praj GenX)
segments.commentary: 22% of revenue and 28% of order intake. Praj GenX won a hyperscale data-center modular supply framework with a minimum of about USD 50 mn over 2.5 years; management said booking is phased, not the full INR 500 crore headline.

segments.name: Praj HiPurity Systems
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue and 10% of order intake. First combined ultrapure water and ZLD contract for an Indian semiconductor company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management declined to give margin or segment-level margin targets, citing ongoing investment in Praj GenX, R&D and new ventures.
Praj GenX expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (management said 'to start with, consider EBITDA breakeven'); PBT breakeven not confirmed.
International order share rose to about 40-43% of Q1 orders; management expects international revenue share to move up from about 25-30% in coming quarters, with export execution from Q3 FY27.
Bio-IBA commercial-scale demo plant construction expected to complete by December 2026.
Management expects new-vertical results (GenX, internationalisation, alternatives to ethanol) to show more clearly in the latter part of FY27, based on current order book.
Material cost upward pressure from geopolitical situation; management said it is using contracts and advance procurement to offset.
capex_capacity: Bio-IBA (bio-isobutanol) commercial-scale demo plant ordered in prior quarter; construction to complete by December 2026. Management cited 2% diesel blending mandate potential of over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity.
Brazil greenfield corn-to-ethanol plant of about 800 KLPD, executed end-to-end by Praj.
Ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering order from an international customer, following a completed basic engineering order last quarter.

Ballpark capex for a 100 KLPD ethanol/isobutanol plant: INR 100-120 crore, depending on feedstock and product. Praj scope typically 50-60% of project value (process and critical equipment; installation/construction optional).
Mangaluru facility used for Praj GenX precision fabrication and modular manufacturing; first data-center project deliveries expected across Q2-Q4 FY27.
Dr. Pramod Chaudhari Centre of Excellence for Advanced Bioeconomy inaugurated at SPPU on August 10, 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield inquiries limited to ethanol-deficit states (Tamil Nadu, Assam); management expects this to persist until higher blending mandates are announced.
Funding issues at end customers and ethanol supply-demand imbalance are extending first-gen project execution cycles.
Strong demand for ENA greenfield plants, where management claims a technology edge; brownfield demand driven by efficiency and co-products such as DCO.

CBG: GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme approved with outlay over INR 23,000 crore for FY27 to FY35-36; management expects better CBG margins as market opens, but noted many new CBG entrants.
Margin drag: material cost up about 10% YoY in Q1 on higher African export mix (lower margin); other expenses down about 7% YoY.
Q1 FY27 quarter-on-quarter: material cost down about 3% and other expenses up about 4%, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Collections and execution: why was bioenergy revenue (INR 474 crore) low versus the opening order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to slow conversion of domestic first-gen ethanol projects due to end-customer funding and ethanol supply-demand imbalance, partly offset by acceleration on other projects. Collections are lagging because of slow backlog conversion; management is working on it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin expand, and will RM and site expenses weigh on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material cost and other expenses offset each other depending on the equipment vs site mix. YoY, material cost rose about 10% on African export mix, while other expenses fell 7%. Management expects steel-driven cost pressure to be managed with advance measures.

qa_highlights.question: Praj GenX breakeven timing and order book share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets EBITDA breakeven by end-FY27 and would not disclose GenX backlog share; engineering is still reported as one basket. Order-book buildup is improving with shorter delivery cycles on data-center orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports decline YoY while domestic revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export revenue timing depends on order entry and execution cycles; a large export order batch was booked in Q1 with execution starting around Q3 after engineering. International share of orders was 40-43% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over the next decade and service mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said services margins are higher than project margins and the mix shift (domestic/international, services/projects, new biofuels) is the route to better margins. Current investments in GenX, R&D and new ventures are absorbing margin.

qa_highlights.question: Bio-isobutanol mandate timing and biomaterials (bio-bitumen, PLA)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the timing of any diesel blending mandate is unknown, but Praj is technology-ready. Lactic acid technology for PLA exists; co-product progress is expected by fiscal year-end.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 820 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
from 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit on sale of fixed assets (oil exit)

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.name: Edible oil / packaged oil (exited)
segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant to restart in about 15 days from the call, and that the new 150 KLPD Bathinda unit (commissioned in early July 2026) will substantially offset the lost volume.
Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.
Management guided to a sustained distillery/overall margin range of about 10% to 12%, while noting raw material and fuel price volatility.
Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
No share buyback planned for now. Debt will rise only if a new capex project is started.
capex_capacity: Svaksha Distillery (350 KLPD, Kharagpur, West Bengal) became wholly owned on 30 June 2026 after the remaining 25% stake was acquired.
Newly added 150 KLPD Bathinda unit began commercial trials at end-June 2026 and was commissioned in the first half of July 2026.
200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.
Bio-CBG is under active evaluation (Haryana policy noted), with paddy straw feedstock seen as tricky. The company is not making biodiesel.
demand_pricing: ENA and private ethanol supply face price pressure from oversupply. Average private ethanol price is about INR 58/litre ex-factory, mainly to Reliance.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.

532906|2026-06.headline: Maan Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR232 crore and EBITDA to INR7 crore, with margin near 3%.
532906|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR232 crore, up 10% YoY from INR211 crore but down from INR255 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR7 crore from INR5 crore sequentially, with margin about 3% versus about 2%, and PAT was about INR3 crore (EPS INR0.52 vs INR0.29). Management said exports fell to about 45% of manufacturing revenue (from 60-70% earlier) due to duties, and freight and Middle East shipping disruption continue to weigh on volumes and costs. Capex of about INR166 crore over three years is planned, with Dewas precision tubing and Pithampur Italian press ramp-up the key near-term items.</overview>

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q1 manufacturing turnover above INR70 crore with about 40% exports (management also cited ~45% export share of manufacturing revenue in prepared remarks). Production about 1,558 MT against 24,000 MT extrusion capacity. Anodizing utilisation ~45-50% and machining ~55%.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Described as opportunistic and pass-through; the remainder of the INR232 crore revenue (about INR160 crore implied) comes from trading. Management expects trading to decline as manufacturing mix rises.

guidance_outlook: Volumes expected to stay flattish QoQ and for FY27; ramp-up possibly toward end of FY27 or start of FY28.
Manufacturing revenue guided flattish; management would be 'okay' with FY26 level of ~INR300 crore manufacturing top line.
Pithampur Italian press: management targets ~35%/50%/75% ramp in a three-year plan; currently ~25% ramp-up; significant contribution expected by mid-FY28.
Dewas aluminium precision tubing plant: online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28 (no firm date given); capex mostly in H2 FY27.
Recovery of gas/energy cost increases: about 50% passed to customers over last two quarters, balance expected to be recovered in one to two quarters as contracts renew.
Management said no new debt planned for capex; company is deleveraging and has sufficient cash. Employee expenses expected not to rise materially as technical team is already hired.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: foundry 12,000 TPA; extrusion 24,000 TPA; anodizing 3,600 TPA; machining 1,400 TPA.
Three-year capex plan of ~INR166 crore cumulative, including Pithampur, new dials and general capex, and new plants under development; ~INR90 crore allocated to new plants.
Dewas precision tubing project: total capex ~INR45 crore, of which ~INR15-20 crore spent to date; aimed at aerospace, defence and automotive; expected asset turn at least 2-3x at peak utilisation.
Capex spend in Q1 FY27 was less than INR5 crore; overseas visit planned to finalise extrusion press and other machinery for Dewas; majority of capex in H2 FY27.
Pithampur capacity was expanded from 1,200 MT to 12,000-24,000 MT near end of last year; Italian press now online.
demand_pricing: Export share has dropped from around 60-70% to about 45% (about 40% in Q1 per call Q&A) because of duties hitting the export business; management aims to shift volume to domestic high-value business, which is slow to convert.
Freight rates up 5-10x on Strait of Hormuz and Middle East disruption; customers in GCC and East Asia holding back orders; delays and backed-up shipping persist.
Conversion margins: plain extrusion 6-10% (management cited 6-8% and 6-10%); value-added processing (powder coating, machining, anodizing) targeted at 15%+.
Commodity exposure: most manufacturing volumes hedged via LME/MCX on order basis; unhedged positions kept under 5%; management says commodity moves impact margins by less than 5%.

Trading is a pass-through business at metal prices; management said EBITDA per ton is reported on a blended basis only, with manufacturing EBITDA per ton not readily available (last quarter's USD340/ton reference not updated).

qa_highlights.question: What was the capacity volume this quarter and EBITDA per ton (last quarter USD340/t)?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA is reported only on a blended basis; manufacturing per-ton figure not available. Total extrusion production was about 1,558 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any ramp-up in volumes sooner than expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management reiterated flattish volumes, with any ramp-up toward end FY27 or early FY28. The export loss from duties is being replaced by slow-converting domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium prices hedged and how do margins change with value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging is order-linked on LME/MCX, with under 5% unhedged; plain extrusion margins are 6-10%, rising to 15%+ with value addition. Management said absolute EBITDA per ton is the right metric for conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Dewas project status, timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-20 crore of INR45 crore spent; online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28, with no firm date. Asset turn at least 2-3x; no margin figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take on debt for capex, and how will employee costs move?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned; management said the company is deleveraging. Employee costs are not expected to rise materially as the technical team is already on payroll.

qa_highlights.question: How has other expenses fallen and how are energy costs being recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell from INR18 crore to INR13 crore over four quarters. About 50% of the gas cost increase was passed to customers, with the rest to follow as contracts renew.

540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
540678|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,068.59 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +2.4%)
vs INR 249.54 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
vs INR 187.82 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
Around INR 27,000 crore after NGSV contract (L1, about INR 5,000 crore)

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +120.64% YoY vs INR125.24 crores; +39.85% QoQ vs INR197.59 crores

financial_highlights.metric: FMCG + FMCG intermediate share of consolidated revenue

segments.name: Roorkee facility
segments.commentary: Soap INR27.50 crores (vs INR17.63 crores in Q4 FY26) and noodles INR87.62 crores (vs INR44.47 crores in Q4 FY26).

segments.name: Bhilwara facility
segments.commentary: Home care and detergent INR40.98 crores (vs INR32.50 crores in Q4 FY26); edible INR30.34 crores (vs INR29.26 crores).

segments.name: Guwahati facility
segments.commentary: Cosmetics INR26.15 crores (vs INR20.91 crores in Q4 FY26); noodles INR37.75 crores (vs INR26.01 crores).

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Management said textile revenue was roughly flat and margins were hit hardest by dye, chemical and fuel costs; no price increase could be passed through in the quarter. Long-run textile share guided at 8-10% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected in INR900-1,000 crores; FY28 growth of 15-20% over FY27 cited, with the INR1,000 crores target for FY28 reiterated.
FY27 profitability expected around 6%, improving by 0.75-1% in FY28; a separate remark targets 7% by FY28 with EBITDA margin up another 2-2.5%.
Management expects raw-material cost pressure to normalise by Q3 or Q4 FY27; textile expected to turn good by Q3 FY27.
Near-term priority: neutralise the Q1 cost increase over the next two to three quarters and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.
Long-run revenue mix: textile 8-10%, FMCG 90-92%.
capex_capacity: Roorkee soap line commissioned in Q1 FY27 adds ~1,700 MT per month; aggregate FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity is 20,840 TPM (from 19,640 TPM at Q4 FY26).
Utilisation is currently ~50-55%; management expects another 25-30% utilisation gain by FY28.
Little further capacity addition expected over the next one to one-and-a-half years; only balancing capex is planned.
Bhilwara spices and savories plant runs one shift; second shift is free for expansion.
Management says existing capacity is enough to reach the INR1,000 crores FY28 revenue target without new capex.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to newly acquired units and new soap and FMCG capacity added in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, with customer base added during the quarter.
Business is B2B only; no B2C revenue. Over 200 customers, with quarterly planning forecasts and firm monthly orders.
Textile could not pass on dye, chemical and fuel cost increases in Q1; PP packaging prices spiked with geopolitical tension.
Spice margins described as lower and savory margins as higher.
Management expects revenue growth to come mainly from food and soap segments over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: How did raw-material and crude-linked costs behave in the quarter and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dyes, chemicals, consumables, boiler fuel and LABSA rose; PP packaging spiked. Textile prices could not be raised in Q1; management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR900-1,000 crores, FY28 growth 15-20%; FY27 profitability about 6%, rising 0.75-1% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raised funds went to Roorkee, and is further fundraising planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Roorkee capacity was funded from the subsidiary's retained earnings. INR98.65 crores raised was used for Bhilwara food and Guwahati soap/noodle/cosmetics facilities, not for Sunrakshakk Agro acquisition, which predated the raise. No further fundraising is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Will textile continue or be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger plans; textile is expected to improve by Q3 FY27 after a weak Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the next two to three quarter milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Offset the Q1 cost increase and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 10.19% QoQ; recovery depends on input costs normalising by Q3 or Q4 FY27, which management itself flagged as uncertain given renewed pressure in Q2.

540153|2026-06.headline: Endurance Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 35.9% to ₹3,194.15 crores, with EBITDA margin at 11.2% after a commodity pass-through headwind.

508954|2026-06.headline: Finkurve's Q1 FY27 AUM grew 135% YoY to a 118-branch network, with gross NPA at 0.54% and debt-to-equity up to 2.9x.
508954|2026-06.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as a transition quarter for the gold loan industry, with new RBI norms prompting sector-wide alignment and some near-term drag on customer and channel momentum. Reported AUM rose 135% YoY, revenue about 89% YoY and PAT about 65% YoY, with branches up from 83 to 118. Asset quality was stable (gross NPA 0.54%, net NPA 0.48%), while leverage rose sharply (debt-to-equity 0.7x to 2.9x) and ROA fell to 2.9%. Management reiterated 50-60% AUM growth guidance for FY27 and disclosed the first institutional NCD subscription (Rs 50 crore from Franklin Templeton).</overview>

544342|2026-06.headline: Stallion Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.78% YoY to ₹124.68 crore while PAT jumped 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore; management says margins are partly one-off.
544342|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached ₹124.68 crore (+12.78% YoY), EBITDA rose 75.85% to ₹25.27 crore and PAT rose 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore. Management attributed the margin jump to a mix of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and inventory gains, splitting EBITDA roughly 50:50 between inventory gains and operations. The high-purity helium plant at Khalapur (1,200 MTPA) is complete with commercial operations expected next quarter, while the 10,000 MT R32 plant at Bhilwara slipped from a July 2026 target to end-December 2026, and Mambattu (HFO blending) is now due by year-end. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion is pricing vs product mix, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combination of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and high stock-keeping during the Gulf crisis; said inventory gains are roughly 50:50 of EBITDA, and that margins will not necessarily repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% revenue growth guidance still intact after the R32 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said the 30-35% is intact, while acknowledging the FY27 R32 contribution will change slightly from ₹250 crore; Q4 R32 revenue expected around ₹125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the R32 plant delayed and what funding was used?
qa_highlights.answer: A planned preferential issue was abandoned after a share-price spike; a rights issue was used instead, reaching the market only by February, so the planned December startup slipped to March-end under the original plan.

qa_highlights.question: What are the helium volumes and how is supply secured given Middle East shipping disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~5 containers in FY27, 12 in FY28, 24 after; utilisation about 20% of 1,200 MTPA next year. Supply secured via Sharjah Oxygen, swap arrangements and multiple sources; price expected to rise.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it previously preferred internal accruals, but now sees dilution and debt as likely for faster growth ('some dilution, some debt, not all debt'); no decision made yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose pre-sales, calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs; said the company will not commit to take-or-pay contracts ahead of plant readiness.

capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Third captive solar plant in Bikaner: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, commissioned in Q1 FY27; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement. Further 6.5 MWp (Borosil) and 3-4 MWp (Stylenest) solar under evaluation.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.
West Asia conflict net impact on Q1 FY27 about INR10 crore (INR12 crore cited in Q&A), with price increases compensating only a couple of crore.

Fuel cost run-rate: Opalware fuel impact about INR6 crore in Q1, expected to fall to about INR1.5 crore a quarter; borosilicate fuel impact about INR2.5 crore a quarter, expected to fall to INR60-70 lakh. Fuel at 5.8% of sales vs 2.9% a year ago.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that 14-15% is the historical level and ~18% is the steady-state margin without West Asia impact; FY27 target is for 18% on the year, with improvement dependent on price realisation and lower fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.

520073|2026-06.headline: RACL Geartech Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose about 22% YoY to ₹132.6 crore, with PBT up about 50% to ₹16.8 crore.
520073|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated turnover reached ₹132.6 crore in Q1 FY27 versus ₹108.7 crore a year earlier, with exports at ₹85.06 crore (64%) and domestic at ₹40.54 crore (31%). Management said operating revenue grew about 31.5% on a consolidated basis as non-operating income was negligible this quarter. Consolidated EBITDA rose about 18% to ₹32.19 crore, and PBT rose about 50% to ₹16.82 crore. 543910|2026-06.headline: AVG Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29.98% to INR6.46 crore on revenue growth of 5.97% to INR132.48 crore; FY27 guidance 15-20% revenue growth.
543910|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 5.97% YoY to INR132.48 crore, while PBT grew 24.42% to INR8.71 crore and PAT grew 29.98% to INR6.46 crore, with PBT and PAT margins expanding 98 bps and 89 bps. Management attributed the profit growth to fleet productivity, asset utilisation and cost discipline. The company completed a rights issue raising INR52.93 crore in Q1, secured a 100-vehicle Haldiram contract, and formed a JV (Carbonlite Logistics) with Baidyanath Group for LNG/EV transport. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20%, while noting Q1 is seasonally a softer quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore of capex is planned (also referenced as INR50-60 crore), with leasing evaluated to balance the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.answer: Two tanker trains bought; one more on lease for about a year. Management expects margin improvement from FY26 capex and higher utilisation, and says liquid, EV and LNG segments carry higher margins.

500472|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 5.9 billion, up 27% YoY and down 1% QoQ, while sales of products were INR 5.5 billion, up about 22% YoY and down 0.7% QoQ. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to close to 20%, versus the earlier ~12% guidance, and said the ~17% margin is a normalised level for the next two years. Capex of about INR 500 crore is planned, with INR 170-180 crore expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~27% growth moderating, and is capacity sufficient?

qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the Haridwar capacity starts in Q4 CY2026. It mainly reduces dependence on SKF Industrial trading volumes and is secondarily for growth; growth impact comes in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~17% margin normalised for the next two years?

Management attributed the decline to the Middle East war and repeatedly deferred on specifics such as debtor balances, Club 2.0 membership counts and strategic investors.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

financial_highlights.change: About INR326 crores after IPO proceeds of INR142 crores and September-quarter capex

segments.name: API (steroid and hormone APIs)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, +6% YoY, driven largely by volume; API EBITDA INR66 crores, +9% YoY; gross margin 60%+. Management says more than 90% of FY27 revenue comes from API. Capacity utilisation is about 70-80%.

segments.name: Biotech CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27. Built on about 400 kL of large-scale fermentation at Ujjain, with signed 10-year take-or-pay with a US alternate-protein player and 5-year take-or-pay for insulin drug substance. Small revenues are guided for Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenues for FY28.

segments.name: Complex injectables (dual-chamber vials/bags)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 (Q4 FY26 had about INR33 crores of milestone revenue across CDMO and injectables). First DCV ANDA filed in September 2026; second molecule ANDA planned for Q4 FY27. Term sheet with a large US pharma multinational; definitive agreement expected early Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% and EBITDA growth of about 25% on a consolidated basis, with a plus/minus 5% band citing global operating uncertainty.
PAT growth will be lower than EBITDA growth because of depreciation drag; cash PAT (PAT plus depreciation) growth is expected to be above 25%.
New-business opex of about INR23 crores and depreciation of about INR11 crores per quarter to run for the next two to three quarters.
Management expects the first couple of quarters to be lumpy, with a strong H2 FY27 from milestone cash flows (Q3/Q4) that management says will offset the new-business opex.
Insulin/biologics revenue expected to start early FY28, pending stability studies and DCGI approval.
Capex of INR200-250 crores per year for the next two to three years, funded by internal accruals and customer contributions.
capex_capacity: Cumulative investment of more than INR1,000 crores in the two new businesses, of which over INR500 crores is in biomanufacturing/biopharma fermentation.
Gross block in API about INR640 crores as of 30 June 2026; management cites INR800-900 crores of API revenue and asset turnover of about 1.5x.

Phase 0: existing 400 kL fermentation capacity, largely booked under current contracts. Phase 1: brownfield expansion of about 600 kL (about 4x the current capacity) with construction starting Q3 FY27 and 15-18 months to build.
DCV: five to six products developed and moving to plant-level validation; a second DCV line may be needed soon due to capacity constraints.
Mhow injectable facility is part of the roughly INR1,000 crores invested in new businesses.
demand_pricing: Management says demand and traction are very strong, with discussions with more than half a dozen potential customers, each seeking about 1 million litres of fermentation capacity.
Take-or-pay contracts are multi-million-dollar per customer; management declined to disclose per-litre pricing, minimum revenue or contract values, citing confidentiality.
Management guides to industry-level margins for complex injectables and CDMO: gross margin above 70% and EBITDA margin above 35%, and expects Symbiotec to be in a similar range.

API gross margin guided at around 60% (currently above 60%), with EBITDA margin near 30%. Management attributes margin strength to backward integration (make vs buy) and mix shift toward regulated markets.
Customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries; about 70% of FY26 revenue from customers served for more than seven years.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity, revenue and take-or-pay minimums in the fermentation business be framed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the advanced-stage contracts would require about four times the current capacity (Phase 1, over 2-3 years). It did not give per-litre revenue or minimum revenue numbers, only that each contract is multi-million dollar and asset turnover should exceed 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 kL expansion for existing or new customers, and what is the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The 600 kL Phase 1 is tied to a customer with a signed term sheet, with construction starting Q3 FY27 and taking 15-18 months. Funding combines internal accruals with customer contributions; no specific outlay was given beyond INR200-250 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are opex and milestone expectations for the new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR23 crores quarterly opex run rate should continue for two to three quarters. Management said H2 milestone revenues would offset the full-year new-business opex, without giving amounts.

qa_highlights.question: How long before DCV launches, and how many products follow?
qa_highlights.answer: The first DCV ANDA is filed, the second is due in Q4 FY27, and five to six products are in development. Management said capacity, not product count, is the constraint, and a second line may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no revenue from CDMO and injectables in Q1, and what were last year's milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone revenue is periodic, not quarterly. About INR33 crores was recognised in Q4 FY26, and none in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is API capacity utilisation and gross and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: API utilisation is about 70-80%. Management expects gross margin around 60% and EBITDA margin near 30%, with variance from logistics and solvent prices.

qa_highlights.question: Premarin generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timing, saying the partner controls formulation development and FDA submission; Symbiotec's part is the API.

qa_highlights.question: API share of revenue two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: API is over 90% of revenue today. Management expects it to fall below half in 5-6 years as CDMO and DCV scale.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.</overview>

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

500214|2026-06.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
500214|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

financial_highlights.value: INR 112 crore / loss of INR 34 lakh
financial_highlights.change: +33% revenue YoY; loss was INR 45 lakh
excludes Hyundai win of about USD 52 million

segments.name: Treatment Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 210 crore (+14% YoY) with EBIT loss of INR 17 crore, hit by legacy projects including the UP project. Dispatches to GCC resumed post-quarter; a Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore per Q&A) was won after quarter end.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 105 crore (+14% YoY) and EBIT INR 13 crore, margin 11.89% vs under 6% a year ago, driven by water treatment solutions and membranes. Institutional products moved here from Consumer.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72 crore (+28% YoY) and EBIT INR 7 crore (9.92% margin vs 10.55%), with margin pressure from higher input costs. Includes a 20-year O&M concession in Oman with PDO.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 230 crore (+21% YoY) but EBIT INR 22 crore (-52% YoY), impacted by geopolitics and Roha ramp-up costs; Roha cost drag about 6% of segment margin. FX gain in the prior-year quarter also reversed (about 3-4 pts).

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 112 crore (+33% YoY) with a small loss of INR 34 lakh vs INR 45 lakh a year ago; breakeven targeted in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Specialty Chemicals capacity to grow at least 50% over the next couple of years as Roha reaches full capacity over about four years, with asset turnover just under 2x.
Roha utilisation guidance of 25% in year one is still held but described as softer than expected; management will review by end of Q2 FY27.
UP legacy project is not expected to close in FY27 and will spill into FY28, dependent on government fund flows; other large legacy project expected to see significant progress by FY27 end.
Consumer Products targeted to break even in FY27.
Management aims to restore double-digit profitability over time; no timeline given. Input costs expected to moderate if crude stays near USD 80.
capex_capacity: Roha resin plant commissioned and in stabilisation; with Ankleshwar debottlenecking, total resin capacity expected to reach about 5x the pre-Roha level (Phase I doubles capacity, Phase II plus debottlenecking takes it to about 5x).
Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, targeted within the next 12 months; described as asset-light, technology-led rather than capex-heavy.
Membrane business: second Goa plant under construction to add UF and MBR capacity; tie-up with MANN+HUMMEL for UF PVDF technology. Management targets 3x business growth over the years.
Standard plants capacity expanded across Hosur, Goa and Wada.
Management would not disclose capital earmarked for BOOT/BOO service projects, saying it will remain asset-light.
demand_pricing: Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore) won post quarter end; supplied to an EPC, FOB Mumbai, kickoff under way.
Bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crore as of the call.

Price increases taken across customers and segments, but pass-through lags input cost increases; management sees some moderation in input costs with crude near USD 80 vs over USD 100 in March-April 2026.
Geopolitical situation (West Asia) impacted invoicing and dispatches; Roha volumes expected to lean on overseas markets, including North America after WQA certification.
UP project unexecuted portion is about 11% of June order backlog; receivable exposure said to be broadly unchanged over recent quarters.

532804|2026-06.headline: Technocraft Q1 FY27: Drum Closure EBIT margin near 43% on record volumes and rupee depreciation; management targets sustainable 30% for drums, 15% for scaffolding and engineering services.
532804|2026-06.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, with Drum Closure posting its highest-ever revenue and EBIT margin (about 43%) on higher export volumes and a weaker rupee. Scaffolding volumes rose year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand, with realisations broadly stable. Mach One (aluminium formwork) volumes fell year-on-year but edged up sequentially, which management attributed to site and project readiness rather than competition. Management repeatedly declined to treat the current margins as the new normal and kept its sustainable-margin guidance unchanged. No significant new capex is planned for FY27.</overview>

segments.name: Drum Closure
segments.commentary: Almost 100% export. Volumes and rupee depreciation drove record revenue and EBIT. Management targets a sustainable margin of 30% or more. Non-seasonal, not order-book based.

segments.name: Scaffolding (Steel)
segments.commentary: Volumes up year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand (data centres, semicon, AI chip plants, energy). Operating at about 95% utilisation. Sustainable margin guidance of 15%. Middle East is 2-3% of sales and declining.

segments.name: Mach One (Aluminium Formwork)
segments.commentary: Volumes down year-on-year, up marginally quarter-on-quarter. Utilisation about 75-80%. Order book of 3-5 months. Aluminium extrusion plant at over 95%-100% utilisation and helped EBIT amid higher aluminium prices.

segments.name: Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Growing fast on US outsourcing demand, including AI-based vision, embedded systems and automation. Sustainable margin target about 14-15%, which includes ongoing tech investment.

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Fabric business shut down and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn business profitable. Garment business loss-making, with breakeven targeted within two quarters. Working capital released about Rs 15-20 crore (figure varied during the call).

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: JT Cooler approved by DRDO and an Israeli sensor maker, with export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at roughly 15% margin. Missile canister repeat orders. Confirmed order book about Rs 20-21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Drum Closure: sustainable margin of 30% or more; similar volumes expected in the immediate quarter.
Scaffolding: volumes expected to be maintained or improved for the next two quarters; beyond that not guided due to volatility. Sustainable margin 15%.
Engineering Services: sustainable margin 14-15%, inclusive of ongoing investment.
Capex: no significant new capacity capex in FY27, only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN plant and Aurangabad Mach One Phase 2 expected next year.
US tariff refund of close to $3 million expected in the Scaffolding segment, not yet received; timing not stated.
Middle East scaffolding sales expected to stay volatile for one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: No significant new capacity capex planned for FY27; only maintenance capex across divisions. The last major capex (CSN plant, FY25) is fully operational.
Aluminium extrusion plant running at over 95% (management said 100%) utilisation since the March quarter; 100% backward integrated for Mach One.
Mach One utilisation about 75-80%, after a recent Aurangabad capacity expansion. Phase 2 expected sometime next year.
Scaffolding utilisation about 95%. Management says it can add capacity within about 3 months using space in Mumbai and China plants, and is studying options.
Next year: CSN Phase 2 and extra extrusion capacity plus forward integration.
demand_pricing: US scaffolding demand strong since January 2026, driven by AI chip, semicon and energy construction; realisations stable as steel prices did not rise sharply.

US tariff on Chinese scaffolding is 75% (50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301) vs 50% for India and others. Management says Chinese steel costs are 20%+ lower, but Technocraft is only about 5% higher on cost.
Management says it does not compete on price; it competes on inventory availability, distribution and a 150+ component mix.
Indian project launches strong across 7 major cities; demand also from commercial, GCCs and data centres.
Drum Closure: no price cuts planned; competitive position as the world's second-largest producer. Rupee depreciation lifted realisations.
Europe scaffolding sales started in the last two quarters (CE certification), still small due to weak construction in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mach One volumes decline year-on-year, and how is competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to site and project readiness, not competition or demand. Volumes rose slightly quarter-on-quarter. Focus is on quality customers and profitability, not rapid volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43% Drum Closure margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the sustainable margin is above 30% and 43% is not the new normal, given volatility in freight, tariffs and geopolitics. Rupee depreciation and volumes drove the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Defence JT Cooler opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at around 15% margin. Management said quantum is hard to estimate because defence procurement is slow and product-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What are the scaffolding tariff and competitive dynamics in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff is 50% for India, 75% for China. Chinese prices are sometimes lower, but Technocraft does not sell on price. Its US subsidiary and inventory-led distribution are its edge.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capacity capex this year; only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN and Mach One expansion next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Textile plan after the fabric exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric shut and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn profitable; garment loss-making, with breakeven targeted in two quarters. No active plan to sell the rest of the business.

risks_watch: Drum Closure margin normalisation from 43% toward the 30% guidance if the rupee strengthens or freight and tariff costs move.
Scaffolding volume visibility limited to about two quarters; US tariff regime (50%/75%) and Chinese price aggression.
Middle East scaffolding disruption from war and shipping problems.
Garment business breakeven within two quarters; restructuring execution.
Timing of the approximately $3 million US tariff refund.
Defence order timing is slow; JT Cooler export scale is small so far.
Mach One volume recovery depends on site readiness; Y-o-Y decline.

500575|2026-06.headline: Voltas Q1 FY27 net profit rose to Rs 213 crore (Rs 141 crore) on revenue of Rs 4,765 crore, with RAC market share at 17.3%.
500575|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated income grew to Rs 4,765 crore from Rs 4,021 crore, with PBT of Rs 285 crore versus Rs 203 crore. Segment A (unitary cooling) grew 33%, with RAC volumes up 45% and secondary market share at 17.3% against 15.9% for FY26, widening the lead over the nearest competitor to 4 percentage points. Commodity inflation, rupee depreciation and freight costs were largely passed on (10-12% cost increase, near full pass-through), and UCP EBIT margin improved to 5.3% from 3.7%. Projects (Segment B) was soft on execution issues and delayed new orders in the Middle East, while Commercial Refrigeration and Air Coolers were muted. Management also signed a binding term sheet for a 50-50 compressor JV with Atomberg.</overview>

Electromechanical projects: Q2 may not be much better; recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
