Channel cautious on stock; July-August demand not yet clear, festive season view too early.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor JV: capacity, capex, timeline and split among the three entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 2.8 million compressors; total capex still early-stage. Commercial production about 18 months away; the JV was driven by supply security and QCO import limits.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier target for this year; West Asia-driven commodity spike meant brands could not pass through all costs, so breakeven may slip by a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How do QCO norms get met until the JV is operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed up to 30% based on FY25 volumes; continued purchases from Highly and GMCC (India capacity blocked), blending with own supply later.

qa_highlights.question: Why UCP margins are 5% in a strong quarter, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers saw EBIT fall 3-4 pts; Voltas improved YoY on scale, no factory disruption, cost absorption and cost-out. Aspiration of 7%+ over the next ~8 quarters; CFO said margins vary quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Projects margin outlook and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Calibrated order booking to avoid fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses; shifting to shorter-gestation private, data-centre and MEP jobs.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory and July-August demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel cautious; inventory around 4 weeks; too early to judge festive season, with a 4-6 week monitoring window.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek loss in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of JV loss booked at Rs 37 crore; EMP margins to improve in Q3-Q4 after a soft Q2.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

financial_highlights.change: vs 23.5% in Q1 FY26 and 20.4% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA (incl. share of associates and JVs)

financial_highlights.change: interest on inter-corporate loans plus realised and unrealised treasury gains

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates (Lonsen Kiri, 40% stake)

segments.name: Dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Realisations rose across Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemicals; management said H-Acid prices are INR 800-900/unit versus INR 350-400 earlier. Average capacity utilisation was about 60% last quarter, targeted at 70-75% for FY27 if markets support.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri (associate, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 21 crore to consolidated profit in Q1 FY27. Management cited a JV result of about INR 71 crore EBITDA and INR 51 crore PAT on INR 368 crore revenue, as referenced by an analyst; Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, with 60-70% of JV raw materials sourced from Kiri.

segments.name: Copper and fertiliser integrated project (under construction)
segments.commentary: Total project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, with INR 1,400 crore deployed to date, all equity so far. Downstream copper tube, rod and refinery phases are planned for Q1 FY28, FY28 and Q3 FY29 respectively.

guidance_outlook: Copper tube plant (35 KT) expected operational June 2027; 2.25 lakh tonne CCR rod plant (8 mm) expected August-September 2027, both stable by January 2028, using imported Japanese LME-grade cathodes.
Part refinery of 1.75 lakh tonnes (anode to cathode) targeted around January 2028, with scrap melting furnace by December 2027-January 2028.
Copper foil trial production targeted around March 2028 (10 KT Phase 1, 40 KT ambition under ECMS scheme); smelter, sulphuric acid plant and fertiliser balance of plant expected Q1 2029.
First copper revenue expected around end Q1 FY28 (May-June 2027); majority of copper operating revenue expected in FY30.
Management said the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore no longer holds; the numbers are dynamic and depend on vendor timelines.
Debt repayment expected to start in 2029 given moratorium; cash flow expected to ramp stepwise over FY28-FY30.
No dividend declared; no Board decision yet, per management.
capex_capacity: Total copper project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, excluding additional infrastructure spend; outflow expected over the next two years.
Financial closure incomplete; more than 50% of debt commitments received, balance in process, with complete closure hoped within a few months.
Copper concentrate: MoUs of about 1 million tonnes secured against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation; firm contracts typically converted around October each year.
Captive jetty (for bulk imports of copper concentrate, phosphate and ammonia), desalination facility, raw material conveying system and power infrastructure in progress; site near Pipavav Port.
MCB Copper-Gold mine: development not started; 70% off-take structured for Kiri, but Celsius is contesting the off-take in court.
demand_pricing: Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemical prices strengthened in Q1 on tighter global supply and Chinese environmental compliance measures.
Demand is mixed across product categories; input costs rose with crude oil-linked raw materials, with pass-through supporting margins.

Management said existing H-Acid and Vinyl Sulphone capacity could drive about INR 2,000 crore of dyes revenue at 75-80% utilisation if current prices hold, versus about INR 1,200 crore cited as the current base.
Copper: management sees sales as not a constraint because India consumes about 1.8 million tonnes a year with about two-thirds imported; customer quality approvals still required.
Management said sustaining margins depends on passing through input cost movements.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore still hold given staggered tube and rod commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 figure does not hold; projections are moving with vendor delivery timelines. It added that sales are not a constraint since the output would substitute imports.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper revenue start and when will it be fully ramped?
qa_highlights.answer: First copper revenue expected around May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28), with commercial operations from Q2 FY28; majority of operating revenue expected in FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kiri's standalone profitability low when Lonsen Kiri earns strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, which captures finished-product margins; the JV also makes products Kiri does not, so the combined value chain should be assessed. Lonsen Kiri is operated by Kiri management with no plan to replicate its products in Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to raise equity to reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity dilution is a plan B option with investor interest tested, but the Board prefers deferred dilution after execution to capture more value. Debt repayment begins in 2029 due to moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MCB Copper-Gold mine and the off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Development has not started; design complete. Shareholder disputes and Celsius litigation are ongoing and sub judice, so management declined to speculate and said Kiri remains a lender.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a stake sale or MMCI interest?
qa_highlights.answer: No current talks on a 40% stake sale in Lonsen Kiri. Management said it would be 100% interested in an MMCI mine stake, subject to the litigation outcome.

544860|2026-06.headline: Ardee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore, but EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore and margin fell to 10%.
544860|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore on 17,645 MT sales volume, with PAT up 6% YoY to Rs 19.9 crore. EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore, with margin at 10% versus about 13% in FY26, attributed to higher domestic raw material and petroleum input costs and freight/supply-chain disruption linked to geopolitical issues. Installed capacity rose 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA effective 29 May 2026 via a brownfield debottlenecking of the existing refining unit (about Rs 15 crore capex). Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 10-20%, volume-driven, and EBITDA margin around 10%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 and Rs 36,000 in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,167.7 crore / Rs 147.1 crore / Rs 84.7 crore
Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore (created 14 Aug); working capital limits almost unutilised; about Rs 150 crore FDR

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: 61.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says domestic scrap procurement is costlier than imports and faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 38.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue; exports rose from about Rs 81.6 crore in FY24 to Rs 465 crore in FY26 across eight countries. Management says export margins are better after incentives and drawbacks, with working capital the same.

segments.name: Lead alloys
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-35% per management; ramp-up is slow due to OEM approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 10-20%, entirely volume-driven with no metal price contribution; volume target about 85,000 tons vs about 70,000 tons in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 10% for the full year given the geopolitical situation; management said higher margins are possible only if conditions improve.
Plant utilisation expected to be below the 70-75% optimum range in FY27, with the full 70-75% level now expected to spill into FY28.
Working capital guided at 90-100 days; gross working capital requirement for FY27 above Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 220 crore funded from IPO proceeds.
Management expects return ratios to fall after the equity raise but to stay above 20% in coming years.
EBITDA per ton of about Rs 19,000 seen as fair if raw material costs stay at current levels; management expects a recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 if the market normalises.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity raised 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA from 104,025 MTPA, effective 29 May 2026, via brownfield debottlenecking of refining capacity in the existing Naidupeta plant at about Rs 15 crore.
Management says the added capacity is a buffer and does not expect it to be fully used in FY27; current utilisation is about 65%.
Acquired and handed over a 5.56-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, for medium- to long-term expansion.
No further expansion planned for now; exploring a mix of lead and other non-ferrous recycling for the new plant.
Company operates from a single facility in Andhra Pradesh and focuses on the southern market, exports, and Southeast Asia.
demand_pricing: Sales volume rose 13.6% YoY to 17,645 MT; management says the Q1 volume decline sequentially from Q4 was due to war-related import disruptions and deliberately measured procurement.
Realisation of about Rs 2,09,000 per MT on finished goods; management expects FY27 realisation to be broadly in line with Q1 but subject to metal prices.

Procurement: Middle East route blockages and higher trade and freight costs; the company is sourcing domestically via corporate tie-ups and auctions. Payment is made when goods arrive at Chennai port.
Customer concentration: largest customer down from about 70% to about 40% of revenue; top four to five customers account for most business.
Management says the LME listing of the Ardee 99.97 brand has generated more export inquiries; no specific new export orders were quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes fall sequentially, and what is the revenue potential of the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited war-related import disruption and deliberately measured procurement. The new capacity is the same facility's debottlenecking, with optimum utilisation at 70-75%; the company is currently at about 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-20% top-line guidance conservative and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given trade and import/export uncertainty and would be happy to outperform; no FY28 numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 inventory build temporary and what is the cash impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was temporary and driven by OEM delivery timing at quarter-end; it varies quarter to quarter by customer need, and no cash impact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 220 crore IPO working-capital allocation be used and what cash conversion cycle is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly for scrap buying from new sources and export credit to new customers. Working capital days are about 95 (110 earlier), expected to stay at 90-100 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and what is the post-IPO position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore taken on 14 August, working capital limit utilisation almost nil, and about Rs 150 crore in FDRs.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided for around 10% given geopolitical uncertainty, rather than the FY26 level of about 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation and implied FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 realisation was about Rs 2,09,000 per MT; an analyst's implied FY27 revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore at 84,000 tons was described by management as a reasonable number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross profit and EBITDA per ton fall versus Q4 and Q1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs for domestically procured raw material and petroleum-based inputs, plus freight and supply-chain disruption; management expects a recovery if the market improves.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.
544921|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a recovery-led quarter: total recoveries rose 151% to INR1,066 crores and standalone PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores, driven by a large corporate resolution. Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

financial_highlights.change: +151% vs INR425 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Write-back of security receipts, fees and expenses written off earlier

financial_highlights.change: +107% YoY; PAT margin about 52% of total income
From INR1,200 crores in March 2026; debt-equity 0.34x
About INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26
Relates to receivables expected to be realised near term
Per analyst question; not stated by management

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: About 68% of AUM and a corporate book of about INR13,000 crores; recoveries are chunky and event-driven, which drove the Q1 spike.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: About 24% of AUM; over 3.29 million retail borrowers on the platform, with steady granular repayments. Retail and SME rose from about 21% to 31% of AUM since March 2024.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: About 8% of AUM; management treats SME as an independent business it wants to grow.

segments.name: Collection as a service
segments.commentary: Still at infrastructure-build and proof-of-concept stage with own assets and a few NBFCs; no revenue or pipeline numbers given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical AUM or acquisition guidance; management expects AUM to rise while acquisitions are matched by equal resolutions, with resolutions of about 20-25% of opening AUM each year.
Management expects acquisitions to rise through Q2 and Q3, with pipelines described as strong, and to draw down more borrowings and marginally increase leverage.
Write-backs of previously written-off assets are expected to decline over time; maximum write-offs over the next three years are cumulatively under INR100 crores.
Management expects its fee income momentum to be maintained, though it said the Q1 write-back was not a full-year trend.
capex_capacity: Borrowings were reduced to INR1,100 crores in Q1 to fund acquisitions later in the year; cash and bank balances INR252 crores, which management says gives ample capacity to fund acquisitions.

Own investment in AUM was about INR4,200 crores (about 22% of AUM) as of June; the FY26 average investment ratio was about 33% (INR2,000 crores on INR6,000 crores acquired), and Q1 FY27 is running at about 40%.
Mandatory minimum SR investment is 15%; co-investor deals allow as low as 2.5%.
Last-mile funding of up to 25% of acquired loan value is available to support turnarounds.
demand_pricing: Industry stress (banks and NBFCs, including SMA, NPA and written-off) is about INR23 lakh crores per management, growing about INR1 lakh crore a year; ARCs participate in roughly 10%.
Special mention accounts were about 30% of new ARC acquisitions in FY25, up from about 14% in FY24 (CRISIL data cited by management).
Acquisition cost held at 26-27% of dues every year; Arcil's AUM is about 14% of the INR1.4 lakh crore dues under management.
Arcil's share of industry AUM rose from 11% to 15% over two years; share of new acquisitions was 17% in FY26 on about INR6,000 crores acquired.
Management attributed improved industry recovery rates (cited as moving from about 35% to about 85%) to a stronger economy and real estate recovery.

540073|2026-06.headline: BLS International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to INR 891 crores, a record, with EBITDA of INR 252 crores (28.3% margin) and PAT of INR 202 crores.
540073|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter for BLS on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with growth coming from both Visa & Consular and Digital Services. Visa application volumes were flat at 11.3 lakh, and growth came from net revenue per application rising 11% to INR 3,521. Digital Services grew 32% to INR 330 crores, with EBITDA up 45% to INR 27 crores. Net cash stood at INR 1,617 crores. Management was firm on a 15-20% organic growth target over five years, but gave no clear answer on buybacks or on the return from past acquisitions.

financial_highlights.change: +24% YoY from INR 204 crores; margin 28.3%, broadly stable
vs 8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26; management expects ~12% for FY27
vs INR 25 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR 23 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Visa & Consular Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 560 crores (+22% from INR 461 crores), EBITDA INR 226 crores (+22%), margin 40.3%. Core Visa applications 11.3 lakh, broadly flat YoY; net revenue per application INR 3,521 vs INR 3,167 (+11%).

segments.name: Digital Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 330 crores (+32% from INR 250 crores), EBITDA INR 27 crores (+45% from INR 18 crores), margin 8.2% vs 7.2%. Growth led by business correspondent (BC) and loan distribution. BC GTV above INR 29,500 crores vs INR 26,200 crores a year ago.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Visa & Consular about 63% of consolidated revenue (vs ~65%); Digital about 37% (vs ~35%). Visa & Consular still contributes close to 90% of consolidated EBITDA.

segments.name: Acquired and new businesses (Q1 revenue)
segments.commentary: iDATA INR 72.5 crores, Aadifidelis INR 225 crores, Citizenship Invest INR 17.5 crores (vs INR 11 crores a year ago), Aadhaar INR 17.5 crores, UK hotel INR 16 crores (vs INR 2.5 crores). Management described the Citizenship growth as partly driven by Middle East NRI demand.

guidance_outlook: Organic growth target of 15-20% a year over the next five years on the increased base; management said Q1 (25% revenue, ~24% EBITDA growth) was ahead of this.
Management intends to hold Visa margin near 40% and Digital margin around 8%; it did not give a separate consolidated margin guidance beyond the 28.3% achieved.
Aadhaar contract: full revenue expected from Q4 FY27 once the three-phase investment completes next quarter; expected lifetime revenue about INR 2,500 crores over six years at a 10-15% EBITDA margin.
Visa & Consular growth expected at 12-15% (travel industry 7-8% CAGR plus about 5% from pricing and mix), and later described as 10-15%.
Effective tax rate expected to close FY27 at about 12%. D&A may rise slightly next quarter before stabilising.
capex_capacity: Aadhaar project: about INR 75 crores invested so far against a total of about INR 125 crores; phase 2 in final stages and full investment expected to finish next quarter.
Visa & Consular platform: Belarus visa applications launched in Mumbai; AI-powered 24/7 bot rolled out across missions.
Atyati Technologies acquisition completed (about INR 138 crores). It had about INR 275 crores revenue and INR 20-21 crores EBITDA last year, with BC and bank/NBFC software verticals.
Management said about INR 1,100 crores was invested in acquisitions last year and that M&A remains the first use of cash while the pipeline is active.
demand_pricing: Visa application volumes were flat YoY at 11.3 lakh; management attributed this to the war affecting Q1 and said growth came from other contracts. It said the war is now over and volumes are recovering, but declined to give current-quarter numbers.

Net revenue per application growth of 11% came from newer contract pricing and mix. Management said the increase over three years reflects the shift from partner-run to self-run offices, and that per-application revenue is now stabilising.
Management said it has won contracts with Belarus, Portugal, Slovakia and Italy governments, with multiple tenders at different stages in the pipeline over the next 8-12 months or more.

Digital: West Bengal government contract for beneficiary verification and card approval under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and Ayushman Vay Vandana; Tamil Nadu Grama Bank mandate; Coverfox partnership covering 1.58 lakh BLS touchpoints.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated between M&A, core growth and shareholder returns, and what return threshold applies?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Amit Sudhakar listed organic expansion first, then M&A that improves ROI, then dividends. He said all M&A to date earns returns of 17-20%, which is the baseline. Management did not quantify the economic value created by past acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Will buybacks be considered given INR 1,617 crores net cash and reserves of about INR 2,500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said M&A is the first priority, that buybacks and higher dividends are on the agenda, and that the Board will decide. It said a buyback is not currently under consideration but may be discussed at the next Board meeting.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue per application growth slow over the past year, and what revenue is at risk from contracts ending within 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the step-up over three years came from moving to self-run operations, and that per-application revenue is now stabilising. It said some contracts are ending but new wins offset them, and it still expects 10-15% Visa growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate and D&A rise, and how long before Aadhaar revenue arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate depends on the country profit mix; FY27 is expected near 12%. D&A rose mainly from Aadhaar investment under lease accounting. Full Aadhaar revenue is expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Citizenship Invest revenue growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue rose to about INR 17.5 crores from INR 11 crores. Management attributed this to Middle East NRIs seeking permanent residency or citizenship in Europe and elsewhere, and said it should be maintainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Visa gross profit per application fall as a share of revenue sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reconcile the analyst's calculation (Visa gross profit about INR 400 crores, around 51%) and said it would review the working offline.

543936|2026-06.headline: Senco Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY and EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% (INR213 crores) on gold-price, discounting and one-off cost effects.
543936|2026-06.overview:
Senco crossed INR3,000 crores of sales in a single quarter, with consolidated revenue up about 67% YoY and retail up 50%, same-store sales growth around 39%. April was the strong month (about INR1,500-1,600 crores), while May and June moderated to roughly INR500-600 crores a month amid West Bengal elections, Adhik Maas and heat wave. Reported EBITDA was INR213 crores at 7.0% margin and consolidated PAT INR101 crores at 3.3%, with margin pressure from other expenses (about INR195 crores vs about INR80 crores a year earlier), a gold-price decline, discounting and GML-related finance cost. Management retained FY27 guidance of 20%+ value growth and a 7.5%-7.8% sustainable operational EBITDA margin, and said July and August are running about 25% YoY ahead.</overview>

segments.name: Retail / owned and franchise stores
segments.commentary: Retail sales +50% YoY, growth broad-based across zones including newly launched Central region (7 stores) and Delhi NCR; 3 COCO and 4 franchise stores added plus 1 Sennes showroom in Q1.

segments.name: Diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Value +43% YoY and volume +18%, with management flagging stud-ratio improvement as a margin lever.

segments.name: Factory subsidiary
segments.commentary: Captive design and jewellery supply hub performing well, enabling about 100 designs per day; more than 150,000 designs a year.

segments.name: Sennes / Sennes Fashion / Dubai entity
segments.commentary: Start-up phase (lab-grown diamonds, perfume, leather bags); together weighed on consolidated PAT.

segments.name: Aham (men's titanium-gold-diamond range)
segments.commentary: Newly launched, priced INR20,000 to INR1 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guidance retained at 20%+, with 25%+ possible depending on the year; implies revenue above INR10,000 crores vs INR8,430 crores in FY26; revisit after Q3.
Sustainable operational EBITDA margin guided at 7.5%-7.8% for the full year, over a normalised 2-3 quarter period; management aims to move toward 8% via higher stud ratio.
PAT margin target of around 4.5%-5%; ROE and ROCE targeted toward the 20% range.
12-15 further store openings planned in the rest of FY27, majority franchise, focused on East and North India.
Q2 expected to be seasonally softer and a planning/inventory-build quarter; July and August running about 25% YoY growth and 8%-10% above May-June level.
Longer term: INR20,000 crores+ revenue and 300+ stores in 4-5 years (currently ~200 stores).
capex_capacity: Store network at around 200 stores; 12-15 more openings planned for the rest of FY27, mainly franchise.
Inventory of roughly INR5,000 crores; inventory per store guided at 15-18 kg to 35-40 kg depending on market.
Management estimates INR8,000-9,000 crores of inventory may be needed to reach INR20,000 crores revenue.
Inventory to be built from September ahead of festive season, then sold through.
Factory subsidiary supports about 100 new designs per day.
demand_pricing: Old gold exchange accounted for ~43% of sales quantity on a blended basis, above 55% at owned stores.
Customers shifted to lightweight, design-led, lower-ticket jewellery (9-carat, 14-carat, lightweight ranges), with grammage down ~1% on a 24-carat-equivalent basis.
Discounting and schemes intensified after the customs-duty increase; management cites competitive intensity as a margin drag.
Monthly mix: April ~55% of quarterly sales; May-June ~45% combined.
Hedging held at about 50% under Board policy; management intends to move toward 75%-80% as gold volatility eases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 20%+ after a strong Q1, and what is July-August trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has historically guided conservatively; July and August are running about 25% YoY and about 8%-10% above the May-June level, with a stronger build expected in October-November.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump to about INR195-229 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to marketing, store renovations in lean season, and customer offers and schemes; it said this run rate is quarter-specific and expected to subside.

qa_highlights.question: Why was GML availability constrained and finance cost up?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks restricted GML in March-April amid duty uncertainty and efforts to curb gold imports; company bought more gold locally and cut GML exposure, and says GML is now more available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.5%-7.8% EBITDA range operational and what is the hedge effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the range is operational, assuming a neutral gold-price environment and appropriate hedging; hedge at about 50% is intended to still deliver it.

qa_highlights.question: What was the customs-duty gain in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a gross gain of INR12-15 crores for the roughly 45 days of impact in Q1, partly offset by schemes; benefit expected over 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cash flow from operations expected to look negative and what is inventory strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will disclose CFO with H1; lower GML borrowing may make CFO appear negative on accounting basis. Inventory days ~152, reduced on store-by-store basis.

risks_watch: Margin volatility: Q1 margin at 7.0% vs guided 7.5%-7.8%; hedge ratio at ~50% leaves exposure to gold-price moves.
Other expenses (~INR195 crores) and discounting: management says quarter-specific, watch whether they normalise in Q2.
Inventory days at ~152 and capital efficiency; ROE/ROCE target of 20% depends on inventory productivity.
Cash flow from operations not yet disclosed; management expects it may be negative in Q1 on lower GML borrowing.
Sennes and Dubai subsidiaries weighing on consolidated PAT; 65-70% of business from Eastern India and West Bengal, concentration risk.
Discrepancy: business update reported 62% growth vs 67% in limited review numbers; management attributed gap to accounting adjustments.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.</overview>

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

517206|2026-06.headline: Lumax Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore, with EBITDA margin flat at 9.2% as commodity recoveries slipped into Q2.
517206|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore and EBITDA rose 34% to INR 113 crore, with margin held at 9.2%, in line with Q1 FY26. PAT including associates rose 41.2% to INR 51 crore, at a 4.2% margin. Management said OEM price recoveries for West Asia-driven commodity and electronics costs were not realised in Q1 (about 150 bps margin drag) and are expected in Q2. FY27 capex guidance was raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore on new order wins.

financial_highlights.change: +34% y-o-y (vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26); margin flat y-o-y
+41.2% y-o-y (vs INR 36 crore); margin +30 bps y-o-y

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles
segments.commentary: 64% of Q1 revenue. Tata Motors Tiago headlamps and VW Taigun rear lamps launched during the quarter.

segments.name: 2 and 3-Wheelers
segments.commentary: 31% of Q1 revenue. Won Suzuki Burgman Street front turn signal orders; management said 2-Wheeler growth at HMSI is expected to be significant.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles and others
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 revenue, unchanged y-o-y per management; won Force Motors Traveller 2 headlamp orders. The 'others' category grew 133% y-o-y, mainly Skoda/VW from Chakan 3.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Front lighting 68% of revenue, rear lighting 23%, other products 9%.

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: Maruti revenue +43% y-o-y and Tata Motors +68% y-o-y, both driven by new-model SOPs. TVS also grew; Hero share declined y-o-y per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 10.5-11% maintained; Q2 margin expected to be above 10%, with Q1 recoveries expected to be realised in Q2.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (full year), with growth slowing in H2 on high base after GST rationalisation.
Medium term: 15-20% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years, targeting about INR 9,000 crore+ revenue by FY30-31 from INR 4,500-5,000 crore base; EBITDA of about 13% in 3-4 years.
FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore (from INR 100-150 crore); maintenance capex INR 40-50 crore. FY28 capex indicated at INR 150-200 crore, but management called it premature.
FY27 mould sales targeted at INR 250-300 crore vs INR 180-185 crore in FY26, mostly in H2 (Q3/Q4) depending on SOP timelines.
Order book about INR 2,500 crore (about 90% LED); about 60% (roughly INR 1,500 crore) to enter SOP in FY28. Maruti wallet share expected to rise from under 30% to 35-40%.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore, driven by order wins over the last four months; FY26 capex was INR 410 crore.
Bengaluru plant expansion for Maruti and Toyota models is on track, with commissioning from Q4 FY27.
Brownfield projects underway at Sanand and Bawal to support new order wins at those locations.
Localisation: SMT already 100% localised; bare PCB localisation expected to rise from 40-50% to 70-80% and connectors from about 24% to 40-50% over 2-3 years; projected gain of 70-90 bps.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 production per SIAM: total 93.5 lakh units (+22% y-o-y); PV +17%, 2W +23%, 3W +39%, CV +15%.

Commodity recoveries: OEMs have not agreed to monthly amendments for most of the industry (only aluminium accepted); still quarterly or six-monthly. About 150 bps Q1 margin impact from unrealised recoveries.
Management expects competition intensity to rise as new players enter, but says top OEM concentration (4-5 players, 80-90% share) limits new entrants' share.
Content per vehicle for a passenger car currently INR 15,000-20,000 (outliers up to INR 30,000); management expects at least 50% growth over 4-5 years.
Honda HVAC business was about INR 18-20 crore annualised vs an estimated peak of INR 35-40 crore; Honda volumes weaker than expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin still below 10% despite LED penetration and localisation, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said OEMs have not agreed to monthly price amendments, so recoveries slipped; margin was hit about 150 bps in Q1. Realisations expected in Q2 could lift margin to about 10.5-11%, in line with FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are CV and tractor orders not yet visible, and how is the company positioned on EV content?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said CV lighting tech is standardised and the company is in talks on new platforms. Anmol Jain said CV is about 5% of revenue and grew 30-35% annualised. Lighting is powertrain-agnostic; EV content is higher in value per vehicle. 12% of order book is EV.

qa_highlights.question: Why did M&M revenue stay flat when the company holds a 40-50% wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said the XUV700 EV platform, where Lumax is not present, drove Mahindra volumes; management expects full-year growth in line with Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mould revenue outlook and FY27 capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mould sales are targeted at INR 250-300 crore (vs INR 180-185 crore), mostly in Q3/Q4. Maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crore; the rest goes to new business and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand 50-100 bps a year, and can 30% growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed about 100 bps expansion in FY27 (9.8% in FY26 to 10.5-11%). It said 30%+ quarterly growth will not persist due to high base; full-year growth guided at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the localisation plans and tooling sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said localisation is a priority but not all in-house; tooling remains imported, with tool localisation possibly by 2030. China sourcing continues for cost, with a new China office set up.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
544144|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.</overview>

Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.

Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
544495|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.</overview>

530521|2026-06.headline: Virat plans Rs 95 crore primary investment in Brahm Lifestyle for 70.2% stake, pivoting toward lifestyle brands; socks contract sales ~6 million pairs.
530521|2026-06.overview: The investor call, hosted by the Brahm Group (promoter, ~75% owner), centred on a strategic pivot rather than Q1 FY27 operating results. Management said Virat will be renamed Brahm Virat Industries Corporation Limited (pending ROC approval) and will invest Rs 95 crore via preferential allotment for a 70.2% controlling stake in Brahm Lifestyle Products Private Limited. Virat's core business is contract manufacturing of socks (9 million pairs capacity, 145 machines), with a nascent branded push (Lord Walker). No audited Q1 FY27 financials, margins or segment numbers were presented; forward figures were management projections and were explicitly labelled forward-looking.

financial_highlights.metric: Proposed investment in Brahm Lifestyle Products Pvt Ltd
Expected cash in Brahm Lifestyle post-deal (incl. existing cash)
Average selling price per sock pair (INR)
financial_highlights.change: from Rs 52.93 in Mar 2026 and Rs 42.60 in Mar 2025; ~47% over two years

segments.name: Socks (contract manufacturing and branded)
segments.commentary: Management cited ~6-6.5 million pairs contract volume at ~Rs 60 per pair (~Rs 36 crore revenue, 10-12% operating margin); branded target of 2 million pairs in two years at Rs 200-250 per pair.

segments.name: Handbags (Ahikoza, via Brahm Lifestyle)
segments.commentary: About 600 bags sold this year at ~$1,200 retail; target of 2,000 bags at ~$2,000 in two years (~$2 million sales).

segments.commentary: Run-rate ~Rs 1 crore per month; management targets ~Rs 100 million FY-end sales at ~10% EBITDA margin; app launch mid-September.

segments.name: Skill by Brahm (fitness/wellness, Pune)
segments.commentary: Targeting Rs 5 crore sales in first year via memberships; online launch planned November in Pune.

segments.name: Restaurant and spas (Pune, Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Pune Club restaurant breaking even; three spas in Bengaluru operated under Unwind by Brahm. Described as small-scale with no significant capital need.

guidance_outlook: Socks: branded plus contract revenue of ~Rs 100 crore and EBITDA of Rs 20-40 crore in two years (management's own projection).
Brahm Lifestyle: management said it would be disappointed if Rs 400-500 crore sales with ~20% EBITDA were not reached in three to four years; cited a Rs 1,000-3,000 crore market cap as achievable.
Lord Walker: target of ~1 million pairs in calendar 2027, with 5-year plan toward a global lifestyle brand.
Management aims for a 50-60% CAGR on deployed capital; this was described as a personal track record, not a guarantee.
Inorganic acquisitions: 5-6 LOIs under NDA, to be brought to the Virat board when appropriate; no specifics disclosed.
capex_capacity: Capacity: 9 million pairs per year from 145 machines (up from 33 machines and 2 million pairs in 1995); current output ~6 million pairs.
Spare capacity cited as the rationale for branded and DTC expansion, with contract manufacturers in the Gujarat ecosystem available for support.
Brahm Fresh app launch mid-September; Skill by Brahm online in Pune in November.
Handbag production: leather sourced from Indonesia, assembly in India; apparel tie-ups in Kolkata, Coimbatore and Bengaluru.
No explicit Virat capex figure or commissioning timeline was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Virat exports to UK and Switzerland; UK FTA operational from 15 July 2026 removes 11% import duty on Indian socks, per management.
Customers include John Lewis, Waitrose, Barbour, FootAsylum, Umbro, Castore, Sudu, Kukri, Migros (~300 stores) and Galaxus (Switzerland).
Lord Walker launched domestically on Amazon, Myntra, Nykaa, Instamart and Blinkit; first year is focused on brand awareness.
Management said it has zero sales so far in North America, Far East and Middle East, and named these as future targets.
Competition: management referenced China and Turkey sock production and cotton prices, without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is each business and how will management bandwidth be handled across multiple businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the socks business is mature and cash generative. Other businesses were described as self-sufficient, with funding and teams in place and shared Brahm platform services for technology, HR and admin.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the Rs 95 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no major need for money in socks or handbags. Funds are earmarked for Skill by Brahm, possible acquisitions (5-6 LOIs under NDA), international distribution and marketing, with no specific allocation given.

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide revenue, EBITDA or ROCE guidance for 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave two-year socks projections (Rs 100 crore revenue, Rs 20-40 crore EBITDA) and a handbag target (~$2 million sales), and said a Rs 3,000 crore market cap was achievable. Caveated as forward-looking.

qa_highlights.question: Will Virat expand into products beyond socks, such as gloves or knitwear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said apparel for men, women and kids is planned under Lord Walker, including undergarments, t-shirts and kidswear (Little Walker), with knitwear for kids a future option. Emphasis remains on getting socks right first.

risks_watch: Related-party style transaction: Rs 95 crore primary raise into a promoter-linked entity, with ambiguity on valuation, pricing and minority-shareholder protection (management said near book value).
Heavy reliance on promoter's unaudited forward projections across socks, handbags, fresh seafood and wellness; no historical audited financials for the new verticals were presented.
Management bandwidth across many new businesses, with the group management focus on the lifestyle platform.
Execution milestones to track: ROC approval of name change, Brahm Fresh app launch in mid-September, Skill by Brahm launch in November, Lord Walker volumes against 1 million pairs in CY2027.
Regulatory check on the NSE trading permission; the company clarified it is not yet listed on NSE, only permitted to trade.
530521|2026-06.management_tone: Highly promotional and forward-looking, with heavy use of aspirational language ("billion dollar opportunity", "most valuable corporation"). Hard numbers were limited to socks pricing and existing sales; most growth claims were unquantified or hypothetical and were hedged as forward-looking statements.
key_quotes: So right now we are selling 6 million.
And as of the latest figures published, that is on June 30th for the first quarter, our price has gone up further to 63 rupees per pair.
We are 75% owner, but we are sharing this platform with every other minority shareholder in the company.

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.</overview>

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)
Loss per order ₹(346) vs ₹(447) in Q4
1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.
capex_capacity: InstaHelp: management said the company is investing aggressively in micro-market density, with the investment level still under evaluation.
Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

544515|2026-09.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
544515|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.

540078|2026-06.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q1 FY27 net profit rose 566% YoY to INR 873.83 lakhs on a 16.29% EBITDA margin, with total income up 11.62%.
540078|2026-06.overview:
Total income reached INR 9,532.78 lakhs (+11.62% YoY) and EBITDA INR 1,549.48 lakhs (+209.50% YoY), with margin expanding to 16.29% from 5.87%. Net profit of INR 873.83 lakhs was up sequentially from INR 771.73 lakhs in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the gain to operating efficiency and product mix, and announced a proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition on top of 32,450 MTPA. Management said it now prioritises bottom line over top line, and that the INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY28 remains in place.</overview>

segments.name: Packaging (containers, paint containers, jerry cans, caps and closures)
segments.commentary: Management says packaging is about 80% of business and will remain the largest contributor; the 80:20 split with furniture/other parts is expected to hold to INR 1,000 crores. Containers described as in strong demand.

segments.name: Healthcare furniture (Furnastra brand) and other parts
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 19.8% of the business per management, including furniture parts and other parts. Management expects faster growth here than in containers, but gave no target mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sequential revenue growth of roughly the same rate each quarter, 'almost same', while focusing more on bottom line.
Sustainable EBITDA margin described as 10-13% on average; management said double-digit EBITDA will remain, with quarterly variation from product mix.
INR 1,000 crore annual revenue target by FY28 reiterated; management says it is in line with the capacity expansion.
IBC (intermediate bulk container) project expected to start commercial production around Q3 FY27; investment amount not yet disclosed.
Proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition: management stated capex of approximately INR 2 crore and that the capacity is already online. Revenue contribution to be announced soon.
Management expects utilisation to stay around 64-65%, or about 70% as a healthier level.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity above 32,450 MTPA across four facilities, with 53 blow moulding and 22 injection moulding machines.
Proposed addition of 3,550 MTPA, to be used across all three verticals (containers, furniture parts and others).

Capex for the 3,550 MTPA addition stated as approximately INR 2 crore (the transcript figure, which looks low for this capacity and should be verified); funding is a mix of internal accruals and debt. Management said this depends on machinery source.
Lead time from machinery order to commercial operation is about 6-9 months, per management.
Utilisation was 60-64% through FY26; seasonal peaks reach about 85%.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strong across all verticals, with containers in particular high demand.

Raw material prices rising on geopolitical and crude-linked pressures; management says suppliers have raised prices and customers have accepted pass-through, with local sourcing used since imports were stopped years ago.
Raw material pass-through to customers is generally on a one-month lag; specialised cases are negotiated individually.
Pricing is a cost-plus markup on raw material; management said other value-add and efficiency gains drive the margin, not the pass-through alone.

Company is rationalising SKUs (around 500) by dropping low-margin products; added more than 30 customers in Q1 and more than 150 in the last year (the two figures were stated inconsistently on the call; the 150 figure is probably cumulative for the year).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion to about 16%, and is it sustainable given raw material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited innovation, manufacturing efficiency and product mix, and said raw material increases are passed to customers. It later said sustainable margins are 10-13%, with some quarters higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the 3,500 MTPA expansion and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately INR 2 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt, and that the capacity is already online.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly the same sequential growth each quarter, while focusing more on profit than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does a 16% EBITDA margin represent a new normal, and how does the pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% is the normal range and double-digit margins will remain, with pass-through about one month in arrears.

qa_highlights.question: Why add capacity when utilisation is only 64%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery lead time plus 6-9 months of set-up requires planning ahead; utilisation is seasonal, reaching about 85% at peak.

qa_highlights.question: Which businesses will drive the INR 1,000 crore target, and what is the IBC project?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging remains about 80% and the mix is expected to stay around 80:20. IBC commercial production is expected around Q3, on new machinery with the cost not yet disclosed.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation linked to geopolitical and crude-price moves; pass-through is one month in arrears, which can squeeze margins during rapid price rises.
Margin sustainability: Q1's 16.29% is well above the 10-12% range management described as normal, and EBITDA has been volatile quarter to quarter.
The FY28 INR 1,000 crore target needs a sharp step-up. Quarterly revenue is about INR 95 crore, so the run rate needs to reach roughly INR 120-130 crore per quarter or more.
Capex disclosure is thin: the INR 2 crore figure for 3,550 MTPA looks low, and the IBC project cost and the revenue from new capacity are both still undisclosed.
Low export share (about 2%) and an unquantified international healthcare contract; ramp-up timing unclear.
Governance: the warrant allottee (Rikhav Securities) was questioned; management said it was a small investor with no existing relationship, and the warrant proceeds are for working capital.
Utilisation of 64% against a 3,550 MTPA addition; management expects utilisation to remain about 64-65%.
540078|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and demand, but often vague or deflective on numbers: capex, the IBC investment, the revenue from new capacity and the Furnastra international timeline were all left for later disclosure. Management repeatedly pointed to the bottom line over top-line growth. Audio problems on the call also made several questions hard to hear.
key_quotes: So it's approximately INR 2 crores.
But double-digit EBITDA will remain the same for sure.

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.
544572|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 9,708 million, up 18.3% YoY (on management's constructed comparison) and 2.6% QoQ. PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Down QoQ due to forex and demerger one-offs
Rupee depreciation, linked to Middle East war; on imports mainly from Europe
Incremental one-time cost in the quarter
Operating cash flow hit by name-change and land-transfer charges

segments.name: General machinery (pumps, motors, gears)
segments.commentary: Management called general machinery the strongest segment this quarter and said its share of business has grown.

segments.name: Wind and heavy industry
segments.commentary: Named as other strong performers in the quarter; rail described as solid.

segments.name: Distribution channel
segments.commentary: Highest-margin channel; management cited high double-digit margins versus high single-digit for OE.

segments.name: OE channel
segments.commentary: About 54% of revenue; lower margin but supports aftermarket share growth.

segments.name: Solutions (services, remanufacturing, condition monitoring)
segments.commentary: Around 6-7% of India business, below 10%; being scaled with added technology and direct sales staff.

guidance_outlook: Long-term PBT margin guidance of 14-16%, described as conservative; aspiration 17-19%, with near-term pressure from investments through 2028.
Management expects demerger IT costs to continue for two more quarters, tapering by end-2026 and ceasing around Q4/Q1 FY28.
Management said ~12% is a fair margin on current performance excluding the one-offs; manufacturing efficiency could add a couple of percentage points more.
Aspiration to double the India Industrial business in about five years, with no firm timeline committed.
Pune plant (capex INR 850-950 crore; 900-950 in one remark) expected to start production in 2028, with payback of 5-7 years including channel transfers and new third-party and SKF group channels.
Sujeeth Pai to succeed Mukund Vasudevan as MD effective 1 September 2026.
capex_capacity: New Pune factory is the key constraint: majority of new channel installations are tied to the factory coming online in 2028; capacity is currently constrained by space, not demand.
New tapered roller bearing (TRB) line in Pune adds 3 million units annually, serving agriculture, gearbox and aftermarket; supports exports too.
One additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027 despite capacity constraints.
Plan to add around 15-20 lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new; most depend on the new factory.
Capex plan quoted as INR 900-950 crore in prepared remarks and INR 850-900 crore in later Q&A; figures are inconsistent in the transcript.
demand_pricing: Order book reported as growing, with sustained growth over the last few quarters.
INR 140 crore gearbox-manufacturer order (wind-related, one-year, spread through the year) and INR 35 crore agricultural tractor OEM contract.
Innovation traction strongest in general machinery (gearboxes, motors, pumps); agriculture uses customised offerings.
Data center and humanoid opportunities are early-stage; current data center traction is in basic pumps, with no material revenue yet.
Management said the Indian Automotive sales share is being reduced to improve mix.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14-16% is the conservative long-term path and 17-19% the aspiration; near-term margins dip due to investments. CFO quantified FX plus demerger one-offs at about 3% of margin, implying ~12% underlying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are one-time or one-year contracts, typically extending one to two years. Some services and condition-monitoring contracts are longer-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will one-off costs end, and is 12% margin achievable now?
qa_highlights.answer: The IT cost should taper through end-2026 and stop around Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28. CFO said ~12% is a fair current margin, with further gains from efficiency and the Pune plant.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company merge with the SKF automotive or other group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no active plans; it wants the demerger to stabilise first but continuously evaluates options.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation linked to Middle East tensions raised import costs on European-sourced products; margin impact depends on INR movement.
Demerger one-offs: IT separation costs of about INR 150 million per quarter expected for two more quarters; watch for taper.
Capacity constraint until the 2028 Pune plant; growth above current capacity is limited, with only one added TRB channel by early 2027.
Execution risk on INR 850-950 crore capex and the 5-7 year payback; management figures varied across the call.
Management transition: Sujeeth Pai takes over as MD on 1 September 2026.

544572|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, tailwinds and order momentum, but cautious on near-term margins, which management tied to FX and demerger costs. Answers on the margin path and capex figures were somewhat inconsistent, and the call had audio interruptions.
key_quotes: So our revenue from operations was INR9,708 million for the quarter.
We are trying to bring down the India Automotive sales to ensure our mix improves further.
