542812|2026-06.headline: GFL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 1,588 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR 219 crore on R32-led fluorochemicals growth.
542812|2026-06.overview: Chemical segment revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 1,574 crore with EBITDA up 29% to INR 458 crore and segment PAT up 33% to INR 261 crore. Fluorochemicals was the standout, with revenue up 52% YoY and 44% QoQ on R32 sales, and existing R32 capacity is already at peak utilisation. Battery materials remain pre-revenue to small (INR 20-30 crore per quarter cited by an analyst), with a ramp promised from Q4 FY27 and a significant step-up in FY28. The Oman battery project has been put on hold and its capex is being moved to India, and the approved sovereign funding for Oman will not transfer.

financial_highlights.change: +24% YoY; +39% QoQ; margin 27% vs 22% in Q4 FY26
+19% YoY; PAT margin 14% vs 7% in Q4 FY26
+29% YoY; +30% QoQ; margin 29% vs 26% in Q4 FY26
-43 days vs 192 days in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by mix shift to higher-value grades and new-age applications (semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen, batteries). Management guides 15-20% (later 17-20%) annual growth.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (R32 and refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 44% QoQ, mainly R32. Existing R32 capacity is fully utilised; a R32 expansion (about 20,000 t total capacity cited by an analyst) is due in Q2 FY27. R134A is on track for commissioning in FY27.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY and 1% QoQ, primarily on better realisations; described as steady.

segments.name: Battery materials
segments.commentary: LiPF6 has nearly completed qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF qualification is close; LFP and cathode active material revenue expected toward end-FY27. Current revenue is small, with dispatches on CIF terms recognised in the next quarter.

guidance_outlook: R32 capacity expansion to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; management expects full utilisation of the incremental R32 capacity in calendar 2027.
R134A capacity to be commissioned in FY27 (management said it is targeting earlier than year-end); capacity size not yet disclosed.
Battery materials: management says it is on track for a 3-digit INR crore quarterly revenue in Q4 FY27, with significant ramp-up in FY28 and full potential from FY28 onwards.
Gross block of INR 836 crore expected to rise to about INR 1,200 crore by end-FY27 as CWIP is capitalised.
FY27 capex plan held at about INR 2,300 crore in EV/battery and about INR 800 crore in chemicals; total announced plan of INR 6,000 crore over the next two years.
AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid) capacity to come in phases, first set by end-FY27 or Q3, mainly for captive use.
capex_capacity: R32 capacity expansion due Q2 FY27; existing R32 capacity at peak utilisation.
R134A brownfield project at an existing refrigerant site, to be commissioned in FY27; TCE feedstock to be imported, not backward integrated.

Oman battery materials project (about USD 216 million capex) put on hold; capex being redirected to India. Sovereign funding of about INR 1,200 crore approved for Oman will not be available for India.
Land for battery expansion available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) site; a second Dahej site is being added for FY27-end/FY28.
Fluoropolymer debottlenecking is done continuously, roughly every second quarter; new-age fluoropolymer capex sized in the previous quarter at about INR 250 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer price increases were marginal and pass-through of input cost increases (methanol, sulfur, oil-linked inputs since March 2026); management said formula-based contracts protect margins.
R32 is sold globally: about 40-50% under long-term contracts, remainder spot or contract-to-contract. Domestic and export pricing described as 'very close'.
Management said 3M's exit is past and it has taken the impact; AGC's announced UK facility shutdown has begun generating customer enquiries, with traction expected in a quarter or two.
Domestic BESS demand projected at 220-250 GWh by 2030 (versus earlier global ~1,800 GWh view).

qa_highlights.question: Have Chinese peers' fluoropolymer price increases been passed on by GFL, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said only a marginal increase was taken to recover input costs; growth is mainly from higher-value grades where competition with Chinese players is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth visible for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said it is absolutely visible; new fluoropolymer capacity is nearly fully utilised and further capacity will be added for semiconductor and battery applications, without disclosing specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Oman funding shortfall require a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said fundraising is ongoing and project-by-project; he does not see funding as a constraint for India capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How is fluoropolymer growth split between volume, price and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it precisely, saying growth is primarily mix (higher grades) plus volume from new fluoropolymers, not price.

qa_highlights.question: Will R32 capacity be fully utilised in calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said full utilisation is expected as capacity is commissioned, based on contracts and market understanding.

risks_watch: Oman project shift to India: loss of about INR 1,200 crore sovereign funding for that project and need for new funding of about INR 4,000 crore for battery chemicals.

R32 and R134A quota allocation under the formula (baseline and production over 2024-26) is not yet clear; management declined to say which new players will receive quota. An analyst also raised a question on consumption quota that management could not answer and will follow up on.
Battery materials revenue remains small; ramp is contingent on customer qualification (about 1.5 years stabilisation cited) and CIF-term revenue timing.
Standalone-to-consolidated revenue gap widening sequentially, which management attributed to CIF consignments booked in Germany and US subsidiaries.
Raw material cost volatility (sulfur, fluorspar, methanol) with only formula-based or marginal pass-through in fluoropolymers.

538734|2026-06.headline: Ceinsys Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) but EBITDA rose 27% to INR39 crore, margin 24.4%; order book INR990 crore.
538734|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was INR158 crore, up about 1% YoY, while EBITDA grew 27% to INR39 crore and margin expanded 505 bps to 24.4%. PAT was INR31 crore, a marginal decline, with PAT margin at 19.6% (down about 59 bps). Order inflow was INR143 crore against about INR157 crore executed, lifting the order book to INR990 crore from INR880 crore. Management withheld forward guidance throughout, citing policy, and focused on receivables recovery (JJM dues), a proposed AI cloud JV, and undeployed funds from the earlier fundraise.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR880 crore in Q4 FY26
broadly flat vs prior two quarters (162-164 days)

segments.name: Geospatial Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR94 crore, up 30% YoY; majority of the INR143 crore fresh order inflow came from geospatial enterprise solutions. Management said the mix shifts with project execution phase.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR63 crore, down about 25% YoY. Management aims to take this segment beyond 51% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Mobility (incl. international subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobility is now a division after the Allygrow merger; management reported improving order book and a top-line increase and margin improvement at the US subsidiary. Mobility is run-rate and not built into the order book.

guidance_outlook: No forward guidance given on revenue, margins or order inflow, citing company policy.
Management said growth should show in the next 2-3 quarters as orders with 3-6 month execution convert, and expects to sustain the growth trend seen over the last 2.5 years.
Management said it is on track with order book milestones and believes margins of around 22-23% are achievable, citing the 24.4% in Q1.
Management expects a better operating cash flow in FY27 than in FY26, without quantifying it.
Expected collection of about INR100 crore of JJM/IoT dues by end of Q3 FY27, with overdues expected to be cleared before 31 March 2027 per the Maharashtra GR.
Management expects one large national-program order (similar to the earlier INR350-400 crore L1 opportunities) possibly in FY27 Q4 or Q1 FY28, and said two L1 positions were pending award.
capex_capacity: Board approved up to INR25 crore investment in a 50:50 JV with AI Fabric USA for a sovereign AI cloud (GPU-as-a-service, model-as-a-service, AI services); first tranche INR5 crore for incorporation, second INR20 crore after due diligence.
JV incorporation expected in about 1-1.5 months; due diligence (technical, market) to take 3-4 months; business model to be frozen after that, with commercial activity indicated for FY28.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, aiming for vertical integration and margin-accretive deals; no deal announced. Acquisition multiples cited at 5-10x EBITDA.
Around INR230 crore raised earlier, of which INR130 crore received in March 2026 and INR100 crore in September 2024 (per management clarification).
demand_pricing: Order book INR990 crore; execution timelines range from 3 to 18 months, with some O&M contracts running 2-5 years. Weighted average execution 12-18 months.

Run-rate businesses (mobility, OEM products and services) sit outside the order book; about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue came from these. Management estimated 20-25% of FY26 revenue (of INR660 crore) was outside the order book.

Key Q1/recent wins: INR67 crore Madhya Pradesh PMAY manpower/LoI (over 3 years); INR17 crore Bhandara Municipal Council AMRUT 2.0 smart water meters (12 months); INR4 crore EKS InTec order; INR4 crore US subsidiary order; INR30 crore aggregate T Second purchase orders.

Management said JJM-related bids are being deprioritised in favour of transport (ITMS/ATMS), energy and other geospatial opportunities where budgets are funded. Transport positive developments expected in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline of the INR990 crore order book and the funnel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution spans 3 to 18 months, with O&M extending to 5 years; weighted average 12-18 months. Management said the funnel is strong and it will not give a numeric funnel figure or guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book roll-forward not match inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said run-rate businesses (about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue) are not booked in the order book. Net order book increased about INR110 crore after INR157 crore of execution. Reconciliation to be sent via the IR agency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI cloud JV economics and will Ceinsys be an EPC player?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV is 50:50 with AI Fabric USA, targeting defence and government sovereign cloud. Management said it intends to be an AI solutions company, not EPC, with contractors used for construction.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and JJM dues outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle at 164 days, flat. About INR100 crore of IoT/JJM dues expected by end of Q3 FY27, per the Maharashtra GR. Management said billing is being collected with no new build-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are large orders (INR350-400 crore L1 positions) likely by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR67 crore order already received. Two more in process, with one possibly in Q2. Management declined to commit on timing but said tender pipeline remains strong, and a large national program order could come in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a share buyback given idle funds and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said buybacks are funded from surplus operating cash, and the raised funds are for growth. Management said it would not invest only to deploy capital; acquisitions must preserve margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and when will it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the large unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore at 31 March, per the analyst) is mainly JJM; it is expected to be billed and reduce over the next 2 quarters as government funds come in.

Saicriti existing domestic critical care franchise about Rs 52-53 crore, currently produced via CMOs and to move to the new site.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration: 15% to 20% revenue growth and 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. Management said it expects to be in that range, after FY26 margins of about 15.6%.
Domestic lab growth expected to accelerate in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 as satellite labs and scanner-linked customers mature.
Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.
Margin expected to be maintained or improved through the year; gross margin should stay stable excluding scanner mix effects.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.
demand_pricing: Domestic lab growth slowed to about 12% y-o-y ex-scanners, which management attributed to scanner-led adoption maturing with a 6-month to 18-month gestation period.
Scanner penetration in the industry estimated at about 7% to 8%, with management saying the adoption curve (J-curve) has not yet clearly started.
Management said competition in aligners persists but declined to detail it, citing counter-strategies such as cross-selling.
Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 800 to 1,000 scanner deployments in FY27 and an 18% to 20% margin aspiration; it said Q1 margin supports that range.

risks_watch: Scanner mix drives quarterly gross margin swings; a strong scanner quarter dilutes margin.
Domestic lab growth at about 12% ex-scanners is below the company's 15% to 20% aspiration; Q2 to Q4 acceleration is unproven.
FX tailwind on international growth (USD from about INR85 to INR95) may reverse.
AI-led automation and ECL provisions raised other expenses to INR15.9 crore; cost pressure may persist this year.
Palghar land and facility transition: timing, capex size and rent savings not yet quantified.
Aligner competition, which management declined to detail.
Share price weakness after results drew analyst and retail investor questions; management had no explanation.

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
544407|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

Funding: debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x; about $3 billion of the $5 billion capex to come from debt, with about $2 billion equity net worth target and mandatory dilution to 25% of equity by 2 June 2028.
capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.
Liquid terminaling is charged per cbm capacity, not occupancy, so revenue is not driven by utilization.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.
531266|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR313.4 crores from INR282.4 crores, and PAT rose to INR48.7 crores from INR44.6 crores. Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from raw material inflation; Q1 margin down about 45 bps YoY.
Tractor market share: domestic tractor growth of 4.5% trails the industry; July volumes were lower YoY.
Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.
Possible capex for a new facility in about two years; capital deployment plans to be disclosed in 18-24 months.
Management has not given a FY27 outlook; next update expected in about one month.
531266|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term tractor and tiller growth targets, but cautious on near-term tractor volumes and on FY27 guidance, which it deferred pending monsoon clarity. Vague on capital deployment and inorganic plans.
key_quotes: And I have in last call also, in the last quarter I have said upwards of 15,000 numbers we will aim to reach, close to 20,000 numbers we will aim to reach in FY '30.
So giving an FY '27 outlook, I think it's a little too early.

532395|2026-06.headline: Axiscades Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹346 crore, but reported PAT loss of ₹14.8 crore; normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore.
532395|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. Reported EBITDA for the combined business was ₹27.9 crore, with one-offs of ₹13.1 crore (including ₹9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction and ₹3.5 crore hedge provision) and ₹21.81 crore divestment transaction cost below EBITDA. Management says normalized EBITDA was ₹41 crore (11.8% margin) and normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore. Guidance was reaffirmed: FY27 continuing revenue of ₹1,377 crore, EBITDA of ₹270 crore and PAT of about 50% of that, with acquisitions and divestment proceeds central to delivery.

financial_highlights.value: ₹183 crore (₹180.7 crore cited in Q&A segment overview)

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹20.9 crore PAT in Q1 FY26
mainly ADD Solutions (EBITDA -₹4.8 crore, PAT -₹6.7 crore)

segments.name: Defence (continuing)
segments.commentary: Record ₹125 crore revenue, up 112% YoY, with underlying EBITDA of ₹13 crore (up 15% YoY). Reported EBITDA ₹2.6 crore after ~₹9.6 crore one-time costs; management cites underlying 9.7% margin. Assured forecast visibility ₹4,557 crore after 8 wins since April.

segments.name: XiDA (ex-ESAI, US-headquartered)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹49.5 crore, up 63% YoY, at ~33% EBITDA margin (EBITDA ₹14.7 crore cited, ~30% in another remark). Added two large global technology customers via a business transfer.

segments.name: Aerospace manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹6.1 crore in Q1 with negative EBITDA; 30-member leadership team built ahead of acquisitions.

segments.name: Mistral
segments.commentary: Delivered ₹122 crore revenue at ~14.5% EBITDA margin while absorbing its own provisions.

segments.name: ADD Solutions (non-core, European)
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss ₹4.8 crore and PAT loss ₹6.7 crore; exit targeted by Q4 FY27 with a sale process that could realize over FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing operations revenue guidance reaffirmed at ₹1,377 crore on an annualized pro forma basis.
FY27 EBITDA target of ₹270 crore; PAT expected at roughly 50% of EBITDA (~₹135 crore), could be higher with lower interest after debt paydown.
Defence revenue expected to grow over 75% YoY in FY27 and over the following years; ESAI/XiDA expected to grow over 100% this year.
Aerospace manufacturing target: annualized run rate of ₹375 crore revenue and ₹84 crore EBITDA by Q4 FY27, with the platform aiming at ~₹1,000 crore by FY29.
Power 930 targets (FY30 PAT of ₹960 crore) stated as unchanged.
Deferred ~₹140-142 crore revenue: ~40% (over ₹60 crore) recovered in Q1; balance planned across Q2 and Q3.
capex_capacity: Akkodis divestment valued at US$237 million (~₹2,256 crore); Phase 1 targeted by Aug 31 with ~₹190 crore post-tax cash; Phase 2 by Nov 30 (management later said it is trying to pull it to about September) bringing ~₹525 crore cash.
Extraordinary gain of ~₹1,255 crore to be recognised on closing; ~₹200+ crore expected in Q2, the bulk in Q3 (or late Q2).
Aerospace services divestment expected to close in Q2 FY27; combined divestment proceeds ~₹920 crore cited.

Devanahalli AeroLand Complex (DAL) commissioned; Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Complex (DAC) construction ongoing on 20 acres; Missile Atmanirbhar Complex in Hyderabad groundbreaking early July, construction begun; Center for Advanced Manufacturing (240,000 sq ft, 20 acres) being planned.
PP&E rose ₹40 crore in one quarter for Power 930 ramp-up. CapEx to be matched to inflows, with a short-term bridge facility; actual drawdown not more than ₹100-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Defence assured forecast visibility rose to ₹4,557 crore after ~₹332 crore of new wins; management says it converts over ~3 years to FY30. Total pipeline cited at ~₹24,000 crore.

Wins include BrahMos and anti-tank missile onboard electronics (development-cum-production), helicopter ERP, Uttam radar antenna beam control, and a 30 kW laser directed energy weapon technology transfer.
LUH Maritime order visibility of ₹150-170 crore this year, stated as backed by confirmed orders.
MBDA test bench programme: about 5 test benches per year for 3 years; launcher maintenance expanding with a Rafale-linked order.
Aerospace: non-binding offer signed for an AS9100 precision manufacturer; FY27 revenue ~₹180 crore and EBITDA ~₹39 crore (22% margin) annualized, due diligence to complete in Q2.
BrahMos NG seeker: prototype in advanced stage; seeker business expected from next financial year (FY28).

540692|2026-06.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
540692|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR258 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.name: EU and UK
segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

segments.name: Ready-to-Eat (RTE)
segments.commentary: 16% of Q1 volume vs 15% last year; management targets at least 18-20% of volume in FY27, with RTE margin about USD 0.50/kg above RTC at minimum.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 production guided at around 12,000 MT, reiterated from the start of the year; management said the earlier 14,000 MT figure was not a company guidance.
Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.
Realisation in Q2 expected near INR900/kg, similar to Q1.
Margins expected to stay broadly stable, with partial pressure from higher ocean freight (more than doubled since Q4 FY26) and rising farm-gate prices.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 35-40% through FY27; next growth stage of 14,000-15,000 MT considered for FY28-29, not yet firmly committed.
Japan business initiated; Russia expected to start by end-Q2 or Q3 FY27; Australia still at audit stage.
capex_capacity: Volume capacity utilisation 38% in Q1 FY27 vs 39% in Q1 FY26; management targets sustained 35-40% through the year.
RTE capacity utilisation 16%, similar to prior year.
Labour shortage in April-May due to summer heat was resolved toward end-Q1 per management.
Raw material supply tightness expected to ease as new crop comes in.
No capex plans were announced in the call.
demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 because of war-led disruption; freight is the main risk to margin stability.
EU and UK volumes dropped to 25% of sales; watch whether shipments normalise in Q2 and whether testing or certification delays persist.
Full-year volume of about 12,000 MT requires roughly 9,000+ MT in the remaining three quarters versus 2,624 MT in Q1 FY27.
Capacity utilisation of 38% is well below the 14,000-15,000 MT next-stage ambition.
Possible US tariff refunds are unclear; the CVD review in December 2026 and the ADD determination in September 2026 could change pricing.
Farm-gate price increases and tight raw material supply could pressure costs.
540692|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and pricing, but cautious and hedged on volumes, freight and the timing of FTA benefits. Management avoided committing to FY28-29 volume figures and said it was too early to say.

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.</overview>

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers across consumables, wear parts, heavy engineering and trading; domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was 30%+ across the three segments, driven by a higher starting order book. Growth was mainly domestic because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

543328|2026-06.headline: Krsnaa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 25% from 27% on Rajasthan ramp-up costs.
543328|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, with like-to-like projects up about 12%. EBITDA was INR588 million (25% margin vs 27% in Q1 FY26) and PAT was INR166 million (7% margin). Management attributed margin compression to upfront fixed costs in Rajasthan (about 4,000 manpower onboarded ahead of revenue) and loss-making RPL retail, and guided to EBITDA-positive by Q2 FY27. Retail revenue rose 64% YoY to INR193 million, about 9% of group revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY vs INR1,930 million in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Rajasthan PPP revenue booked in quarter

financial_highlights.change: up sharply QoQ and YoY, attributed to Rajasthan, Manipur

segments.name: PPP institutional (pathology/radiology)
segments.commentary: Pathology is the larger contributor at about 59% of mix vs radiology 41%. Like-to-like centres grew about 12%; Rajasthan ramp-up and MRI go-lives are the main volume drivers.

segments.name: Rajasthan PPP
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR26 crore; management guides INR100-150 crore for FY27 (conservative), steady state of INR150-175 crore per quarter-run-rate commentary, below earlier INR200-250 crore aspiration.

segments.name: Retail (RPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR193 million, +64% YoY, ~9% of group revenue, 4,000+ touch points across 7 states. RPL at negative EBITDA in Q1 due to ground fleet and manpower costs; targeted EBITDA breakeven in Q2 FY27. Target retail contribution 10-15% of revenue this FY.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA positive by Q2 FY27 at group level; RPL also targeted EBITDA-positive by Q2.
Margins expected to return to double digits by year-end FY27 once Rajasthan operations mature.
Rajasthan revenue expected to roughly double in Q2; FY27 Rajasthan guidance INR100-150 crore, with earlier INR200-250 crore stated as aspiration.
Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh receivables expected to be collected by Q2 FY27; other projects on track.
Retail contribution targeted at 10-15% of revenue in FY27.
8 MRI centres in Maharashtra operationalised in Q1; balance of pipeline (17 MRI centres total) expected live by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan network substantially operational: 31 Mother labs, 62 hub labs and 1,228 collection centres at end of Q1 FY27.
8 MRI centres inaugurated in Maharashtra in Q1; remaining centres expected by end of Q3 FY27.
Himachal Pradesh CT project awarded: 34 CT scans statewide (22 new locations), ~10-year revenue visibility, predominantly cash-paying; revenue and investment details not yet disclosed.
Apulki Hospital, Pune, commenced operations with exclusive radiology and pathology rights, multi-decade partnership.
Warrant issue from promoter; proceeds earmarked for capex and acquisitions.
NABH/NABL/CAP/ACR accreditations at 124 after 12 new NABH additions in Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth attributed to new Rajasthan pathology and MRI centres plus like-to-like activation; value growth from new footfalls and repeat cycles in retail.
Management said margin drag in new projects stems from fixed costs ahead of utilisation, not pricing pressure in the core business.
CGHS rate revisions will not benefit current tenders (contractually at tender rates); only forthcoming tenders may benefit.
Retail customer acquisition, per management, is supported by quality accreditations and pricing; management denied doctor commission arrangements when questioned.
Management said RPL/retail mix shift is still early; retail described as 'just scratching the surface'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees to hospital rise to ~INR41 crore in the quarter, and how much Rajasthan revenue was booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees to hospital are revenue shares to local partners who run field operations in remote Rajasthan and Manipur; Rajasthan revenue was about INR26 crore, annualising to INR100-150 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200-250 crore Rajasthan FY27 guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative with clear visibility on INR100-150 crore; the higher figure remains an aspiration. Mitesh Dave indicated steady-state of about INR150-175 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is radiology revenue flat despite centre expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: MRI centres were operationalised in a staggered way over the last three months and are not at full utilisation; some radiology contracts ended their tenure. Radiology is improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How much is RPL dragging EBITDA, and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: RPL is EBITDA-negative in Q1 due to manpower and ground-fleet costs across 5 states (management said drag is nominal); breakeven targeted in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to improve QoQ as Rajasthan revenue doubles and RPL turns positive; margins to return to double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of receivables from Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: HP has allocated funds and money has started flowing; Karnataka receipts have begun but below expectations. Management expects collection by Q2, with HP, Karnataka and part of Maharashtra being the only delayed states.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Rajasthan revenue doubling in Q2 and RPL turning EBITDA-positive; slippage would extend the 25% margin trough.
Receivables delays from Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra government clients; collection timing guided to Q2.
Rajasthan FY27 revenue guidance cut from INR200-250 crore aspiration to INR100-150 crore; watch for further revision.
Fees to hospital (partner revenue share) run-rate of ~INR41 crore; cost sensitivity to partner economics.
Radiology growth has lagged; MRI utilisation and remaining 9 MRI go-lives by Q3 FY27 need to materialise.
Interim CFO in place; questions on retail customer acquisition and doctor relationships went partly unanswered.
543328|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, Rajasthan go-live and retail momentum, but defensive on margins and fees to hospital. Repeatedly framed margin dip as a timing issue, while guidance was softened to 'conservative' and several questions (CGHS, doctor partnerships, HP revenue) were deferred.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.

Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.

Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.

Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.

Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.

capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore; ~INR60 crore in CWIP expected to capitalise over the next two quarters.

Commodities: no forward hedging; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.
Inventory: in-house inventory mix roughly 70-75% AC and 25-30% non-AC; working capital days ~50-60, with inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions.

capex_capacity: Mumbai (Jogeshwari) workshop of about 50,000 sq ft inaugurated to serve Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep; BYD and Jeep part due to be completed in the next few months.
New Mahindra workshop in Hyderabad to start operations soon; existing Hyderabad Mahindra capacity already exhausted, per management.
BYD outlets in Pune became operational in July 2026; two new BYD outlets opened about 7-10 days before the call.
MG network to reach 17 outlets with an LOI received for an additional Ahmedabad showroom.
Management said workshop capacity will be added in bays rather than workshop count, and smaller workshops will be consolidated into larger sites.
demand_pricing: Management said OEM price hikes (Mercedes-Benz and others) raise absolute gross profit per car, not percentage margin, since Landmark receives a percentage of the hike.
Price contributed roughly 3% of the 22-23% top-line growth; the remainder (about 19%) was volume, per management ballpark.
Mercedes-Benz sold 9,786 units in H1 CY2026, up 9% YoY; Mercedes-Benz plans over 40 new global models from 2027.
MG: new SUV launching in August expected to boost volumes; new Majestor deliveries began last quarter.

Mahindra: strong momentum with more launches to come; BYD: supply to improve through the rest of the year, hybrids later this FY; Kia: Syros EV orders healthy, new Sorento in September; Honda: City facelift, ZRV and Alpha 0 EV later this year.
Management argued that competition such as Audi's share push expands the luxury market (about 50,000 units) rather than cannibalises it.
Premium and mass segments grew faster than luxury in recent months per Aryaman Thakker.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM price hikes improve Mercedes gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Thakker said price hikes raise absolute margin per car but not the percentage margin, as Landmark receives a percentage of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Could Audi's share push pressure Mercedes sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants expand the luxury market; the segment has hovered near 50,000 units and luxury penetration fell last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ChargeZone partnership add revenue, and at what economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ChargeZone runs about 16,000 charging points; Landmark onboards EV customers and earns a recurring revenue share with wallet credits for customers. Commercials were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin normalisation and Mercedes QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2-Q4 to be normalised, with an EBITDA margin around 1.5% on pro forma new car sales; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter and Mercedes grew strongly YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV aftersales margin versus ICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV margins are similar to the ~15% currently seen and are not expected to be lower; warranty costs (such as batteries) were excluded from the analysis.

qa_highlights.question: Will rental costs and cash conversion change?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease amortisation was about INR19 crore, with lease plus interest about INR27 crore; full-year rental cost expected around INR100-110 crore including Ind AS adjustments. EBITDA-to-CFO conversion was about 0.95x last year and expected to be similar.

512573|2026-06.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore despite 19% higher gross income, as feed raw-material costs squeezed margins.
512573|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore but PBT fell 15% QoQ to INR 157 crore and 37% YoY. The Feed division's gross income rose 27% YoY to INR 1,615 crore on 28,287 MT higher volume, yet PBT dropped 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices surged. Feed PBT margin fell to 7.06% from about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26. Shrimp Processing and Export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations and forex. Management took a roughly 10% feed price hike in June 2026 and said industry and government are working on a raw-material price mechanism.</overview>

On the Q2 question, management agreed that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the benefit of the price hike and any government intervention plays out.

Pet food capex estimated at about INR 175 crore in total, of which about INR 25 crore spent on land so far.
No feed capacity, utilisation or new feed plant commentary was given in the call.

Government of Andhra Pradesh has formed a committee with a big-four consultant to design a feed price mechanism linked to fish meal, soya bean meal and wheat flour; management said further hikes need affordability balance for farmers.

543950|2026-06.headline: Yatharth Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 3,927 mn with record EBITDA of INR 917 mn; consolidated EBITDA margin 23.3%.
543950|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR 3,927 mn (up 51% YoY, 15% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 917 mn, with PAT of INR 454 mn. Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra) contributed 27% of revenue. Faridabad Sector 20 reached EBITDA breakeven in about 9 months, while the group margin was diluted by new-hospital losses (adjusted margin ex-New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 was 28.1%). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of upwards of 24% EBITDA margin and ARPOB growth of 8-10%, and announced a maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value.</overview>

532827|2026-06.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
532827|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.4% in Q1 FY26; within planned 19–21% range
from 73 days at start of quarter
from 56 days at start of quarter

segments.name: Jockey innerwear and core range
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 5.7% was ahead of revenue growth of 7.9%-minus-mix, with lower-ASP accessories and socks gaining share due to scheme design. Schemes are now spread across quarters under the ARS model.

segments.name: Groove 3 (street fashion line)
segments.commentary: Launched in June 2026 across close to 500 exclusive brand stores; management said sell-through looks very good.

segments.name: Disney/Marvel character merchandise
segments.commentary: Go-to-market planned for end-June; a large portion of revenue expected in Q2.

segments.name: Speedo
segments.commentary: Multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1 from consolidation in swim offline; online is upwards of 35% of Speedo business. Combined Q4+Q1 view is about 950 stores.

guidance_outlook: Full-year volume growth target remains double-digit, phased across quarters; Q2–Q4 must show above-average volume growth to recover Q1 shortfall (analyst read-through of about 11–12% average).
Majority of the roughly three days of undelivered billing (seven days vs normal three to four) expected to be reported in Q2.
Full benefit of the mid-May price increase to flow through in Q2 under FIFO billing; difference between volume and value growth expected to widen from Q1 levels.
Annual EBITDA margin outlook retained at 19–21%.
Management intends to hold prices and drive volumes if margins stay within 19–21%; another price action possible if input costs re-escalate.
Marketing spend to remain at 4–5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Management is augmenting in-house manufacturing capacity and investing above plan, alongside outsourced garment supply.
Odisha and K.R. Pet manufacturing facilities are scaling up progressively.
Distribution: 115,871 multi-brand outlets, 1,640 exclusive brand stores, 930 large format stores.
E-commerce: two fulfilment centres (one South, one North); management prefers outright model over marketplace.
Consumer data platform (CDP) expected to go live by end-August 2026, subject to DPDP Act compliance.
DMS rollout: all distributors targeted on DMS by end-2026 or Q1 FY28 at latest.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 5.7% was driven by healthy consumer demand across EBOs, e-commerce and wider retail.
Price increases: about 2.5% in January 2026 (product-quality related, not input-cost linked) and about 2.2% weighted average in mid-May 2026 (input-cost linked).
Input cost inflation in cotton, nylon, synthetic fabrics and packaging peaked in May; prices eased by late June but remain volatile.
Management said the May price increase only partially offsets the raw material escalation.
Pricing is uniform across channels with no flash sales or markdowns; quick commerce is on an outright model.
Secondary growth was better than primary in Q1 because of undelivered billing; tertiary and EBO performance was better than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth below the double-digit target flagged in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was affected by a planned scheme phasing change under ARS and about three days of undelivered billing; the full-year double-digit target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price increase offset input costs and restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The May increase only partially covers input costs; the full benefit flows from Q2 and management said prices have eased below April–May levels, so it is a 'waiting game'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days fall from 73 to 66?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not intend to reduce inventory further, that Q1 had some lost sales from non-availability, and that inventory is now at an optimum level.

qa_highlights.question: What were the logistics and manpower disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Speedo multi-brand outlets decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall 5% in FY26 and is the company shifting to outright e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included a disproportionate World Cup campaign; marketing will stay at 4–5% of revenue. E-commerce has tilted to outright because of quick commerce, and price governance is maintained through partnerships.

risks_watch: Recovery of about three days of undelivered billing and above-average Q2–Q4 volume growth needed for double-digit annual volume target.
Input cost volatility (cotton, nylon, petroleum-based synthetics) and possible re-escalation requiring another price action.

Karnataka minimum wage: garmenting wage hike applied from April; second announcement affecting third-party support staff was withheld in late July; impact on margins from a garment-level hike not quantified.
Logistics and third-party labour reliability at quarter end.
Speedo multi-brand outlet consolidation and channel shift online.
Shift of e-commerce towards outright model and its implications for pricing control.
532827|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year volume and margin outlook, but defensive on the Q1 miss, which management attributed to timing and temporary disruptions. Answers on input cost hedging and quantification were hedged ("very difficult to put a number"), and the company did not quantify the Karnataka wage impact.
key_quotes: The underlying demand and volume momentum therefore remained better than what was reported as revenue growth.
So typically, every quarter we have – quarter ending we have about three to four days of billing that does not get delivered and gets pushed to the next quarter.
I think we've reached optimum level of inventory both in the value chain as well as the inventory at Page level.
As long as we're able to operate in that space, I think the intent would be to hold prices and drive volumes.

544912|2026-06.overview:
First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.</overview>

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ).
