544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, a record, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 11.5% versus 5% a year ago.
544679|2026-06.overview:
Revenue reached INR 437 crore, up 32% reported and 21% in constant currency, and almost 10% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose from INR 17 crore to INR 50 crore, with margin expanding to 11.5% despite the seasonally weak Q1 from annual increments. PAT rose to INR 34 crore (7.5% margin), and would have been about INR 40 crore excluding a one-time non-cash FX charge. Management reiterated operating leverage, highlighted AI product wins, and said gross margin will be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year.</overview>

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 249 crore, +39% YoY, driven by existing customer expansion, ~10,000 channel deliveries and 451 distributors (+21%).

segments.name: Monetization and Marketplace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, +30% YoY, volume-driven; monetized ad impressions a record 13.6 billion, +59% YoY and +21% QoQ.

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% reported; management said ~32% excluding the prior-year rev rec benefit from a large deal.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin to be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year, with Q3 seasonally strong; management described it as not structural deterioration.

Management is focused on full-year profitability rather than quarterly margins; H1 was ~47% of FY26 revenue and ~37% of FY26 adjusted EBITDA, indicating back-half EBITDA weighting (historical context, not guidance).
Q2 YoY comparison carries ~600 bps headwind from prior-year rev rec timing benefit; management said Q2 may not be the best marker for growth.
Broader AI product suite to be announced at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27; AI revenue contribution expected more visibly in late FY27.
Aspiration to maintain growth rates through the year, without explicit guidance.
capex_capacity: Cloud cost optimisation delivered ~USD 282,000 monthly run-rate gross margin savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives.
Live event delivery supported 104 FIFA World Cup matches on Amagi infrastructure for key customers; one US broadcaster received 100% on-air availability across 325 events and 450 hours.
Q1 is the weakest cash quarter each year due to incentive payouts, increments and software renewals.
Since January, 33 M&A opportunities evaluated, 23 passed on, 10 under active evaluation; management said this is not a signal of an imminent deal.
demand_pricing: Content processed reached 959,000 hours, +43% YoY; deliveries reached 9,900+ endpoints; distributors ~451, +21%.
Ad impressions 13.6 billion in the quarter, +59% YoY; management said FIFA did not add ad insertion upside and growth is organic (CTV penetration).

AI: 10+ active pilots; a major US news network selected Newspulse (agentic newsroom platform) after an earlier first paying customer; AI credit model introduced for some media operations, with outcome-based pricing possible later.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the sequential gross margin improvement and will it recover to 69%? What is AI's impact on gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gross margin to 67% to 69% for this year, citing mix, live events, pricing and AI costs. AI is a small base with no substantial margin impact yet; a 2 to 3 year S-curve with a possible initial dip is expected. Gross margin was ~64% three to four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Do distribution platform additions drive customer growth, and is in-sourcing a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Several distribution platforms (Vodafone, Kogan TV, Virgin UK) became customers, but it is not a prerequisite. Management sees platforms outsourcing rather than in-sourcing and is not aware of in-sourcing impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross retention (GRR) disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: GRR is not disclosed; management pointed to logo churn in low single digits and top 10 customer vintage of ~5 years as stickiness indicators.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being priced and how is cost inflation protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage; AI credits model mirrors a cost-plus approach for agentic media operations, with telemetry built with Newspulse customer to measure cost and revenue benefit. Business model not yet settled; a few more quarters needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is NRR constant currency and what is the growth impact of last year's one-time item?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR is in reported currency on a TTM basis, as in the DRHP; full-year NRR to be disclosed at Q4. The prior-year rev rec benefit affected growth by ~450 bps. Management aspires to sustain growth but Q2 will still lap the base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Can channel deliveries be split between new channels and additional deliveries on existing channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Not tracked internally; directionally growth is from existing channels going to more deliveries. Net revenue retention contributed ~26 points of the ~31% growth from existing customers.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from live event mix, customer pricing and AI costs; guided to 67% to 69%.
Cash burn remains negative in Q1 (operating outflow INR 65 crore reported), with DSO improvement of ~8 days QoQ still needed.
Q2 FY27 faces a ~600 bps headwind from the prior-year rev rec base; growth optics may be weaker.
Monetisation of AI products (Newspulse and broader Q2 suite) is still early; revenue contribution expected late FY27.
Capital deployment: active M&A pipeline (10 opportunities under evaluation) against INR 1,616 crore cash.

demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea: about 45,000-site rollout plan over 18-24 months (3,000-3,500 per month); INR6,400 cr secured from SBI, with a further INR25,000-30,000 cr under discussion. Vodafone currently plans about 12,000 sites through September, and management expects roughly 30,000 in FY27.
Airtel and Jio not doing major rollouts per management. BSNL announced INR77,000 cr capex for 2 lakh sites over 5 years, but no new BSNL work is being taken until billing is confirmed.
Revenue share (per management): Airtel 48.1%, Vi 27%, Jio 22.6%, BSNL 2.3%.
MSAs with all operators are blanket frameworks with no fixed volume commitment; a 10-year lock-in with Vodafone was cited.
Sharing mix: 80% anchor and 20% shared on new Vodafone sites; macro sites carry tenancy ratios of 2-3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the zinc battery project, its cost, and its margin and revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Zinc battery is bought from GBB Batteries, not manufactured in-house. Management said it cuts CapEx (100H unit at INR33,000 vs INR48,000 lithium) with no quantified EBITDA impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence and breakdown of the 3,000 Vodafone tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident. It sees 850 tenancies in hand (150 done, 700+ open), expects 35-40% in H1 and 60% in H2, and says 80% will be on new towers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL no longer being pushed in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not commit BSNL volumes until billing is confirmed. Tejas equipment issues have delayed BSNL rollouts by 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall from 25% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year quarter included a vendor-provision reversal from Vi; management says the underlying margin is about 20-21% with electricity included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Vodafone target fall from 12,000 to about 10,500 tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3,000 figure is conservative and tied to funds already secured; the target will rise as Vodafone confirms more funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tenancy ratio path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ratio is about 1.2x; target is 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29, since macro sites carry 2-3 tenancies with recovery in 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are fibre's share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre is 5-8% of revenue and stays at that level in FY27; management says it is 100% recurring and carries a similar EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 189/186-site BSNL billing status?
qa_highlights.answer: 186 sites are still pending billing; management expects revenue from them to start in Q2.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea funding: the 3,000-tenancy target depends on further SBI and consortium funds of INR25,000-30,000 cr; management says it will only raise its own targets once those are confirmed.
BSNL: 186 sites billing pending, Tejas equipment issues unresolved, and no firm rollout date.
Monsoon season may slow Q2 conversions.
Lithium battery costs up ~50% in 2.5 months; zinc battery first batch due mid-September and not yet proven on sites.
Funding: management is not ruling out a fundraise; the earlier call suggested one could come, and the analyst flagged this as an open question.
Margin optics: electricity reimbursement now in revenue, so margins are not comparable with prior periods, and the CFO flagged Ind AS rent accounting as muting EBITDA in early years.

544647|2026-06.headline: Nephrocare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 30.7% to INR65 crore and margin at 23.1%.
544647|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore on 13% higher guest count (38,262) and 13.3% more treatments (10.3 lakh). Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to INR65.1 crore, with margin up about 120-125 bps, mainly from a 175 bps lower COGS-to-revenue ratio that management attributed to procurement scale. Adjusted PAT rose 41.7% to INR37 crore. Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term growth guidance, while the Saudi tender remains an investment-phase drag of roughly INR3 crore per quarter on the JV line.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after ESOP and Saudi JV add-backs)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR43 crore in Q1 FY26
down 133 bps QoQ, up YoY; includes ECL provision of 2-2.5% of revenue

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: 19 clinics added in Q1 (mix of PPP in Bihar, four private, and one or two greenfield); India RPT about $22-23. Management said it will not pursue PPP contracts below return thresholds and exited two Uttarakhand PPP clinics as value dilutive. Tamil Nadu PPP contract signed.

segments.name: Philippines
segments.commentary: 7 clinics added in Q1 (7 acquisitions, towards quarter end), taking the count to 50 clinics across 39 cities; management says it is the second-largest network with about 6-7% share of about 900 standalone clinics. Average centre size is 10-12 beds.

segments.name: International (overall)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 45% of revenue, up from about 30% a year and a half earlier. Uzbekistan is the only private operator, servicing about 1,800 of roughly 9,000 patients.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: First clinic at Riyadh Hospital operational in July; home dialysis started; medical operator licence obtained; tender RFI response submitted. Still in investment phase with JV losses of about INR3 crore cited by analysts; no tender documents issued yet.

segments.name: Kazakhstan
segments.commentary: Subsidiary incorporated in Q1 to evaluate Kazakhstan and Central Asia; no revenue or timeline yet. Price points around $75 noted in the market.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance of 15-20% over the next three to five years maintained.
Expansion plan: 40-50 clinics a year in India, 10-15 clinics a year in the Philippines, and a new international market every 12-18 months; management does not give capex guidance.
Saudi tender formal process expected to begin in a couple of months; management sees three to four quarters before benefits or clear visibility; no guidance on JV losses.
Tax rate of about 20% offered as a proxy for the year (India and Philippines at 25%, Uzbekistan at 0% if healthcare revenue exceeds 90%).
NIDA renal nurse academy first batch to begin training in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR44 crore towards centre acquisitions and growth, vs INR43 crore a year earlier.

Depreciation life for machines is 7-10 years depending on country and regulation; RFID asset tracking reduced India depreciation, and about 50 machines a month of replacement activity was paused in the last three months.
Philippines acquisitions generate goodwill split into intangibles amortised over 5-7 years, adding to D&A.

Dialysis is a fixed-capacity business: about three cycles per machine per day; management says network growth comes from adding capacity, and clinics at about 85% utilisation need spare capacity for unplanned guests.
Management says the Philippines greenfield cost about 4 million per bed (referenced by an analyst) and declined to give acquisition cost per bed.
demand_pricing: India is still early in its dialysis market life cycle; management puts the organised (pure-play) share at about 20-22%, with 78-80% still hospital-run.
More than 300 private hospitals partner with NephroPlus on a built-own-operate model, where hospitals provide space and utilities and NephroPlus funds equipment.
Price increases are lumpy: CGHS raised rates about 35% in October 2025 after roughly 10-11 years; PhilHealth raised rates by 55-60% in October 2024.
RPT growth of about 11% CAGR was driven mainly by the international mix; management cautioned that the CAGR will not persist.
Management declined to split revenue or same-centre growth by country, saying it reports at platform level only.
75%+ of clinics are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; India operates in 300+ cities across 25 states.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from international mix versus cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COGS fell 175 bps as a share of revenue, driven by taking India procurement scale to other markets and by utilisation and supplier terms, not only reuse counts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise YoY, and how did they move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell 133 bps QoQ. Drivers were ECL provisions of 2-2.5% of revenue (KPMG-assisted model), public-company costs such as audit and legal fees, and upfront business development spend for new international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&A decline QoQ despite Philippines acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RFID-based asset tracking that cut machine replacements (about 50 a month previously) and a one-time benefit, partly offset by goodwill amortisation from seven Philippines acquisitions late in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi breakeven path and cost exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi is a binary tender market with four clusters; management does not give clinic-count breakeven and said further investment will depend on tender terms. Tender timelines are uncertain, and the company may not win.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose country-level or same-centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined, saying it manages capital at platform level and that dialysis growth comes from adding capacity rather than same-store price and volume.

533155|2026-06.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q1 FY27: Domino's LFL 2.5% on high base; Popeyes LFL cited at ~45%, EBITDA margin target of 200 bps reiterated.
533155|2026-06.overview: Management described Popeyes as a second growth engine, with LFL growth of 40-45% attributed to product quality, flavour innovation and store execution. Domino's delivered 2.5% LFL in Q1 FY27 against 11.6% in the prior-year quarter, and management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1. Cost pressure rose: LPG, cheese, oil, labour code and minimum wage hikes were partly offset by pricing and efficiencies, leaving the net margin headwind at about 20 bps QoQ. Management held FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore and the 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with about 100 bps viewed as ahead of track.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin (consolidated, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.6% in Q1 FY26; 0.5% in Q4 FY26
Vs ~70-80 bps remaining headwind flagged last quarter after ~110 bps of pricing already taken

segments.name: Domino's
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 LFL 2.5% on a high base; delivery order volumes not impacted by price increases per management. Minimum order value cut to INR 99 (from INR 149 free-delivery threshold) to match aggregators, lowering average order value.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: LFL growth 40-45%; about 90 stores, with 7 cities above INR 100K ADS for the full quarter. Target ADS is above INR 100K; gross margin still scaling and marketing spend high (about INR 100 crore revenue base invested to reach INR 1,000 crore).

segments.name: Dine-in / takeaway channel
segments.commentary: Dedicated channel team and regional structure built; 2,500 neighbourhood stores; early reversal of trend seen on Wednesdays via Best Deals Ever Wednesday offer. Goal is to hold LFL flat in this channel.

guidance_outlook: Domino's LFL to reach 5-7% for rest of FY27 as bases correct; Q2 FY27 expected better than Q1 FY27 (2.5%).
EBITDA margin expansion target of 200 bps retained (roughly half from Domino's, half from emerging brands); ~100 bps from Popeyes viewed as ahead of track.
FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore maintained; capex increasingly tilted to new Domino's and Popeyes stores, dine-in store investment and technology; supply chain capex materially down.
Management will take calibrated price increases if input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour) persists; commodities described as still in flux.
Expects positive free cash flow for the company over time; tracks ROCE and EPS as primary capital allocation metrics.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance INR 750-900 crore, in line with the previous two years; quarterly capex not disclosed.
Mumbai food factory commissioned in March; some commissioning still pending.
Supply chain investments described as past peak; new commissaries are lowering supply chain costs.
Capex mix: new store expansion (Domino's and Popeyes), existing store upgrades (dine-in), and technology.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 140 bps overall in the quarter per analyst; management said price hikes were 1.5-2% and delivery order volumes were not impacted.
Minimum order value on delivery reduced to INR 99 (and INR 49 on some aggregator platforms) to match aggregators; lower AOV and higher cost per order.
Management said demand is not the constraint; growth is increasingly a question of profitable delivery.
Popeyes competes with fried chicken incumbents; ADS still behind the number one player in the market.
Management declined to disclose AOV; said chicken AOV is higher than pizza and Popeyes can become the highest AOV brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Popeyes LFL acceleration from 9.2% to 45%, and where does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited superior product (marination, fresh chicken, intact pieces), six chicken wing flavours and bun focus, and better store execution with strong openings over the last 3-4 quarters. It declined to forecast normalisation, saying 45% is not a target to hold forever.

qa_highlights.question: Why has per-store employee cost not risen despite minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged per-store headwinds from minimum wages and new stores; productivity gains (orders per labour hour) offset some of the cost, though labour rate per hour has risen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dine-in strategy and expected outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: A dedicated dine-in channel team, store segmentation into dine-in clusters, mall, campus and delivery-first stores, service audits, and offers (Wednesday deals, payment and aggregator partnerships). Early Wednesday results show reversal of trend; first goal is to hold dine-in and takeaway LFL flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can LFL reach 5-7% for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing a two-quarter average of 2.5% (Q1 FY27) and 11.6% (Q1 FY26), which gives over 7%. It said Q2 FY27 will be better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company maximise free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exits from Hong's and Dunkin' and the supply chain build-out now past peak. Capex is shifting to revenue-generating store investment; the internal focus is ROCE and EPS rather than FCF alone. FCF was positive in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is the EBITDA margin target progressing given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 bps of the 200 bps is ahead of track from Popeyes. Domino's is on track, with price increases and supply chain efficiency offsetting LPG, cheese, oil and labour costs. Management said a quarter ago LPG alone cost about 120 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to Domino's margins QoQ after the MOV cut and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost headwinds were about 200 bps against about 100-110 bps of pricing already taken, leaving 70-80 bps. Further pricing, waste reduction and efficiencies cut the net headwind to about 20 bps in the quarter.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour code, minimum wages in about 14-15 states) could widen margin headwind; commodities described as still in flux.
Domino's LFL needs to hold 5-7% on a lower base in H2; Q3 and Q4 face tougher base comparisons.
Delivery volume and MAU-to-MTU conversion softness after price increases; lower AOV from the INR 99 minimum order value.
Popeyes EBITDA breakeven still pending; marketing costs high at current revenue scale; gross margin still scaling at about 90 stores.
Dine-in traffic recovery is early; results so far limited to Wednesdays.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 40% to INR 294 crores, with adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to minus 9% of revenue from minus 21%.
544799|2026-06.overview: Platform premium grew 49% YoY to about INR 1,205 crores and revenue grew about 40% to INR 294 crores in Q1 FY27. Service EBITDA rose nearly 90% to INR 39 crores (about 13% of revenue), and corporate overheads fell to 22% of revenue from 30%. Adjusted EBITDA loss was INR 26 crores (minus 9% of revenue) and PAT loss was INR 38 crores (minus 13%), versus a INR 47 crore loss a year earlier. Management reiterated a target of adjusted EBITDA breakeven for the full year, with profitability weighted to H2 given seasonality.

financial_highlights.change: about 37% absolute improvement; from -21% of revenue
improved from INR -47 crores (about -22% of revenue)
about 30-33% YoY; vs 72,244 a year ago

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Management implied motor growth of about 50%+ YoY, with PoSP growth and a new Turtlefin platform partner contributing. Motor market Q1 is 16-18% below Q4 and H2 is about 55% of the year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Q1 health grew about 45%+ YoY. Motor-only DPs starting to sell health grew 40%+ YoY. Nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

segments.name: Term life
segments.commentary: Term life grew about 60%+ YoY in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Business expected to grow about 40% YoY for the year, per July post-listing guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA breakeven targeted for full FY27, with profitability weighted to H2; management said PAT should 'not be too far away' but declined to give a PAT timeline.
Service EBITDA margin expected near-term to step up about 2 pp to about 16%, then 18%, reaching about 23-24% over 4-5 years as renewal book grows.
Corporate overheads expected to fall to 7-8% of revenue over 4-5 years (from 22% now).
Fixed costs below service EBITDA expected to rise in line with inflation.
demand_pricing: Digital partner base about 690,000+ after 32,000+ recruits in Q1; Turtlemint Academy ~55,000 monthly active users.
Take rate stable YoY; management said mix shift to renewals is the only change and there was no GST-related impact.
Renewal service EBITDA said to be 2.5-3x new service EBITDA; renewal servicing cost about 0.2% of revenue. Commission cost rises in line with top line.
Insurer relationships: for 17 insurers, Turtlemint's growth contribution was at least 2x industry growth in Q1.
DP attrition: 28-30% in first 24 months, falling to 2-3%; about 65% retained by year 5-6, management said trends unchanged.
Management said PoSP market growing at 30%+ CAGR; claims that Turtlemint has the highest PoSP share among players; competition seen as a 2-3 player market.
Motor TP pricing and commission regulation remain uncertain; management said insurers other than ICICI Lombard are awaiting the GIC appeal before provisioning.

qa_highlights.question: What drives seasonality, given the business is motor-heavy?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor market is about 45% H1 and 55% H2; Q1 is typically 16-18% below Q4. Q1 growth YoY remains strong and Q2, Q3 and Q4 should each be bigger than the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is take rate change driven by renewals or GST, and why did other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate is unchanged; the only shift is renewal vs fresh mix. Service EBITDA improved about 3 pp: roughly 2 pp from non-commission costs and 1 pp from commission costs. Commission rises with volume.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission cuts affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said health saw three full quarters after the GST-related commission reset, with revenue and margin still growing as volume offset the reset. Strategy will be decided once there is more clarity.

qa_highlights.question: How will service EBITDA margin reach 24-25% and how fast will renewal share rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal payout and servicing costs are much lower than new business. Management declined to confirm the 70-80% renewal share, saying renewal premium is growing faster and nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity trend across DP cohorts?
qa_highlights.answer: Older cohorts are also improving. Revenue grew about 40% while P3M Active grew about 30-32%, with the difference attributed to productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI lift long-term EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI is cutting costs and driving growth through personalised onboarding and renewal calling, but it is too early to quantify. AI renewal calls showed a renewal rate 500 bps higher and AI handles 55% of support tickets.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for FY27 and said PAT is not far off, with ESOP cost about INR 7 crores per quarter. No PAT timeline was given.

risks_watch: Commission regulation and motor TP pricing changes (Supreme Court case; insurers awaiting GIC appeal) could affect payouts and renewal economics.
Seasonality: Q1 is lowest; H2 must carry profitability to meet the FY27 adjusted EBITDA breakeven target.
Mix shift to renewals is the core margin driver; watch renewal share (22% now) and renewal growth versus new.
Competition: management views the market as 2-3 players; new entrants face high tech and distribution barriers.
Track DP activation (P3M Active), cohort productivity and attrition, plus whether AI renewal gains hold.
Corporate overhead ratio trajectory from 22% toward 7-8% over 4-5 years.
544799|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and renewals. Management was more guarded on regulation ('speculative', 'we do not know') and declined to give a PAT timeline or new-vs-renewal margin and renewal-share figures.
key_quotes: Our service EBITDA grew by 89% to INR 39 crores as margins continue to expand.
We also indicated that we'll try really hard for the entire year to be adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the current year.

Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

540797|2026-06.headline: Shalby Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr, but EBITDA was flat at ₹49 cr and margin fell to 14.5% from 16%.
540797|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr while EBITDA was nearly flat at ₹49 cr, pulling margin down about 150 bps to 14.5%. Consolidated PAT rose to ₹10.5 cr from ₹7.7 cr, helped by a lower group tax rate, though PBT fell to ₹19.7 cr from ₹22.7 cr. Hospitals grew revenue about 7% but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 18.4% from 21.6%, while MedTech revenue (about ₹47 cr) and India entity revenue (about ₹36 cr) grew sharply and consolidated MedTech EBITDA turned positive for a fourth straight quarter. Management guided to hospital margins of up to 20% for the full year and to double-digit MedTech EBITDA margins, with both reliant on items not yet visible in the numbers.

financial_highlights.change: down from ₹22.7 cr YoY; PBT margin 5.8%
up from ₹7.7 cr YoY; PAT margin 3.1% vs 2.5%
~+130% YoY per entity figure; ~+98% YoY per call

segments.name: Hospitals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹259 cr (+7% YoY), EBITDA ₹47.8 cr at 18.4% margin vs 21.6%. Occupied beds 701 (+9.8% YoY), occupancy 51%, ARPOB ₹44,711 (vs ₹45,673), ALOS 3.69 days (vs 3.53).

segments.name: Shalby International (Gurgaon)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹26.2 cr (vs ₹23.2 cr YoY), ARPOB ₹91,326, ALOS 3.8 days. Achieved first EBITDA break-even since acquisition, reported at about 7% EBITDA margin; occupancy about 24% per analyst question.

segments.name: MedTech – SMTL India
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36 cr per call (+29% QoQ, +98% YoY); management also cited India revenue growth of over 100% in volumes. Figures in the call are inconsistent (₹22.9 cr cited elsewhere).

segments.name: MedTech – US (SATUS)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹38.8 cr with about 9% sequential growth; standalone EBITDA marginally negative. US volumes flat YoY; FX headwind cited.

segments.name: MedTech – Singapore (SGTPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹9.9 million, lower sequentially; EBITDA about ₹5.8 million, a significant improvement vs prior quarters.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin: management is 'strongly confident' of reaching up to 20% for the full year FY27.
Gross margin expected to rise 100–200 bps each quarter going forward.

MedTech: double-digit EBITDA margin expected after US cost initiatives; half of progress made, remainder expected over the next 6 months. Monthly cash burn to fall ~₹3 cr/month from initiatives done in Q1 and a further ~₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27.
Shalby International occupancy expected to reach ~30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27; PBT break-even targeted around Q3–Q4 FY27 (6–9 months).
Group ROCE, currently ~7% (standalone ~9.5%), expected to reach 11–13% in 1–2 years.
Gurgaon unit to pay no tax for next 2–3 years due to carried-forward losses. Hospital tax rate moved to ~26% from 35%.
Inventory holding days expected to improve about 30%.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of about ₹160 cr in recent years, including bunker facility, robotics and MedTech investments; management expects minimal capex in the current and next year.
Bunkers (radiation facilities) installed in units last year; activation in Q1 with further uptick expected in Q2, including government-scheme coverage for bunker treatments.

Mumbai expansion: 200-bed greenfield Asha Parekh Hospital project; discussions ongoing with trustees, no approval yet. Funding by debt or internal accruals to be decided; no further debt for hospitals or MedTech expected.
47 transplants in Q1 (41 kidney, 5 liver, 1 bone marrow); liver transplant and KTP doctors recently replaced, full effect expected from Q2.
demand_pricing: Government share of payer mix rose to 32% from 24% a year ago; mix now 30% self-pay, 38% insurance, 32% government. Management cited a super-specialty rate win at Krishna unit.
TPA renewals underway, with management expecting a 5–7% revenue uplift from renewals and tie-ups in discussion.
Units Krishna, Mohali and Naroda grew ~30% YoY; Surat and Indore underperformed and are recruiting doctors.
International revenue ~42% of Shalby International operating revenue; group international business ~₹13 cr (₹2 cr Gurgaon, ₹11 cr other units).
Consolidated revenue of ₹923 mn in FY25, ₹1.3 bn in FY26, ₹472 mn in Q1 FY27 (MedTech-related, as stated).

532915|2026-06.headline: Religare Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR2,358 crores, but PBT swung to a loss of INR76.7 crores as RBI declined the demerger approval.
532915|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income reached INR2,358 crores against INR1,876 crores a year earlier, while total expenses of INR2,435 crores drove a PBT loss of INR76.73 crores versus a profit of INR5.73 crores. Care Health Insurance grew GWP 37% YoY on a full-premium basis and raised INR150 crores of equity, but its combined ratio stayed above 100% at 102.6% under Ind AS. RBI did not accede to the demerger application, and management said it is engaging with the regulator with no timeline. Broking profit rebounded, while RFL and Religare Housing reported lower income and losses as they rebuild.

segments.name: Religare Broking
segments.commentary: Total income INR99.5 crores (+7% YoY), brokerage 47% of revenue, interest income 30%, e-governance 16%. Client debit book +78% YoY; cash ADTO INR375 crores vs INR334 crores; AUC INR47,946 crores.

segments.name: Religare Finvest (RFL)
segments.commentary: Core SME book about INR53 crores; net worth about INR915 crores; cash over INR600 crores; CRAR 238%; NNPA about 0.8%; collection efficiency 98%. Income fell on smaller loan book and lower GNPA recoveries.

segments.name: Religare Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR247 crores (66% home loans, 34% LAP); about 15 branches in eight states; GNPA 4.4%, NNPA 3.3%; yield 14.6%; net worth about INR180 crores, CRAR above 121%.

Religare Housing to receive about INR250 crores further capital over the next few years against INR180 crores current net worth.
RFL: INR618 crores of INR1,500 crores warrant proceeds converted; INR881 crores remains due for conversion by March 2027.
Legacy written-off pool of INR350-400 crores under recovery; Q1 recoveries about INR20 crores.
demand_pricing: Care attributes growth to a 'land grab' in the market post-GST relaxation; growth driven by Tier 2/3 geographies and fresh business.
Industry health insurance grew 22.4% overall and 32% in retail; Care grew 18% above industry in retail.
Care's Q1 skews to corporate employee wellness business with upfront claims, which the company says inflates the combined ratio.
Broking: management attributes the revenue softness to market conditions and attrition; unique traded clients broadly stable.
RBI letter: no reasons attached; management says RBI did not object on capital structure grounds as stated in the letter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the demerger rejected and is a partial demerger or stake sale of Care under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Lamba said the RBI letter gives no reasoning; the company is engaging with the regulator and is not pursuing other options for now. No timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Care's CISR 102.7% when insurance service result is only about -INR3 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambrish Jindal said CISR includes non-attributable expenses; an INR66 crore item after net finance result is added in CISR computation, which explains the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why does consolidated Care show a loss when standalone Ind AS shows profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambrish Jindal said Care took a one-year forbearance on Ind AS 117 at consolidation, so the impact is not in consolidated accounts; this aligns from next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RFL/Housing growth plans and why is cash so high at RFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RFL was under PCA/CAP and lacked market funding for 7-8 years, so disbursements stopped; it expects to start business in about four months, with capital of INR1,500-2,000 crores targeting INR10,000-15,000 crores book.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the written-off book can be recovered and at what pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Srinivasan Karthik said the pool is INR350-400 crores of secured legacy loans facing litigation and repossession; recoveries are expected to decline each quarter and happen over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the RBI approval tied to merging the Burman-held private NBFCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Pratul Gupta said RBI's observation does not relate to merging the two sets of NBFCs; Arjun Lamba said the company is not aware of any such condition in the letter.

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR248.29 crore, up 34% in both volume and revenue; management linked this to zero GST on paneer from September 2025 and FSSAI/state bans on analogue paneer. Company claims ~20% share of the organised paneer market.

segments.name: Yogurt (incl. protein range)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR84.5 crore, up 153%; management calls it a key margin driver, with Greek yogurt and Skyr in the protein range.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Volume +45%, revenue +60% YoY, aided by extended summer; management expects demand to stay robust around the year in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).
Operating margin: management guided to about 0.5% leverage benefit from scale; asked whether 18% EBITDA margin is achievable in 3-4 years, CFO said 'you can expect that' but CEO declined to quantify.
Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.
Whey protein concentrate plant expected to be operational in about 15-18 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

Capex in the RHP: about INR500 crore plus INR150 crore, about INR650-700 crore in total; another ~INR380 crore WIP carried from last year. CFO said capex is funded through IPO proceeds and bank funding, with no cash-flow pressure this year.
Planned expansion covers whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, processed cheese and yogurt capacity.
Capacity utilisation: CEO said more than 12 product categories have spare capacity; paneer utilisation is about 50%.

Milk procurement averaged 13.2 lakh litres per day in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY. Third-party share is about 10-12% of volume, and the company is expanding direct procurement in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party share is about 10-12% through a five-year exclusive contract with MilkLane (linked to a PE-owned entity). Management says payments go directly to farmers and that quality premiums are about 50 paise/litre, with no financial dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement volume is up 28% YoY. Initiatives include bank credit via Kisan Credit Cards, herd-size expansion, AI/breeding, feed and health camps.

531859|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.7% YoY to INR137.6 crore, with EBITDA up 43.7% to INR20.9 crore and margin at 15.2%.
531859|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR137.6 crore against INR117.9 crore a year earlier, up 16.7% YoY. EBITDA rose 43.7% to INR20.9 crore, with margin expanding 286 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 83% to INR10.7 crore (7.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential revenue moderation to the US-Iran war and a fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, which it says is now largely resolved. The consolidated order book stood at about INR1,692 crore as of August 11, 2026, with INR1,526 crore at OFPL wagons and INR166 crore in coach interiors. Management also laid out smart wagon, next-gen wagon, wagon leasing and JV initiatives.</overview>

segments.name: Freight wagons (Oriental Foundry Pvt Ltd, OFPL)
segments.commentary: About 75% of consolidated revenue and about INR106 crore in Q1; management guides wagon volumes up more than 45-50% YoY on better capacity utilisation. Installed capacity is 2,400 wagons per annum, with FY26 utilisation around 50%.

segments.name: Seats and berths (rolling stock interiors, ORIL)
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the business holds over 30% market share with installed capacity of about 3,600 coaches per annum. Management expects other businesses to grow 8-10%.

segments.name: Rexine upholstery (ORVIN)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; in-house capacity is 36 lakh meters per annum serving railway and non-railway users.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 wagon dispatches of about 500 vs roughly 300 plus in Q1; FY27 turnover expected at around INR700 crore.
Order book execution at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December), which management says fully uses the 2,400-wagon capacity.
Medium-term EBITDA margin targets: 15-17% for freight wagons and 13-15% for rolling stock interiors; consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 15-17%.
Capacity expansion: application by Q1 FY28; target of 3,600 then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28; capex of about INR60-70 crore for the 2,400 to 3,600 step.
No order inflow targeted in FY27; order inflow of about INR600 crore expected in Q1 FY28 (management said FY27 in the call, then corrected to FY28).
capex_capacity: Wagon capacity 2,400 per annum at OFPL, around 50% utilised in FY26; more than 4,000 wagons delivered to date.
Expansion to 3,600 wagons (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28, with capacity applications starting Q1 FY28.
Dedicated smart wagon component facility planned in North India by end FY28.
Four manufacturing facilities across 100 acres; in-house bogies, draft gears, springs, couplers and side bearers. Spring plant became operational in FY26.
AAR certification application in progress.
demand_pricing: Wagon realisation about INR40 lakh per wagon (plus or minus 5%).
Wagon price escalation clause linked to steel WPI, labour index and other commodity indices; management says it does not cover vendor-driven component price hikes.
Management says FY26 and FY25 weakness was due to railway wheel shortages and reliance on external component suppliers, which squeezed margins.
Smart wagon monitoring system priced at about INR2.5-3 lakh per unit; target 30,000 units per annum, implying about INR750 crore revenue (management estimates a INR10,000 crore market).
Freight wagon market expected to nearly double to INR25,000-30,000 crore by 2031; National Rail Plan 2030 targets wagon fleet growth from about 4 lakh to 6 lakh.
Management expects 'at least two or three players' in smart wagons and says competition is anticipated.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for sequential revenue moderation and Q2 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 to the US-Iran war and the fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, now largely resolved. Q2 is running faster, with about 500 wagons expected versus roughly 300 plus in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many wagons does the INR1,526 crore OFPL order book represent and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,800 wagons, executed at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December).

qa_highlights.question: Capacity expansion plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is to go from 2,400 to 3,600 (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 over 12-18 months from FY28; the capacity application is planned for Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight revenue not grow in FY25-FY26 (INR458 crore to INR409 crore), and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a railway wheel shortage that restricted supply and underutilised capacity. Backward integration into springs, draft gears and couplers has since stabilised supply.

qa_highlights.question: Debt, cash flow and leverage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow should improve with utilisation and debt will reduce, but declined to give FY27/FY28 debt or debt-to-equity figures.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow pipeline for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 order additions targeted; management expects about INR600 crore of inflow in Q1 FY28. Government wagon tenders are typically clubbed for about two years.

risks_watch: Execution ramp: the plan requires about 200 wagons per month from October 2026 versus about 300 plus in Q1 total; a slip would hit the INR700 crore FY27 target.
Order book inflow is lumpy and tender-driven; no FY27 inflow is targeted and the next inflow of about INR600 crore is pencilled for Q1 FY28.
Smart wagon (HUM JV) timing has slipped: the earlier expected date was June 10 and the tender financial bids are now expected end August; revenue is guided from FY28-29.
Working capital and debt: management gave no debt or D/E figures and said operating cash flow was absent in FY25-FY26.
Input cost exposure to vendor-supplied components not covered by the price variation clause; competition expected in smart wagons.
531859|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term freight demand and capacity utilisation, but cautious and evasive on specifics. Management declined to give debt, D/E, growth-CAGR and pipeline figures beyond broad statements, and several answers were unclear due to line quality.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview:
Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.</overview>
