segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio (80-86% range) and whether it moves toward high-70s as guided.
Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment: review outcome and possible retrospective provisioning; solvency at 1.93x.
Reinsurance renewal terms after soft market and GIFT City capacity; loss of commissions or higher retention risk.
Health portfolio profitability and rebuilding of retail health capabilities; combined ratio of group health was flagged as a concern.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027, with impact on profitability and ROE still unquantified.

522101|2026-06.headline: Kilburn Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to about INR117 crores with 20.1% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance of INR700 crores kept, H2-weighted.
522101|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR117 crores, with EBITDA of INR24.2 crores (20.1% margin), which management called below the level it had targeted. Management attributed the shortfall to customer-driven timing: delayed approvals of drawings and inspections, deferred project executions, and longer decision cycles linked to geopolitical conditions. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue at 20% EBITDA margin and said the year is expected to be significantly second-half weighted. Order inflow was about INR134-135 crores in the quarter and about INR190 crores year-to-date, against an internal group target of INR800 crores for FY27. Management also said the equity fundraise is complete and the balance sheet is net debt-free.

financial_highlights.metric: Order inflow year-to-date (group, to date of call)
Closing order book (as cited in Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited INR467 crores for prior quarter; not confirmed by management

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR98 crores subscription money received in the quarter, shares allotted at INR425

segments.name: Kilburn Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said standalone performance was relatively weak this quarter; drying solutions inquiries expected to close by end Q1/early Q2, carbon black jobs on hold pending environmental and land clearances. Nuclear jobs (NPCIL, Heavy Water Board) face longer approvals than fertilizer jobs (Casale).

segments.name: M.E. Energy (waste heat recovery)
segments.commentary: Entering ferrous alloy via a Bhutan project; multiple ferrous alloy and cement inquiries; steel-sector inquiries in the INR10-15 crore size range. Capacity expansion at Kilburn and M.E. Energy expected to complete by end October 2026.

segments.name: Monga Strayfield (sheet metal / drying)
segments.commentary: Expanding metal sheet fabrication capacity for data-center storage equipment; details to be disclosed over time. Developing new drying-sector products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue expectation of around INR700 crores maintained, with 20% EBITDA margin; management said the number could change over the next two months depending on order cycle length.
FY27 expected to be significantly second-half weighted as deferred projects and deferred order intake move into execution.
Group order inflow target of INR800 crores for FY27 maintained.
Group capacity being built for a medium-term aspiration of INR1,000 crores annual revenue; no FY28 guidance given, to be clearer after order booking through March 2027.
Management expects drying-solutions inquiries to close around end of Q1/early Q2 FY28 (per Ranjit Lala).
capex_capacity: Kilburn Engineering and M.E. Energy manufacturing and execution capacity expansion at advanced stage, expected completion by end October 2026.
Monga Strayfield expanding metal sheet fabrication capacity; no amount or timeline disclosed.
Part of the equity raise to fund capex; management says no further fundraise needed for INR1,000 crore revenue and capex plans.
Capacity expansion meant to support INR1,000 crore revenue ambition.
demand_pricing: Group inquiry pipeline about INR4,000 crores across sectors and geographies; management cautioned it is not an order book.
Traction highlighted in fertilizer (new orders, EPC tie-ups with Casale-type customers), nuclear, data-center infrastructure, ferrous alloy, steel and cement, and petrochem/oil and gas.
Middle East: no current orders; a couple of large inquiries in the region were at final commercial negotiation stage before the conflict and remain on hold.
Customers delaying approvals of engineering drawings and quality inspections in 3-4 projects, extending execution cycles by a quarter or more.
Raw material: about 80% booked within 48-72 hours of order; delay-related cost escalation pursued for compensation from customers, but contracts are largely fixed price.
Management said order intake is a mix of repeat and new customer orders.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the INR98 crore fundraise proceeds and whether further fundraising is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Amritanshu Khaitan said proceeds strengthen the balance sheet (net debt-free) and partly fund capex to support over INR1,000 crores revenue; acquisitions are being evaluated but none announced; no further fundraise needed.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in reaching INR800 crore order inflow with 9 months left, and Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR4,000 crore inquiry pipeline and fertilizer traction; no current Middle East orders, but a couple of large inquiries were at final commercial stage before the conflict, now on hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why revenue growth ambition of about 25% has slipped to about 10-12% and what is being done differently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer-side dependencies, nuclear approvals taking longer than private jobs, and greenfield projects held by environmental clearances; no FY28 guidance until order booking through March 2027 is clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure linked to Kilburn standalone weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said the company has consistently maintained 20%+ margins on a consolidated basis, citing cost and execution discipline, and reports consolidated because of cross-selling.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital status?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said collections were received after March; debtors and net working capital have not changed substantially but are better than the March quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why were two managers (Nitin Varadkar, Dinesh Nikam) designated senior management personnel?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said it is a SEBI LODR disclosure requirement for reporting lines one level below the CEO after recent promotions; no board induction planned.

risks_watch: Revenue timing: Q1 shortfall and FY27 guidance depend on H2 execution; management acknowledged possible slippage of a quarter or two.
Order inflow of about INR190 crores YTD against INR800 crore target implies a sharp pick-up in the remaining months.
Geopolitical conditions (Middle East) delaying customer decisions and approvals; cost escalation from delays on fixed-price contracts.
Nuclear and greenfield projects dependent on regulatory approvals and environmental/land clearances (e.g., carbon black order on hold).
Capacity expansion completion by end October 2026 and capex returns; Monga Strayfield capex details not yet disclosed.
Discrepancy noted in Q&A: closing order book cited as INR485 crores by an analyst and by management, versus INR540 crores implied by an analyst's arithmetic; the company did not reconcile the figure.
522101|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margins, but cautious on near-term revenue: management repeatedly attributed the Q1 miss to customer-side timing and geopolitical decision delays. Answers on FY28 and the 25% growth ambition were hedged, with no FY28 numbers given. Management also declined to commit to a revenue path, saying the FY27 figure could change within two months.

543273|2026-06.headline: KMEW Q1 FY27 revenue rose 138% YoY to INR115.41 crore and PAT to INR62.75 crore, driven by one-off-heavy dredging execution.
543273|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR115.41 crore (+138% YoY), EBITDA INR73.41 crore (+258% YoY, ~64% margin) and PAT INR62.75 crore (+466% YoY, ~54% margin). Management attributed the quarter to dredging execution at JNPA (capital rock dredging, completed) and Pondicherry Port (maintenance dredging). Management said revenue and profitability are project-driven and vary by quarter. FY27 growth guidance was raised to "northwards of 60%" from an earlier 30-40%. The company also secured a INR62.40 crore IWAI hybrid ferry contract and raised INR150 crore via preferential issue plus a INR100 crore block deal.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 combined average EBITDA margin (as cited by CEO)
Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 combined average PAT margin (as cited by CEO)

financial_highlights.value: More than INR1,300 crore: dredging ~INR240 crore, charter & hire ~INR850 crore, shipbuilding ~INR240 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Intercompany order book placed with Knowledge Shipyard

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Core segment and main revenue driver this quarter from JNPA capital rock dredging (River Pearl 47, completed) and Pondicherry maintenance dredging (River Pearl 18). Dredging order book ~INR240 crore; management expects ~INR200 crore to execute in FY27.

segments.name: Charter & hire
segments.commentary: Recurring revenue from tugs, mooring, pilot, patrol, survey vessels under multiyear port contracts; order book ~INR850 crore across 15 contracts. Management says it is 3-5% of revenue currently.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Order book ~INR240 crore across 4 contracts, including IWAI contract for 10 hybrid electric 20-seat ferries (INR62.40 crore, ~10 months, built at Saphale yard). Currently ~9% of revenue; 42 third-party vessels and 5 captive vessels under construction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided to northwards of 60% YoY, up from earlier 30-40%.
Dredging revenue for FY27 expected to exceed FY26 levels; management expects INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book to execute this year.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore in FY29; management described it as the next milestone.
Shipbuilding expected to scale significantly from Q4 FY27 after Phase 1 of Saphale yard (14 vessels per year at Phase 1, 18 at full build-out); Phase 1 operational by end of FY27.
Operating (EBITDA) margins guided at 35-40% across segments; management said dredging margins will expand with volumes and it does not expect ~48-63% margins to persist.
FY29 revenue mix target: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, charter ~5%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over roughly the next 1.5 years: ~INR250 crore for Green Tugs and green vessels, ~INR450 crore for dredging, balance for shipyard and shipbuilding.
Adding larger TSHDs, CSDs, backhoe dredgers and water injection dredgers; new dredgers of 5,000-7,000 cubic metre capacity cited for deep-sea (Samudra Manthan) work.
Saphale shipyard: Phase 1 to Phase 3 build-out to ~18 vessels per annum; Phase 1 alone 14 vessels.
Portfolio under construction: 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, 4 CSD vessels, 2 60-ton bollard pull Green Tugs, 10 hybrid electric passenger ferries.
demand_pricing: Management said dredging faces very little to no competition; it is selective, requiring entry barriers to be met, and targets EBITDA margins of 35-40%.

Bid pipeline results expected in 30-45 days; dredging bids to be executed over 3 years. Maintenance dredging additions of INR100-120 crore in FY27, rising to more than INR250 crore from next year; capital dredging additions ~INR70 crore in FY27 and ~INR150 crore next year.
Historical bid hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years; management said it cannot assume this will continue.
Management attributed peer DCI's margin trend to older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW's fleet is more efficiently utilised.
Green Tug contracts are with Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar ports, 15-year fixed charter regardless of utilisation; EBITDA margin cited at 75% for Green Tug.
Export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe for ~3,000 DWT vessels under evaluation; payment terms still being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth guidance including the INR60 crore revenue shift from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was 30-40% YoY; management now sees potential northwards of 60% for FY27 on order book momentum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~INR1,300 crore order book executes in FY27 and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging book is expected in FY27. Management said margins will expand, not contract, though not at the 63% operating margin seen in Q1, which it described as not guidance (35-40% stays the guide).

qa_highlights.question: Why are KMEW's dredging margins rising while DCI's are falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCI has older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW is better sweating its assets for efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting expense trend?
qa_highlights.answer: FY23-24 subcontracting was high because of a JV structure where KMEW was lead partner. Now projects are executed individually; FY26 subcontracting expected at 5-6% of turnover, mainly shipbuilding and ancillary boats.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging vs shipbuilding mix in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering ~5%. Shipbuilding pre-subsidy margins 15-20%, post-subsidy expected to go beyond 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is shipbuilding captive or third party, and how is working capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 5 captive vessels (3 tugs, 2 boats) and ~42 third-party vessels. Working capital funded from stage payments (every 10-50% milestone), with no further loans needed; shipbuilding subsidy of 15-20% comes on delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Is dredging a moat given privatisation of ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, citing perpetual government demand, DCI's 50-year role and tender structure (domestic below INR250 crore, international above).

542337|2026-06.headline: Spencer's Retail Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs 469 crore; EBITDA doubled to Rs 9.4 crore (2% of sales).
542337|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 469 crore, with Spencer's format up 18% and Nature's Basket down 13% on a YoY basis (quarterly sales Rs 59 crore). Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 9.4 crore versus Rs 4.7 crore a year ago, but last year's base included about Rs 10 crore of lower non-operating income that management stripped out. Management said the EBITDA improvement is shifting from cost-led to sales-growth-led. Nature's Basket saw a management change about 45 days before the call and a reset plan focused on inventory, assortment and execution.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 86 crore YoY; percentage margin flat
vs Rs 4.7 crore (1%) YoY; prior year included ~Rs 10 crore lower other income
vs 19.1% YoY; ~19% like-for-like per management (difference from membership accounting)
vs Rs 15 crore YoY (which included ~Rs 7 crore non-operating income)
-13% YoY (vs Rs 69 crore); +8% QoQ (vs Rs 55 crore)
vs negative Rs 4.5 crore in Q4 FY26; slightly positive in Q1 FY26
vs loss of ~Rs 18 per order in Q1 FY26; ~Rs 12 in Q4
SRL Rs 1,019 crore; NBL Rs 237 crore

segments.name: Spencer's (format)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18% YoY and 8% QoQ, with offline +14% and online +49%. Sales per sq ft Rs 1,850 in Q1 (internal target Rs 2,000 in festive quarter); store EBITDA reportedly 2x year-ago, from ~2.5% toward a 7.5-8% short-term aspiration.

segments.name: Nature's Basket
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 59 crore, down 13% YoY but up 8% QoQ. Management says the setback was internal (stock availability, long-tail SKUs, online build-out); a reset plan is in place under a new management team about 45 days old.

segments.name: Jiffy (online platform)
segments.commentary: Management cited FY25 scale of about Rs 200 crore; no Q1 figure given. Online growth at Spencer's (+49%) is attributed to the platform.

guidance_outlook: Full-year online business growth to steady at around 25%, with no heavy customer-acquisition spend and unchanged unit economics.
Spencer's offline growth guided at mid to high single digits for the year.
Nature's Basket expected to reach early double-digit growth from Q3 and Q4 FY27 after the reset.
No new Spencer's store additions in FY27 beyond relocations and a few cluster tests; calibrated expansion considered for FY28.
No new Nature's Basket stores; limited capex directed to refurbishing existing stores. Management frames EBITDA breakeven as the ambition, with Q2 as the next update.
capex_capacity: No new stores added in Q1 FY27; productivity gains come from the existing footprint of 89 Spencer's and 31 Nature's Basket stores.
Spencer's sales per sq ft Rs 1,850 in Q1; internal target Rs 2,000 in the festive quarter.
Nature's Basket capex limited to refurbishing ageing stores; a small Spencer's store launched in suburban Kolkata two days before the call.
Nature's Basket online tech stack ready, riding on the Jiffy platform; customer acquisition deferred until inventory is fixed. Update promised in Q2.
Debt refinancing process started, with some expected to close in the current month (August).
demand_pricing: Spencer's YoY growth split about 70% from higher number of bills (NOBs) and 30% from higher average bill value (ABV), which management called underlying volume growth.
Category mix broadly unchanged: staples +100 bps, liquor +100 bps, non-food (apparel, E&E, GM) -100 bps, fresh flat.
Membership: launched July 2025, 125,000+ members (~25% of active monthly customers) contributing ~1/3 of monthly sales; member retention ~2x and monthly spend ~3x non-members, with frequency near 5.
Online ABV above Rs 780; repeat rate ~67%; NPS 85+; in-full rate above 90%; on-time delivery just under 30 minutes.
Management declined to enter quick-commerce marketplaces (Instamart, Blinkit) for Nature's Basket, citing margin sharing and sustainability concerns.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the growth trajectory across Spencer's, Jiffy and Nature's Basket over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give segment targets. Online is guided to ~25% full-year growth, Spencer's offline to mid-to-high single digits, and Nature's Basket to early double digits from Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What KPIs track the Nature's Basket turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Three KPIs: sales per sq ft, rupee gross margin (not percentage), and cost control. Cost cuts are limited in NB's premium format; support overheads were optimised once.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any store expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Nature's Basket stores. Spencer's has no additions this fiscal beyond relocations and cluster tests; a calibrated expansion may come in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Could membership reach 50% of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focuses on absolute numbers: target 200,000 members shopping at least 5 times a month, contributing 39-42% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Spencer's growth, volume or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% from more bills and 30% from higher ABV; category mix stable, with member special pricing cited as a driver of basket-wide buying.

qa_highlights.question: Update on quick commerce for Nature's Basket and debt status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce was not pursued; the tech platform is ready but customer acquisition waits on inventory fixes. Consolidated debt Rs 1,266 crore, with refinancing under way and some expected this month.

risks_watch: Nature's Basket remains loss-making at EBITDA level (negative Rs 2.5 crore) with revenue still down YoY; reset success depends on the new management team.
Q1 EBITDA improvement partly reflects a Rs 10 crore non-operating income gap versus last year; underlying gains need confirmation in Q2.
Debt of Rs 1,266 crore with a large portion due for refinancing this year; closure timing is not yet confirmed.
Spencer's gross margin fell to 18.2% from 19.1% YoY on reported basis; management attributes this to membership accounting.
Online growth relies on order volume with unit economics positive at about Rs 18 per order, and the target is limited customer acquisition spend.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said it manages the business as one group and will not disclose segment-level numbers for H-One or Mag Filters.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.</overview>

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, citing RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline store expansion.
Crude/rupee-linked price increases in manufacturing expected to be fully passed on by end-Q2 FY27, with full margin normalisation for that component from Q3.
Diapering margin recovery expected over four to six quarters, with competitive intensity easing in July and August per management.
Adding around 100 net offline stores in FY27 (management said 90-100); FY28 expansion expected to be larger.
Management declined to give a timeline for International EBITDA breakeven, pointing to input metrics instead.
Management said the 280 bps gross margin gap should 'dramatically' reduce, but gave no quantified target for the full year.
capex_capacity: Offline store expansion was paused for two quarters to realign the product portfolio; now resuming with ~100 net new stores targeted in FY27.
RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.
GMV growth (12%) trails India revenue growth (18%) because the revenue line includes manufacturing and the GMV is at MRP, with GST 2.0 reducing MRP from Q2.
Management said non-diapering consumables are about 15% of India GMV, with healthy margins and no challenge from quick commerce.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

521016|2026-06.headline: Indo Count Q1 FY27 total income rose 13% QoQ to INR1,224 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 13.1%, with volumes up 12% QoQ.
521016|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with total income of INR1,224 crore (+13% QoQ, +27% YoY) and EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% QoQ) at a 13.1% margin. Sales volume rose 12% QoQ to 23 million meters but fell 3% YoY on container shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. The new business (utility bedding and US brands) reached INR387 crore in the quarter. Bhilad plant was hit by flooding from 23 July 2026 and only partially resumed on 12 August 2026; the company says it is fully insured.

financial_highlights.change: Nearly tripled over past one year (per management)
vs INR80 crore last year (per management)
Q4 FY26 included one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related hit

segments.name: Core business (bed linen, quilts, comforters etc.)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR837 crore, +4% QoQ; ~70% US and ~30% non-US. Management says core blended margin is around 15%, with standalone margin slightly above 15% in Q1. Quarterly realisation fell on product mix.

segments.name: New business (utility bedding + US brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR387 crore in Q1, all US-linked. Split is roughly two-thirds utility bedding (manufacturing) and one-third brands; brand revenue was slightly above INR125 crore. FY27 target INR1,500 crore; brands target about INR500 crore for the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance reiterated at 105-110 million meters; core business revenue about INR4,000 crore.
FY27 new business revenue target INR1,500 crore; USD275 million new business ambition for 2028 and INR8,000 crore revenue aspiration by CY2028 reiterated.
Non-US revenue expected to grow 20%+ in FY27.
Endeavour to maintain about 13% blended EBITDA margin for FY27 on a consolidated basis; long-term stabilisation target 15-16% for the company as a whole.
Price increases concluded with customers; impact on realisations expected from Q2 onwards. Full-year realisations expected broadly intact.
Interest cost expected at about INR120 crore for FY27 (INR30 crore per quarter), at roughly 6-7%.
Utility bedding utilisation targeted at 60-65% for FY27.
Potential US tariff refund: management expects no material financial benefit; ~80% of exports are FOB; quantification premature, clarity expected by year-end.
capex_capacity: New greenfield facility in North Carolina commenced in January 2026; operations ramping, adding employee costs and a lower-margin gestation period.
Existing US facilities in Ohio and Arizona; utilisation overall around 60-65% in Q1 despite new capacity.

Bhilad (Gujarat) plant hit by flooding from 23 July 2026; partially resumed 12 August 2026 with phased normalisation. Management says other plants are absorbing lost output (endeavour, not confirmed).
Utility bedding business investment about 70-75% complete per management, with balancing investments still to come.
demand_pricing: Volumes recovering as US tariff uncertainty eased; Q1 seen as seasonally softer than Q2 and Q3 (US festive period).
Container availability constraints from the West Asia conflict hit Q1 dispatches; management says the container issue continues.
Raw material costs rose after the February-end war; price increases were negotiated case by case and concluded, with impact from Q2.
Non-US: UK FTA restores level playing field (UK business 8-10% of total); management says client interactions in UK rose from about 4 to 8 a year. EU FTA expected to add further duty-free access.
Competition: India at about 10% US tariff vs neighbours at 10-12.5%; management says no orders or customers were lost even at 50% tariff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference between core bed linen and the new utility bedding and branded businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15% for both bed linen and utility bedding over time, and brands 100-200 bps above that. Utility bedding is currently lower because the new facility is in gestation; bed linen did slightly better than 15% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is any US tariff refund expected and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff refund was booked in Q1. Management expects no material benefit as ~80% of exports are FOB, and says quantification is premature until year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone margins decline in Q2 and Q3 given Bhilad disruption and cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined precise quarterly guidance; the endeavour is to hold about 13% blended consolidated margin for the full year. Any one-time losses are covered by insurance (property, inventory, loss of profit).

qa_highlights.question: Why is utility bedding utilisation guided at only 60-65% when Q1 already achieved that?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-65% is the satisfactory level to plan on for the full year, with stability expected for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost run-rate and weighted average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost is about INR30 crore per quarter (INR120 crore annual); the Q4 figure included a one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related charge. Cost is roughly 6-7%, varying by bank; company rated A1+.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins go beyond 15% long term given the shift to branded and e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: No ceiling is set. Long-term target is to stabilise at 15-16% for the company as a whole, to be recalibrated as the business progresses.

risks_watch: Bhilad plant recovery pace after flooding; whether lost output is made up in Q2-Q3 without delays in shipments.
Container availability and West Asia-linked freight constraints, which cut Q1 volumes 3% YoY.
Quarterly realisation pressure from product mix; price increases on raw material costs to flow through from Q2.
Utility bedding: non-cotton input cost inflation, and whether it is fully passed on (management says yes, with 2-3 month lag at times).
New business ramp: management says variability is still unknown and about 70-75% of the investment is in place; USD100 million brand target is three years out.
Potential US tariff refund accounting, with clarity expected only by year-end.
521016|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on recovery and the INR8,000 crore aspiration, but noticeably reluctant to give precise quarterly margin or volume guidance. Management was defensive on Bhilad impact and on the margin question, and fell back on insurance cover and full-year averages.

542669|2026-06.headline: BMW Industries Q1 FY27 operating income rose 11.6% YoY to INR166.0 crores; PAT up 25.8% to INR19.1 crores, but operating EBITDA margin fell to 20.3%.
542669|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 11.6% YoY to INR166.0 crores and gross margin expanded 536 bps to 67.9%. Operating EBITDA rose 7.1% to INR33.7 crores, but margin compressed to 20.3% from 21.2% on a sharp rise in fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict. PAT grew 25.8% to INR19.1 crores with a 10.8% margin. Bokaro greenfield capex is in progress: colour-coated line hot trials are underway with capitalisation and commissioning expected from Q2 FY27, and ROCE and ROE are diluted because the plant is not yet contributing.

financial_highlights.change: +7.1% YoY; margin vs 21.2% in Q1 FY26
Of which INR202.4 crores long-term borrowings for Bokaro

financial_highlights.value: INR139.2 crores; total capital deployed INR341.6 crores

segments.name: Rolling mill
segments.commentary: Annualised capacity utilisation of about 83.5%; management attributed higher volumes to demand and customer offtake rather than company action.

segments.name: Pipes and tubes

segments.name: Bokaro greenfield downstream (colour-coated, galvalume, cold rolling)
segments.commentary: Colour-coated line commissioning from Q2 FY27 with hot trials on; 1,50,000-ton line expected to take 3-4 quarters to ramp. Cold rolling and Galvalume lines to follow. Throughput target about 0.5 million tons.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated consolidated revenue CAGR of about 70%-75% over FY25-FY28, driven by Bokaro ramp-up and organic growth in existing verticals.
Operating EBITDA CAGR of about 40%-45% and PAT CAGR of about 35%-40% over FY25-FY28.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at about 12%-13% and PAT margin at about 5%-6% by FY28.
No specific FY27 revenue guidance given; management declined to quantify a quarterly run rate or Q2 trends.
ROCE expected to improve progressively as Bokaro commissions from Q2 FY27 and ramps up.
capex_capacity: Bokaro colour-coated line: hot trials ongoing; to be capitalised in Q2 FY27.
Cold rolling and Galvalume lines to be commissioned in subsequent quarters; full ramp across about 6 quarters through FY28.
Bokaro capital drawdown already in capital employed; plant not yet generating returns.
Certifications (ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, 17025, IATF 16949) not yet applied for; to be pursued after commissioning and stabilisation.
demand_pricing: Management says steel consumption growing 10%+ vs GDP of about 7-7.2%, supported by government infrastructure and private capex.
Colour-coated products demand growing 7%+; antidumping duties, QCOs, PLI and import substitution cited as supportive.

Fuel and power cost spike from Middle East conflict hit margins; industry-wide, so management sees a level playing field. Talks under way with customers to add gas price indexation to price variation mechanisms.
ZAM adoption encouraged by MNRE order for rooftop solar; company does not yet have ZAM customers and plans to offer Galvalume, galvanised and ZAM together.
Bokaro output of about 0.5 million tons vs India flat-product market of about 80-85 million tons; management calls it an entry-level position.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company give a Q2 or FY27 revenue run-rate and state how much revenue Bokaro will generate and when it reaches INR500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on FY27 or Q2 numbers. It said ramp-up will take at least 3-4 quarters for the 1,50,000-ton line, and the FY28 guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company collect the delayed receivables from a key customer in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said collections typically arrive in the first 1-2 weeks of a quarter, and all pending amounts were received at the start of Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a competitive moat in ZAM given the technical entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 14 years of galvanising process experience and a planned full range of Galvalume, galvanised and ZAM. It acknowledged the company has no ZAM customers yet, so stickiness must be built over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand-supply outlook for colour-coated and galvanised products in the East, given new industry capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects steel demand growth to persist for 3-5 years, cited Eastern region catch-up and roofing/cladding, PEB and pre-galvanised structural demand, and said quality (not capacity) is the main differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company capitalised the colour-coated line and what is the industry landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Capitalisation is expected in Q2 FY27 once hot trials finish. Management said colour-coated demand is growing 7%+ and that quality will matter more than capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the improved pipes and tubes and rolling mill utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling mill improvement was demand and customer driven. Pipes and tubes utilisation rose from about 34% in FY26 to 40% annualised in Q1 FY27, which management expects to reach 65-70% by about FY29.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin pressure from fuel and power costs; gas price indexation in customer contracts is still under negotiation and not yet agreed.
Bokaro ramp-up execution (3-4 quarters per line) and capitalisation timing in Q2 FY27 will drive ROCE, which is currently 9.5%.
Pipes and tubes utilisation at about 40% leaves large unused capacity; delivery to the 65-70% target by about FY29 is unproven.
Rising colour-coated capacity in the East and quality concerns among domestic suppliers could pressure pricing.
Net debt of INR468.9 crores (0.57x D/E) with Bokaro debt still being drawn; leverage should be monitored.
Limited disclosure: management declined to give FY27 or Q2 numbers and did not give a timeline for certifications or export plans.
542669|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets and demand, but guarded on near-term numbers. Management repeatedly refused to give FY27 or Q2 figures and said Bokaro certification and export plans were too early. On margins, it attributed the EBITDA compression to fuel costs and said these had since eased.

532808|2026-06.headline: Pearl Global Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.5% YoY to INR1,528 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.7% (up 140 bps) and PAT of INR99 crore.
532808|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR1,528 crore grew 24.5% YoY, the highest ever Q1, driven by volume growth (20.8 million pieces vs 17.2 million). Adjusted EBITDA excluding ESOP was INR164 crore (up 44.1%), margin 10.7%, and PAT INR99 crore (up 51.4%). Standalone (India) EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 7.3% because of Haryana wage revisions. Management reiterated double-digit full-year EBITDA margin and said FY28 INR6,000 crore revenue target could be reached earlier.

financial_highlights.metric: Dividend received from Pearl Global Hong Kong

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Largest geography at about 45%+ of group volume; business growing with existing and new customers. Capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces expected operational in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: About 27% of group volume; key for high-value and outerwear products; management evaluating further capacity expansion and land acquisition completed.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: About 22% of group volume. Utilisation 65-70% on capacity basis, efficiency about 50-58%. Standalone EBITDA margin 6.6% due to Haryana wage hikes; Bihar second shed to add run-rate revenue of INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Healthy momentum off a lower base with focus on premium clients; described as not fully utilised; management expects both top line and bottom line growth.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Operating strategy reworked; management confident of break-even in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue target of INR6,000 crore could be achieved earlier than planned if current trend holds; management says it may be exceeded.
Revenue CAGR range of 12-14% now seen as conservative; management indicated FY27 high-teens growth looks feasible at current run rate, subject to H2 US conditions.
Double-digit EBITDA margin expected for full FY27 and Q1 margin of about 10.7% expected to be sustained in subsequent Q1s; long-term aim 10-12% by FY28 and 11-12% as levers converge.
Installed capacity to reach about 108 million pieces after Bangladesh expansion (Sept-Oct 2026); target of 125-130 million pieces by 2028 retained, with interim capacity via partner factories.
Finance cost guided at 1.7%-1.8% of sales for FY27.
Capex of approximately INR200-250 crore planned for FY27 across geographies; detailed plan to follow in coming months.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces plus eco-friendly laundry unit starting September, operational for orders in H2 FY27.

India: Bihar two sheds of 450 machines each; first shed (woven) operational at about 120,000-130,000 pieces per month; knit shed production expected Oct-Nov 2026; full capacity 4-5 lakh pieces per month once ramped.
India second shed revenue run-rate potential INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation, expected ready Sept-Oct.
Vietnam: land acquisition completed; greenfield project planned later, with partner-factory capacity also being added.
Overseas utilisation about 75-80% on quarterly available capacity; India utilisation about 65-70%.
demand_pricing: US consumer behaviour described as healthy despite inflation; similar trends in EU and UK; retailers expected to pass on IEEPA refunds, which may support order books.
Realization uplift of INR20 per piece YoY attributed mainly to product mix (outerwear shipped in Q1); management says it is not a sustainable benchmark versus full-year average of INR643 in FY26.
Last year India had double-digit discounts tied to tariffs; management expects these to fade, supporting realization in Q2-Q4.
Retailers are ordering short-term rather than long-term; no shift to early ordering seen.
Japan: China share of clothing imports fell from about 65% to about 50%; Vietnam at 17.4%, Bangladesh at 4.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in Q1 revenue and any revision to full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth is not one-off; the end of tariff overhang lifted customer orders. Full-year FY28 INR6,000 crore target now seen as achievable earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.7% margin free of tariff impact and is standalone margin recovery possible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tariff impact in Q1 and the margin is operational. Standalone margin would be about 9%+ excluding the Haryana wage impact; target is high single-digit to double-digit in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 51% while gross margin rose to 51.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed this to a mix of outsourced/partner-factory production booked under other expenses and higher-value overseas products improving gross profit; management said the gross margin is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital days stable at about 43-44; more internal cash used instead of some receivable financing. Finance cost guided to 1.7-1.8% of sales for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are India utilisation and efficiency levels?
qa_highlights.answer: India capacity utilisation about 65-70% and efficiency about 58%; Bihar ramping up line by line; India volume up about 27% YoY.

risks_watch: Standalone India EBITDA margin compression (6.6%) from Haryana minimum wage hike of 38% and Noida hike of 21%; labour availability issues in Q1.
US tariff regime: MFN plus 10% additional tariff on India, Bangladesh, Indonesia and 12.5% on Vietnam after Section 122 expired on July 24; potential 301 tariff changes.
Freight and shipping disruption (container shortages, Bab-el-Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz energy volatility); customers currently bear freight under FOB terms.
Dependence on H2 US demand, with management flagging possible Fed rate hikes and war-related uncertainty.
Guatemala break-even targeted in FY27; Bangladesh expansion ramp-up timelines; Q2-Q4 realization trend relative to Q1 seasonality.
532808|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, FTAs and capacity; more cautious on macro, US demand in H2 and the India margin drag. Some answers were loose on specifics (capacity, utilisation), with several figures deferred to later communication.

544304|2026-06.headline: Jungle Camps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, but EBITDA fell to ₹1.69 cr (27% margin) after a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge.
544304|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, with occupancy up 2 pts to 45% and RevPAR up 9% to ₹4,763. EBITDA declined to ₹1.69 cr from ₹1.81 cr and margin compressed to 27% from 32%, partly from new-property ramp-up costs and a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge tied to the discontinued Parsili project. PAT fell to ₹0.47 cr from ₹1.13 cr. Management outlined Devprayag and Palash Kothi (42 rooms combined) as FY27 additions, Mathura (105 rooms, IHG Holiday Inn Express) and Sheopur Fort (35–40 rooms in phase 1) for FY28, and a debt build-up to about ₹50 cr by FY28.

Second half (October–March) margins expected to be better than the same period last year.
Devprayag (Uttarakhand, 22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism Board) to start in Q2 FY27; ADR guided at ₹5,000–6,000; capex up to ₹1 cr; lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, scaled to 105 rooms) targeted for FY28 opening; revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ₹12 cr; project cost ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; lease rental 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever higher.

Sheopur Fort: development commenced; ₹3.5 cr spent on Sheopur and Pench renovation under CWIP; ₹7 cr standalone tangible assets increase YoY largely CWIP.

Panna, Satpura, Sariska and Jawai at advanced/exploration stage; Ratapani land held, construction expected to start shortly.

Holiday Express brand chosen for Mathura; IHG fee structure of around 7–8% of revenue across four or five components.

544580|2026-09.headline: Canara Robeco AMC Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 17% YoY to INR 121.6 crores and PAT rose 21% to INR 59.2 crores.
544580|2026-09.overview:
Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 17% YoY to INR 121.6 crores and PAT grew 21% to INR 59.2 crores, with H1 PAT up 23% to INR 134.8 crores. Closing AUM was INR 1.17 lakh crores, with September quarterly average AUM up 4% YoY, while management described the quarter as challenged by a roughly 6% Nifty fall in September. The company declared an interim dividend of INR 2 per share. Management did not disclose net flows, and analysts questioned SIP book and folio trends, which management attributed to ELSS tax-law changes, vintage SIP maturities, and market-driven closures.</overview>

532929|2026-06.headline: Brigade Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 36% (from 28%) on real estate margin recovery, though net sales fell 5% to INR1,061 crore.
532929|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue was INR1,179 crore with EBITDA of INR425 crore, and PAT of INR217 crore (up 37% YoY). Real estate EBITDA margin recovered to 21% from 12%, driven by recognition of higher-margin projects, while realisation rose 21% YoY to INR14,256 per sq ft. Q1 had no launches; the Morgan Heights relaunch was stalled after SEIAA revoked its environmental clearance, and management cut that project from the launch schedule. FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore was reiterated, with launches back-ended and the launch pipeline trimmed to about 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27.</overview>

500135|2026-06.headline: EPL Q1 FY27 revenue grew 25.3% (20% underlying ex pass-through) with EBITDA margin at 18.8%; revenue guidance raised to high teens.
500135|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue growth of 25.3%, or 20% underlying excluding pass-through of higher raw material prices, with EBITDA up 15.2% and margin at 18.8% (19.6% underlying). Reported PAT fell 1.4% while PBT rose 10%, which management attributed to a low base-year effective tax rate and phasing. Working capital rose roughly INR 180 crore in the quarter, mainly inventory, which management linked to raw material price inflation and safety stock. Revenue growth guidance was raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters, with the 20% underlying EBITDA margin target held. Europe margins contracted on operational issues and transitional costs, and the Indovida merger received CCI approval but is still pending final approval.

financial_highlights.change: Management says in line with plan; FY PAT expected to grow double digits
Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% vs 18% in FY26

financial_highlights.change: FY26 full-year increase cited as about INR 170 crore

qa_highlights.question: What are the Europe transitional costs and is manufacturing footprint changing again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe had operational challenges now getting focus and expects resolution in coming quarters. Manufacturing stays in Poland and Germany; it did not quantify the transitional cost adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: Does the upgrade to high-teens growth also lift PBT growth, given FX and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed high-teens revenue and EBITDA growth for the year, with PBT translating to a similar trajectory; PAT was held back by ETR and phasing, with a double-digit FY PAT still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain from sharp price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said old inventory did affect consumption costs, but the company recovered the entire cost impact in Q1 and expects to continue doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Americas EBITDA and EBIT fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue includes pass-through pricing, which distorts sequential comparisons, and that investments in Brazil and the US capabilities weigh on margins; underlying margin is higher than reported.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ETR outlook and post-merger tax impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% (Q1 22%). Management declined to comment on consolidated post-merger ETR but said Indovida's PAT is in line with EPL's and the deal is EPS accretive.

Americas margin pressure from ahead-of-curve investments in Brazil and US.
Effective tax rate variability (18-22% range) can keep PAT growth lagging PBT growth.

Sugar sales volume rose to 0.89 LMT from 0.56 LMT, lifting revenue to about Rs. 410 crore from Rs. 347 crore, though average realisation slipped to Rs. 40.02 per kg from Rs. 40.97. CPG turnover roughly halved to Rs. 94 crore from Rs. 188 crore as management deliberately recalibrated the model toward higher-margin products, with quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters. PSRIPL refinery operations have ceased and Rs. 665 crore was infused in the quarter to settle bank obligations.

517035|2026-06.headline: RIR Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.3% YoY to Rs 27.16 crore, EBITDA Rs 3.98 crore, with Odisha epi-wafer output targeted from Q3 FY27.
517035|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 27.16 crore (up 29.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 3.98 crore and EPS of 39 paisa. The Odisha epitaxy facility is nearing commissioning: power connection is nearly done, and epi operations are expected by end-Q2 FY27, with epi-wafer revenue from Q3. financial_highlights.change: from migration to new tax regime (25.17% vs 34.9%)

BTPL (fabric unit) remains loss-making at the operating level, with merger expected in Q3 FY27.

segments.commentary: Q1 saw good volume growth and strong margins, plus recovery of old pending billings that aided the quarter. Management said this contribution is not expected to recur at the same level.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Florens Farming Ltd is the key focus for own farming and land tie-ups; management said it contributes about 10% of F&V and could pay off from next year. Prime Fresh Retail India Pvt Ltd is held for strategic partners; B2C entry deferred.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 7.5%; net profit margin guidance stated as 5.5% to 5% (as transcribed, likely a typo).
Volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum in one answer and 15% to 25% in closing remarks; value growth of 25% to 30%.
Internal aspiration of 9.5% to 11% EBITDA margin in 2 to 2.5 years (around 2029) and a vision of INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031; longer-term EBITDA margin of 14% to 16% in 4 to 5 years.
Operating margin expected to rise slowly from mid-FY28.
Debtor target of 88 to 94 days of sales, debtors below 25% of sales, and no single rupee of working capital or equity needed for an incremental INR60 crore sale by FY29.
Product portfolio to add three to four more categories within a year (currently 9 to 12 F&V products).
capex_capacity: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board: company as implementing agency; expected award in August 2026; INR75 crore investment (excluding INR5-6 crore preoperative spend), of which INR50-52 crore eligible for 40-50% grant (about INR24 crore grant expected on milestones).
Capex to start around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18 to 20 months; Phase 1 INR6-9 crore, Phase 2 INR12-15 crore, balance in Phase 3, funded from own balance sheet including debt.
Project debt peak about INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned, falling to INR18-20 crore after grants.
Farmer component of about INR60 crore with around 35% government subsidy; target of 15,000 farmers and 15,000 tons incremental sourcing in year 1, scaling to 2 lakh tons in six years.
Sourcing capacity close to 2.5 lakh tons vs FY sales of about 65,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Customer mix: about 20 large modern trade and e-commerce accounts, around 90 APMC partners, 10 to 15 food processors, 20 to 30 exporters; added four to five food processing customers in Q1.
Price pass-through of 4 to 8 days on procurement changes for most business; HoReCa about one month; 5-star and tender business up to 3 months, which is under 4% of business.
Pomegranate: about 13,000 farmers and 40 plus local area aggregators; onion prices rising sharply, benefiting inventory gains.
Procurement advantage of direct farm sourcing stated at 3% to 15% on price, with 10% to 15% operational cost initially; long-term advantage 5% to 8% over supplier purchase.
Company is positioned as a pan-India supplier to modern trade and e-commerce across 10 cities for onion, pomegranate and orange.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables (about one-third of revenue) be reduced and can trade payables be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a client credit exposure system, stricter onboarding with PDCs and security cheques, and about INR12 crore debtor reduction in Q1. It aims at 88-94 debtor days and a 25% of sales cap; a BoB limit rise to INR20 crore plus INR20 crore for Nashik was cited; payables to farmers are expected to rise to INR10-15 crore on credit by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Nashik Sinnar project add beyond the asset-light model?
qa_highlights.answer: Prime Fresh is implementing agency for a farmer component (subsidy-led) and an IA component of INR75 crore with 40-50% grant on eligible capex; it aims at order-book model, farm-gate packhouse and cold chain, and a separate call was offered.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative capex, revenue/tonnage and margin impact, and replication to other cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex over about 18-20 months with phased balance-sheet spend; quantified margin uplift not given. Replication via subsidiary or SPV route is open, with full equity payback in up to 5 years targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Lag between procurement price changes and customer price resets?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 4 to 8 days; HoReCa up to one month; tender business up to three months, under 4% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 trading and direct expenses up faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the numbers and said it would respond by mail.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter B2C given the city footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C needs heavy upfront investment; an earlier franchise attempt cost INR55-75 lakh in 2021-2023. Management decided not to pursue it now, with B2C at 1-2% of business.

538562|2026-06.headline: Skipper Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.5% to a record INR1,310 crore, EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore, margin 10.7%; FY27 guided at 15% growth.
538562|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 4.5% YoY to a record INR1,310 crore, with EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore and margin expanding 60 bps to 10.7%. PAT rose 26% to INR56.5 crore, helped by lower finance costs and operating leverage; management said the INR433.5 crore preferential equity raise came in late July/early August and did not benefit Q1. Order book closed at a record above INR9,200 crore and Q1 inflows were about INR1,674 crore (call also cites INR1,600 crore). Management reiterated 15% FY27 revenue growth and said the year is H2-weighted, with Engineering (export-heavy) soft in Q1.

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR1,674 crore (INR1,600 crore cited later)

segments.name: Engineering (incl. export)
segments.commentary: Soft in Q1 on low export and domestic order intake in FY26 and customers deferring shipments due to high freight costs; management called it temporary. Export order inflow guided up more than 50% YoY, about INR1,100 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue muted versus last year's above INR500 crore run-rate due to commodity price volatility and trade destocking; management guides about 20% top-line growth for FY27 with some margin improvement.

segments.name: Infra (EPC services)
segments.commentary: Strong growth in Q1 and past two quarters; revenue of about INR250 crore over two quarters cited. Management expects higher growth in this segment for FY27. Order book of about INR1,800 crore is infra, roughly 25% of order inflow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%, reiterated despite Q1 growth of about 5%; management expects H2 weighting.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,000 crore-plus, implying closing order book of INR10,000 crore-plus; about INR1,100 crore from exports.
Expects about INR5,000 crore of the INR9,200 crore order book to execute in FY27; orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.
FY27 finance cost expected at 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue after the fundraise.
Long-term aspirational EBITDA margin 12%; export share of order inflow targeted at 50% long term (about 15% in FY27, 20-25% next year per management).
Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes expected to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (a few months' deferment), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa.
Indian transmission bids expected at INR90,000-100,000 crore in FY27 vs INR50,000-60,000 crore TBCB bidding in FY26.
capex_capacity: 75,000 tonne capacity expansion to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (slight delay), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa; bulk of this capacity is export-focused.
Fundraise of INR433.5 crore via preferential equity; entire proceeds used for debt repayment per management.
Subsidiaries established in Brazil and UAE; US entity expected to become operational shortly.
Two 765 kV projects secured in Maharashtra from a reputed developer in Q1.
Legacy low-margin contracts now under 5% of order book, largely executing out this year.
demand_pricing: Steel spiked in Q1 but normalised to pre-February levels by May; aluminium also eased. Management said firm-price contracts carry buffers, variable-price contracts adjust monthly, and inventory build-up and partial hedging are used.

Export inflow hit by tariffs and Middle East geopolitics last year; management says export ordering has rebounded, with advanced talks in the US, Australia, and other developed markets; Europe slower pending approvals.
Export shipments being deferred by customers due to elevated shipping costs.
Order book by segment: about 75% T&D-related infra/EPC services versus 25% of total order book; Q1 inflow almost entirely T&D.
Biggest challenge cited: quality technical manpower; company takes about 200-250 graduate trainees annually.

qa_highlights.question: Is ordering picking up versus FY26, and what is the outlook for the Indian transmission market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ordering has picked up, bids are being finalised, and inflows should translate from Q2. It expects INR90,000-1,00,000 crore of Indian transmission bids in FY27 and said about 40% of the INR9 lakh crore pipeline has been bid so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the finance cost decline due to the fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Fundraise funds arrived late July or early August, so Q1 had no benefit; the decline came from working capital management and operating leverage. FY27 finance cost guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is export revenue lost or delayed, and which segment drives 15% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export ordering has not stopped and export order inflow should rise more than 50% YoY. The 15% growth is expected from all three segments, with Infra growing fastest; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally slow due to monsoon, West Bengal elections, and freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR5,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, with short-term orders adding to this. Orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Polymer revenue muted and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to commodity price volatility and trade destocking. It expects about 20% Polymer top-line growth in FY27 with margin improvement, and says growth will come from both volume and value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited legacy low-margin contracts rolling off, better new-contract quality, operating leverage, and commodity mitigation through firm/variable price mix, inventory and hedging. It called the expansion structural and aimed toward 12% long-term margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does the delay in capacity expansion affect the 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said commissioning is deferred only by a few months to end of Q2, with no impact on the 15% target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Engineering soften while Infra jumped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Engineering is affected by weak FY26 export and domestic order intake plus shipment deferrals due to high freight costs; it called this temporary. Infra growth is from TBCB transmission EPC services, with no change in scope of work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 order inflow target, and what is the export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR7,000 crore-plus of FY27 order inflow, with about INR1,100 crore from exports (about 15% of inflow).

544862|2026-06.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
544862|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management attributed the weak quarter to seasonality, ALMM-2 (ALCM) timing shifts that delayed module off-take, and full-quarter costs of the 4 GW capacity, and reiterated FY27 guidance of a 5-6% PAT margin with an H2-weighted year. Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

financial_highlights.change: +1.8% YoY vs INR261 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR42.7 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR4.3 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR5.4 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Module manufacturing (4 GW, Tadkeshwar, Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Four module lines operating; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025 and reached full utilisation by March 2026. FY27 average utilisation assumed at about 55%, versus about 70% in FY26 per an analyst question.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Not a focus; management targets INR100-150 crore of EPC business at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop. Government EPC revenue booked in Q1 FY26 was not repeated.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin of 5-6% reiterated.
FY27 module utilisation assumed at about 55% on average across the year.
Executable order pipeline of INR845.84 crore (INR628+ crore order from July, INR42.47 crore order from August, INR175 crore LOI with MSA at signing stage) targeted for execution by December 31, 2026.
2.2 GW N-type TOPCon+ cell line on track for commissioning by end of calendar 2027.
Vision 2030: 10 GW module, 10 GW cell, 10 GW BESS and 2 GW wafer/ingot capacity; INR4,000 crore MoU with Government of Gujarat.
Module capex reduced: planned 2.5 GW module line dropped; cell project cost now about INR1,050 crore (INR700 crore debt, INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs).
capex_capacity: Module capacity 4 GW at Tadkeshwar, Gujarat; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025.
2.2 GW cell line (phase 1 of 5 GW single-site cell plan; phase 2 of 3 GW). Commissioning targeted by end CY2027.

Cell project cost about INR1,050 crore: debt of about INR700 crore at advanced discussion with lender; equity of INR350 crore via NCDs/CCDs in due diligence. QIP/preferential route abandoned due to market conditions.
Land: parcel procured per management; 30 MW power connection in Gujarat has verbal approval, written approval awaited.
Cell technology partner and KPI-linked operator being onboarded for line design, commissioning and operations.
BESS: containerised manufacturing setup under evaluation with technology partners; to sit in a separate subsidiary. No timeline given beyond 'coming quarters'.
demand_pricing: Order book approximately INR3,400 crore (per management), across confirmed POs, signed MSAs awaiting POs, and advanced-stage MSAs; management says visibility is not contingent on ALMM-2 outcome.
ALMM-2 (ALCM) on cells: no extension announced on 25 May 2026, causing project holds and customer-driven delivery rescheduling in Q1 and Q2. Management calls these timing shifts, not cancellations.
Management estimated about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment; said this was resolved by the government's selective extension to December 2026 for commissioning.

Domestic DCR cell supply constrained: three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner to supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; total about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells expected from MoU partners.
Export focus: Europe, Middle East, Africa, with US market being tested; FY27 export revenue projected to be low.
OEM/contract manufacturing for global brands under discussion; two global top-five brands already served; Q4 FY27 targeted for Indian projects.
Customer concentration: largest closed order above INR600 crore; second INR175 crore; third INR42 crore.

543442|2026-06.headline: Brand Concepts Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~11% and EBITDA rose, but PBT loss widened; management expects growth to resume from October.
543442|2026-06.overview:
Management said revenue grew almost 11% YoY and EBITDA grew on lower overheads, while the PBT loss widened marginally on higher depreciation, interest and operating investments. Primary billing took a dent from an e-commerce SKU realignment and channel consolidation, though secondary sales were said to be strong and market share was claimed to be intact. Retail tail-clipping continued: about 75-80% of the store consolidation is done, with completion targeted by September. The new hard-luggage and PP plants are ramping, with the PC unit at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only.</overview>

segments.name: Luggage / travel gear
segments.commentary: Management said luggage grew low single digits YoY in Q1; travel care overall was negative, driven by backpack SKU consolidation. Pricing pressure from new D2C entrants persists.

segments.commentary: Primary billing hit by high-volume SKU realignment; management expects e-commerce to be back on track from August 2026. Secondary sales described as strong.
