segments.commentary: EBO business was about 10% of overall business. Multiple BAGLINE stores closed as unprofitable; nine further stores on notice per analyst question. Shoppers Stop secondary growth upwards of 12% per management.

segments.name: Tommy Hilfiger
segments.commentary: Overall flattish; volume down low single digits but ASP up. Licence renewal from international counterparty is pending paperwork; 10-year business plan and royalty terms said to be closed, royalty 'same'.

segments.name: Benetton
segments.commentary: Primary de-growth; earlier strategies failed. Management pivoting to a sharp-price e-commerce line and new offline styles launching next month, with CSD entry planned.

segments.name: New brands (Off-White, Superdry, Juicy)
segments.commentary: Off-White launched about April 2026 with Bangalore and Delhi stores; plan of five stores in total, four done. Superdry luggage not yet launched; Juicy FY26 revenue INR12 crore, FY27 target INR20-22 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects company-level growth to resume from October 2026, with consolidation ~80% complete and to finish by September.
Phase three (operating leverage) expected in about 1.5 years, per management's conservative view.
Management expects EBITDA margins to keep showing a healthy trend and FY27 to be a good year.
No new debt planned beyond the government scheme already availed; FY27 end expected to be the debt peak; long-term aim of a debt-free company in about 5 years.
No major capex for the next two years unless a large order pipeline emerges; existing building can host up to four lines, with ~INR10 crore needed for another 50,000 capacity.
Apparel in-house for Juicy targeted at ~70-75% by Q3 FY28; PP launch from October could add ~20,000 pieces/month at ~INR1,500 ASP.
Management said it is too early to quantify PP revenue contribution for the festive season.
Management is not planning new Off-White stores beyond the five planned; Juicy to add a couple of stores then slow down over the next year.
capex_capacity: PC unit ~25,000 pieces/month capacity, at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only; no external clients yet.
PP plant (one machine) trials complete, targeting 75-80% utilisation within about two months; moulds to arrive by end-September with production from October.
Combined ~50,000 pieces/month capacity; ~20,000 running now, ~40,000 targeted by October or November.
Plant reportedly profitable at 20,000 pieces/month vs earlier breakeven estimate of 30,000-35,000; management estimates ~11-13% EBITDA at plant level at 40,000 pieces, not yet verified.
Building can house four lines of 25,000 each (100,000 pieces/month); ~INR10 crore of machinery adds ~50,000 capacity.
Third-party manufacturing planned; Samsonite group is a backpack client for Go-To-Wander bags. Management aims for no more than 50% captive consumption of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure persists from new D2C and premium entrants in travel gear; management says it will not chase unhealthy discounts.
Management claims no market share lost at company level; some volume decline at Tommy Hilfiger offset by higher ASP.
Travel demand reduced; raw material costs up due to war-related conditions, per management.
Management said premium-end consumers remain resilient, citing top-selling INR27,000-32,000 luggage sets at Tommy Hilfiger.
Management declined to give same-store sales growth now; will consider SSSG metrics in a couple of quarters.
Seasonality shift: Q2 now bigger than Q1 due to festive-season primary orders, and expected to continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: Tommy Hilfiger licence status and terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the international licence renewal is delayed but paperwork-only; the 10-year business plan, royalty and figures are closed, with royalty unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Manufacturing utilisation, benefit and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: PC at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption; PP ramping. Management said most of the plant margin benefit is being passed to consumers via pricing to stay relevant.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow, funding and capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is not a constraint; inventory fell ~INR5 crore, Q1 negative is temporary and INR20 crore promoter capital was committed (INR15 crore in). No new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: When does consolidation end and when does growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation about 75-80% done; stores to exit by September, e-commerce reset this month, and growth expected back from October.

qa_highlights.question: Store closure impact and INR1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reported figures are post-closures, EBO is ~10% of business, and the INR1,000 crore target over 4-5 years remains on track.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and Benetton plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory INR123 crore at June-end, about 130 days per management. Benetton had failed strategies; pivoted to e-commerce price-led line and new offline styles next month.

531225|2026-06.headline: Xtglobal Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 7.6% from 4.8% in Q4 FY26, while consolidated revenue grew only 1.1% YoY to ₹93.30 crore.
531225|2026-06.overview: Management described a steady quarter with a cautious IT services demand environment and a shift from onsite to offshore delivery. Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹719.19 crore and standalone PAT rose 19.8% YoY to ₹1.82 crore. Consolidated revenue was ₹93.30 crore (+1.1% YoY, +2% QoQ), with consolidated EBITDA of ₹7.06 crore and PAT of ₹3.89 crore (+4.3% YoY). The company added seven FinAcc engagements across Australia, the US and Ireland, and entered Ireland with its first FinAcc outsourcing client.

segments.commentary: Around 14% of revenue, described as recurring; clients typically start with AP and add AR and R2R, with one client scaling from one resource to 10.

AI moving from experimentation to practical enterprise deployment, creating both pressure and opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: How does management see PaaS evolving as a growth engine, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on Australia and Ireland/Europe; management expects these to reach about US$1 million each in local currency over the next year. International is under 10% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.question: Which areas (AI, cloud, automation, digital transformation) offer growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees most growth in AI and cloud; the company has won general empanelment in a couple of US government contracts, with individual RFPs still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to deepen wallet share with existing global clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing US clients were the main revenue base until last year; AP SaaS is 15-20% of revenue and grows with client volumes. One new client was added and incremental work is being sold to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: How to build scale in US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue to rise via public sector and onshore delivery, versus mostly offshore delivery over the past three years. Europe started with the first Irish client.

qa_highlights.question: How is GCC engagement building into larger relationships?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting mid-market GCC customers that start with 3-5 people and can grow to about 50 members, mainly in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated revenue up only 1.1% YoY and how sustainable is 7.6% EBITDA margin?

qa_highlights.question: Which services have the highest margins?

segments.commentary: Posted a positive PBT for the first time in about four years, a token amount (share ~Rs 10 lakh), driven by higher ELV feedstock inflows under EPR norms.

Margins expected to average near current levels, but may come under pressure at higher volumes, per the CFO; the 60%+ margin is not guaranteed.
TReDS platform: internal target to operationalise within FY27, contingent on RBI approval; transaction fee is the primary revenue source; no revenue quantum projected.
EPR e-trading portal is ready and integrated; awaiting government notification. Initially 5 sectors, expanding to about 15.
Travel portal: B2B live for government/PSU use; B2C launch awaits IATA empanelment. Revenue expected to be selection-fee based and slow to build.
Dividend: policy guided by DIPAM minimum of the higher of 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT; FY26 dividend already declared and subject to AGM approval.
Management declined to quantify EPR revenue potential (analyst's ~Rs 400 crore estimate for 2030-31 was called premature).
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: new verticals are being added selectively, stabilised, then scaled.
Travel portal and TReDS built on existing infrastructure; management says cost to establish was low.
Coal and mineral exchange feasibility under study; no timeline or capex quantified.
Corporate office opened in New Delhi; pan-India operations expanded.
demand_pricing: Scrap is cyclical with steel sector pricing and volumes; management expects mineral-block sales to be sustainable but cannot say whether 20-25% growth will continue.
Gross trading volume (about Rs 23,900 crore in the quarter, per an analyst) is driven by mineral block output and can swing widely; management declined to guide on it.

Competition: multiple coal exchanges are expected under the government gazette, and IEX has announced one; MSTC says it has the credibility advantage. APR (EPR) exchange: MSTC said it is the only applicant so far.
Karnataka liquor-licence auction is a new client won via the Rajasthan reference; stickiness depends on process integrity and licence tenure (e.g., 3 years).
Scrap revenue is spread across about 3,000 sellers; private-sector clients (Tata, Reliance, Vedanta, ArcelorMittal) are a stated focus.

533272|2026-06.headline: Jupiter Wagons Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR671 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 10% and PAT margin 4%.
533272|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 46% YoY to INR671 crore, with EBITDA up 9% to INR65 crore (about 10% margin) and PAT of INR26 crore (4% margin). Management described Q1 as a transition quarter in which wagon production dipped to about 1,141 units from 1,347 units in Q4 as new private-wagon designs went through prototype approval, and consolidated revenue fell marginally sequentially. Key corporate events were the 100% acquisition of Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory, a partnership with Lucchini RS and SIMEST for a combined 25% stake for about INR290 crore, and the RDSO approval of Stone India's freight brake systems with commercial production from July 2026. Jupiter Electric Mobility (JEM) won BESS projects in West Bengal and now has a BESS order book of about 500 MW valued above INR500 crore.</overview>

segments.name: Railway wagons (incl. private)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR3,000 crore; around 80% is private wagon orders per management. Q1 production dipped on prototype approvals for new designs; management expects improvement from Q2 and about 7,000 pending wagons.

segments.name: Wheelsets (JTRWF / Odisha project)
segments.commentary: Order book close to INR700 crore. Odisha facility rated at 100,000 wheelsets; axle line targeted for FY27 and wheel line for FY28, with revenue target INR2,500-3,000 crore and EBITDA of at least 15%.

segments.commentary: Order book about INR500 crore. Management cited substantial increase in CV bodies and axles in Q1, while wagons declined.

segments.name: Stone India (freight brakes)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received; commercial production from July 2026. Expected borderline negative EBITDA in Q2, positive from Q3; about 15%+ EBITDA from FY28. Management targets 100% internal supply of freight brakes by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: JWL DAKO JV
segments.commentary: Expected to start execution in coming quarters; management expects all JVs except JEM to report positive EBITDA before end of Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects 60-70% of current order book to be executed in FY27, with most wagon deliveries scheduled in FY27.
Wagon execution expected to improve over next three quarters versus last year; sharp rise in wagon numbers from Q2 FY27.
JEM targets BESS order book of about INR1,000 crore in FY27 and at least INR5,000 crore over the next three years; EBITDA positive from FY28.
Odisha wheelset project: axle line commissioning in FY27 and wheel line in FY28; majority of capex expected by Q1 FY28; Lucchini RS and SIMEST equity infusion expected before mid-September 2026.

capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield railway facility: rated capacity about 100,000 wheelsets, 50% for domestic/captive use and 50% for export; partial production targeted by end FY27/Q4-Q1 FY28, full commissioning FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wagon production fall sequentially to 1,141 units from 1,347?

qa_highlights.question: Odisha wheelset economics: capacity phases, EBITDA and ramp?

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiaries loss-making and when do they turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Stone India borderline negative in Q2, positive from Q3; all JVs except JEM expected positive before end-Q3; JEM EBITDA positive only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Wheelset project funding after new partner?

qa_highlights.question: Project IRR and funding for West Bengal BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Project IRR 15%+ due to vertical integration (own containers, BMS, EMS); funding via internal accruals or debt yet to be decided.

544866|2026-06.headline: Molbio Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹408 crore with 25% EBITDA margin and PAT ₹52.7 crore; FY27 guidance ~25% top-line growth.
544866|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹408 crore in Q1 FY27, with 164 devices and 62.4 lakh test kits sold. EBITDA was ₹104 crore (25% margin) and PAT ₹52.7 crore (about 13%). Export revenue was about ₹67 crore (16% of revenue), helped by a catch-up of orders deferred from Q4 FY26 due to Gulf disruption. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24–25%, while cautioning that quarters are non-linear and OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~₹67 crore (16% of revenue), includes catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals

financial_highlights.value: Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore; Prognosys ~₹11 crore; OptraScan minimal

financial_highlights.metric: OptraScan loss (Q1 FY27 and comparable 5-month period FY26)

segments.name: Truenat molecular platform (core)
segments.commentary: Kits are about 75% of revenue; installed base ~12,500 machines in 90+ countries, 43 assays across 30 diseases; 40M+ cumulative tests. Gross margin 60–63% across devices and kits per management.

segments.name: Prognosys (70% subsidiary, digital X-ray)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹154 crore and PAT ~₹12 crore; management expects similar ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27. Q1 FY27 revenue ~₹11 crore; US FDA approval for digital imaging and EU MDR for X-ray products.

segments.name: OptraScan (60% subsidiary, digital pathology)
segments.commentary: US FDA clearance received July 2026 for end-to-end workflow incl. software and AI; ~$30 million fresh equity invested. Not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected FY28–FY29.

segments.name: Bigtec Labs (100% R&D subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Bangalore R&D entity with 150+ scientists and 220+ total staff; intercompany kit sales to Bigtec are eliminated on consolidation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at roughly 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 24–25%.
Prognosys expected to deliver ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27, similar to FY26.
OptraScan not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected in FY28 and FY29.
Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range for the year, in line with historical levels.
HPV-related revenue timing and volumes to be guided next quarter; R&D to stay at 5–6% of revenue.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds ~₹200 crore: ~₹72 crore for automation and ~₹105 crore for an integrated R&D centre in Bangalore consolidating Bigtec staff.
Current utilisation: ~58% for test kits and ~42% for devices; management says minimal capex can allow doubling of top line from FY26 levels.
Facilities: two kit plants in Goa, device manufacturing in Vizag, a small kit facility in Bangalore, and a Pune site for OptraScan.
Any further manufacturing consolidation in Goa to be funded from internal accruals; no major capex planned beyond what is disclosed.
Certifications: MDSAP; EU IVDR for Truenat CT/NG; EU MDR for X-ray; US FDA for Prognosys imaging and OptraScan.
demand_pricing: TB remains the bulk of the Truenat test mix, mainly public health; management says pricing is similar across diseases in public health.

Government of India HPV validation led by AIIMS; recommended for national rollout; health technology assessment found it cost-effective for women aged 30–45. Volumes not yet quantified; WHO prequalification application in progress.
Two-year TB rate contract with the government signed last month.
India molecular diagnostics share cited at ~90%; ~8,000–9,000 of an estimated 25,000–30,000 TB diagnostic centres are on Truenat.
Pricing is contract-based, not MRP-led; realisation moves driven by device variant mix (Uno/Duo/Quattro), geography and dollar movements.
Export business started around 2023; distributors in 90 countries; ramp expected to take longer, with EU and US entry being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on the HPV tender and test kit off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are in place and a recommendation has been made to roll out the test in the national programme; volumes will be clearer by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the life cycle of a Truenat device and are consumables exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D at 5–6% of revenue; ₹72 crore automation and ~₹105 crore Bangalore R&D centre are the major capex items; no other major capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore, Prognosys ~₹11 crore, OptraScan minimal. FY26 Prognosys revenue ₹154 crore, PAT ~₹12 crore; OptraScan loss ~₹9 crore in the period.

qa_highlights.question: Is device volume growing and how will the TB/other-disease mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range, in line with history; kit volumes in Q1 were well above Q4 FY26. Non-TB assays such as HPV and hepatitis expected to contribute meaningfully over 2–3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TB market share sustainable and what is the realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Truenat is the only WHO-endorsed battery-operated point-of-care TB test; remaining centres use microscopy. Pricing is contract-based; realisation moves reflect device mix and FX, with gross margin of 60–63%.

risks_watch: Quarterly lumpiness: management asks investors to track annually; Q1 was helped by export catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals linked to the Gulf situation.
OptraScan loss-making in FY27 and ramp dependent on US lab and hospital adoption after July 2026 FDA clearance.
HPV national-programme volumes and timing not yet quantified; next guidance deferred to next quarter.
Inventory days still high at 230 (trailing 12M), though down from 280 in March.
Export ramp slower than expected; past export volumes have been uneven.
Dependence on public-health TB programme for the bulk of domestic revenue under a two-year rate contract.

500148|2026-06.headline: UFlex Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin at 17%.
500148|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and reported EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin up 480 bps to 17%. Normalized EBITDA (after Rs 825 million forex derivative adjustment) was Rs 8,373 million, up 78%, at a 15.5% margin. Overseas operations (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria) contributed about 91% of the Rs 4,410 million incremental EBITDA, while India volumes and Aseptic softened. Management guided to 35% growth in FY27 revenue and EBITDA over FY26, while saying Q2 would see some normalization from exceptional Q1 realizations.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBITDA (post Rs 825 mn forex derivative adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 580 million, 1.5% margin in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Packaging Films (India)
segments.commentary: Volume 29,323 MT, up 9.1% QoQ but declined YoY against a high Q1 FY26 base affected by industry supply shortage. Converters resumed buying after May-June price normalization.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Volume 31,724 MT, up 18% YoY, supported by US onshoring push and constrained West Asia/India imports.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Volume 35,653 MT, flat YoY; low-priced imports pressured CPP, CIS BOPET steady. Demand expected to moderate next quarter on seasonal holidays.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa
segments.commentary: Volume 39,486 MT, up 14.9% YoY and 16.5% QoQ; Egypt led growth and Nigeria benefited from export opportunities as customers derisked supply chains.

segments.name: Packaging (Aseptic and flexible)
segments.commentary: Volume down 8.4% YoY to 37,285 MT due to shift to high-margin products in India, Aseptic softness from duty-free Indonesian imports, larger pack-size mix overseas and West Asia consignment delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of about 35% over FY26 (management also cited 30%-plus in places); management said it normally avoids guidance.
Q2 expected to see some normalization from exceptionally strong Q1 realizations; management asked investors to benchmark YoY, not QoQ.
Expects FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus; said margins could be better if geopolitical conditions hold.
Debt-EBITDA targeted at about 3x in FY28 and below 3x by FY29; interest cost expected to fall by about 1% over the next year.
Volume to roughly double over three years to FY29 as Egypt Aseptic, Noida recycling and Mexico WPP ramp; FY26-FY29 CAGR indicated at least 10%, to be confirmed by IR.

Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) expected commissioning in H1 FY27, targeting around 30% utilization in year one annualized (about 2 billion packs in FY27 if started 1 October) and 60-70% in year two.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex Rs 4,782 million: Egypt Aseptic Rs 1,236 mn, Mexico WPP bags Rs 205 mn, Noida Sector 155 recycling Rs 320 mn, Dharwad BOPP line Rs 215 mn.
Noida Sector 155 recycling plant (39,000 MT per annum) commissioned 30 April 2026; capex about USD 30-32 million, no further capex planned.
Mexico 80-million-unit WPP bags plant commissioned 31 July 2026; capex about USD 54 million.
Egypt Aseptic greenfield (12 billion packs): over USD 100 million spent, about USD 15 million remaining; commissioning H1 FY27.
Dharwad BOPP brownfield: USD 10 million spent, about USD 50+ million planned over FY27-FY28. Remaining new capex about USD 80-100 million; management says FY27 capex cycle about 75% complete.
Domestic utilization about 70-73%; specialty films (metallizer, ultra-high barrier) utilized about 30-40%. India Aseptic installed capacity about 24 billion packs.
demand_pricing: BOPP prices up about 25-32% and BOPET up about 30-35% from February 2026 (pre West Asia war) levels, per management.
Management said raw material prices rose but less than finished goods, and prices now appear to be normalizing; prices described as stable at current levels while the West Asia crisis persists.
Overseas selling prices said to be about 2.5x India prices; overseas margins higher because pass-through is easier.
Aseptic faces duty-free imports from Indonesia under India trade treaty at aggressive prices; management says value realization improved via shift to value-added films.
Management said it carries little inventory, so Q1 realizations were passed through to customers; customers prefer UFlex's integrated, local supply for security of supply.

qa_highlights.question: How are price realizations and raw material trends shaping up in India and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; raw material costs rose less than finished goods prices, which are normalizing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 margin and growth sustainable for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing 2-3 years of capex; FY27 guided to about 35% revenue and EBITDA growth over FY26, with FY27 EBITDA margin about 14%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalization expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined QoQ benchmarking; said Q2 will normalize from exceptional Q1 realization but growth remains about 35% YoY, with shipment timing risk around West Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.5% normalized margin sustainable and how much currency impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex impact about Rs 70 crore in the quarter (Rs 825 mn per the prepared remarks); management said margins are sustainable over next 3 years, not just FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash: debt reduction vs capex vs shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash to go to debt reduction; leverage to fall to about 3x in FY28. No buyback planned; management prefers wealth creation via growth. 60-70% of future capex to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate and rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rated AA by CRISIL and India Ratings; interest cost fell 0.3-0.4% this quarter and management targets a further 1% reduction in the next year.

517498|2026-06.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
517498|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.</overview>

segments.name: Solar cells
segments.commentary: Production 259 MW vs 126 MW in Q1 FY26, utilisation 92%; average cell efficiency 23.3%. About 153 MW sold externally in Q1, with the rest consumed captively for modules.

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Production 103 MW vs 50 MW, utilisation 81% vs 39%. Module margins are lower than cell margins, and module-led mix is the main driver of the margin decline.

guidance_outlook: Cell utilisation of about 92% to be held; management expects close to full run-rate utilisation across lines except TOPCon upgrade downtime.

TOPCon upgrade of 600 MW mono PERC line to 750 MW TOPCon, lifting total cell capacity to 1.3 GW (about 55% TOPCon), expected by March 2027 at about INR270 crore, funded from internal accruals with possible debt.
Management expects payback of 2 to 3 years on the TOPCon capex; cell efficiency expected around 25% post-upgrade.

Phase 3 (4 GW total, cell and module, two phases of 2 GW each): land approval expected in August; construction targeted mid-September; equipment lead time 4 to 6 months; trial run after about 2 months post installation; management says no change in timelines or capex.
Margins: management expects cell margins to fall somewhat but not aggressively, and believes current margin levels can hold for a year or two.
Silver consumption cut 20% in FY26, with a further 10% reduction target for cells.
capex_capacity: Current capacity: cells about 1.2 GW pre-upgrade, rising to 1.35 GW (per management, with 750 MW TOPCon) after the TOPCon upgrade; the upgrade adds about 150 MW of cell capacity.

Phase 3: 4 GW of additional cell and 4 GW of module capacity in two 2 GW phases; location moved from Andhra Pradesh (Naidupeta) to West Bengal (land shortlisted near Falta facility, approval pending).
Expected timeline: land approval in August 2026, construction from mid-September, equipment ordered around December, arrival April to May 2027, about 9 months to complete, then 2 months of trials.
Module utilisation of 81% described as close to full effective utilisation; industry comfort range cited at 70-75%.
demand_pricing: Prices softened in the previous quarter; management says prices rose in the current quarter on ALMM-related expectations, but the ALMM cell mandate was deferred from June to December 2026.
Current cell price quoted at about USD0.13 per Wp and module at about INR21 per watt, against Q1 levels of about USD0.125 and INR20.50.

Demand is mainly DCR (PM-Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM); management sees no decline. Inventory rose about 7% QoQ and management attributes it to monsoon-season offtake slowdown and captive cell blocking in modules.
Input costs: silver prices have eased but imported paste carries a lag; wafer prices are flat. The West Asia conflict has raised BOM costs for modules, not cells.
Management said Q1 margin decline reflects lower cell prices and higher silver and BOM cost, alongside mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company moving Phase 3 from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, and does it change timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to module-heavy mix plus lower cell prices and higher silver/BOM costs; it expects cell margins to fall but not aggressively and to hold current levels for a year or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory rising, and what were Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 7% QoQ, which management attributed to monsoon-led offtake slowdown and cell cost blocked in modules; Q1 realisations were about USD0.125/Wp for cells and INR20.50/W for modules.

qa_highlights.question: What returns does the TOPCon upgrade generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company targeting a larger order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book reports only firm purchase orders and repeat business, and the company is not targeting a higher order book; it sees regular DCR-market inquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ability to execute and ramp Phase 3 at the same pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TOPCon conversion will serve as practical training before the greenfield expansion; it cited the mono PERC installation timeline as precedent.

risks_watch: Margin compression as module mix rises: EBITDA margin fell 13 percentage points YoY to 34%, and management expects further cell margin softening.
Phase 3 execution: relocation to West Bengal depends on pending land approval (targeted August 2026); no incentive terms disclosed yet.
Inventory build (about 7% QoQ) and monsoon-season offtake; watch whether it clears in Q2.
ALMM cell mandate deferred to December 2026 and dependence on domestic cell capacity; price direction after that date.
Investor-communication concerns raised by several participants (valuation, share-price moves, lack of disclosure). The company said it is increasing investor interactions.
Pledge release: promoter pledge reduction from 80% to 16% depends on lender formalities; timing unconfirmed.
517498|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and utilisation and on the debt repayment, but defensive and vague on valuation, share price, Phase 3 incentives and cost savings, where it declined to give figures and said it would disclose later.

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +56.9% YoY; +16.3% QoQ (Q1 FY26 Rs 464 mn; Q4 FY26 Rs 626 mn)
+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)
+95% YoY (from Rs 60 mn); +39.3% QoQ (from Rs 84 mn)
Management said it improved steadily through FY26

segments.name: Direct advertisers
segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.name: PiiX (Apple ecosystem)
segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

guidance_outlook: Long-term 'Rule of 50' framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% or higher, with a vision to 2030.
Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.
Expects a growing share of optimisation decisions to be made by the Neural Engine over the next 12 to 18 months.
FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Mobavenue Neural Engine launched as a unified AI layer at the core of GMP360; management said core decisioning moved fully to neural network systems in FY26.
Platform processes over 1.3 billion signals per day and reaches about 2.6 billion devices monthly, with decisions in under 15 milliseconds.
Campaign lifecycle (plan, launch, create, report) said to run in under 59 seconds / under a minute per step.
Asset-light model; management said platforms can scale with limited incremental infrastructure investment.
Balance sheet supported by a FY26 preferential raise (about Rs 50 crore per an analyst's reference); capital prioritised for AI stack, international expansion and selective acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Growth led by direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail, plus premium formats such as connected TV and video streaming.
Revenue per outcome of Rs 49.94 on 14.16 million verified outcomes; management said both outcomes and price per outcome are rising.
Top five sectors (FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Travel) contribute about 70-80% of revenue; management did not disclose top-5 or top-10 client shares.
Data and supply costs are the largest cost line and are largely variable with revenue.
Named global competitors: AppLovin, Unity and The Trade Desk; named India competitors: Affle and InMobi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.
Regulatory risk, which management named as the primary risk; also currency risk and AI disruption.
Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.
Deployment of the FY26 preferential raise into acquisitions, which management has not yet named.
539682|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability; the tone was more qualitative when answering questions on client concentration, the scale of PiiX revenue and the acquisition pipeline, where few figures were given.

543419|2026-06.headline: Shriram Properties posted record Q1 FY27 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) but revenue of INR271 crores (+4%) and PAT of INR11 crores lag, with growth back-ended.
543419|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales value rose 10% YoY to INR484 crores on 0.85 million sq ft, the company's highest-ever Q1, driven by launches at Shriram Stellar (Chennai), Shriram Southbrook (Kolkata) and Green Meadows phase (Chennai). Revenue of INR271 crores, EBITDA of INR42 crores and PAT of INR11 crores were steady, with margins diluted by low-margin legacy Kolkata handovers. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance, pointing to Q2 and H2 OCs (about 2,900 units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential) and a back-ended launch calendar. Net debt to equity stood at 0.29x, with gearing expected to rise in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow before new project investment
Closing cash / gross external debt / net debt
financial_highlights.value: INR219 crores / INR651 crores / INR432 crores

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Shriram Stellar, a premium launch late June, sold about 20% on launch weekend; Green Meadows new phase (0.2 million sq ft) also launched.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Shriram Southbrook (0.4 million sq ft) launched; branded plotted development had about 55% of inventory sold within 30 days. Legacy Grand One and Sunshine One handovers carry thin margins.

segments.name: Bengaluru / Pune
segments.commentary: Doddagubbi JDA (about 0.7 million sq ft saleable) added in Q1, expected on board end-Q3/early Q4; Manjari (Pune, 2.3 million sq ft via FSI purchase) expected to launch after plan approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: sales value INR3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth) and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth), per Q&A.
Revenue recognition expected to grow at least 20% in FY27; PAT growth guided at 20-25%; FY27 PBT margin about 8-9%.
FY28 mission reiterated: sales value about INR5,000 crores, revenue INR2,500 crores, PBT about INR250 crores (around 10% margin); FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

Handover pipeline: 410+ units of pent-up handovers, 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) for OC in Q2, and 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores) for H2; total 2,900+ units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential for balance of FY27.
Management expects gearing to rise temporarily in FY27, with long-term comfort at 0.5x-1.0x net debt to equity.
Management reiterated FY27 sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores; launch GDV of about INR6,000 crores from 7.23 million sq ft targeted supply.
capex_capacity: FY27 launch calendar: about 6 million sq ft planned out of 7 million sq ft potential across Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; 2 projects (0.7 million sq ft) launched in Q1.

Current pipeline 33.7 million sq ft (16 million ongoing, 17.7 million upcoming) with GDV potential about INR13,530 crores; 7.3 million sq ft (GDV above INR6,000 crores) at advanced stage for addition in 3-6 months.
Kolkata: about 110 acres of land; 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval obtained pre-election, to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possible in FY27.
Management targets nearly doubling the upcoming pipeline over 18-24 months.
Cash flow: INR88 crores invested in new projects in Q1.
demand_pricing: Sustenance sales prices rising about 4-5% annually, versus 10-15% in the post-COVID period; launch prices set by competition in each micro-market.
Average mid-market selling price about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft, versus about INR5,000 pre-COVID; Sunshine 2 and 3 realising about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft.
Management sees no material slowdown in conversion or housing loan application momentum; Bengaluru launches described as slow, upper-end investment demand flagged as softer.
Legacy Shankari (Chennai) and Grand One (Kolkata) realise about INR4,500-5,000 and INR18-24 lakh tickets, dragging margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR2,500 crores revenue, INR250 crores PBT) still intact and how credible is a 10% PBT margin versus historic EBITDA of 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.

534076|2026-06.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR1,014 crore and EBITDA rose 42% to INR147 crore, a 14.5% margin; management keeps the 13% FY27 margin guidance.
534076|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,014 crore, up 9% QoQ and 6% YoY, led by the steel business on favourable realizations and healthy demand. EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR147 crore and margin expanded to 14.5% from 10.8%, which management attributed to steelmaking execution, price realisation and operating leverage. PAT nearly doubled to INR65 crore from INR35 crore. Management said price increases were largely war surcharges, and it kept FY27 guidance of 13% EBITDA margin and 7-8% volume growth, while stating 9% is a stretch. A leadership change was announced with Pankaj Malhan as MD and CEO, and Parmod Sagar continues as Chairman.</overview>

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Main driver of Q1 revenue growth on favourable realisations and healthy demand; flow control business cited as the growth engine, with one large group's market share up almost twofold in about 6 months. Management said Dalmia business is flat and growth came from RHIM India.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Recovered in Q1 on seasonal maintenance demand; management said cement season is almost over by end-September.

segments.name: Industrial (non-ferrous, glass)
segments.commentary: Described as weak in Q1 with few projects in H1; silica and glass project orders expected in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Coke oven project (PSU)
segments.commentary: Final-stage negotiation with pricing adjustment pending; production to start next month, with a 14-16 month project life.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 13% for FY27 reaffirmed; management said upside possible only if raw material costs ease.
Volume growth guidance of 7-8% for FY27 (management said 9% is a stretch); long-term volume guidance of steel/cement market growth plus 1-2%.
Management said the EUR45 million group pricing and mix benefit is already reflected in Q1 and that India will contribute proportionately.
Capex guidance of INR80-100 crore per year maintained, covering Dalmia plant modernisation, 4PRO machinery, robotics and maintenance.
MINPRO JV (51% RHIM, 49% Khemka) targeted to start production around Q4 FY27; initial investment about INR35 crore over two years, EBITDA 8-10%, payback under 3 years after production.
Quartzite mines (Chiraipani and Bhikampali) expected to open by end of Q1 FY27, with cost benefits from Q2.
Magnesite prices up 6-8% over the last two months; company is working on recipe optimisation and price pass-through.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR8 crore in Q1 vs INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; management kept the INR80-100 crore annual run-rate.
MINPRO greenfield mineral processing facility in Odisha, via JV with Khemka Refractories; roughly INR35 crore initial investment over two years.
Quartzite mines Chiraipani and Bhikampali came with the Dalmia deal; all licences received.
SAIL SMS4 expansion (about 6-6.5 million tonnes) expected to open refractory tenders in about 6-8 months.
Four or five products being transferred to India production within about one year (investor deck pages 21-22).
demand_pricing: Management cited steel production growth, high capacity utilisation and blast furnace/steelmaking investments as demand support; Indian steel grew 7-8% in H1 and steel capex of INR50,000-60,000 crore is expected this financial year.
Cement demand strong, but cement margins under pressure from fuel, energy and raw material costs.
Competitive pressure from domestic and multinational players, with greenfield and brownfield capacity additions and some excess capacity.
Exports reduced QoQ in Q1 per CFO; management expects isostatic flow control export growth over a year.
Alumina prices stable over the last six months; magnesite up 6-8% recently.
Realisation rise attributed mostly to war surcharges and product mix; no price/mix/FX split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Split of ~12% realisation growth into price, mix and currency; sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: No split given. CFO said most price increases were war surcharges, so growth is primarily product-mix driven.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capex only INR8 crore vs INR150 crore guidance; will guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term capex of INR80-100 crore a year unchanged; covers Dalmia modernisation, 4PRO robotics and maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth of about 9% be achieved for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 7-8% is achievable but 9% is a stretch unless large high-volume orders come in.

qa_highlights.question: How should medium-term margins be viewed; split between Dalmia and RHIM India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia flat; growth from RHIM India (flow control heavy, Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur). Medium-term margin supported by MINPRO and captive mines; no numeric range given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EUR45 million group pricing benefit flow into India?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefit is group-wide across six regions; India contributes proportionately and it is already in Q1 numbers. FY27 margin guidance held at 13%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q1 numbers affected by project orders, and what is the H2 project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No project revenue in Q1. Coke oven project to start next month; glass and silica projects expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quartzite mine and MINPRO JV deliver quantified savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantification still in progress by FP&A; management will share later. Mine opening expected by end-Q1 with benefits from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Auditor resignation and goodwill impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Auditor change aligned with group auditor rotation; Dalmia goodwill fully written off, non-cash and below EBITDA, with headroom. No reversal planned.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (magnesite up 6-8%) and geopolitical risk (war surcharge dependence) could limit the 13% margin.
Volume guidance gap: H1 volume growth is below the 7-9% range, requiring a strong H2 for 7-8% growth.
Weak industrial segment until Q3-Q4 project orders (glass, silica) materialise.
Export volumes declined QoQ in Q1 and management has no near-term recovery timeline.
Capex run-rate far below the INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; check whether it catches up.
Execution on MINPRO (Q4 FY27 start) and quartzite mine (cost benefit from Q2).
CEO transition to Pankaj Malhan and auditor change at the AGM.

505978|2026-06.headline: Triton Valves Q1 FY27 group consolidated sales rose 38.5% YoY to ₹186.5 crore; EBITDA ₹12.4 crore, with ₹4.75 crore one-time tax credit lifting PAT to ~₹9.75 crore.
505978|2026-06.overview: Management reported group consolidated sales of about ₹186.5 crore, up roughly 17.5% QoQ and 38.5% YoY, with about 20% volume growth and the rest value growth. EBITDA was about ₹12.4 crore versus ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY (the slide labelled the YoY figure incorrectly). Gross margin contracted about 145 bps QoQ and 181 bps YoY, which management attributed to commodity pass-through with copper and brass prices near historic highs and the Iran/war disruption. Management also flagged that climate control shrank, metals was hit by delayed Middle East raw material supply, and the merger tax credit flattered PAT.

financial_highlights.value: Down ~145 bps QoQ and ~181 bps YoY
financial_highlights.change: attributed to commodity pass-through, not absolute margin erosion

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Sales ₹103 crore, up from ₹78 crore YoY and ₹86 crore QoQ; growth led by tubeless (~25% volume YoY), TPMS (~75-80% YoY) and EV components (~103% YoY). Tube valves ex-motorcycle segment grew ~20%. Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines running above 85-90% utilisation.

segments.name: Metals (Triton Valves Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹79 crore, up from ~₹50-52 crore YoY and ₹68 crore QoQ; capacity utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, implying ~30% headroom. Current ROCE above 16%, with management targeting 20%+ and possibly 25%. Scrap sales now netted off under Ind AS, reducing reported standalone top line without affecting EBITDA.

segments.name: Climate control
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹3.9 crore, down YoY and QoQ. Management cited Chinese dumping, copper costs and a weak AC season; it is lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected to be quiet, with recovery from Oct-Nov.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a 'reasonably good' Q2 if the second half of the quarter holds, and says FY27 will be much better than FY26.
Annualised Q1 group EBITDA ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26; PBT, EBITDA and revenue expected to run slightly above annualised Q1 levels.
Group ROCE expected to rise from ~12.5% to 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid-next year; new investments targeted at 20-25% internal ROCE.
Ambition of a ₹1,000 crore revenue target by about FY30; management says it has a plan that does not depend on climate control recovery.
EV component vertical targeted at ~₹100 crore over the next few quarters, with climate control also scaling to ~₹100 crore if trade remediation happens.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is not expected until commodity prices stabilise; management said it would take a long time.
Tax credit of ~₹4.75 crore already availed, plus a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore claimed, subject to assessment; no advance tax outflow expected for ~14-15 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 group capex planned at ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore for automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore for metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment).
About 50-60% of the ₹15 crore is expected to be commercialised in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation; management said capacity will run out during the year without investment.
Metals utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, leaving ~30% volume headroom.
Climate control has spare capacity; management said it only needs orders.
demand_pricing: Automotive growth described as ~80% vehicle production growth and ~20% share gain; passenger car and two-wheeler production grew ~12-15% YoY in Q1 (per management).
Management expects automotive growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 but remain positive; new programmes cited with AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch (LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA in TPMS).

Metals: Q1 started slowly from Middle East raw material disruption; ~₹10 crore of metals sales were not delivered on time due to Hormuz issues. Demand strong into Q2; management expects Q3 seasonal traction in metals and climate control.
Prices pass through to automotive and climate control customers every three months. Brass selling price to external customers now above ₹1,000/kg vs ~₹500-550/kg last July-August.
Management expects metals to reach 60%+ of group revenue over 2-3 years; special alloys (naval brass, marine grades) being developed as import substitutes.
Climate control faces Chinese dumping; management is refusing to cut margins to win volume.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview:
Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.</overview>

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview:
Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.</overview>

544466|2026-06.headline: Aditya Infotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 89.5% YoY to INR1,402 crore; EBITDA margin 14.8%, adjusted PAT INR142.2 crore.
544466|2026-06.overview:
Revenue of INR1,402 crore grew 89.5% YoY, with CP PLUS contributing about 87% of revenue and IP products about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio. EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR208 crore, with margin up 604 bps to 14.8%, helped by product and brand mix and operating efficiencies. Gross margin was 30.8%, up 8-10 bps YoY but moderated from Q4 as lower-cost inventory was exhausted. Adjusted PAT of INR142.2 crore rose 332.5% YoY, aided by a 59% fall in finance costs; management reiterated its FY27 EBITDA guidance of 14-15%.</overview>

531201|2026-06.headline: Shilchar Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 134.60 crore with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore, hit by West Asia shipping costs and slow price pass-through.
531201|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 134.60 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore. Management attributed the soft quarter to a sharp rise in container costs from the West Asia crisis, which delayed export dispatches, and to slow negotiations to pass on raw material price increases on domestic orders. Management said it lost roughly Rs 30-35 crore of potential revenue and that Q1 capacity utilisation was about 60-65%. It maintained FY27 guidance (Rs 800 crore revenue was referenced by an analyst, not reiterated as a number) and expects Q2 to be notably better than Q1, with Phase-3 expansion (6,500 MVA) due for commissioning in April 2027.

Phase-3 expansion (about 6,500 MVA) on track for commissioning in April 2027; new facility to drive growth from FY28; bigger-KV transformer orders expected later due to customer audits, approvals and type testing.
Margin normalisation depends on exports returning; if domestic-heavy mix persists, margins could dip slightly. New capacity to carry lower initial margins to build references.
capex_capacity: Phase-3 expansion adds about 6,500 MVA; commissioning targeted April 2027, possibly slightly earlier than projected.
Civil foundation work complete; PEB erection and utility work progressing; all equipment ordered.
Additional about 4.5 acres of land bought adjacent to existing Gavasad site for future expansion; product and KV class not yet disclosed.
Prototyping for larger transformers takes about 3-4 months after production starts; discussions under way with a few customers on bigger units.
Company will not supply state utility companies; plans to focus on exports once domestic references are established.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand in both export and domestic markets remains firm; customers are buying minimum volumes due to freight costs and uncertainty.

Management says competition is not the issue for exports: customers are not buying from rivals, just holding purchases.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to call it a loss but said Rs 30-35 crore could have been done without the crisis; it reiterated FY27 top-line target with no anticipated problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost increase was passed to customers?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay near 30% EBITDA, and will the 220 KV expansion be lower margin?

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 export focus not shifted to domestic earlier, leaving capacity underused?

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capacity utilisation and export/domestic revenue split and receivable/inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was about 60-65%; export/domestic revenue split and inventory and receivable days were not disclosed on the call and will be sent by email.

risks_watch: Persistent West Asia conflict keeping container costs elevated (three to five times pre-crisis for some routes) and delaying export orders.
Q1 EBITDA margin (about 21.7% implied) well below the roughly 30% historically cited; Q2 margin recovery depends on domestic price pass-through and mix.
Phase-3 commissioning slippage in April 2027, and ramp-up of larger KV transformers which need customer approval and type testing.

This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.</overview>
