qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

524372|2026-06.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.
524372|2026-06.overview: Orchid Pharma reported Q1 FY27 on a combined basis after the Dhanuka Laboratories merger (effective 10 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2024), with FY25 and FY26 restated. Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: up ~15% from INR263 crore in Q1 FY26
up ~3 percentage points from ~30% in Q1 FY26
up from INR10 crore in Q1 FY26
down from INR1,398 crore in FY25
down ~4 percentage points from ~36% in FY25
EBITDA loss ~INR50 lakh, much better than prior quarter
earlier quarterly run-rate cited as INR20-25 crore

segments.name: Cephalosporin API / core business
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes and pricing fell 15-20% by product in a difficult cephalosporin year. Cefixime faces the most margin pressure, mainly in rest-of-world markets. 7-ACA pricing has been stable for about a year.

segments.name: Exblifep (Cefepime-Enmetazobactam)
segments.commentary: Europe volumes grew about 300% QoQ in Q3 FY26, about 170-175% in Q4 FY26 and about 50% in Q1 FY27. The Russia licence has an estimated 10-year value of about USD178 million, not current revenue. South Africa registration is done and GCC coverage is in place, but Middle East rollout is delayed by regional conflict.

segments.name: AMS (Antimicrobial Stewardship)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Orblicef and other brands. Quarterly EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR50 lakh.

segments.name: NP-NC (Dhanuka Laboratories)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore in Q1 FY27, against an earlier quarterly run-rate of INR20-25 crore. Management said it would not reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 YoY revenue growth guidance; it said it hopes for better QoQ sales in H2, when regulated demand is seasonally stronger.
Merger synergies are expected to show initial benefits from FY28.

Cefiderocol: facility commissioning targeted for December 2026, then validation and initial batches in January-March 2027. Indian approval expected 6-9 months after that, subject to a DCGI trial waiver, so around Q3 FY28.
7-ACA (Jammu): first commercial batch targeted by March 2027. Ramp-up to 80-100% utilisation within the first year, with long-term split of 80% captive and 20% third-party sales.

US formulations strategy: guidance still 2030, with annual updates only. Generic ANDA filings from the cefiderocol facility take a few years; some new molecules may be filed by end of next year, with nothing commercial before 2028.
capex_capacity: 7-ACA project capex about INR750 crore, with commissioning and first commercial batch targeted by March 2027.
Cefiderocol project capex about USD20-25 million; facility commissioning by December 2026.
Management said FY27 capex is not significantly large beyond completing the 7-ACA and cefiderocol projects.
Equipment originally sourced from China was rerouted through Italy, adding execution complexity without changing timelines.

Jammu site chosen for low power costs, abundant water and cheap steam from agricultural waste, plus GST benefit. PLI incentive expected for 2 years, with extension to be sought after the plant starts.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry still has overcapacity and cutthroat competition in non-regulated markets.

7-ACA weighted average price about USD60/kg per management, stable over 10-12 years. 7-ACA supply is concentrated among 3-4 Chinese producers (Sinopharm Weiqida, Zhuhai United, Yili Pharmaceutical, Livzon named).
Cefixime is under the most margin stress, driven by rest-of-world volumes.
Management expects regulated-market demand to improve over the next 2-3 quarters, with H2 seasonally stronger.
Ceftriaxone non-sterile supply from the new 7-ACA-linked capacity is planned for other Indian sterile manufacturers, which currently import from China.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover in H2 FY27 or only in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-regulated competition will persist and is hard to predict. It hopes regulated demand improves over the next two to three quarters, and called Q1 mediocre.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 7-ACA ramp-up and captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up to 80-100% by the end of year one, starting slowly. Long-term guidance is 80% in-house and 20% third-party. All output goes in-house until customer GMP approvals are obtained.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant new capex beyond completing 7-ACA (INR750 crore) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth reach about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not be prudent to give an annual growth number at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Exblifep partner pipeline and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced talks for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco and Australia. Management does not guide yearly numbers; the USD1-2 billion is lifetime potential. Management hopes for three or four more agreements by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of Chinese 7-ACA price cuts once the plant is running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese producers have stable pricing and no cartel-like Pen G situation, so it sees little room for drastic cuts. It also acknowledged that Chinese pricing is unpredictable and that the company is working on yield and tighter concentration as its plan A.

544871|2026-06.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.
544871|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 34% YoY to INR592 crore, with transactions up 36% and GMV up 31%. Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. Loss before tax narrowed to INR13.7 crore from INR18 crore, and management said the emerging share of revenue reached 30%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 18.0% last year; CM amount +43% YoY, +10% QoQ
YoY; gap vs adjusted EBITDA driven by share-based payments

segments.name: Core (shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR412 crore, up 22% YoY; transactions up 31%. Adjusted EBITDA INR52.7 crore at 12.8% margin, up 50 bps YoY. Contribution margin 8.4% vs 8.7% last year.

segments.name: Emerging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 70% YoY and 14% QoQ; now 30% of revenue vs 24% last year. Adjusted EBITDA margin -24% vs -38%; contribution margin about 15% per CEO vs 9% to 10% last year (39.6% vs 47.3% per CFO's company-level breakdown, which is inconsistent).

segments.name: Omnichannel (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 92% YoY, the largest emerging sub-business; driven by quick commerce and PTL (cargo) fulfilment.

segments.name: Cross-border (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue down marginally YoY; management cited global volatility hitting merchant confidence and a focus on higher-margin customers.

segments.name: MarTech (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Youngest and smallest emerging unit, growing very fast at a slightly better margin; checkout (Quikpay), Steal Deal, AI Assist and AI Ads launched this quarter. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance. Management said core contribution margin should stay around its recent trajectory and gave no timeframe for emerging EBITDA break-even.
Core adjusted EBITDA margin has moved from about 6% to 12.8% over three years, but management said it will keep investing behind growth, so no steady-state margin was given.
Management expects Q3 to be the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: Shiprocket owns no logistics assets and works with 42+ courier partners and 250+ partners overall.
Company has about 1,500 employees, with much of the investment going into emerging products and tech.
No capex or capacity figures were discussed.
demand_pricing: Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22%, which management attributed to input cost (courier rate) compression passed on to merchants and mix shift toward larger D2C merchants.
Cross-sell: share of core merchants buying emerging rose to 8.8% from 7.3% a year ago; merchants served via emerging rose to about 48,000 from about 30,000.

Power merchant ARPU rose about 25% while the power merchant count was slightly lower YoY, per the analyst's question; management attributed this to top merchants growing faster and a focus on expanding the funnel.
Blended CAC was about INR3,600 this quarter vs INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management said it is experimental, not seasonal, and that it breaks even within a short period.
Management said pricing is volume-based and that competition in single-point solutions exists, but its data scale is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Will core contribution margin and EBITDA margin keep growing faster than revenue, and is 12.5% to 13% a steady-state core EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CM improved slightly over revenue growth and should stay around that range. It declined to give a steady-state margin, citing continued investment in growth and operating leverage over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeframe was given. Management said MarTech is higher margin and growing fast from a small base, and that growth is the main lever for margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Top merchants are growing faster, and the company is expanding the merchant funnel to convert more merchants into power merchants over time. Management said near-term results depend on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q3 is typically weakest, because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season. No other seasonality was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why has realization per shipment fallen (from about INR96 in FY24 to about INR72 now, per analyst's calculation)?
qa_highlights.answer: The 216 million figure is total unique transactions, not core shipments. Management said the decline reflects the mix shift toward emerging (30% of revenue) and a rise in transactions, while margins as a percentage improved. Core shipment count was not disclosed.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

500003|2026-06.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
500003|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.</overview>

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Logistics
segments.commentary: Throughput held steady at 1.124 million MT. Sourcing volumes rose marginally 1% YoY to 1.21 lakh MT.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Distribution
segments.commentary: Record 2.77 lakh MT volume. Management cites a distribution margin of INR7,000+ per MT as sustainable, versus INR4,000 historically.

segments.name: Liquids
segments.commentary: Highest-ever Q1 EBITDA of INR136 crore, with five consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth. Mangalore liquid capacity of 193,000 CBM is fully utilized after a 75,000 CBM addition.

guidance_outlook: Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion targeted in FY27.
Capex pipeline of about $5 billion through FY2030-31; funding via equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing of about 0.6.
Distribution volume: management aims for 2 million MT, now expected to cross 1 million MT this year and possibly 1.5 million MT next year; growth rate closer to 50% per management.
Logistics throughput: worst-case growth of about 25% a year, with step-up growth possible as Pipavav and KGPL enablers are used.
Mumbai 64,000 CBM liquid storage (INR125 crore) targeted for commissioning in H1 FY27.
JNPA first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage targeted for Q3 FY27; Kochi additional 49,577 CBM expected early next fiscal year; Kandla CRL 4 (94,148 CBM) targeted next year.
capex_capacity: Mumbai: 334,000 CBM liquid and 21,000 MT static LPG; 64,000 CBM expansion under way.
JNPA: 101,900 CBM liquid today; about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT bottling plant under a roughly INR1,675 crore program. Board also approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank.

Pipavav: LPG capacity now 70,800 MT after a 48,000 MT terminal commissioned June 2025; 36,000 MT ammonia terminal commissioned; VLGC-compliant jetty due this year; liquid rail gantry with 0.5 million MT/yr take-or-pay due by year-end; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline complete.
Kandla: 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; VLGC-compliant; CRL 4 expansion targeted next year.
Kochi: 82,545 CBM liquid today, rising to 132,122 CBM after a 49,577 CBM addition.
Mangalore: 82,000 MT LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; LPG rail gantry and bottling plant at INR52.5 crore; liquid capacity 193,000 CBM; evaluating 60,000 CBM more.
Haldia: about 25,000 MT LPG terminal under HPCL terminaling agreement to 2038; 226,890 CBM liquid storage; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion.
Vadhavan port: non-binding MoU for a potential INR20,000 crore investment, subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Management says distribution volume growth reflects new customers, wider geography and ullage added from Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals, not only the war.

Blended distribution margin was about INR7,000/MT in FY26 and Q1 FY27. Management says the margin should be INR7,000+ going forward, supported by shipping savings from VLGC carriers (freight of about $15 vs $50 on MGCs).
Management states margins were not INR5,000 in Q4 or Q1 and said blended FY margin matters more than quarterly figures.
Ammonia: distribution to industrial customers starts within weeks of commissioning; no cylinders or gas stations. Margins not disclosed.
Management says it is a distributor, not a trader, and does not take inventory or price positions.
Morbi demand has partly restarted; management says Morbi is no longer the core of the business.
Logistics tariffs are uniform across ports; no port-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution volume growth ahead of expectations, and are the customer contracts sticky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2 million MT aim predates the war and reflects infrastructure build-out; new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore have added ullage and geography.

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the per-unit margins for sourcing, logistics and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids EBITDA is divided by capacity (about 2 million CBM). Logistics throughput gives close to INR1,000/MT EBITDA. Sourcing is a low contributor, at about $85-90/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook beyond 25% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not fill more storage given the ITOCHU partnership and the LPG supply deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.</overview>

segments.name: Temperature Sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR60 crores, up 42%, led by thermal power and OEMs including CVD equipment makers; EDGE pyrometer series (with Micro-Epsilon) to start dispatch in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with blended three-year growth; management pointed to about 25% in analyst's framing but said visibility improves in H2.
EBITDA margin to remain broadly similar to FY26 profile; margin recovery visible in H2 FY27 as employee cost is absorbed by revenue.
Management expects profit growth to be in line with revenue growth by end of FY27.
Lower finance cost to be visible from the coming quarter after INR55 crores of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment.
OEM and new products expected to contribute more than 25% of revenue starting FY28.
capex_capacity: Brownfield 50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 1 for OEM contact sensors, commissioning by Q3 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 6 for medium-voltage heaters, completion by Q1 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR200 crores; heaters tested to 7.2 kV, explosion-proof certification targeted by Q4 FY27.
Unit 8 greenfield cable plant, completion by Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores; capacity can be ramped quickly.
Victura JV to acquire 80,000 sq ft facility with existing shed; production to start by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

Aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores across four projects versus FY26 revenue of INR445 crores; existing capacity running at about 80%. Additional 25,000 sq ft planned for custom furnaces this year; land acquired for about INR25 crores in Q1 for cable expansion.
demand_pricing: Pipeline healthy across thermal and nuclear power in India and steel and glass globally; quoted pipeline in Middle East has increased but firm orders still awaited.
OEM order visibility of 9-12 months versus about 4-4.5 months order book for heavy-industry customers; furnace contract is 5 years.
Inventory of INR110-120 crores, 65-70% in raw material; raw materials booked at order receipt and price fluctuations passed through to customers.
Management says Chinese competition is limited for engineered make-to-order products; some customers shifting sourcing to India.
Export share rose to about 34%; new subsidiaries in Mexico, Poland and South Korea; Korean JV supplying battery manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How has the fuel cell OEM order trajectory evolved and what run-rate exit FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said field trials and run-up are advanced and focus is now on scaling execution; it declined to quantify exit run-rate, calling it a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from critical, high-barrier industries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-age industry TAM and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR500 crore incremental capacity reach full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.

544613|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn; EBITDA margin 18.9%, normalized PAT Rs 1,652 mn after Bawal fire exceptional loss of Rs 1,436 mn.
544613|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn and EBITDA rose 140.6% to Rs 2,548 mn, with margin up to 18.9% from 17.7%. A Rs 1,436 mn provisional exceptional loss from the Bawal facility fire brought reported PAT to Rs 578 mn (4.3% margin), while normalized PAT was Rs 1,652 mn (12.3%). Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, kept the margin guidance at "sustainable to improve," and added distributors, dealers and two states. Ratlam capacity additions (2 GW solar panel, 2 GW power electronics, 2 GW battery due Q2 FY27) and stake increases in Zayo entities were the main capex and integration moves.

financial_highlights.change: expected to be fully recovered via insurance

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized PAT (ex post-tax fire provision Rs 1,074 mn)

segments.name: Residential rooftop / B2C
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% of revenue comes from the B2C channel. Sales are sold as a package of panels, inverters and batteries; no segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Off-grid vs on-grid vs hybrid
segments.commentary: Management said on-grid growth was the main driver this quarter, enabled by in-house DCR cells; off-grid is still growing but more slowly. No split was disclosed.

segments.name: Tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Tubular battery output (about 10% of revenue) was lost in the Bawal fire; management estimated the gross margin impact at below 0.5% as batteries are now bought from outside vendors.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to about 70% from the earlier 50%, with a stated intent to trail it upward in later quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 'sustainable to improve' (Q1 at 18.9%).
Insurance claim on the Bawal fire (net carrying value about Rs 1,436 mn) expected to settle by end of FY27; management expects full recovery.
Ratlam 2 GW lithium-ion battery plant on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27.
FY27 gross block (incl. CWIP) expected at about Rs 1,300 cr, up from about Rs 800 cr at start of year.
Channel partner target of more than 15,000 (distributors, dealers, shoppes) by end FY28.
Zayo Energy plant expected to add Rs 400-500 cr top-line in the next financial year; Fujiyama's share of Zayo capex about Rs 50 cr.
capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity: 2 GW added at Ratlam (capitalized 14 May 2026), taking total to 3.5 GW; Ratlam running one shift and ramping in phases.
Power electronics: 2 GW facility at Ratlam commissioned in August 2026, taking total to 4 GW; initial utilization of Ratlam capacity guided at 40-50%.
Solar cell (DCR) plant at 1 GW (some reports say 1.2 GW) running at 80%+ utilization; non-Ratlam panel plants at 70-80% utilization.
TOPCon line: building complete and machine orders placed; target commissioning in about 9 months (within the next financial year per the call).
Zayo Energy/Zayo Cables: stake raised from 19% to 50% each; Zayo Energy capex about Rs 180-200 cr total, with land acquisition under way and production targeted within about one year.
demand_pricing: Management cited current PM Surya Ghar installation run rate of about 1 GW per month; about 50 lakh of the 1 crore household target covered.
Industry rooftop capacity installed to date put at over 30 GW, with about 15 GW under PM Surya Ghar; government target 90-100 GW rooftop of 300 GW solar by 2030.
System pricing quoted at Rs 26-30 per watt (BOM with panel, inverter, battery) at distributor billing level, including GST.
Industry growth rate cited at about 40%; Fujiyama estimates about 10% share of the on-grid market (not officially confirmed).
Distributors rose from 950+ to 1,150+ in the quarter; channel partners rose from about 8,900 to over 10,100 with Odisha and Uttarakhand newly moved to covered states.
Management said DCR pricing and higher realization on Mono PERC DCR panels drove the higher average realization.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year revenue and profit be modelled after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, citing demand and Ratlam capacity, and said it will trail the guidance upward as the year progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR cell capacity supports margins but raw material price volatility is a factor, and it will pass on part of the gains; margin guidance remains 'sustainable to improve'.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the damaged assets with net carrying value about Rs 143 cr are fully insured, the survey is done, the full loss was booked in Q1, and claim settlement is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 26-30 per watt figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an average distributor BOM (roughly Rs 15 panel, Rs 5 inverter, Rs 5 battery), varying with DCR/non-DCR, battery type and system type, with GST included.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution this year; about Rs 200 cr of the Rs 500 cr additional capex will be debt-funded, with Rs 100 cr from IPO proceeds and Rs 200 cr from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon commissioning is targeted within about 9 months. The fire-hit lead-acid plant will not restart until insurance work is done; the company is in talks to lease an operating plant.

risks_watch: Bawal insurance claim settlement (management targets end FY27); any delay or shortfall versus Rs 1,436 mn would hit reported earnings.
Margin sustainability as market share is pushed with price cuts and as module prices fall; non-DCR margins are under pressure.
PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is not yet notified; loan sanction and DCR supply constraints are slowing installations.
Ratlam battery plant (2 GW) commissioning in Q2 FY27 and new power electronics ramp-up at 40-50% utilization.
BIS compliance: 15 of about 500 SKUs were flagged by the authority; management says these are now certified and represent under 1% of stock value.
Revenue is not disclosed by segment, which limits visibility into on-grid, off-grid and hybrid mix.
Zayo Energy stake commitments and capex (Rs 180-200 cr total) plus the lead-acid plant lease.

506655|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs.2,642 Cr and business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr for One Sudarshan; FY27 guidance held pending Q2 review.
506655|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27 for One Sudarshan, with revenue from operations of Rs.2,642 Cr, business EBITDA of Rs.247 Cr and reported EBITDA of Rs.266 Cr, cited as roughly 60%+ YoY EBITDA growth and about 5% revenue growth. The acquired (Heubach/Clariant pigments) group delivered business EBITDA of Rs.128 Cr versus Rs.65 Cr a year ago, while RIECO was weak with revenue of Rs.38 Cr on customer readiness and subcontractor labour issues. Net debt fell to Rs.531 Cr from a Rs.922 Cr peak. Management kept the acquired-group guidance of EUR 700 Mn turnover and EUR 35 Mn EBITDA unchanged, citing geopolitical uncertainty, and will review it after Q2.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs.78 Cr; inventory overhead impact Rs.18 Cr

financial_highlights.value: ~6% (modest growth, per Rathi), ~5% (per Rathi's acquired-group remark)
financial_highlights.change: YoY; prior-year Q1 base included only partial post-acquisition sales
management: movement of ~2% QoQ, sustained at 50%+

segments.name: Acquired group (pigments, ex-RIECO)
segments.commentary: Business EBITDA Rs.128 Cr vs Rs.65 Cr YoY; reported EBITDA Rs.146 Cr after Rs.18 Cr inventory overhead impact. Management says business margin has been consistently double-digit historically, and sees a 6-7% level as a stepping stone to high single or low double digits.

segments.name: RIECO
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.38 Cr, with EBITDA down on execution delays (customer readiness, subcontractor manpower shortages). Management expects normalisation from Q2 and a positive EBITDA before year end.

guidance_outlook: Acquired group FY27 guidance unchanged: turnover EUR 700 Mn and EBITDA EUR 35 Mn; management will revisit after Q2 despite a stronger Q1.
Legacy Sudarshan growth expected at roughly 12-13% in the near term.
Value capture and cost reduction are expected to drive most EBITDA growth, mainly in FY27-FY28, with some flowing into FY29.
FY29 consolidated targets (about 16-17% revenue CAGR at higher end and EBITDA near doubling vs FY27) are described as previously stated, not new.
Revenue of Rs.12,000 Cr+ cited as the long-term projection from the investor deck (slide 9).
Gross margin expected to stay above 50%; seasonality expected in Q3.
capex_capacity: No new capex needed for volume growth in guided numbers, per management; existing capacity is sufficient.
Possible moderate capex for backward integration or special projects, to be approved only on acceptable ROI.
Global capability centre set up in Pune; second global headquarters opened in Frankfurt.
Project Integra (One SAP) targeted to go live within FY27; currently running more than four SAP instances and 130 applications.
Management cites 55-60% of assets located in Asia.
demand_pricing: Customers delayed purchases amid geopolitical uncertainty; logistics cycle lengthened by about two weeks.
Energy, raw material and logistics costs rose in Europe and India; price increases so far passed on cost increases only, with management committing to reverse pricing if raw materials soften.

Coatings: US decorative and automotive subdued; plastics demand choppy on polymer price spikes and hand-to-mouth buying; volume printing inks declining while specialty inks, agro and digital inks grow well.
Management says a meaningful part of growth will come from recapturing business lost post-integration (lack of focus, insolvency issues), not from market growth.
Pigment pricing is contract-driven; switching pigments takes 1-2 years, up to 5 years in automotive, and pricing is generally negotiated quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 growth reflects underlying volume after FX translation and price increases; can growth be 2-2.5x industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the volume-decline inference, citing ~6% growth and a weak prior-year Q1 base with partial post-acquisition sales. It said growth will come from winning back lost business and value capture.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA path to FY29 is volume versus cost/value capture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is substantially cost reduction and value capture.

qa_highlights.question: Capex needs in the next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No volume capex needed; only moderate capex on backward integration or special projects if ROI is good.

qa_highlights.question: Is ~54% gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin moved about 2% QoQ on yields, utilities and production cost cuts, plus minor one-offs; management expects 50%+ to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plans and RIECO hive-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Some acquisition debt has been prepaid, with faster repayment planned as net debt falls. RIECO is in transformation with no hive-off mentioned; management expects a positive EBITDA before year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the acquired group's stake in Sudarshan Colorants held indirectly, and what is the restructuring provision after June 30?
qa_highlights.answer: The indirect holding was for financing reasons, with a plan to hold directly from the parent, so this is group restructuring with no business impact. The restructuring charge is not yet quantifiable, with clarity expected by end of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given Q1 run-rate, and is 6-7% margin the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not revising guidance until Q2 review. It does not expect 15%+ margins; the target is high single digit to low double digit.

risks_watch: Unquantified restructuring charge tied to a post-June 30 employee agreement at a European subsidiary; quantification expected by end Q2.
FY27 guidance not revised despite a strong Q1; Q2 result is the next checkpoint.
RIECO execution: revenue Rs.38 Cr and EBITDA decline in Q1; recovery depends on labour and customer readiness.
Raw material and energy volatility (Middle East crisis) and logistics delays; pricing may need reversal if raw material costs fall.
Delayed customer purchasing and subdued US/EU coatings demand.
Project Integra (One SAP) go-live and value capture delivery within FY27.

500336|2026-06.headline: Surya Roshni Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR2,046 crore and PAT 77% to INR60 crore, but steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,006 sits well below the FY27 INR4,600-4,700 guidance.
500336|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR2,046 crore (up 28% YoY), EBITDA of INR120 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 77%) were driven mainly by Steel Pipes & Strips, where volume hit a record Q1 of 2.28 lakh tons. Management attributed the EBITDA/ton shortfall to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM cost increases (about INR200/ton), and expects recovery as new orders are booked at higher freight rates. Lighting & Consumer Durables grew 15% to INR456 crore with margin up to 7.9%. The company remains debt-free with net cash of about INR155 crore; buyback and demerger decisions were deferred with no firm timeline.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +17% YoY (from INR31 crore); PBT +12% YoY (from INR21 crore)

financial_highlights.value: About INR155 crore (B.B. Singal cited INR154 crore) as of 30 June 2026

segments.name: Steel Pipes & Strips
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,590 crore (+32% YoY) on record Q1 volume of 2.28 lakh tons (+21% YoY); section, ERW API, spiral, cold rolling and GP pipes led, galvanized soft on delayed government fund releases. Capacity utilisation about 82%, value-added products 47% of volume, exports 20% of segment volume.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR456 crore (+15% YoY), best-ever Q1, led by LED bulbs, battens and downlighters; EBITDA INR36 crore with margin 7.9%, passing through about 7% input cost increase. Professional lighting order book about INR150 crore.

segments.name: Wire & Cables
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 sales nearly matched FY26 full-year volume; FY26 revenue target INR250 crore, against a 3-year INR500 crore goal. Electrician loyalty program enrolments reached 36,000.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume about 11 lakh tons (+20-22% volume growth); quarterly path of about 2.6-2.65 lakh tons in Q2, 2.8-2.9 lakh in Q3 and about 3.2 lakh in Q4.
FY27 steel EBITDA/ton guidance of INR4,600-4,700 reiterated; management expects about INR4,400-4,500 in Q2 and INR4,600-4,700 full year, implying above INR5,000 in H2 per Q1 analyst math.
Company FY27 EBITDA guided at INR670-680 crore on revenue of INR9,400-9,500 crore; Q2 EBITDA about INR150 crore and H2 about INR400 crore.
Lighting FY27: revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore FY26), value growth 19-22%, volume growth about 25%, EBITDA about INR200 crore.

Steel value growth 30%+ expected for FY27; US market contribution 10-11% of volume (about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27), total exports about 3 lakh tons; export share of steel to rise from about 20% to 25%.
Ocean freight: new orders booked at higher rates, with July impact described as very low and no freight impact expected in the next two months; break-bulk shipping arranged for US volumes.
Full-year API/spiral EBITDA/ton expected to recover from Q1 INR3,420 to about INR5,000 (vs INR5,500-5,700 in FY26).
Per-ton cost reduction target of about INR1,100 and manpower cost reduction of about 20% over the next year; 15-18% CAGR targeted for the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity 14 lakh tons currently; target 16 lakh tons by end-FY27 with three DFT mills commissioning between August and December 2026 at Gujarat, Malanpur and Bahadurgarh; about 2 million tons by FY28-29.
Adding 2-3 lakh tons of capacity every year; capex about INR100 crore for the 14-to-16 lakh ton expansion, funded from internal accruals.

Hindupur (South) greenfield-style expansion on 10 additional acres: first mill about January 2027, total 4-mill plant adding about 15,000 tons initially, about INR60 crore investment, roughly 3 lakh tons overall.
Greenfield projects under evaluation with clarity promised by next board meeting; expansions focus on DFT and section pipes.
demand_pricing: Steel order book INR800 crore (export API orders include 78,000 tons for the US) vs INR1,000 crore at end-March; management said about 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed.
Ocean freight rose sharply; Q1 exports carried about INR3,800/ton higher freight, costing about INR800/ton of blended EBITDA. Management says new orders are priced at the higher freight.

US market opened for ERW API pipes, with realisation EBITDA/ton of about INR7,200 in Q1; Middle East orders fell (roughly one-third of usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter now able to ship), and API orders down about 50%.
Steel prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April, then fell in May-June, leaving the quarter roughly neutral on inventory; steel now seen stable within INR1,000/ton.
Q1 API/spiral EBITDA/ton of INR3,420 cited with coating material as a significant drag; water pipe faces higher competition.
Lighting: about 80% of production in-house, about 20% outsourced, with the outsourced share largely made exclusively for Surya.

542650|2026-06.headline: Metropolis guides 14-15% growth ex-price and ex-M&A, Q1 FY27 growth was 17%, and targets EBITDA margin of 27-28% from 24.4%.
542650|2026-06.overview: Management held an investor and analyst meet (transcript dated 27 Aug 2026) covering strategy, growth levers, margin path and Q&A. Q1 growth was stated at 17%, ahead of the company's 14-15% medium-term guidance, which excludes price increases and acquisitions. Management outlined five growth engines: network expansion (collection-centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35), TruHealth, specialty and genomics, technology/digital, and inorganic growth. Radiology "mini hubs" (about 100 centres, 50 upgrades) were introduced as a new adjacency, with capex of about INR35-40 lakh per hub. Management said the FY26 EBITDA margin was 24.4% (25.9% organic, adjusted for the breakeven Core Diagnostics acquisition) and targeted 27-28% over the next 2-3 years.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue CAGR 23.6% (as stated); 3-year revenue CAGR 17.6%
Core Diagnostics (breakeven at acquisition) diluted margin by about 1.5 pts
Above 14-15% guidance; B2C grew about 18% in the last quarter
B2B grew about 15% in the last quarter, aided by Core test menu
Added about 380-400 specialty tests in the last 15 months
Home collection contribution growing about 40% per quarter (as stated)
North India fastest-growing region in Q1; North could reach about 25% in a few years
Five countries, about 24 labs; Kenya and Zambia market leaders

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: About 57-59% of revenue; grew about 18% in the last quarter. Centre network of about 5,000 (about 700-800 company-owned, rest franchise); plan to add 250-300 centres every quarter and reach a 1:35 centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: About 41-43% of revenue; grew about 15% last quarter, helped by Core Diagnostics' oncology test menu (about 350 tests, about 2,000 connected oncologists). Management targets B2B at about 45% with margin-accretive accounts only.

segments.name: Specialty and genomics
segments.commentary: About 40-42% of business; genomics volume reportedly doubled in the last year. Company claims a 2-CAP-accredited genomics labs footprint (West and North) and a clinician support vertical.

segments.name: TruHealth
segments.commentary: About 18-20% of revenue; target 25%. Adding diet consultation (blood-work based), body composition/vital check-up, and obesity/diabetes panels.

segments.name: Radiology mini hubs (new)
segments.commentary: Plan for about 100 hubs over the next couple of years (about 50 upgrades of existing centres, about 15-50 new per management, as stated); capex about INR35-40 lakh per hub for basic X-ray, ultrasound, echo, treadmill, with pilots of 50 centres in year 1. Advanced MRI/CT limited to 1-2 preventive-care pilots.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Five countries (Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania), about 24 labs; Kenya and Zambia rated market leaders, others top-3. Self-funded, with no capital sent from India.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance reiterated at 14-15%, excluding price increases and acquisitions; management expects FY27 growth to run faster given Q1 at 17%, but is holding 14-15% until more clarity by end of year.
EBITDA margin ambition of 27-28% (from 24.4%) over the next 2-3 years, driven by specialty/genomics mix, digitisation and automation, and higher centre-to-lab utilisation.
Working capital aspiration to move from double-digit days to single digit; focus on ROCE and capital-light expansion.
Price increases not in guidance; management said it will give clarity on FY28 and pricing once the year ends.
Management described 2026-2029 as a period to harvest investments made in 2021-2025; further reinvestment expected in future cycles.
capex_capacity: Network: about 5,000 centres (about 700-800 company-owned, concentrated in top 6-8 towns); 209 labs; 750 towns served; plan to raise centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35.
Radiology mini hubs: about 100 over the next couple of years (about 50 upgrades of existing centres); capex about INR35-40 lakh per hub; first 50 centres in year 1, next 50 in about a year after.
Opex-versus-capex model under evaluation for mini hubs; corporate health checks and insurance to lift productivity 2-3x per centre (as stated).
Company-owned centres' real estate could be used beyond 10:30-11 AM for allied services; management said one lab need not be paired with one radiology centre.
Tier 3 labs already in place across 750 towns; no new labs needed, only more collection centres (250-300 added per quarter).
demand_pricing: Management attributes most growth to volume; price increases of 2-3% p.a. in prior years, plus product-mix-driven revenue per patient gains.
CGHS rate hike benefited peers in last year's Q3; Metropolis says it had negligible CGHS exposure, so it does not face a fade from Q3 onwards.
Semi-specialty and specialty tests carry the same price across India, while routine tests vary by market; Tier 3 margins said to be equal or better than metros.
Large-city share (Mumbai, Chennai, Pune) said to be stable or improving despite competition from health-tech players and pharma entrants.
Management criticised private players buying businesses at 18-19x EBITDA multiples and said it will remain disciplined on M&A pricing.

541929|2026-06.headline: Synergy Green Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹75.71 crore and 7% PBDIT margin were weak; management reiterates ₹500 crore FY27 revenue and 300 bps margin uplift.
541929|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 total income was ₹75.71 crore with absolute PBDIT of ₹5.3 crore at a 7% margin, as dispatches slipped on customer lifting, prototype approval delays and shipping constraints. Production rose about 10% YoY and the new 45,000 tpa capacity reached 66% utilisation in Q1, with July utilisation at 85% (about 3,200 tons). Raw material, consumable and energy inflation (linked to the West Asia conflict and an MSEDCL solar banking change) cut margins, which management expects to partly recover from Q2 via one-quarter-lagged indexation. Management maintained FY27 guidance of ~₹500 crore revenue (33% growth) and ~300 bps PBDIT margin expansion.</overview>

Utilisation target of 80% on full 45,000 tpa capacity for FY27; 80-90% within 2-3 months from July.

Land for 100,000 tpa project targeted by December or March; next project start by Q3 of next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa (expanded from 30,000 tpa); in-house machining 20,000 tpa; 10 MW captive solar.
Plan for 100,000 tpa capacity; land acquisition targeted by December or March; greenfield capex takes 15-18 months to commission.
Additional 5 MW wind PPA via open access to offset power cost inflation; solar + PPA to cover 50-60% of power needs.
Vestas 4 MW platform: tooling started mid-May; samples expected Q4 FY27, full production Q1 FY28. Nordex NX N 5 MW prototypes cleared in Q1.
Inventory held at 8-10 weeks; target to keep shop order book below 8 weeks.
demand_pricing: Q1 dispatches lower due to delayed customer material lifting and prototype approvals with a key customer; export rollouts hit by ship availability amid West Asia conflict. Unsold production went into inventory.
Furan Resin (third-largest cost item) rose ~60%; PNG/LNG prices up 60-70%; pig iron and CRC inflation from shortages and imported scrap logistics.
Realisations expected to rise from ₹138-140/kg to ₹145+ levels in coming quarters; management said no change in realisation in Q1.
Vestas ~40-45% of business historically, expected to fall toward ~30% as new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) are added; Nordex growing; Adani 3.3 MW in serial production.
Indian suppliers estimated 5-10% cheaper than China on landed cost for wind products after yen appreciation; US market favours non-Chinese suppliers.
Management views wind demand stronger than solar; night-time wind tariffs 25% higher than solar daytime, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Could the ₹500 crore FY27 target slip into next year given slow offtake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 production was strong but did not convert to sales; Q2 execution is at a much higher flow rate, and product approval has come from 50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: Did realisations spike given 66% utilisation implies ~7,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said produced material was not all sold, creating inventory, and realisation is unchanged, with revenue recognition pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income of ₹4.4 crore from power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No; likely FX-related or export incentives. Management has not sold power; solar lapsed units were lost under the MSEDCL policy change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the ₹600-700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Renamed the executable order book; ₹500 crore set for FY27 given hurdles, with ₹600 crore possible next year on higher capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next capex and fundraising happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three good quarters needed first; land by December or March; project start by Q3 next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vestas concentration stay the same at ~₹600 crore revenue in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Vestas wants more allocation but capacity is going to new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) each allocating ₹100-150 crore; wind is ~₹400 crore of revenue, non-wind and gearboxes ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is offshore wind or Adani 5 MW participation viable?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani 5 MW parts often exceed 30 MT, so imported from China; Adani 5.2 MW bearing (6-7 ton casting) supplied. Offshore volumes not expected for 5-10 years; company focuses on 3-4 MW onshore.

544880|2026-06.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR200 crores, with EBITDA of INR161 crores (80% margin) and a net loss of INR12 crores.
544880|2026-06.overview: Management's first earnings call after the August IPO, which raised INR4,250 crores of primary capital used for deleveraging to a proforma net debt of about INR2,500 crores at 30 June. Revenue was INR200 crores (+23% YoY) and EBITDA INR161 crores (+36% YoY). Management steered attention to a proforma cash PAT of INR116 crores, arguing the reported net loss is distorted by non-cash depreciation and pre-deleveraging interest. Leasing was 1.9 million sq ft across 13 transactions, with contracted revenue run rate at about INR967-970 crores.

financial_highlights.change: expected to fall 40-50 bps post deleveraging

segments.name: Large-format industrial and warehousing parks
segments.commentary: 29.5 million sq ft operational across 46 assets in 9 states and 10 markets; 26.9 mn sq ft on operational area, plus 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased under construction. Yield on cost about 11-12%.

segments.name: In-city (urban mid-mile/last-mile) assets
segments.commentary: 17 assets across 7 cities, about 6-7 mn sq ft; rentals about 2.5-3x big-format; yield on cost 13-14% after CWC revenue share. Three mid-mile assets fully leased at INR65-70 per sq ft (as stated). First Pune (Pimpri) delivery targeted Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Value-added services (rooftop solar, worker accommodation, hospitality, skill centre)
segments.commentary: Rooftop solar about 38 MW, of which about 20 MW operational and 17-18 MW being operationalised. Worker accommodation of 6,000-7,000 beds under construction; target 5-10% of revenue in 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 mn sq ft (about 30% growth vs last fiscal), with 4-4.5 mn sq ft of incremental leasing expected over the next 9 months.
FY27 completion target of 6 mn sq ft, taking operational area to about 34-35 mn sq ft by year-end at high-90s occupancy.
Net loss expected to turn to profit from Q2 or Q3 FY27 (management guidance on reported P&L).
Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over next 3 years, roughly one-third internal accruals and two-thirds incremental debt.
Target to double large-format park capacity over 4-5 years; in-city 6 mn sq ft over next 3 years.
Incremental capex yield on cost guided at 13-14%; in-city construction cost about INR4,500 per sq ft with rents guided at INR70-75 per sq ft (as stated).
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 30 mn sq ft is fully paid, with approvals and financing largely in place; 25 mn sq ft of large-park development remaining.
Build cycles are 9-12 months; 20-30% of development pre-leased, with a stock-in-trade of 1.6 mn sq ft across the operational network.

Pimpri (Pune) in-city multi-storey asset targeted for Q4 FY27 delivery; a Delhi High Court case challenging the tender for 13 in-city warehouses is sub judice, with management expecting large part delivery in 12-24 months.
Approximately 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1; 5 mn sq ft of buildings to be delivered over the next 9 months.
demand_pricing: Re-leasing spreads of 12% in Q1 (on about 300,000 sq ft expiries), versus 12-15% historically, above the 5% contractual annual escalation; WALE about 7.1 years.
Industrial-segment leases at about INR29+ per sq ft versus about INR24 for bare-bone warehousing; blended in-place rent plus CAM about INR27.20 per sq ft.
High single-digit market rent growth in deeper markets (as stated).
Expiries of about 1.4 mn sq ft in the next 9 months and 2.2 mn sq ft next fiscal (about 13% of portfolio over 21 months).
Three-fourths of Q1 leasing came from industrial customers; industrial and manufacturing customers are close to half the portfolio. Over 120 customers; nine new customers onboarded in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does 25% volume growth plus 5% escalation imply about 30% revenue CAGR over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four growth engines: contractual escalations plus re-leasing spreads on 29.5 mn sq ft, 6 mn sq ft of large-park development, in-city expansion of about 2 mn sq ft a year, and value-added services at 5-10% of revenue. It did not confirm a 30% CAGR figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR967 crore contracted run rate translate into reported EBITDA and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-85% sits on existing assets with nearly full 12-month revenue flow expected; the 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased, under-construction area should contribute within 9-12 months. Further 4-4.5 mn sq ft of leases are expected over 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for leverage, capex and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over 3 years, funded one-third internally and two-thirds by debt. Cost of debt (about 8.2%) expected to fall 40-50 bps as ratings improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond its 10 markets and pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will explore Tier 1-minus/Tier 2 markets opportunistically (cited Nagpur, Goa, Nashik), focus on share gains in existing Tier 1 markets, and keep acquisitions (land parcels and consolidation of sub-scale platforms) central. No quantified annual addition target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive intensity in institutional supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market can absorb many more Horizon-scale players; Grade-A stock is under 500 mn sq ft nationally, and more than 90% of stock is fragmented or non-compliant.

qa_highlights.question: When will the reported P&L turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided that the P&L should turn black from Q2 or Q3 FY27 onwards.

544890|2026-06.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.
544890|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27, with operating revenue up 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores and operating EBITDA up to INR50.12 crores from INR27.31 crores. Management attributed much of the revenue jump to per-unit freight cost increases driven by fuel indices, with volume growth of 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean freight. Employee and other expenses fell as a share of revenue, lifting margins. The company also flagged a board-approved INR30 crore international office expansion and INR20 crore capital infusion into existing overseas subsidiaries, and repaid around INR140 crores of borrowings post-listing.

financial_highlights.metric: Employee benefit expense as % of revenue

financial_highlights.change: absolute increase in quarter; percentage cost reduced per management

segments.name: Air cargo
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 23% YoY; air cargo is about 81% of revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 77% in FY26. Air export volume grew 19% against a market increase of about 3.8%.

segments.name: Ocean freight
segments.commentary: Realisation growth of more than 64% and volume growth of 18% YoY; management cited revenue growth of 63%.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Revenue up 64% YoY to INR63 crores, with 59,700 shipments across 31 locations.

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (Odyssey)
segments.commentary: Pharma was 8-9% of business before Odyssey and reached 23% last year. Odyssey standalone revenue rose from about INR130 crores to INR182 crores quarter-on-quarter.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance; management will give volume guidance each quarter with the earnings call.
Management expects volume growth trend to continue in Q2 FY27 and says Q2 operating performance is improving QoQ.
Board approved INR30 crores for five new Asian international offices; breakeven at EBITDA level expected in 15-18 months and at PAT level in 2-3 years.
Generic group capex of about INR35-40 crores per year; cold chain warehouse expected to be operational next quarter.
Digital booking platform (ASAP) expected to launch within 30-60 days.
capex_capacity: Board approved INR30 crores for international office expansion; management said about 15% is capex and the rest is setup cost and working capital.
INR20 crores incremental capital infusion approved for existing overseas subsidiaries in UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.
Generic group capex of INR35-40 crores per annum, including warehouses and offices.
Cold chain warehouse project to become operational in the next quarter.
No acquisitions approved beyond the INR30 crore and INR20 crore allocations; management prefers organic growth.
demand_pricing: Management attributes about 23-25% of revenue growth to volume and the balance to higher per-unit freight cost driven by fuel indices; Brent-linked fuel index rose from about USD61/barrel in January to about USD110/barrel in May.
Management says fuel surcharges are a full pass-through, and yield moves up or down with fuel indices.
Air yield rose to about 416 from 259 in Q1 FY26 (per management).
Company ranked number one air freight forwarder in India and 44th globally by WorldACD chargeable volumes; Indian market share rose from 5.9% to 6.2% QoQ.
West Asia disruption reduced airline capacity by about 20%; management said it secured alternate carrier capacity and gained new customers.
Sector strength cited: pharmaceuticals, textiles and readymade garments, automotive, consumer electronics; no non-veg handling.
Indian air export market rose about 3.8% to about 3.06 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state revenue run rate, given revenue has roughly doubled YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 23-25% of revenue growth came from volume and the rest from per-unit cost increases driven by fuel indices; it did not give a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% volume growth sustainable, and is the realisation growth tied to fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of sustaining volume growth and aims to improve it; yield is market-driven and fuel is a pass-through. Focus is on higher-yield trade lanes.

qa_highlights.question: Gestation period and capex for new Asian offices?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical gestation is 2-4 years; management targets 2-3 years. About 15% of the INR30 crores is capex. Current footprint covers Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Bangladesh.

qa_highlights.question: Which markets get the INR20 crore subsidiary infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the digital booking platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Air, ocean and express are in pilot; trucking is in final development. Launch expected in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the EOW matter in the prospectus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub judice and under investigation in final stages, and it sees no financial impact at present. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the post-listing debt repayment and capital raise drag ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical ROE is 14-15%, the September quarter will show the post-listing capital effect, and it targets around 15% over time. About INR140 crores of borrowings were repaid.

risks_watch: Revenue growth is largely price-driven by fuel indices; management says yield can fall if crude declines.
Margin sustainability: management has chosen to absorb some cost increases to stay customer-centric, and gross margin percentage may be affected.
Pending EOW investigation: management says the matter is sub judice with no timeline and no expected financial impact.
Finance cost rose in absolute terms to INR17.7 crores; debt repayment benefit is expected from Q3 and Q4.
ROE may dilute temporarily after the post-listing equity increase and debt repayment, per management.
Swissport bid was not successful; company is now bidding with a Swissport alliance.
Brace Port (listed subsidiary) share price has declined since listing; management declined to comment on the stock price.

544167|2026-06.headline: JNK India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore; EBITDA margin 11.8% after Chemdist losses, PAT up 8.5x to INR 9.6 crore.
544167|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore and EBITDA rose 3.1x to INR 21.9 crore, with margin at 11.8% versus 7% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA margin was 14%, with the gap explained by an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore at the JNK Chemdist JV. Order book stood at INR 1,801 crore as of 30 June 2026, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin was reiterated. An export order received on 8 June 2026 was cancelled before any costs were incurred, due to licensor technical approval not materialising.

segments.name: Heating equipment (core)
segments.commentary: About 60% of the current opportunity pipeline; management targets heating at about 60% of revenue in the medium term. Export bids (about INR 3,000 crore) are mainly heating, largely routed through JNK Global.

segments.name: Non-heating / adjacencies (process plants, metals & minerals, offshore, renewables)
segments.commentary: About 40% of pipeline, with domestic bids of INR 3,000-plus crore. Target is about 40% of revenue from non-heating within 3-5 years; hit rate expected 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.8% of group revenue in Q1 FY27 with an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore on high fixed costs. Guided to 10-15% of JNK India revenue and about 20% gross margin; expected to turn profitable by year-end. Current green hydrogen orders about INR 50 crore.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of about 20-25% for FY27 maintained.
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance of about 12-14% maintained; management said there is no change, though the company later said it would recheck the figures it had announced.
Pipeline of more than INR 6,000 crore (about 50:50 export and domestic); management expects these bids to be finalised in FY27 with a hit rate of 20-25% in heating.
Refinery and fertiliser order finalisation expected in Q2-Q3 FY27.
BPCL Bina execution to occur uniformly in FY27 and FY28; EBITDA in line with guidance.
Chemdist expected to be EBITDA-positive by year-end FY27 (full year, not a specific quarter).
capex_capacity: Unbilled revenue at end-Q1 about INR 200-221 crore following shift to input-method revenue recognition.
Company has board approval to register a branch office in Iraq; no physical setup yet and an agent is in place.
Non-fund-based (bank guarantee) limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; no significant debt raising expected in the next 4-6 quarters, per management.
Revenue seasonality: Q1 is 10-15% of full-year revenue, H1 30-35%, H2 60-70%.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 1,801 crore at 30 June 2026; pipeline above INR 6,000 crore, up from about INR 4,000 crore previously.
Export pipeline about INR 3,000 crore, mainly Africa (Nigeria, Ethiopia) and Middle East; Dangote Phase 2 under discussion, described as a likely repeat order.
Non-heating TAM in India cited as USD 300-500 million (offshore) and USD 500 million-1 billion (metals and minerals); target project size USD 30-60 million, up to about INR 1,000-2,000 crore.
Commodity prices fluctuating; management said ongoing projects are costed and sub-vendor orders placed on fixed-price basis, so no major margin impact.
Working capital: large customers (Reliance, private companies, BPCL Bina) have friendly payment terms; JNK Global bank guarantees on back-to-back export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue target beyond FY27 and capacity to ramp non-heating business?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 20-25% annually; non-heating to reach about 40% of revenue in 3-5 years. Management said diversification will not ramp within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export order cancelled and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancelled due to end-user licensor technical approval not materialising; EPC contractor was confident, and no costs had been incurred. The licensor has since qualified JNK for future projects but not ongoing ones. SOPs being tightened.

qa_highlights.question: Margin decline in Q1 despite gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Chemdist operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore; standalone EBITDA margin was 14% on lower Q1 revenue of about INR 170 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Hit rate and TAM in new non-heating segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected hit rate of about 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating; target bids of USD 30-60 million, and EBITDA margin in line with 12-14% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: JNK Global cooperation agreement renewal (3-year term in DRHP)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not formally renewed yet; management believes it is in force or continues automatically, with no change in terms.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and accounting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue recognition moved from output to input method; unbilled revenue about INR 200-221 crore at end Q1. Management said working capital cycle is unchanged as customer payment schedules are unchanged.

risks_watch: Export order cancellation (8 June 2026 order) shows licensor approval risk on international EPC contracts.
Chemdist JV losses until break-even; management expects year-end profitability but gave no quarterly guidance.

Unclear reconciliation of EBITDA guidance (12-14% now vs 14-15% previously cited by an analyst) and corrections to the presentation, including a revised filing for standalone profit-after-tax margin rows.
Lower hit rate and new technology qualification risk in non-heating businesses; reliance on technology partners.
Governance: activist dispute at JNK Global (sub judice) and status of the JNK Global cooperation agreement, which is not formally renewed.
Revenue seasonality and back-ended recognition; unbilled revenue of about INR 200 crore to watch.
Bank guarantee limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; Dangote Phase 2 award pending.

534680|2026-06.headline: SRG Housing management denies Rs 400 crore siphoning report and NHB red flag; no hard financials or audit timeline given on the 16 Sep 2026 call.
534680|2026-06.overview:
This was a clarification call, not an earnings call, held after an Economic Times article (10 Sep 2026) alleged Rs 400 crore of promoter-linked diversion and NPA manipulation. The MD denied all allegations and said the NHB red flag is part of a routine supervisory audit that began in July 2026, with no reasons yet shared. He cited a 39.21% capital adequacy ratio, 25% QoQ PAT growth, and no delays on lender obligations, but gave no amount for collections or liquidity. New disbursements have been slowed, the board has resolved to convert from a housing finance company to an NBFC, and promoters raised their stake by 1%.</overview>

500368|2026-06.headline: Patanjali Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR11,337 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR543 crore (4.80% margin).

Textured soya margin guided at 16% to 18%, with management expecting to stay above 18%.
FMCG revenue expected to reach about INR12,500 crore this year from about INR11,000 crore+ last year (CEO estimate).
Oil palm business expected to grow more than 15% this year.

E-commerce and quick commerce plus modern trade targeted to rise from about 15% to 20% of revenue within 18 months.

No capex or new capacity figures were discussed on the call.

Calibrated price increases taken in edible oils; targeted discounts in FMCG; smaller pack sizes introduced. Pricing measures continue in Q2.
Palm oil prices firmed from March 2026, eased late in the quarter, then recovered to a two-week high in mid-August; rupee depreciated about 2.5%.
Soya oil futures rose about 40% by end-March, then stabilised; FOB prices corrected 6%.
Milk and sugar prices firmed; wheat stable. Packaging, freight and logistics costs rose in the quarter.
