538446|2026-06.headline: Moneyboxx Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR77 crore from INR92 crore as AUM reached INR832 crore; management guides to normalised disbursements by January 2027.
538446|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter in which Moneyboxx deliberately shifted toward secured, higher-ticket and higher-bureau-score loans, which cut disbursements and income. Disbursements were INR77 crore versus INR92 crore a year earlier, and total income was INR52.12 crore. Net interest and fee income fell to INR31.02 crore from INR38.52 crore, NIM dropped to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore versus INR0.24 crore. Management pointed to partnership channels, solar lending and a digital product as the next growth drivers, with secured AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR92 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest income and fee income
financial_highlights.change: vs INR38.52 crore in Q1 FY26
incremental cost said to be declining
vs INR29.75 crore in prior-year quarter (speaker said 'last quarter')

segments.name: Secured lending
segments.commentary: Secured loans were 87% of Q1 disbursements vs 67% in FY26; secured book is about 75% of AUM (incl. DLFG-backed loans) vs 49% in June 2025. Target is about 80% by March 2027.

segments.name: Unsecured lending
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending now about 13% of lending, down from 100% at start. Stopped from April 2026 except via partnership model and in Punjab.

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar) loans
segments.commentary: Cumulative disbursements crossed INR10 crore by July 2026; monthly disbursement grew from INR0.3 crore (first month) to INR5 crore (latest), with INR7 crore targeted for August and about INR20 crore per month by January. Target about 10% of AUM by end FY27; 15% of July disbursements.

segments.name: Partnership channel
segments.commentary: Partnerships were 15% of July disbursements, targeted at 20% in September-October and at least 30% by January 2027. Solar yield is about 23%; dairy partnership yield targeted at about 22%; opex expected at 1-1.5%.

guidance_outlook: Disbursements expected to normalise by Q4 FY27 (around January 2027), per management, with the pace 'maybe even sometimes better than peers'.
Secured share of AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027, including guarantee-backed loans.
Renewable energy loans targeted at about 10% of AUM by end FY27, implying roughly INR80-85 crore of AUM per the analyst's framing.
AUM of INR1,600-1,700 crore cited as the level at which profitability 'will completely change', with opex held at current levels.
Partnership share of monthly business targeted at 20% in Sept-Oct and at least 30% by January 2027.
Institutional equity infusion expected in H2 FY27; company said it aims to raise equity from institutions this year.
capex_capacity: Branch consolidation done in the quarter; closed some rural branches. Per-branch savings of about INR1-1.25 lakh per month (fixed staff and rent); quantified annual savings not given.
Moneyboxx One loan origination system launched May 2026 and now live; Sikka app, Cattle AI and MBCollect platforms also in use.
Headcount described as flat to slightly declining; solar disbursement of INR5 crore run by five people with no dedicated sales or collection team.
Dairy partnership expected to start disbursing from the month after the call (about September 2026) at INR3-5 crore per month.
demand_pricing: Disbursements moderated as the company stopped unsecured lending from April 2026 (except partnerships and Punjab) and stopped secured loans below INR5 lakh (except some solar branches). About 70% of disbursements were above INR5 lakh and about 75% went to customers with bureau score of 650 and above.
Management attributed the lag versus peers to team transition, the time needed to retrain staff for property-backed sourcing, and earlier higher cost of lending.

Partnership yields are said to be lower in headline terms, offset by lower acquisition cost and default loss guarantee (FLDG) protection. Solar credit cost expected to be under 0.5% for FY27; competitors cited at 3-5% without guarantees.
Management said the company is targeting INR8-15 lakh tickets as the core segment, which it views as offering lower credit cost and reasonable yields.

qa_highlights.question: Why are peers growing AUM and disbursements faster, and is it secured-mix transition, sourcing or branch productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April 2026 stop on unsecured lending in MP, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and Rajasthan, the move to larger tickets, and team retraining. It said it expects normalised disbursements by January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is the unsecured lending stop permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. Unsecured lending will continue under guarantee-backed partnerships such as a dairy tie-up with FLDG, and digital small-ticket unsecured loans with higher yields are planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the partnership contribution and its economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Partnerships were 15% of July disbursements, targeted at 20% in Sept-Oct and 30% by January. Solar yields about 23%, dairy about 22%, opex 1-1.5%, with FLDG and sometimes incentive programmes.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to credit quality when FLDG guarantees are removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said solar loans are asset-backed with 20% customer contribution and payments go directly to OEM/EPC, so guarantees should be durable. It estimated INR300-500 crore of guarantee programmes are obtainable; if guarantees end, yields would be revisited.

qa_highlights.question: Operating leverage and branch savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is flat in absolute terms, and the company says the key is AUM growth; the spread of 12-13% covers opex. Branch closures save about INR1-1.25 lakh per branch per month. A quantified total saving was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and equity requirements for the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR80 crore of monthly debt is needed to cover repayments of INR30-40 crore a month. INR70 crore of NCDs was raised in April-July, including INR50 crore from Capri Global, and a INR100 crore term sheet from a global impact fund is in hand. Equity is expected from institutions this year.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, but gave no numeric revenue guidance. Analyst's INR200 crore+ scenario was not confirmed.
Management expects no EBITDA margin harmonisation for the next six to eight quarters; medium-to-long-term TIL standalone EBITDA target 15-16%, timing 3-7 years.
Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur plant loaded only 30-35% with about 150 acres free; Kamarhati plant is old and fully loaded.
Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.
Supply-chain dependence: localisation of European and US inputs (Cummins engines, gearboxes) depends on OEM and defence approvals and could take several quarters.
Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.
505196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term vision (tripling turnover, 15-16% margins, aftermarket targets) but cautious and explicit on near-term margins, which it said will not stabilise for six to eight quarters. It was candid on the stressed working capital cycle and declined to quantify FY27 revenue or Tulip profit projections.
key_quotes: Hence, we are looking at a few more quarters before we are really able to fix the margins.
You're right, working capital cycle at this stage in TIL looks stressed.

533552|2026-06.headline: Rupa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.1% YoY to Rs 202.4 crore, EBITDA margin 7.8% (+120 bps) and PAT up 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore.
533552|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 10.1% YoY to Rs 202.4 crore, driven by volume, with the value segment the main contributor. EBITDA rose 29.1% to Rs 15.7 crore at a 7.8% margin, and PAT rose 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore. Management said a price hike taken in April was largely passed on to trade through extra schemes, so realisations did not capture it. Management guided to 10-12% revenue growth and a 9-10% EBITDA margin for the coming quarter, with a further price hike planned for August.

financial_highlights.metric: Modern trade including e-commerce share of revenue

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 21 crore, about 10.5% of revenue

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q1 declined 5-7% YoY after a strong Q4; management targets at least double-digit growth from Q2 and more than double-digit for the full year.

segments.name: Women's wear (Softline, Macroman)
segments.commentary: Women's share was about 8% in Q1 and has run at 8-10% on an annual basis. Softline is undergoing a brand and font change, with new fabrics and a new team being built.

segments.name: Thermal (winterwear)
segments.commentary: Management described the order book as sound and expects FY27 thermal sales to be better than last year, but this depends on how the winter unfolds.

segments.name: E-commerce and modern trade
segments.commentary: Management targets 20-25% e-commerce growth, with senior heads appointed and warehousing, inventory and IT infrastructure being built.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 10-12% expected in the coming quarter (Q2 FY27).
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 9-10% range in the coming quarter.
A further price hike of 4-5% is planned to be implemented from August, dependent on competitor behaviour.
Advertising and marketing spend to be rationalised from about 10.5% of revenue to 6-7%, which management says will support the EBITDA margin target.
Athleisure expected to grow at least double digits from Q2 and more than double digits for the full year; e-commerce targeted at 20-25% growth.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
Management said a DMS (distributor management system) is being rolled out state by state, with a hands-on presence expected in a year or two; ARS is described as in place but dependent on DMS.
demand_pricing: Q1 price hike of 4-5% was largely passed to trade through extra schemes because of intense competition, so realisations did not reflect it; growth was volume-led.
Gross margin slipped 30 bps YoY to 37.4%.
Yarn prices are rising, which management sees as a favourable pricing environment, but competitors are offering extra discounts and extended sale periods to gain share.
Old inventory across the industry is described as now largely exhausted, with fresh stock at higher prices, which management expects will allow the new rate to stick from August.
Management said competition is mainly from organised players and that Rupa is taking share, but via higher discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall short of the 9-10% guidance given last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said advertising and marketing spend was about 10.5% of revenue in Q1 and would be rationalised to 6-7%, which should help achieve the desired EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the April price hike not show up in realisations, and when will it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intense competition led to extra schemes that passed the hike on to trade. A new rate is expected from August, and it is yet to be implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What is the thermal order book outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sound and healthy order book; management expects thermal to contribute better than last year, but this depends on how the winter season unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset yarn cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a further hike is planned, but it depends on how competitors behave.

qa_highlights.question: What were the athleisure and women's trends, and what is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Athleisure fell 5-7% YoY in Q1 and is targeted at double-digit growth from Q2. Women's share is about 8%, and Softline is being rebranded and gets a new team and fabrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROCE/ROE decline structural, and is there room to cut costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the returns are not desirable and blamed the tough competitive environment. It cited the shift from wholesale to secondary-led sales, LFS, e-commerce and other channels. Cost efficiency is an ongoing process with no fixed target.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity from organised players continues to drive extra schemes, so price hikes may not stick (the April hike was largely passed on).
Whether the planned August price hike is implemented and reflected in realisations.
Thermal sales depend on the timing and severity of the winter season.
Women's wear and athleisure both declined or underperformed in Q1; the recovery is not yet proven.
Management guided 9-10% EBITDA margin last quarter but reported 7.8%; the cut in ad spend to 6-7% of revenue needs to show up next quarter.
533552|2026-06.management_tone: Optimistic on volumes, channels and pricing outlook, but cautious and hedged on price realisation, thermal and women's wear. Responses on competition and returns were often open-ended and deferred to coming quarters.
key_quotes: So, from August onward, we are quite hopeful the new rate will be implemented.
When there is a scope of 2%, there is a scope of another 2%, we have to do it.

531179|2026-06.headline: Arman Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT rose to INR45 crore from a loss of INR15 crore a year ago, with AUM at a record INR2,925 crore (+36% YoY).
531179|2026-06.overview: Consolidated disbursements of INR686 crore were up 76% YoY, the highest ever Q1, while cost-to-income improved to 44.3% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26. GNPA fell to 2.76% and NNPA to 0.84%, with collection efficiency at 96.6% for the quarter. Management repeatedly said the sector has not fully normalised and that volumes were below expectations, with a stated focus on quality over quantity. Namra Finance (microfinance) drove most of the profit improvement, and the individual loan book rose to 33% of the book.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR59 crore in Q4 FY26
vs loss of INR15 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR41 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Arman Financial (standalone)
segments.commentary: AUM INR758 crore (+26% YoY, +4% QoQ); disbursements INR156 crore led by MSME; GTI INR66 crore (+30% YoY); PPOP INR24 crore; PAT INR15 crore (+17% YoY, +48% QoQ).

segments.name: Namra Finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,167 crore (+39% YoY, +8% QoQ); disbursements INR530 crore; GTI INR138 crore (+35% YoY); PPOP INR52 crore (+64% YoY); PAT INR30 crore vs loss of INR28 crore a year ago; NIM 15.37%; GNPA 2.59% from a peak of 3.8%.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by end of FY27; management said the ratio was about 8% this quarter (vs about 9% last quarter) and expects further decline.

Management said FY27 AUM growth of about 25% to 30% was the context for questions, but did not itself restate the figure; growth to be 'careful, calibrated' and recalibrated to collections and delinquency trends.
Credit cost: Vivek Modi said credit cost is expected to stay about 3% to 3.5%; Aalok Patel said including CGFMU cost, 3% sounds about right, maybe 2.5%, and 2% if lucky.
Borrowing cost: approaching rating agencies for upgrades, expected to cut interest cost by about 20-30 bps.
No explicit ROA guidance; Aalok Patel said on a fully levered basis historically about 4.5% and around 3.5-4% at about 20% capital adequacy with current opex.
capex_capacity: Management said current infrastructure can support disbursements of INR750 crore per quarter; Q4 FY26 consolidated disbursements were cited at INR700 crore-plus, and microfinance alone at INR738 crore per the presentation.
Branch network cited by analyst at about 400-425 branches, up from about 275-280 in 2023; management did not dispute this.
CGFMU coverage: about 94% of eligible microfinance portfolio covered as of 30 June 2026.

Liquidity: INR286 crore across cash, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits; INR335 crore undrawn sanctions from existing lenders. Average liquidity about INR300 crore, roughly 1.5 months of repayments plus one month of disbursements.
Solar loans: about INR50 lakh per month in selected areas; zero NPAs so far; yield about 18-20%.
demand_pricing: Q1 volumes were below management's expectations; rejection rates remain relatively high by design.
Individual loans are 33% of the book; about 68-70% of individual-loan EMIs clear via eNACH/UPI by month-end, around 85% cashless in total, with about 14% collected in cash door-to-door.
Management said the individual book is performing better than JLG, while acknowledging the product is new and opex is the key issue.
LAP (loan against property) disbursement is well below the analyst's expected INR40-50 crore per quarter; management cited secured-lending competition from MFIs, SFBs, banks and fintechs.
Rates: management said it would consider cutting rates if the company were earning too much, but has not given it much thought; RBI scrutiny cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why remain cautious given favourable collection and delinquency data?
qa_highlights.answer: Aalok Patel said the data is favourable but rural income growth and jobs quality are concerning on the ground; he called it a little PTSD and said he has no reason to be pessimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said about INR185 crore of pool written off over 24 months was sold to an ARC in March 2025; recovery on it this year is about 10%, and overall write-off recoveries are about 3-4%, with 12-18 months still to run.

qa_highlights.question: When will liquidity fall and disbursements pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquidity is already sufficiently low, averaging about INR300 crore, and described the current level as a 'Goldilocks' position; the team has been in collection mode for two years and volumes should recover over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Yield, funding cost and opex outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is expected to fall toward 7% of AUM; funding cost of about 11.7% is expected to fall 20-30 bps on rating upgrades; on yields, management said it will reduce rates only if earnings become excessive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MSME 31-90 PAR and LAP GNPA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed about 10-15 bps of upward movement in MSME PAR to higher stress in Telangana, with other states stable; Aalok Patel said there were other reasons too.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance and July collections?
qa_highlights.answer: July repayment rates were marginally lower than June, about 3 bps on zero DPD, attributed to rain in Gujarat, UP and Bihar; credit cost guided at about 3-3.5% by Vivek Modi, with management saying 2-3% is possible including CGFMU costs.

qa_highlights.question: ROA and individual loan economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no formal ROA guidance; historically about 4.5% on a fully levered basis, and about 3.5-4% at 20% CAR on current opex. Individual loans are preferred but the product is still new.

Customer promotion as a percentage of gross bookings at about a five-quarter high, attributed to B2C mix and discounting.
Middle East as an endpoint under 20% of business; including transit, 30%-plus of international travel transits the region.

qa_highlights.question: Will air margins stay subdued for FY27 given supply cuts and incentive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East carriers have not closed annual PLB deals, so revenue is recognised at lower rates; capacity is normalising and margins are expected to improve in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is MICE revenue loss recoverable in the next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MICE restructuring from international to domestic group travel is over; Q2 volumes are about 50% above Q1 with better margin profile.

qa_highlights.question: Can Travel Pro bookings run at about INR200 crore and are contracts multi-year?

qa_highlights.question: How is MICE contribution to profit and what is the long-run profit mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICE carries about 9-10% gross margin and 40-plus% operating margin; it should account for about 20-25% of profit, not 50%. Q1 MICE impact estimated at INR4-5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring, training and infrastructure for Kanoo were incurred in Q1 before revenue; absolute people costs stay at these levels, with revenue contribution from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work has continued for about six quarters across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman and SEC; no timeline given as regulator timing is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate card product and working capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Working with banks on a product that balances MDR of about 165 bps against shorter credit cycles; also working with Amex, HDFC/Citi and SBI on card platforms, targeting airlines and hotels to bear card cost. Long lead time.

532811|2026-06.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.
532811|2026-06.overview: Turnover rose 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore, but PAT fell to INR11.42 crore from INR51.11 crore, with EBITDA margin at 4.29% versus 8.59%. Management attributed the drop to a INR29 crore AIIMS Jammu bill reduction (2.6 percentage points), labour cost increases of roughly 35-40% in NCR (about 50% of the order book), higher staff costs, and SIR/election-related disruption in West Bengal and Assam. Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

financial_highlights.value: Sharp increase YoY; mgmt expects similar ~INR15-16 crore per quarter
financial_highlights.change: due to mobilisation advance for Central Vista

segments.name: NCR projects (about 50% of order book)
segments.commentary: Labour minimum wages rose about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled categories in Haryana and UP, with projects running at 40-50% labour strength. Management estimated a company-level EBITDA hit of about 1.5% this quarter, up to 5% of turnover on some projects where material is client-issued.

segments.name: AIIMS Jammu
segments.commentary: Final bill reduced by INR29 crore after finalisation; the matter is going to arbitration. Impact is 2.6 percentage points on EBITDA. Management says the project is closed and no further hit is expected.

segments.name: Central Vista (Ministry of Housing/CPWD-type govt project)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR700 crore billing in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore in FY28, with Nirman Bhawan demolition complete and Udyog Bhawan 90% demolished. Full project completes in FY29.

segments.name: CST (Mumbai railway station project)
segments.commentary: Q1 billing about INR70 crore; management targets about INR400-450 crore for FY27 (hoping to cross INR500 crore total) and about INR700 crore in FY28. Earlier target was about INR600 crore.

segments.name: Gems and Jewellery Park
segments.commentary: Work on ground delayed by client design changes; expected to start in Q3 FY27. Targets INR100 crore billing in FY27 and about INR450 crore in FY28; 3.5-year completion.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27 retained, with the low end attributed to NGT uncertainty.
No double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26-level margins over the next three quarters, but gave no firm timeline.
Expects some client compensation for labour cost increases to flow over the next two quarters; NGT impact on Q3 unquantified.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus earlier INR8,000 crore guidance; bidding to be less aggressive.
FY27 capex cut to INR220-250 crore (from about INR300 crore); Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Working capital expected to improve from current level (119 days), with Assam receivables collection resuming.
Expects double-digit margin aspiration for FY28 but said it is hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex guided at INR220-250 crore for FY27, down from about INR300 crore earlier; Q1 capex about INR60 crore.

Machinery investment planned to offset labour shortages, and digitisation is in progress.

Dahlias (DLF) and DLF Downtown (about INR1,600-1,700 crore) projects delayed by design changes; billing targets INR30-35 crore/month from Dahlias and INR25-30 crore/month from DLF Downtown.
demand_pricing: Net order book INR20,663.52 crore; private sector about 62% of order book; fixed-price contracts about 10.34%.

Order inflow only INR512.81 crore in FY27 to date; RML (about INR500 crore) is L1 but not converted. Odisha government university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1 hospital/university) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract.

523676|2026-06.headline: Golkunda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.7% YoY to INR85.2 crore and EBITDA rose 69% to INR8.64 crore, with margin up to 10.14%.
523676|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR85.2 crore versus INR69.4 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 69% to INR8.64 crore and EBITDA margin expanding from 7.35% to 10.14%. Net profit rose about 64% to INR5.14 crore (margin 6.03% vs 4.2%). Management framed the quarter as the start of a domestic diversification phase, anchored by a newly operational Andheri (Mumbai) manufacturing facility outside the SEZ. This was the company's first formal earnings call, and management said near-term volumes from the domestic facility will be small.

financial_highlights.change: +22.7% YoY vs INR69.44 crore in Q1 FY26
up from INR230 crore two years earlier
up from INR16.9 crore two years earlier (about 35%)

segments.commentary: Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain) contributes about 85-90% of total business; USA share has fallen to below 10% from 20-30% a year earlier due to tariffs. Management pegs current export run-rate at about INR280 crore.

segments.name: Domestic (Andheri, Mumbai facility)
segments.commentary: Facility covers about 5,360 sq ft with estimated capacity of 125-150 kg jewellery per annum, expected to lift overall capacity by 50-60%. Currently producing sample lines; management expects only INR15-20 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Lab-grown diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Management put lab-grown at less than 5-7% of current revenue, mainly from the US market. Domestic B2C lab-grown retail launch is targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of around 15-20%, predominantly from exports.

Andheri facility peak revenue potential of around INR250-300 crore in about three years; revenue mix depends on gold carat mix (shift from 18k to 14k, 10k, 9k).
Five-year target of revenue more than double the current level.
Domestic EBITDA margin expected to be tighter initially, converging to export levels over time; B2C expected to be better margin than B2B but insignificant in FY27.

Preferential allotment of convertible warrants (about INR27 crore) to fund facility expansion and working capital.
Inventory days cited at roughly 10-11 times for exports, with management expecting domestic to be similar or better.
demand_pricing: Retail customers are shifting from 18k to 14k, and in some cases 9k-10k gold jewellery, following gold price increases.

Competition in domestic lab-grown is nascent; management named no specific head-to-head competitor and cited branded retailers and traditional jewellers as entrants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic expansion strategy given competition from organised players?

qa_highlights.question: Is the US business exported or through a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidiary; sales are to wholesalers, distributors and retailers in Middle East, USA and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the new capacity generate?

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and 2030 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth of 15-20%, mainly exports; domestic to reach 50% of business by 2030, implying INR550-600 crore total on current export base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the lab-grown contribution and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab-grown is under 5-7% of revenue, mostly US; management hopes it will be a significant domestic contributor but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 revenue from the Mumbai facility and when does B2C start?
qa_highlights.answer: INR15-20 crore in FY27; B2C launch targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026), with B2C insignificant in FY27.

risks_watch: Domestic ramp is unproven: FY27 facility revenue guided at only INR15-20 crore against a 2030 target of about 50% domestic mix.
Heavy concentration: top 10 customers are about 60-65% of revenue, and Middle East is 85-90% of business.
Domestic EBITDA is expected to be thinner initially, which could dilute the 10.14% margin as B2B and B2C scale.
Gold price shifts toward lower carat jewellery and the 250-300 crore capacity estimate depend on mix assumptions.
Management said the company is still building a brand and retail experience for B2C; it gave no B2C target beyond the Diwali launch.
523676|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term domestic and lab-grown ambitions, but vague or deferential on specifics; several answers lacked numbers (e.g., competitors, B2C mix, margins) and the CEO had to look up top-10 customer share. Clear and specific on near-term FY27 guidance and the Middle East share.
key_quotes: This is expected to increase our overall manufacturing capacity by approximately 50% to 60%.
So right now for the current year, our target is to have a growth of around 15 % to 20%.

531147|2026-06.headline: Alicon Q1 FY27 crossed Rs 500 crore quarterly sales for first time; total income Rs 579 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA margin 9.5% vs 11.4% last year.
531147|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 37% YoY on a consolidated basis, with total income of Rs 579 crore and PAT of Rs 12 crore (+23% YoY). Margins stayed under pressure from aluminium and other input cost inflation, and the European subsidiary declined as legacy programmes ended. Management guided FY27 underlying growth of 12-15% and at least 1% EBITDA margin improvement, and announced a Rs 125 crore leased facility at Shikrapur expected to generate about Rs 500 crore of annual revenue in 4-5 years. Executable order book stands at about Rs 8,450 crore over 2026-2031.

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.4% in last year; management says 11.4% when aluminium impact removed
about 124 tonnes above prior-year Q1 per management; FY26 tonnage 34,000 tonnes

segments.commentary: Standalone growth 43.6% reported and 22% underlying; standalone profitability stronger than international. Commercial vehicle business grew about 26% on conversion of recently acquired businesses to mass production.

segments.name: International (Europe, Slovakia plant)
segments.commentary: Softer quarter as mature programmes reached end of life; new programmes including an e-Axle business are in development, with SOP expected from Q3 FY27. Management expects the decline to continue for one or more quarters.

segments.name: Non-automotive
segments.commentary: Only about 2% of the Rs 8,450 crore order book (about Rs 126 crore). Wins include industrial HVAC compressor housings for data centres and first tractor cylinder head business; new dedicated sales team created.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at 12-15% underlying (excluding aluminium effect), revised up from earlier 10% expectation.
At least 1% EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY27 versus FY26 levels, driven by customer price revisions and internal productivity.
Aluminium pass-through is contractually immediate from 1 April per management; part of manufacturing-cost recovery still under discussion with customers, with closures expected in Q2 and Q3.
Management aspires to margins of 14-15% over time but declined to give a timeline; ROCE of 10.7% in FY26 targeted to reach about 15% through process changes.
Revenue plan of about Rs 1,600 crore by 2030 (Q&A), analyst characterised this as roughly doubling revenue; management confirmed.
Inorganic growth announcement promised by Q4 FY27; further organic capacity investments to be announced.
capex_capacity: Shikrapur leased facility (about 1.36 lakh sq ft, 5 km from existing plant): Rs 125 crore over 2-3 years; possession from 1 September 2026; SOP targeted by March 2027; about Rs 500 crore annual revenue at full run in 4-5 years, with capacity starting at about 3,000 tonnes and rising to about 7,000 tonnes.
Facility will house GDC, LPDC and machining capabilities; funded mainly by internal accruals plus borrowings; about Rs 70 crore of FY27 capex earmarked for it.
Capacity utilisation close to 100% in the last quarter, and above 90% per management.
Plans to free up some capacity over the next two quarters by exiting lower-value 2-wheeler business (market share cut by 1-2%) and reallocate it to higher-value products; handover takes 6-8 months.

Management indicated a plan to add roughly 10,000 tonnes of Indian capacity (analyst paraphrase); further investments to be announced.
demand_pricing: Executable order book about Rs 8,450 crore as on 30 June 2026 over 2026-2031, including Q1 wins; excludes ongoing programmes that were already in revenue before FY26. About 40% is export and about 30% of total is deemed export.
Order book mix: EV about 16%, hybrid about 12%, structural (technology-agnostic) about 10%, non-auto about 2%; balance is ICE and 2-wheeler per the call.

Acquisitions in the quarter across auto and non-auto with potential revenue above Rs 450 crore over five years; entry into two large Indian PV and CV OEMs with visibility of about Rs 850 crore over five years.
JLR EV supply running at about 600 sets per week, expected to rise from January 2027 and peak by calendar Q3 2026; management said consumption only marginally reflected in Q1.
Value addition grew about 17.6% in the quarter; management says growth is shifting to higher value-added parts.
Management reports competitive pressure is rising but states Alicon is not fighting on price in differentiated products.

qa_highlights.question: How will the overseas business perform for the rest of FY27 and FY28, and what is the revenue outlook over one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European slowdown may persist for one or more quarters but should reverse from Q4 FY27 with new e-Axle and other programmes. FY27 growth guided at 12-15% underlying; the 17.5% Q1 underlying growth is the base for the one- and three-year outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will price increases flow through and where should margins go over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some customer corrections for manufacturing cost inflation are still pending and expected in Q2 and Q3. FY27 target is at least 1% EBITDA margin improvement; no firm FY28-29 margin guidance beyond aspiration toward prior levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth slow after 17% in Q1 versus 12-15% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no clear reason for a slowdown currently, though quarter-by-quarter volatility remains. Guidance was corrected to 12-15%, not 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is ROCE weak despite high utilisation, and what is the capex payback threshold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 ROCE was 10.7%, with a target of about 15% through process tweaks and exiting low-value business. Typical capex payback is 3-4 years. Loss-making JLR-linked investments are expected to turn around in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What changed versus past order book claims that did not materialise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said past EV bets had long validation periods and JLR volumes fell or SOPs slipped. Current order book focuses on ICE, hybrid and structural parts with shorter validation, and growth now comes from traditional products.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the development spend went into capacity and what is the non-auto strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Development spend went into larger, heavier parts (28-30 kg vs earlier 12-15 kg), requiring new machines and dedicated teams. Intangible spend about Rs 18-20 crore last year, Rs 3-5 crore per quarter. Non-auto aspiration unchanged but about 2% today; management expects meaningful change by end-FY28.

532365|2026-06.headline: Dynacons Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR313 crore (from INR328 crore) on OEM-linked delivery delays, while EBITDA rose to INR40 crore and order book reached INR3,104 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 revenue shortfall fold back into next quarter, and how are Q2 and Q3 shaping up?

qa_highlights.question: Can operating margin (about 13%) keep rising toward a mid double-digit level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give margin guidance; it credited business mix, disciplined execution and managed services, and said quarterly margins may fluctuate with project mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA is lease rental, and why did PBT stay flat while EBITDA grew?

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR3,100 crore order book convert and can 20%+ growth be sustained?

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive landscape and why is PSU share higher than private banks?

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.</overview>

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement ~₹104 crores at June end; channel partners up to 1,100+ from 900; 70+ locations across 30 states.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 55% QoQ in Q1, average monthly disbursement ₹144 crores; origination locations expanded from 25 to 50; ~30% of sanctions processed digitally.

segments.name: Business loans / shopkeeper loans
segments.commentary: Business loans growing ~15-16%; shopkeeper loans deliberately not being accelerated given credit cost and ROA considerations.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3% to 3.5%, versus 1.98% today.
Opex to AUM may fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ due to investment and clustered gold branch openings; internal benchmark trends lower over FY27.
Management expects disbursement yield gains to offset any cost of borrowing uptick; no NIM pressure seen at current trajectory.
Gold branch addition of ~400 in FY27, similar to last year's pace; 60 branches already opened this financial year.
Write-offs expected to stay around ₹275-280 crores per quarter run-rate, with no material legacy-book write-offs left.
Management is comfortable on capital for the next 4-5 quarters after the ₹2,500 crore QIP; no further raise indicated.
Provision coverage expected to remain range-bound, with rising gold and education loan share lowering overall PCR over time.
capex_capacity: 460 gold loan branches; plan to add ~400 in FY27, targeting new states including Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh.
Consumer durables capacity to process ~50,000 customers a month, per management.
Education loan origination footprint expanded from 25 to 50 locations; consultant network of 600+ partners.
AI estate: 101 AI projects across 21 departments (50 deployed, 51 in pipeline); ~130 smart agents live in production.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield up ~50 bps QoQ on product mix; portfolio yield up ~17-19 bps; management cites pricing power in prime PL and digital channels.
New products accounted for 26% of disbursements in Q1 vs 24% in Q4 and 20% in the quarter before.
Management says it will slow growth in products where calibration needs it; business loans being grown only to 10-16% levels versus over 40% in used cars.
Retail loan exposure industry-wide grew over 16% YoY as of March 2026; Q1 FY27 cumulative GST collections up 8.4% YoY.
6 MoB 30+ on Q1 sourcing at 0.64%, vs 1.05% in Q4 and 1.66% in Q3FY25 (as stated by management).

524000|2026-09.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 FY27: PAT up 22% QoQ to ₹375 crore, ROA 2.18%, credit cost down to 2.19%, AUM ₹74,008 crore.
524000|2026-09.overview:
Management described Q2 FY27 as an inflection point, with AUM up about 10.4% QoQ to ₹74,008 crore and PAT of ₹375 crore (up 21.8% QoQ). NIM plus fees rose 16 bps QoQ to 9.26%, while credit cost fell to 2.19% from 2.40-2.41% and GNPA fell to 1.20% from 1.37%. Opex-to-average AUM rose to 4.15% on frontloaded investments in collections, AI and gold branches, which management said sits within the 10-25 bps guided range. New products contributed 28% of disbursements, and the company is still building cross-sell.</overview>

segments.name: Commercial vehicles

segments.name: Education loans

segments.name: Consumer durables

guidance_outlook: Credit cost expected to keep sloping down and gradually stabilise; management said it is tracking better than plan, with a visible path over the next one to two years.
Opex-to-AUM expected to move on plan, with 300-400 branches invested in per year and gold branches breaking even in about 13 months.
Management targets a sustainable ROA with a 'peak' expected in about 2.5-3 years; a commitment on ROA by June 2028 was referenced.
A 25 bps lending rate increase was already passed through about a week before the call; pass-through of further hikes is expected to depend on product and market.
AUM CAGR target of 35-40% over the next couple of years was referenced by an analyst; management did not restate it.
Management aims for consumer durable customer franchise to roughly double this year.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network at 550 branches, targeting about 200 new branches in FY27.
AI portfolio at 143 projects (up from 101), of which 84 are live in production and 59 underway; 34 delivered in Q2, a record quarter.

Management flagged possible fee compression from a proposed insurance commission regulation but said earnings could absorb it.

qa_highlights.question: How far has cross-sell progressed (products per customer now vs a year or two ago), and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a products-per-customer figure; said cross-sell has only just started and the metric will be more relevant in about a year, with improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How many new products are profitable, and what blended ROA is possible once they mature?
qa_highlights.answer: No product-level count given. Management said gold branches break even in about 13 months, new businesses are not yet at full ROA, and peak ROA is expected in about 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will credit cost settle, and how will product mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 2.19% a first milestone that looks structural. CRO said 12 MoB 90-plus for origination post September 2024 improved by over 53% versus the book 12 months earlier, and credit cost is tracking better than plan.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50 bps repo hike and fixed vs floating mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of borrowing rose minimally during the tightening; NCDs are about 30% of borrowings and fixed-rate; pricing power allows pass-through. A 25 bps increase was already passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Trade-off between growth and profitability; sustainable ROA and the split of ROA gains between operating leverage and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three levers (spread, opex-to-AUM, credit cost) contribute over the next two years. Quarterly opex may fluctuate because of AI investment; no specific split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality improvement from underwriting or benign credit conditions? Are AI/ML models reducing loss rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to proprietary models (30-35 models) and calibration. It cited bureau data showing consumer durable borrowers completing 9-month loans are about 40% better credit than industry.

qa_highlights.question: With most of the book under 12 months seasoned, why are write-offs still high, and what is the impact of the insurance commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said slippages were contained across stages and GNPA and write-offs are falling; core credit cost impairment is stable in absolute terms despite over 10% QoQ book growth. On insurance commissions, management said fee compression could be absorbed by lending spreads and operating leverage.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.</overview>

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview:
Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.</overview>

541195|2026-06.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.
541195|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover was Rs 239.49 crore (up 40.46% YoY) and value of production Rs 260.36 crore (up 7.9%). PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Defense about 66%, space (ISRO) about 21%, energy about 9%, others about 4%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Current-year export sales Rs 33 crore to date with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore; target about 10% of turnover (about Rs 100-120 crore).

segments.name: Titanium
segments.commentary: Melted about 750 tonnes last year after new melting facility; titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore cited. Management says titanium and super alloys carry higher margins than special steel.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 margins expected to be hit somewhat; management expects normalisation from Q3 FY27, with EBITDA margin returning toward 20-21%.
FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26 growth, though management said sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year is not practicable.
FY27 normal capex about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance; Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex over 2-3 years, with returns from year 4 and proposal still awaiting Board and ministry approval.
Metal bank: procurement under way for one customer; further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, with implementation targeted next quarter.
Aluminium JV plant at Nellore (with NALCO) being closed; a separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied 7000-series aluminium billets has been done as first commercial order.
Export expectation: at least 15-20% increase on the 10% export base over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex proposed for replacing ageing equipment; sent to ministry for evaluation, management declined to give timeline.
Isothermal forging completed in 6,000-tonne press for nickel-based super alloy for fighter aircraft engine; orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year.
New titanium melting facility commissioned last year; about 750 tonnes melted last year, with expected growth.
Spring plant in campus started; sample order received from BEML. Preliminary BAFA licence obtained for metal powder equipment, expected on campus by next year.
Bulletproof jacket (ABHED, from DRDO/IIT Delhi) fabricated; testing expected to complete this quarter, with test certificates by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Raw-material prices of nickel, molybdenum, tungsten rose sharply; cobalt also higher. Adverse price variance of about Rs 13 crore (or Rs 14 crore per later remark) in Q1.
LPG price nearly doubled due to Middle East conflict; furnaces are LPG-fired, affecting Q1 and possibly Q2.
Freight cost mostly booked at fixed terms; management said it sometimes absorbs freight increases on fixed-price contracts.
No nomination-based orders now; all orders won through competitive bidding.
Titanium sourced by import from Eastern Europe (former Russian Federation); management reports no import constraints currently.
Scrap usage in melt typically 50-60% for normal aerospace grades; virgin material mandated for human spaceflight and critical engine parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Madhubala Kalluri cited raw-material prices and LPG prices, which nearly doubled. She said Q2 may be hit, with normalisation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex takes 2-3 years, with returns from year 4. FY27 capex will be about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aluminium plant still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Nellore aluminium JV plant is being closed, pending ministry approval. The separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied aluminium billets is an alternative route.

qa_highlights.question: Will the S400 certification generate meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is testing-only revenue, conservatively estimated at about 10% of export base, with clarity in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to 20-21% in Q3 depends on LPG and raw-material prices easing; Q2 margin likely lower.
Fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed to raw-material and freight cost increases.
Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex is not yet Board- or ministry-approved; no timeline given.
Metal bank benefits are customer-owned and not on company balance sheet; implementation and utilisation are still to be confirmed.
Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.
541195|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and certifications, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, capex timelines and the scale of new orders. Management repeatedly attributed Q1 margin pressure to temporary LPG and raw-material factors and declined to quantify the Rs 1,000 crore capex return or the S400 revenue.
key_quotes: Q2 may be little bit hit will be there, but Q3 we have hope that we will be coming to normal state.
Only because of these little raw material and LPG issues only that was little lower bottom line.
So, we reduced our scrap inventory by Rs. 75 crores.
We are not going ahead with that plant.

vs ~8,200 MT in Q1 FY26, more than doubled

544258|2026-06.headline: Western Carriers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR465 crores, with PAT of about INR9 crores and domestic TEUs up 37%.
544258|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR465 crores from INR416 crores, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores (4.1% margin) and PAT of about INR9 crores, up about 13% QoQ. Total container throughput of 58,261 TEUs beat Q4 FY26 (57,754) for the first time, driven by domestic volumes up 37% YoY while EXIM grew only 3.2%. Management attributed EXIM weakness to Middle East war-linked vessel disruption and freight rate spikes, and said working capital days fell from 120 to about 111 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. Analysts pressed on the lack of price pass-through, weak cash generation and receivables; management did not commit to a price hike.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.7 crore (+40%+) but profitability compressed by high-cost inventory and inability to pass through input costs; management expects gross margin recovery through Q2 and normal levels by Q3. Company proposes to acquire a further 11% stake, taking holding to 62%.

guidance_outlook: Q2 spends on trade and influencer engagement to rise further to widen the gap between Indigo's top-line growth and the industry; management noted bottom line grew faster than top line, meaning it 'did not do enough'.
No concrete Q2 margin guidance; management called the raw material situation a 'fuzzy' roller coaster and said Q2 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter, suggesting a six-month comparison.
July was a very good month with top-line momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August not yet assessed.
No new price increases planned as of now; a price cut in H2 is possible, most likely post-Diwali, with trade spends reduced correspondingly.
Growth versus industry is not formally guided; management said the gap could be about 10 percentage points if industry growth is around 15%, and it would not give a concrete number.
No significant capex expected for the next three years after the Jodhpur water-based plant.
EBITDA margin could decline about 1 percentage point or rise 0.5 percentage point in the coming period; management said margin is not the focus.
A/P spends are to be assessed on an annual basis; brand investment for the full year is 'undiminished'.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant: 90,000 kilolitres per annum, in final commissioning; trial production expected within about 10 days of the call, per management, and to stabilise in about a month. Delay was attributed to a slow civil contractor, not raw material issues.
Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.
Legacy water-based plant to be scrapped and output shifted to the new automated plant; opex expected to be broadly unchanged.
Solar capacity installed 350 kW across Pune and Cochin; a further 1,200 kW planned at Jodhpur.
No significant capex planned for the next three years; free cash flow expected to improve versus the last five years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand has improved progressively from Q3 FY26; management said demand is back near normal growth conditions.
Price increases in March and April were steep and frequent, protecting margins; raw material costs have eased from peaks but remain elevated and volatile.
Channel overstocking not seen at Indigo; management said the market leader may have seen some overstocking.
Distribution: about 19,400 active dealers (up about 800 YoY) and about 12,400 active tinting machines (up about 1,100 YoY).
Wood coatings: two-pack polyurethane launch planned for September and October in phases, in a segment management estimates at upwards of INR9,000 crore; it had no presence there earlier.
Differentiated products are about 29% to 30% of revenue; management said the company is not planning new differentiated launches.
Competition: management said no meaningful change from JSW's acquisition of AkzoNobel or the Birla Opus entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

risks_watch: Raw material prices remain elevated and volatile after the Iran war disruption; Q2 margin path is uncertain given mixed inventory costs.
Festive-season execution depends on the Jodhpur water-based plant stabilising in about one month after trial production.
Apple Chemie margin recovery depends on consuming high-cost inventory by Q2 and normal margins by Q3.
Management plans to spend more on trade and influencers in Q2, which may pressure gross margin by a couple of percentage points.
Possible H2 price cuts post-Diwali if input costs stay at current levels.
Wood coatings two-pack PU launch in September and October is a new category push that needs a specialised sales team.
Quarter's PAT margin includes a mark-to-market treasury gain, so underlying profit growth may be lower than reported.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.</overview>

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.
capex_capacity: Katepally: RDX and HMX plant integration and erection almost complete; water trials expected September 2026, lasting about one month before production.
Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.
demand_pricing: Export licences: several received in the past week, with some in pipeline; material moving out of factories. Export of INR150-200 crore targeted in Q2.

INR350 crore international defence order (April 2026): export licence still in process; management said licence processing takes at least 3-4 months after importing-country import licence; some dispatches expected in the last quarter of the year.
Bulk explosives: pricing tied to raw material costs; more than 40 players in the segment; management declined to predict FY28.
RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.
Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions under DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL testing; management expects about 6 more months.
Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR20 crore to INR11 crore, and is INR11 crore sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the roughly INR400 crore of export licences, and what export revenue is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Several licences received in the past week, with material moving; INR150-200 crore of export is targeted in Q2, and prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR430 crore October 2025 order on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook if raw material prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices are not normalising yet; contracts already signed must be executed first, then prices will be raised. The 15-20% EBITDA target is for this financial year.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to about 6% (per analyst calculation) from about 15% in the prior year, with raw material cost and under-absorption cited; recovery to 15-20% depends on contracts and price pass-through.
FY27 revenue of INR600 crore needs INR500-600 crore in 9 months after INR103 crore in Q1; Chaff imports remain dependent on conditions abroad.
Export licence timing (3-4 months processing plus importing-country licence) could delay the INR350 crore April 2026 order.
Katepally commissioning relies on water trials in September and imported mixer parts; any slippage pushes production later.
Andhra Pradesh expansion land pricing unresolved; Apollo's stance on expansion not yet confirmed.
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal of about INR30 crore on the July 2023 flares order, expected by October-November 2026.
Unclear Apollo synergy details; management said more to come next quarter.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.</overview>
