segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.
capex_capacity: India: 5 kg/day gold casting capacity, upgraded from IPO proceeds to 120% expansion (cited as 5 kg Kerala, 8 kg silver), with about 25% utilisation today.
Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.
At 100% utilisation management cited India about Rs 7 crore/day (about Rs 2,500 crore/yr at 5 kg/day) and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day; these are indicative and not guidance.
Additional working capital needed to reach peak utilisation; to be funded via internal accruals, debt and possibly equity, gradually.
Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total value and rationale of the Sharjah acquisition, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years; when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.
544410|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 76 crore, up 38% YoY but down 27% QoQ from INR 104 crore in Q4, which management attributed to seasonality and deferred execution. EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; -27% QoQ vs INR 104 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1 (about INR 1,090 crore total)

financial_highlights.change: from INR -49 crore in Q4 FY26
from about INR 254 crore as of March 2026

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage) developer projects
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR 855-857 crore of developer business (Bihar and Karnataka/KPTCL). Management said no revenue recognition from these in FY27, only EPC billing on the standalone books; Karnataka dispute was resolved in KPTCL's favour and the company is targeting a sale of that project.

segments.name: Solar EPC and EPC orders
segments.commentary: Solar EPC order of about INR 165 crore from Solarium Green Energy, which management expects to execute fully in FY27. Adani EPC billing was largely completed in Q1 (INR 36 crore of deferred work executed); a further solar EPC order of about INR 12 crore (8.36 MWh) was won.

segments.name: Utility vs C&I BESS
segments.commentary: Company has stopped bidding for utility-scale BESS for about 10 months and is shifting to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh installations), where management says margins are better. Adani project gave about 26% gross margin in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target: minimum 25%.
Margin guidance of 12-13% EBITDA is maintained on a full-year basis, with H2 expected to be stronger; Q1 margin is affected by low turnover and high fixed-cost ratio.
FY27 PAT margin expected at about 8.5-9%, not 10%, due to higher costs from new plants, import costs and hiring.
Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Gujarat UPS plant both expected operational in Q2 FY27; SAP and Salesforce expected operational by end of H1 FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 120-150 by March 2027; management aims for positive operating cash flow by year-end FY27.
Jhajjar BESS utilisation: not more than 20-25% in FY27, 40-50% in FY28 (around INR 500 crore revenue targeted in FY28); steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.2 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in final stage of commissioning; earlier delayed, management cited cost and logistics movements and a strategy shift to C&I. Commercial operation now expected by end of H1 FY27.
Gujarat: new UPS manufacturing facility progressing as planned, expected to start commercial operations in Q2 FY27.
Existing manufacturing in Pune and Navi Mumbai.

Bihar BESS (developer/rental model): yearly cash flow of about INR 16 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of INR 32.40 crore; SBI facility tied up in SPV, LC-backed by Bihar DISCOM, no corporate guarantee.
Karnataka BESS (KPTCL): annual cash flow of about INR 45.72 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of about INR 81 crore; management prioritising a sale post-COD.
demand_pricing: Order book approx INR 1,090 crore including L1. Excluding developer orders (about INR 855 crore), in-hand orders are about INR 236 crore, plus dealer business of about INR 10 crore per month, giving about INR 306-307 crore additional order in hand.
Bids under evaluation of about INR 2,000+ crore, including two large orders of about INR 1,800 crore.
Utility BESS margins under pressure: management said bidders quoted below cost assuming Chinese supply negotiations; cited China export restrictions and a 2% battery tax from 1 September.
Q1 FY27 order wins included an INR 11 crore BESS project from a corporate customer and a INR 165 crore solar EPC order.

Trade receivables: about INR 46 crore realised from the CCTNS (Pune) project in Q1, with a large further amount expected by end-August; management said most of the INR 231 crore is government-funded with no realisation risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the deferred Q4 orders (Adani INR 43 crore, SAIL INR 7 crore, South Eastern Railway INR 13 crore) was executed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 36 crore has been executed. Adani is almost fully billed; SAIL and South Eastern Railway are to be billed mainly in Q2, with some South Eastern Railway work spilling into Q3 pending site clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and that the Adani billing was the major Q4 item. It said the 12-13% margin is a full-year target, with H2 stronger, and that Q1 fixed-cost absorption is weak at INR 76 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days fell to 168 from 185; target about 120-150 by March 2027. Operating cash flow improved to about INR -16 crore from INR -49 crore, with a goal of turning positive by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin should be expected from the Jhajjar plant, and what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 utilisation not above 20-25%; FY28 40-50% with around INR 500 crore revenue targeted. Steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%, with C&I focus preferred over utility BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further equity dilution or significant borrowing over the next 1.5-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution is planned for at least the next year; the Bihar debt sits in an SPV, and the INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital. Any future dilution would be tied to a major expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and realisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell from INR 254 crore (March) to INR 231 crore (June) and dropped further by mid-August. Management expects about half to be collected by end-Q2, with most of the Solarium EPC realised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on order inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR 1,090 crore order book and bids of INR 2,000+ crore under evaluation, and expects the non-developer order book to grow over the next year as qualifications and bid participation increase.

509079|2026-06.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.
509079|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR260.8 crore versus INR226.9 crore a year earlier and INR252.1 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY vs INR226.9 crore; +3% QoQ vs INR252.1 crore
+42% YoY vs INR33.2 crore; +6% QoQ vs INR44.7 crore
+349 bps YoY vs 14.6%; +35 bps QoQ vs 17.74%
+85% YoY vs INR16.3 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR27.6 crore
+86% YoY vs INR12.1 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR20.6 crore

segments.name: Critical Care
segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.name: Women's health / IVF (Puregraf, Ferticare, Zenova)
segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claims to be number 2 in toxin type A in India, made from its own strain. Filler partnership with Revanesse (Prollenium, Canada) expected to launch in India around December-January, subject to registration in Q2 or mid-Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Shifted to a model that earns fee income alongside supply revenue. Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. Approvals were secured in 8 countries in the quarter.

segments.name: GLP-1 (semaglutide, via Hetero)
segments.commentary: Operates purely as a CMO for Hetero, which received permission in May 2026; Q1 revenue contribution was residual. A 10-15 day plant shutdown in Q1 was for a new machine. Management expects traction from Q2 and the main contribution in Q3, with 70% of capacity targeted for international use.

guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Indore has about 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial capacity and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Depot and liposomal lines are in installation and qualification, with both targeted to be operational this year.
Indore has four lines: two lyophilisation lines, one suspension/liquid vial line, and one ampoule line. Target mix is roughly 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation, and 20-30% complex injectables.
Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred until after next year pending cash flow.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per vial is about INR80-100 on current product mix (pantoprazole 10 ml vial at about INR60-80). Management aims to move to INR300-400 and eventually an average of INR500 per vial with depot, liposomal and complex injectables.
Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

532522|2026-06.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.
532522|2026-06.overview:
Standalone PBT rose 33% YoY to INR 1,514 crore and PAT to INR 1,133 crore, with consolidated PBT of INR 1,491 crore described as the highest ever Q1. Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.</overview>

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial

Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.
Strategic ambition: become number two in decorative and number one in industrial coatings, with a 2030-31 vision; decorative aim is market share gains while protecting absolute EBITDA.
Project Akshaya cost programme targets synergies with JSW Paints; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1 and a 3-year roadmap set.
ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.
capex_capacity: Active towns about 3,400-3,500 out of 5,000+ presence; target to lift to about 4,500 this year, focusing on towns above 20,000 population.
Shift to direct/hybrid model in about the top 20 high-share towns; distributor model retained elsewhere.
Cross-manufacturing: JSW Paints made at Gwalior; JSW Dulux products made in JSW Paints plants; some JSW Paints products made in Mohali.
Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

544851|2026-06.headline: MV Electrosystems expects propulsion output to ramp from 10 units in September to about 40 per month by January, against an order book of 564 propulsion systems worth about INR989 crores.
544851|2026-06.overview: This was the first investor call after the company's listing, with no reported financials in the transcript. Management said deliveries have been limited to 2 or 3 small batches so far, with none in the prior two months, and that IPO proceeds (working capital) now fund a scale-up. Management targets about INR400 crore of revenue this year and roughly 10% PAT once run-rate is reached, though it conceded margins are negative or constrained during the initial ramp. Growth optionality was discussed across EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion, OHE auto fault locators (with PNC Technologies), and marine/electrical adjacencies.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore, described as achievable definitively.
Monthly run-rate of about 40 propulsion systems from January, implying roughly INR70 crore a month and about 480 units a year.
PAT of 10%-plus expected once run-rate is reached; management expects profitability within 2-3 months and margins to improve month over month after stabilisation.
R&D spend to be 3%-4% of revenue over time; R&D team to be expanded with a new centre ready by Q3.
Approximately 15-16 months to EMU propulsion approval including development.

Unit 2 already set up; box fabrication and assembly to start the following Monday after the call.

Two additional shifts planned in the existing factory, cited as enabling about 4,500 systems.
demand_pricing: Management cited Indian Railways building about 1,600-1,700 locomotives a year, about 15,000 locomotives in service needing rehabilitation, and 300-500 EMUs tendered or to be tendered this year.

Company said it won about 25-26% of tendered locomotive propulsion quantity, with competitors including Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha and BHEL. In the last tender, 7 suppliers were awarded small quantities.
Management said margins were very thin across bidders; company was L2 in two tenders and L1 in one. Bulk purchasing (200-300 sets) was cited as offsetting electronics price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PLW/CLW propulsion tender cancellation affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was unaware of any cancellation and noted an active CLW tender for 748 locomotives. Tender-to-order conversion typically takes 45 days, sometimes up to 90.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company meet the December 26 order deadline, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply obligations extend to March and into next financial year. Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, and 40 in January; extensions are typically granted for capacity-constrained suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply given rising electronics costs and no price-escalation clause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10%-plus PAT at full run-rate; early months will have constrained or negative margins. Bulk procurement of 200-300 sets is offsetting global price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement lead times range from 7 days to 6 months, averaging about 45 days. Payments were received within 15 days on all three dispatches. Working capital of about INR200 crore needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation per propulsion system?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply price is INR1.67 crore per locomotive propulsion system; AMC over three years roughly matches that figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMU/MCF approval process and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-month validation at the MCF commissioning depot, performance trials on Delhi-Ambala Road, then a four-month trial covering about 30,000 km before approval.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the ramp from 10 units in September to 40 per month by January, with management admitting near-term margins are negative or constrained.

EMU/Vande Bharat revenue depends on approval about 15-16 months out and an MCF delivery window of 24 months.

demand_pricing: Around 55 new programmes in launch phase, of which 28 launched and in ramp-up; customers include Toyota, Ford and BMW with 7-8 year programme life; company is single-source supplier on these.

Air freight incurred because ocean transit rose from 5 weeks to 9 weeks (sometimes 10 or 8) due to the West Asia conflict; customers in US and Europe; one customer agreed to pay roughly 50% of air freight cost, not yet booked.
Price increases sought from domestic and overseas customers for rupee-driven import inflation, manpower, power, fuel, gas and carbide inserts; Haryana labour cost increase of about 40% cited.
About 75% of customers (by management's statement) moved to real-time raw-material settlement; remaining 25% being onboarded.
Company does not hedge aluminium; customers announce prices. Management said aluminium prices eased slightly in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance of ~10% EBITDA margin given in June if air freight pressures were already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transit times rose from 7 weeks assumed to 9-10 weeks; most air freight was incurred after the early-June call as the situation escalated in late June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 39% growth came from higher metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR100-200 crore of revenue was due to higher metal prices on a consolidated basis; standalone raw-material impact about INR100 crore, with consolidated possibly INR10-15 crore higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and full-year margin outlook and what is the path to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margin would be between Q1 and H2 levels, with margins improving from Q3 as freight normalises and price revisions are realised; it expects to be confident of the trajectory if conditions hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aluminium price assumption behind FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the ruling price around INR320/kg (approximately INR32,000 per tonne); raw-material impact estimated at INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the business reach INR4,000 crore revenue without major capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR4,000 crore plus is achievable with the current setup, with die investments largely recovered upfront from customers except for Maruti and Hero, which pay via piece price.

qa_highlights.question: Will hedging be used to manage aluminium volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company does not bank on commodities; the focus is on passing through raw-material cost via real-time settlements to eliminate the lag.

risks_watch: Air freight and sorting costs (INR12.8-13 crore in Q1) may persist into Q2; recovery from one customer (about 50% of freight) is not yet booked.
Customer settlement timing: 25% of customers not yet on real-time settlement; overseas customers may take longer to accept inflation-related price revisions.
Aluminium price volatility (about 57% higher YoY for a grade) and reliance on customer-led pricing; geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) could extend shipping times.
Quality correlation issue with a major customer put some parts on hold; rust issues from prolonged sea transit required repacking.
Margin recovery to ~10% for FY27 requires about 12-13% in H2 per analyst's arithmetic; management has not given a quarterly margin figure.
Capex, land monetisation and railway/defence revenue numbers were not fully quantified on the call.

500038|2026-06.headline: Balrampur Chini guided ~40% average PLA capacity utilisation for Jan-Mar 2027 and held 45.67 lakh quintals of sugar stock at INR 37.19/kg carrying cost.
500038|2026-06.overview:
Management described FY26 as a tighter-than-expected season with lower production, healthy domestic consumption and ethanol diversion drawing down inventory, which firmed sugar prices to roughly INR 48-49 per kg. Q1 is an off-season quarter with almost no sugar production, so results reflect carrying cost and realisation of inventory from the prior season. The 80,000-tonne PLA plant is on track, with lactic acid commissioning expected in October and PLA in December, and about INR 2,180 crore spent by end-July. Management said it sees no B-heavy or juice diversion next season as a reasonable working assumption, but did not give quantified Q1 financials on the call.</overview>

segments.name: Turkey business
segments.commentary: Order book of INR0.46 billion; about EUR3-3.5 million of orders to execute this year, with no major pipeline for next year. Facility is being kept as a service backup for Europe.

segments.name: Hydro refurbishment
segments.commentary: Several hydro refurbishment orders won and already in Q1 order book; management expects this to be one of TDPS's highest hydro years, with more jobs in Q2 and Q3 pipeline. Not pursuing global expansion for now.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance revised to INR2,600 crores, with a small chance of exceeding it.
Order inflow expected at roughly INR700 crores per quarter, about INR2,800 crores-plus for the full year.

Sufficient capacity for FY28 of about INR22 billion, plus debottlenecking (about INR500 million investment per one statement; about INR100 crores per analyst recap) to reach around INR32 billion; management said this is not a hard ceiling.
FY27 capex stated at about INR50 crores.
Gross contribution margin guidance (approx. plus/minus 1%) maintained; EBITDA guidance of 18-19% referenced by analysts, not explicitly re-stated by management.
Capacity plans for FY29-FY30 to reach INR40 billion-plus to be detailed in next earnings call (~3 months); large-generator opportunity announcement expected in August.
capex_capacity: Current capacity sufficient for FY28 at around INR22 billion; debottlenecking investment of around INR500 million (stated) to lift output toward INR32 billion for FY28.
Analyst recap of INR50 crores capex for FY27 and debottlenecking to ~INR3,200 crores; management confirmed the figure as approximate, plus or minus.
Further capacity additions for generators below 100 MW planned; details to be shared next call after assessing products and capacities.
Capacity to reach INR40 billion-plus targeted for FY29-FY30; specific year not committed.
Large-generator (above 100 MW) opportunity under negotiation; management said close to signing agreements. Such generators take 18-20 months to build.
demand_pricing: Management describes market as very buoyant across segments (AI data centres, grid stabilisation, renewables-linked demand), with shortages of gas turbines, gas engines, transformers and generators.
Gas engines and gas turbines: large-volume orders and forecasts show strong growth.
Steam turbine market growing about 10-12% in captive, biomass and waste-heat recovery.
Domestic India demand described as subdued, around 10-12% growth; export share of orders dominant.
Price variation clauses in customer contracts have been implemented where applicable; management declined to split margin drivers between pricing, cost, mix and FX.
Customer advances received from some customers; management declined to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue exceed INR3,000 crores with current base and no new growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to capacity of about INR32 billion next year with debottlenecking, and said FY29-30 additions would take capacity beyond INR40 billion; details due next call.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected about INR700 crores per quarter and about INR2,800 crores-plus for the year; debottlenecking capex ongoing with INR50 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does guidance include large turbine generators?
qa_highlights.answer: No; large generators take 18-20 months to build, so none expected within six months.

qa_highlights.question: Execution or supply-chain delays affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: No disruption to order inflow; products shipped from factory gate, customers taking delivery, though commissioning may be delayed by customer execution.

qa_highlights.question: Service revenue contribution and scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Service is about 5-6% of sales and growing in line with the business; generators need little service in their first 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables (about INR785 crores) versus cash of INR240 crores; QIP/fundraise rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Payment terms are fixed with customers and cannot be altered significantly; management declined to discuss the fundraise before a board meeting on Friday.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs realisation going forward for generator units?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth will come from both units and realisation; larger generators will raise MW per unit; no FY30 unit guidance given.

risks_watch: Large-generator (above 100 MW) entry: no details on market size, capex, or timing; announcement promised in August.
Management declined to quantify several items: market share, TAM for sub-100 MW and 50-100 MW ranges, customer advance levels, and margin driver breakup.
Receivables of about INR785 crores and working capital intensity; pending fundraise (QIP) details due after board meeting.
Execution delays at data-centre customers could slow commissioning even though orders hold.
Railway order book (INR2.11 billion) with no fresh orders; sustainability review at year-end.
Turkey facility a cost-bearing service backup with minimal next-year business; potential US tariff exposure cited in media, not yet assessed by management.
533553|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and FY27 guidance, but evasive on specifics: repeatedly deferred questions on FY29-30 capacity, large-generator details, margin drivers, fundraise and TAM, citing an upcoming announcement.
